Barrett oesophagus typically produces a distal stricture at the gastro-oesophageal junction identical to a peptic stricture
On double-contrast fluoroscopy, Barrett oesophagus may show a reticular web-like mucosal pattern
options_after: Reflux oesophagitis is usually best demonstrated on single-contrast water-soluble swallow
Fluoroscopic findings of reflux oesophagitis are usually distal and include mucosal granularity, thickened folds, erosions and strictures
Barrett oesophagus is a precursor lesion to oesophageal adenocarcinoma
Barrett oesophagus typically produces a distal stricture at the gastro-oesophageal junction closely comparable to a peptic stricture
On double-contrast fluoroscopy, Barrett oesophagus may show a reticular web-like mucosal pattern
updates.explanation: Reflux oesophagitis is due to acid exposure from gastro-oesophageal reflux and is best demonstrated on double-contrast images. Fluoroscopic findings are usually distal and include mucosal granularity, thickened folds, posterior wall erosions and strictures. Barrett oesophagus is metaplasia to gastric-type adenomatous mucosa and is a precursor to adenocarcinoma. It may show a reticular mucosal pattern and often has a stricture that is abnormally high compared with a peptic stricture.

updates.question_text: Regarding infectious oesophagitis patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Candida oesophagitis ranges from scattered plaque-like lesions to a shaggy oesophagus
Herpes oesophagitis characteristically causes a single large flat ovoid ulcer
Radiography reliably differentiates all infectious causes in routine practice
CMV/HIV oesophagitis characteristically causes a large flat ovoid ulcer
Candida oesophagitis is defined by concentric mucosal ring-like strictures
options_after: Candida oesophagitis ranges from scattered plaque-like lesions to a shaggy oesophagus
Herpes oesophagitis characteristically causes a single large flat ovoid ulcer
Radiography reliably differentiates most infectious causes in routine practice
CMV/HIV oesophagitis characteristically causes a large flat ovoid ulcer
Candida oesophagitis is defined by concentric mucosal ring-like strictures
updates.explanation: Candida oesophagitis has a spectrum from scattered plaque-like lesions in mild disease to a very shaggy-appearing oesophagus in severe disease. Herpes oesophagitis typically causes small discrete ulcerations scattered randomly throughout the oesophagus. CMV/HIV oesophagitis characteristically causes a large flat ovoid ulcer. Although radiographic distinctions have been described, endoscopy and biopsy are typically used in clinical practice to differentiate infectious causes.

updates.question_text: Regarding malignant and benign oesophageal narrowing, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A malignant stricture shows irregular narrowing with shouldered margins, producing an apple-core appearance
A caustic stricture has no increased long-term cancer risk
Radiation strictures generally occur after doses below 10 Gy
Extrinsic compression is best assessed with double-contrast oesophagram alone
CT or MRI is best when extrinsic compression from mediastinal adenopathy is suspected
options_after: A malignant stricture shows irregular narrowing with shouldered margins, producing an apple-core appearance
A caustic stricture lacks increased long-term cancer risk
Radiation strictures generally occur after doses below 10 Gy
Extrinsic compression is best assessed with double-contrast oesophagram alone
CT or MRI is best when extrinsic compression from mediastinal adenopathy is suspected
updates.explanation: A malignant oesophageal stricture shows irregular narrowing with shouldered margins, described as an apple-core appearance. Caustic strictures are associated with increased cancer risk after a long lag time of up to 20 years. Radiation strictures usually require more than 50 Gy and develop months after therapy. If extrinsic compression from mediastinal adenopathy is suspected, cross-sectional imaging with CT or MRI is preferred.

updates.question_text: Regarding oesophageal varices, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Uphill varices are due to superior vena cava obstruction and affect the proximal oesophagus
Downhill varices are due to portal hypertension and affect the distal oesophagus
Varices usually change in size and shape with peristalsis and Valsalva manoeuvre
Thrombosed varices can never mimic a tumour
Uphill varices are most common and are due to portal hypertension affecting the distal oesophagus
options_after: Uphill varices are due to superior vena cava obstruction and affect the proximal oesophagus
Downhill varices are due to portal hypertension and affect the distal oesophagus
Varices usually change in size and shape with peristalsis and Valsalva manoeuvre
Thrombosed varices will not mimic a tumour
Uphill varices are most common and are due to portal hypertension affecting the distal oesophagus
updates.explanation: Varices can usually be distinguished from solid mass because they change size and shape with peristalsis and Valsalva, although thrombosed varices may mimic a tumour. Uphill varices are the common type, due to portal hypertension, and affect the distal oesophagus via the left gastric and periesophageal venous pathways. Downhill varices are less common, caused by superior vena cava obstruction and usually affect the proximal oesophagus.

updates.question_text: Regarding malignant oesophageal disease and motility wave terminology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Direct invasion of the oesophagus is most commonly from pancreatic and renal primaries
Mediastinal lymph node metastases often affect the mid-oesophagus because of proximity to mediastinal nodes
A tertiary wave is a non-propulsive contraction that does not result in oesophageal clearing
A secondary contraction wave is abnormal and always indicates cancer
Esophageal lymphoma is always easy to distinguish from primary oesophageal carcinoma
options_after: Direct invasion of the oesophagus is most commonly from pancreatic and renal primaries
Mediastinal lymph node metastases often affect the mid-oesophagus because of proximity to mediastinal nodes
A tertiary wave is a non-propulsive contraction that does not result in oesophageal clearing
A secondary contraction wave is abnormal and characteristically indicates cancer
Esophageal lymphoma is characteristically easy to distinguish from primary oesophageal carcinoma
updates.explanation: Direct invasion of the oesophagus most commonly arises from gastric, lung or breast primaries, and haematogenous spread is very rare. Mediastinal nodal metastases are often prominent and affect the mid-oesophagus because of its proximity to mediastinal lymph nodes. A tertiary wave is a non-propulsive contraction that does not clear the oesophagus and is seen more commonly in elderly patients. A secondary contraction wave is a normal physiologic wave initiated by a bolus in the oesophagus.

updates.question_text: Regarding achalasia and pseudoachalasia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Achalasia results from failure of the distal oesophagus to relax due to abnormal myenteric ganglia in the Auerbach plexus
The classic imaging appearance is a massively dilated oesophagus with a bird-beak stricture near the gastro-oesophageal junction
Chagas disease produces a radiographically distinctive form that is easily separated from primary achalasia
Pseudoachalasia is caused by obstructing gastro-oesophageal junction cancer and always transiently relaxes with standing
Treatment options include pneumatic dilatation, Heller myotomy, POEM and botulinum toxin injection
options_after: Achalasia results from failure of the distal oesophagus to relax due to abnormal myenteric ganglia in the Auerbach plexus
The classic imaging appearance is a massively dilated oesophagus with a bird-beak stricture near the gastro-oesophageal junction
Chagas disease produces a radiographically distinctive form that is easily separated from primary achalasia
Pseudoachalasia is caused by obstructing gastro-oesophageal junction cancer and characteristically transiently relaxes with standing
Treatment options include pneumatic dilatation, Heller myotomy, POEM and botulinum toxin injection
updates.explanation: Achalasia is caused by inability of the distal oesophagus to relax from abnormal myenteric ganglia in the Auerbach plexus. Its classic imaging appearance is a massively dilated oesophagus ending in a bird-beak stricture near the gastro-oesophageal junction. Chagas disease causes secondary achalasia that is radiographically indistinguishable from primary achalasia. Pseudoachalasia is due to obstructing gastro-oesophageal junction cancer and, unlike achalasia, does not relax with standing. Treatment options include pneumatic dilatation, Heller myotomy, POEM and botulinum toxin injection.

updates.question_text: Regarding scleroderma involving the oesophagus, which statement is correct?
options_before: It causes hyperperistalsis of the distal two-thirds of the oesophagus
It involves the oesophagus in fewer than 10% of patients
Oesophageal dilatation appears only after typical skin changes are advanced
It causes a fixed bird-beak stricture at the gastro-oesophageal junction from failure of sphincter relaxation
It produces lack of peristalsis of the distal two-thirds of the oesophagus from smooth muscle atrophy and fibrosis
options_after: It causes hyperperistalsis of the distal two-thirds of the oesophagus
It involves the oesophagus in fewer than 10% of patients
Oesophageal dilatation appears primarily after typical skin changes are advanced
It causes a fixed bird-beak stricture at the gastro-oesophageal junction from failure of sphincter relaxation
It produces lack of peristalsis of the distal two-thirds of the oesophagus from smooth muscle atrophy and fibrosis
updates.explanation: Scleroderma involves the oesophagus in approximately 80% of patients. It causes lack of peristalsis of the distal two-thirds of the oesophagus from smooth muscle atrophy and fibrosis, leading to marked oesophageal dilatation. Secondary candidiasis or aspiration pneumonia can result from prolonged stasis. Oesophageal dilatation may be apparent before typical skin changes of scleroderma develop.

updates.question_text: Regarding diffuse oesophageal spasm and feline oesophagus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diffuse oesophageal spasm produces a smooth posterior indentation from an aberrant right subclavian artery
Diffuse oesophageal spasm is a clinical syndrome of chest pain or dysphagia caused by repetitive non-propulsive contractions
Feline oesophagus has thick concentric strictures that are identical to eosinophilic oesophagitis
Feline oesophagus is thought to be a normal variant with multiple thin transverse oesophageal folds
Feline oesophagus is always diagnostic of severe infectious oesophagitis
options_after: Diffuse oesophageal spasm produces a smooth posterior indentation from an aberrant right subclavian artery
Diffuse oesophageal spasm is a clinical syndrome of chest pain or dysphagia caused by repetitive non-propulsive contractions
Feline oesophagus has thick concentric strictures that are closely comparable to eosinophilic oesophagitis
Feline oesophagus is thought to be a normal variant with multiple thin transverse oesophageal folds
Feline oesophagus is characteristically diagnostic of severe infectious oesophagitis
updates.explanation: Diffuse oesophageal spasm is a clinical syndrome of chest pain or dysphagia caused by repetitive non-propulsive contractions, producing the corkscrew oesophagus appearance on barium swallow. Feline oesophagus is considered a normal variant with multiple thin transverse folds. It has a controversial association with oesophagitis, but its folds are thinner than the circumferential folds of eosinophilic oesophagitis. A smooth posterior indentation belongs to aberrant right subclavian artery.

updates.question_text: Regarding aberrant right subclavian artery on upper GI imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is almost always symptomatic
It usually travels anterior to the trachea
It is seen in approximately 1% of patients with a normal left arch
It travels posterior to the oesophagus and may rarely produce dysphagia
The resulting posterior oesophageal indentation on upper GI study is always smooth
options_after: It is typically symptomatic
It usually travels anterior to the trachea
It is seen in approximately 1% of patients with a normal left arch
It travels posterior to the oesophagus and may rarely produce dysphagia
The resulting posterior oesophageal indentation on upper GI study is always smooth
updates.explanation: Aberrant right subclavian artery with a normal left arch is seen in approximately 1% of patients and is almost always asymptomatic. It travels posterior to the oesophagus and may rarely produce dysphagia. On upper GI study, the posterior oesophageal indentation is always smooth. Anterior tracheal course and frequent symptoms are not the source-described pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding hiatal hernia classification and management, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Type I sliding hiatal hernia is the most common type
Type II hernia has the gastro-oesophageal junction above the diaphragm
Type IV hernia includes displacement of the stomach and other organs above the diaphragm
The SAGES 2013 guidelines recommend surgery for all asymptomatic type I hernias without reflux disease
Symptomatic paraoesophageal hiatal hernias should be repaired, especially with acute obstructive symptoms or volvulus
options_after: Type I sliding hiatal hernia is the most common type
Type II hernia has the gastro-oesophageal junction above the diaphragm
Type IV hernia includes displacement of the stomach and other organs above the diaphragm
The SAGES 2013 guidelines recommend surgery for most asymptomatic type I hernias without reflux disease
Symptomatic paraoesophageal hiatal hernias should be repaired, especially with acute obstructive symptoms or volvulus
updates.explanation: Type I sliding hiatal hernia is the most common type and involves the gastro-oesophageal junction sliding into the posterior mediastinum. Type IV hernia includes stomach plus other organs such as spleen, pancreas, small bowel or colon above the diaphragm. SAGES 2013 guidance does not recommend surgery for type I hernia in the absence of reflux disease, but symptomatic paraoesophageal hernias should be repaired, particularly when obstruction or volvulus is present. Type II hernia has a normally positioned gastro-oesophageal junction below the diaphragm with fundal herniation.

updates.question_text: Regarding the illustrated paraoesophageal hernia and hiatal hernia types, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Type I hernia is defined by isolated herniation of the fundus with the gastro-oesophageal junction below the diaphragm
Type II hernia is paraoesophageal herniation of the gastric fundus with a normally positioned gastro-oesophageal junction
Type III hernia is the least common type
Type III hernia has both the gastro-oesophageal junction and the fundus/body of the stomach protruding into the lower mediastinum
Type IV hernia cannot contain colon or pancreas
options_after: Type I hernia is defined by isolated herniation of the fundus with the gastro-oesophageal junction below the diaphragm
Type II hernia is paraoesophageal herniation of the gastric fundus with a normally positioned gastro-oesophageal junction
Type III hernia is the least common type
Type III hernia has both the gastro-oesophageal junction and the fundus/body of the stomach protruding into the lower mediastinum
Type IV hernia will not contain colon or pancreas
updates.explanation: Type II paraoesophageal hernia is herniation of the gastric fundus while the gastro-oesophageal junction remains normally positioned below the diaphragm, and it is the least common type. Type III hernia is the second most common type and has both the gastro-oesophageal junction and fundus/body protruding into the lower mediastinum. Type IV hernia includes herniation of other organs, which may include spleen, pancreas, small bowel or colon. Type I is sliding hernia with the gastro-oesophageal junction above the diaphragm.

updates.question_text: Regarding gastric polyps, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hyperplastic polyps develop in response to chronic inflammation and are often associated with H. pylori infection
Fundic gland polyps have no association with proton pump inhibitor use
Adenomatous polyps are neoplastic polyps with malignant potential
Hamartomatous polyps are associated with Peutz-Jeghers, juvenile polyposis and Cronkhite-Canada syndromes
Adenomatous polyps are always diffuse and never solitary
options_after: Hyperplastic polyps develop in response to chronic inflammation and are often associated with H. pylori infection
Fundic gland polyps lack association with proton pump inhibitor use
Adenomatous polyps are neoplastic polyps with malignant potential
Hamartomatous polyps are associated with Peutz-Jeghers, juvenile polyposis and Cronkhite-Canada syndromes
Adenomatous gastric polyps characteristically present diffusely rather than as solitary lesions.
updates.explanation: Hyperplastic, or inflammatory, gastric polyps are cystic dilatations of gastric glands that develop in response to chronic inflammation and are often associated with H. pylori. Fundic gland polyps are associated with proton pump inhibitor use and can also occur in familial adenomatous polyposis. Adenomatous polyps are neoplastic and have malignant potential, with risk increased by size, villous contour and cellular dysplasia; they may be solitary or multiple. Hamartomatous polyps are benign and associated with syndromes including Peutz-Jeghers, juvenile polyposis and Cronkhite-Canada.

updates.question_text: Regarding benign gastric masses and ectopic pancreatic rest, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ectopic pancreatic rest is always intramucosal and cannot develop pancreatic disease
An ectopic pancreatic rest is heterotopic pancreatic tissue in the gastric submucosa
The umbilication in an ectopic pancreatic rest represents transmural malignant invasion
Ectopic pancreatic tissue is susceptible to pancreatic diseases, including pancreatitis and carcinoma
A classic imaging appearance is an umbilicated submucosal nodule
options_after: Ectopic pancreatic rest is characteristically intramucosal and will not develop pancreatic disease
An ectopic pancreatic rest is heterotopic pancreatic tissue in the gastric submucosa
The umbilication in an ectopic pancreatic rest represents transmural malignant invasion
Ectopic pancreatic tissue is susceptible to pancreatic diseases, including pancreatitis and carcinoma
A classic imaging appearance is an umbilicated submucosal nodule
updates.explanation: An ectopic pancreatic rest is heterotopic pancreatic tissue in the gastric submucosa. The ectopic tissue can develop pancreatic diseases including pancreatitis and carcinoma. The classic imaging appearance is an umbilicated submucosal nodule, with the umbilication representing a focus of normal epithelium. If the umbilication is not seen, imaging may simply show a nonspecific submucosal gastric mass.

updates.question_text: Regarding gastric adenocarcinoma metastatic spread to the ovary, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is termed a Hampton line
It is termed Menetrier disease
It is usually a benign fundic gland polyp
It is classically described as a Krukenberg tumour
It is diagnostic only when unilateral and calcified
options_after: It is termed a Hampton line
It is termed Menetrier disease
It is usually a benign fundic gland polyp
It is classically described as a Krukenberg tumour
It is diagnostic primarily when unilateral and calcified
updates.explanation: A Krukenberg tumour is classically metastatic spread of gastric carcinoma to the ovary, although the term can also be used for any mucinous metastasis to the ovary. The source example shows bilateral adnexal masses from gastric cancer with ascites. The Hampton line is a benign gastric ulcer sign, while Menetrier disease is hypertrophic gastropathy. Fundic gland polyps are unrelated to this metastatic pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding malignant gastric masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gastric adenocarcinoma presents only as diffuse wall thickening
Gastric lymphoma never mimics gastric carcinoma or GIST
Gastric cancer lymphatic spread occurs along the lesser curvature to the gastrohepatic ligament and along the greater curvature
Adenopathy at or below the renal hila is common in gastric carcinoma but absent in lymphoma
Breast, lung and melanoma are the most common primary malignancies to metastasise to the stomach
options_after: Gastric adenocarcinoma presents primarily as diffuse wall thickening
Gastric lymphoma will not mimic gastric carcinoma or GIST
Gastric cancer lymphatic spread occurs along the lesser curvature to the gastrohepatic ligament and along the greater curvature
Adenopathy at or below the renal hila is common in gastric carcinoma but absent in lymphoma
Breast, lung and melanoma are the most common primary malignancies to metastasise to the stomach
updates.explanation: Gastric adenocarcinoma may present as a focal mass, malignant ulcer or diffuse wall thickening known as linitis plastica. Its lymphatic spread occurs along the lesser curvature to the gastrohepatic ligament and along the greater curvature. Gastric lymphoma can mimic gastric carcinoma or a large malignant GIST, and adenopathy at or below the renal hila favours lymphoma because it is uncommon in gastric cancer but present in one-third of lymphoma patients. Metastatic disease to the stomach is rare, with breast, lung and melanoma the common primaries.

updates.question_text: Regarding small-bowel obstruction and afferent loop syndrome after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Early small-bowel obstruction is most often due to oedema or haematoma at the gastrojejunostomy or jejunojejunostomy
Late small-bowel obstruction may be due to internal hernia or adhesions
Fluoroscopy reliably demonstrates afferent loop syndrome because the afferent limb always opacifies
Afferent loop syndrome only occurs more than seven days after surgery
CT in afferent loop syndrome shows a dilated fluid-filled afferent or pancreaticobiliary limb
options_after: Early small-bowel obstruction is most often due to oedema or haematoma at the gastrojejunostomy or jejunojejunostomy
Late small-bowel obstruction may be due to internal hernia or adhesions
Fluoroscopy reliably demonstrates afferent loop syndrome because the afferent limb characteristically opacifies
Afferent loop syndrome primarily occurs more than seven days after surgery
CT in afferent loop syndrome shows a dilated fluid-filled afferent or pancreaticobiliary limb
updates.explanation: Early postoperative small-bowel obstruction is usually due to oedema or haematoma at the gastrojejunostomy or jejunojejunostomy, and with retrocolic Roux limb may also occur at the transverse mesocolon defect. Late obstruction may be due to internal hernia, especially after laparoscopic surgery, or adhesions, more common after open surgery. Afferent loop syndrome can occur in acute or chronic phases. Fluoroscopy usually does not show it because the afferent limb does not opacify unless there is reflux from the jejunojejunostomy; CT shows a dilated fluid-filled pancreaticobiliary limb.

updates.question_text: Regarding internal hernia after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is less common after laparoscopic than open Roux-en-Y
It usually presents more than ten years after bypass
It is never seen without complete small-bowel obstruction
It most often occurs in the excluded stomach
It is the most common cause of small-bowel obstruction after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y
options_after: It is less common after laparoscopic than open Roux-en-Y
It usually presents more than ten years after bypass
It is not seen without complete small-bowel obstruction
It most often occurs in the excluded stomach
It is the most common cause of small-bowel obstruction after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y
updates.explanation: Internal hernias are more common after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y, occurring in 2.5% of laparoscopic procedures versus 0.5% of open procedures. They usually present within two years of bypass and are the most common cause of small-bowel obstruction after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y. They may also present as mesenteric and bowel oedema without obstruction. Diagnosis can be difficult clinically and on imaging.

updates.question_text: Regarding stomal stenosis and marginal ulcers after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gastrojejunostomy stenosis always requires surgery
Narrowing of the gastrojejunostomy stoma may occur in up to 10% of patients
Marginal ulcers occur at the jejunal mucosa adjacent to the gastrojejunal anastomosis
Marginal ulcer treatment is always operative
Narrowing of the distal jejunojejunostomy is more common than gastrojejunostomy stenosis
options_after: Gastrojejunostomy stenosis characteristically requires surgery
Narrowing of the gastrojejunostomy stoma may occur in up to 10% of patients
Marginal ulcers occur at the jejunal mucosa adjacent to the gastrojejunal anastomosis
Marginal ulcer treatment is characteristically operative
Narrowing of the distal jejunojejunostomy is more common than gastrojejunostomy stenosis
updates.explanation: Narrowing of the gastrojejunostomy stoma can occur in up to 10% of patients and leads to dilatation of the gastric pouch and distal oesophagus. It is usually treated with endoscopic dilatation. Distal jejunojejunostomy narrowing is less common and usually requires surgery. Marginal ulcers occur in the jejunal mucosa adjacent to the gastrojejunal anastomosis due to exposure to gastric secretions and are usually treated conservatively.

updates.question_text: Regarding small bowel anatomy and radiographic obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Valvulae conniventes are circumferential small bowel folds
The ileum has larger and more closely spaced folds than the jejunum
Small bowel distension greater than 3 cm is a radiographic finding of small bowel obstruction
The duodenum receives its arterial supply from the superior mesenteric artery only
Lack of gas in the colon is especially suggestive of obstruction
options_after: Valvulae conniventes are circumferential small bowel folds
The ileum has larger and more closely spaced folds than the jejunum
Small bowel distension greater than 3 cm is a radiographic finding of small bowel obstruction
The duodenum receives its arterial supply from the superior mesenteric artery in typical cases
Lack of gas in the colon is especially suggestive of obstruction
updates.explanation: Valvulae conniventes, or plicae circulares, are circumferential folds of the small bowel, unlike colonic haustra. The jejunum has larger, more closely spaced folds and larger villi than the ileum. Radiographic findings of small bowel obstruction include small bowel distension greater than 3 cm, multiple air-fluid levels at different heights and lack of colonic gas. The jejunum and ileum are supplied by the SMA, whereas the duodenum receives branches from the celiac axis.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT evaluation of small bowel obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Small bowel distension at least 3 cm with a focal transition point to collapsed bowel is highly specific for obstruction
CT helps assess the cause and complications of small bowel obstruction
Closed-loop obstruction is low-risk and can usually be ignored if there is no colonic gas
The transition point should be sought to determine the cause of obstruction
Signs of ischaemia or impending ischaemia include mesenteric oedema, ascites or interloop fluid, wall thickening, absent enhancement and pneumatosis
options_after: Small bowel distension at least 3 cm with a focal transition point to collapsed bowel is highly specific for obstruction
CT helps assess the cause and complications of small bowel obstruction
Closed-loop obstruction is low-risk and can usually be ignored if there is an absence of colonic gas
The transition point should be sought to determine the cause of obstruction
Signs of ischaemia or impending ischaemia include mesenteric oedema, ascites or interloop fluid, wall thickening, absent enhancement and pneumatosis
updates.explanation: CT is highly sensitive and specific for small bowel obstruction, and distension at least 3 cm with a focal transition point to collapsed bowel is highly specific. A systematic read identifies the transition point, determines whether the obstruction is simple or closed-loop, and then assesses for ischaemia or impending ischaemia. Closed-loop obstruction is a never-miss diagnosis because of high ischaemia risk. The small bowel faeces sign is another useful CT feature near the transition point.

updates.question_text: Regarding the small bowel faeces sign, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is gas in the bowel wall caused by necrosis
It is a sign of colonic obstruction only
It describes particulate faeculent material mixed with gas bubbles in small bowel and is often just proximal to the transition point
It excludes partial or subacute obstruction
It requires positive oral contrast for diagnosis
options_after: It is gas in the bowel wall caused by necrosis
It is a sign of colonic obstruction in typical cases
It describes particulate faeculent material mixed with gas bubbles in small bowel and is often just proximal to the transition point
It excludes partial or subacute obstruction
It requires positive oral contrast for diagnosis
updates.explanation: The small bowel faeces sign describes particulate faeculent material mixed with gas bubbles in small bowel, resembling stool on CT. It is often seen just proximal to the transition point and can help localise the site of transition, especially in subacute or partial obstruction. The source attributes it to bacterial overgrowth and undigested food. Gas in the bowel wall due to necrosis is pneumatosis intestinalis, not the faeces sign.

updates.question_text: Regarding closed-loop obstruction and adhesive obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Closed-loop obstruction affects only the efferent segment of a bowel loop
Closed-loop obstruction is a surgical emergency because it may lead to bowel ischaemia
CT findings include a whirl sign, U- or C-shaped distended loops, radially oriented vessels and mesenteric oedema
Adhesions are directly visualised on CT as enhancing linear bands in most patients
Adhesions are the most common cause of small bowel obstruction and usually follow prior abdominal surgery
options_after: Closed-loop obstruction affects primarily the efferent segment of a bowel loop
Closed-loop obstruction is a surgical emergency because it may lead to bowel ischaemia
CT findings include a whirl sign, U- or C-shaped distended loops, radially oriented vessels and mesenteric oedema
Adhesions are directly visualised on CT as enhancing linear bands in most patients
Adhesions are the most common cause of small bowel obstruction and usually follow prior abdominal surgery
updates.explanation: Closed-loop obstruction obstructs both the afferent and efferent segments of a single loop and is a surgical emergency because of ischaemia risk. CT features include mesenteric vessel twisting or whirl sign, U- or C-shaped distended bowel loops, radially oriented vessels and mesenteric oedema. Adhesions are the most common cause of small bowel obstruction and are usually related to prior surgery or intraperitoneal inflammation. They are an imaging diagnosis of exclusion: a transition point is seen but no mass, hernia or other cause is identified.

updates.question_text: Regarding named abdominal wall and pelvic hernias, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Amyand hernia is an inguinal hernia containing the appendix
Littre hernia is a femoral hernia containing only urinary bladder
De Garengeot hernia is a femoral hernia containing the appendix
Obturator hernia is suggested by bowel between the pectineus and obturator muscles
Spigelian hernia occurs through the femoral canal posterior and inferior to the inguinal ligament
options_after: Amyand hernia is an inguinal hernia containing the appendix
Littre hernia is a femoral hernia containing primarily urinary bladder
De Garengeot hernia is a femoral hernia containing the appendix
Obturator hernia is suggested by bowel between the pectineus and obturator muscles
Spigelian hernia occurs through the femoral canal posterior and inferior to the inguinal ligament
updates.explanation: An Amyand hernia is an inguinal hernia containing the appendix, and a Littre hernia contains a Meckel diverticulum. A femoral hernia containing the appendix is called a De Garengeot hernia. Obturator hernia classically contains bowel between the pectineus and obturator muscles and is usually seen in elderly women. Spigelian hernia is a lateral ventral hernia at the semilunar line, not a femoral canal hernia.

updates.question_text: Regarding paraduodenal and foramen of Winslow hernias, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Left paraduodenal hernia passes through the fossa of Landzert and can produce small bowel loops between the pancreas and stomach
Right paraduodenal hernia passes through a defect located anterior to the abdominal wall musculature
Paraduodenal hernias are acquired defects caused only by prior Roux-en-Y surgery
Foramen of Winslow hernia is diagnosed by bowel loops lateral to the pectineus muscle
Foramen of Winslow hernia may show bowel loops in the lesser sac and mesentery or bowel between the IVC and main portal vein
options_after: Left paraduodenal hernia passes through the fossa of Landzert and can produce small bowel loops between the pancreas and stomach
Right paraduodenal hernia passes through a defect located anterior to the abdominal wall musculature
Paraduodenal hernias are acquired defects caused primarily by prior Roux-en-Y surgery
Foramen of Winslow hernia is diagnosed by bowel loops lateral to the pectineus muscle
Foramen of Winslow hernia may show bowel loops in the lesser sac and mesentery or bowel between the IVC and main portal vein
updates.explanation: Left paraduodenal hernia involves the fossa of Landzert, to the left of the fourth duodenum and behind the IMV, and the key imaging finding is clustered small bowel loops between the pancreas and stomach. Right paraduodenal hernia involves the fossa of Waldeyer behind the SMA and SMV. Paraduodenal hernias are congenital anomalies from failure of mesenteric fusion. Foramen of Winslow hernia shows dilated bowel loops in the lesser sac with bowel or mesentery between the IVC and main portal vein.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallstone ileus, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is a subtype of colonic obstruction due to faecal impaction
It is always caused by a calcified gallstone visible on radiography
It requires a femoral hernia containing the appendix
Rigler triad includes pneumobilia, small bowel obstruction and ectopic gallstone in the small bowel
Bouveret syndrome is distal ileal obstruction by a Meckel diverticulum
options_after: It is a subtype of colonic obstruction due to faecal impaction
It is characteristically caused by a calcified gallstone visible on radiography
It requires a femoral hernia containing the appendix
Rigler triad includes pneumobilia, small bowel obstruction and ectopic gallstone in the small bowel
Bouveret syndrome is distal ileal obstruction by a Meckel diverticulum
updates.explanation: Gallstone ileus is a misnomer for small bowel obstruction caused by a gallstone that has eroded from the gallbladder into the duodenum. The classic Rigler triad is pneumobilia from cholecystoduodenal fistula, small bowel obstruction and an ectopic gallstone within the small bowel. Bouveret syndrome is the proximal form with gallstone impaction in the pylorus or proximal duodenum. The source example includes a non-calcified gallstone, so visibility on radiography is not required.

updates.question_text: Regarding Crohn disease imaging and phenotypes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Crohn disease affects only the colon and rectum in a continuous pattern
Perianal disease is classified as penetrating disease in this source
Active inflammation includes mural hyperenhancement, intramural oedema and mural ulcerations
CT and MR enterography have lower ability than fluoroscopy to evaluate extraintestinal complications and vasculature
Stricturing disease is luminal narrowing with upstream dilatation
options_after: Crohn disease affects primarily the colon and rectum in a continuous pattern
Perianal disease is classified as penetrating disease in this source
Active inflammation includes mural hyperenhancement, intramural oedema and mural ulcerations
CT and MR enterography have lower ability than fluoroscopy to evaluate extraintestinal complications and vasculature
Stricturing disease is luminal narrowing with upstream dilatation
updates.explanation: Crohn disease can affect any part of the GI tract from mouth to anus, most commonly the terminal ileum, and is discontinuous with skip lesions. Active inflammation includes mural hyperenhancement, intramural oedema and mural ulcerations. Stricturing disease is luminal narrowing with upstream dilatation. Penetrating disease includes sinus tracts, fistulas, inflammatory mass and abscess, but perianal disease is specifically not considered penetrating disease here. CT and MR enterography evaluate the whole bowel wall, extraintestinal complications and vasculature better than fluoroscopy or endoscopy.

updates.question_text: Regarding complications and mimics of coeliac disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pneumatosis in coeliac disease is always considered bowel ischaemia
Coeliac disease is associated with splenic atrophy and increased risk of venous thromboembolism
Cavitating mesenteric lymph node syndrome is highly specific for coeliac disease when seen with villous atrophy and splenic atrophy
Yersinia and tuberculosis usually affect the oesophagus and spare the terminal ileum
Whipple disease characteristically causes high-attenuation calcified lymph nodes only
options_after: Pneumatosis in coeliac disease is characteristically considered bowel ischaemia
Coeliac disease is associated with splenic atrophy and increased risk of venous thromboembolism
Cavitating mesenteric lymph node syndrome is highly specific for coeliac disease when seen with villous atrophy and splenic atrophy
Yersinia and tuberculosis usually affect the oesophagus and spare the terminal ileum
Whipple disease characteristically causes high-attenuation calcified lymph nodes in typical cases
updates.explanation: Coeliac disease complications include intussusception without a lead mass, pneumatosis intestinalis from gas dissection through inflamed bowel wall, splenic atrophy and increased venous thromboembolism risk. Pneumatosis in coeliac disease is not thought to indicate bowel ischaemia. Cavitating mesenteric lymph node syndrome is rare but highly specific for coeliac disease when combined with villous atrophy and splenic atrophy. Yersinia and tuberculosis have a propensity for the terminal ileum and can mimic Crohn disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding infectious and radiation enteritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Salmonella is the most common cause of food-borne gastroenteritis
Whipple disease causes thickening and nodularity of duodenal and proximal small bowel folds
Whipple disease typically has hypersecretion like coeliac disease
Radiation enteritis should be suspected when bowel involvement matches the radiation field rather than a vascular territory
Radiation enteritis never causes small bowel obstruction
options_after: Salmonella is the most common cause of food-borne gastroenteritis
Whipple disease causes thickening and nodularity of duodenal and proximal small bowel folds
Whipple disease typically has hypersecretion like coeliac disease
Radiation enteritis should be suspected when bowel involvement matches the radiation field rather than a vascular territory
Radiation enteritis will not cause small bowel obstruction
updates.explanation: Salmonella is listed as the most common cause of food-borne gastroenteritis and causes segmental distal small bowel thickening on CT with nodular fold thickening on fluoroscopy. Whipple disease causes malabsorption, abdominal pain and low-attenuation adenopathy, with thickened nodular duodenal and proximal small bowel folds; unlike coeliac disease, there is typically no hypersecretion. Radiation enteritis is suggested by a history of radiotherapy and regional bowel involvement matching the radiation field rather than a vascular territory. It can cause small bowel obstruction in later stages.

updates.question_text: Regarding appendicitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Appendicoliths are diagnostic of appendicitis even without inflammation
A tubular blind-ending non-compressible right lower quadrant structure greater than 6 mm is the key ultrasound finding
Indirect findings include periappendiceal fat stranding, caecal wall thickening, hydroureter and small bowel ileus
For paediatric suspected appendicitis, CT is always first line
A normal appendix filled with air or enteric contrast can measure greater than 6 mm, so a numeric cutoff should be used cautiously
options_after: Appendicoliths are diagnostic of appendicitis even without inflammation
A tubular blind-ending non-compressible right lower quadrant structure greater than 6 mm is the key ultrasound finding
Indirect findings include periappendiceal fat stranding, caecal wall thickening, hydroureter and small bowel ileus
For paediatric suspected appendicitis, CT is characteristically first line
A normal appendix filled with air or enteric contrast can measure greater than 6 mm, so a numeric cutoff should be used cautiously
updates.explanation: The key ultrasound finding in appendicitis is a blind-ending, non-compressible tubular right lower quadrant structure greater than 6 mm, assessed with graded compression. Indirect findings include periappendiceal fat stranding, caecal wall thickening, hydroureter and small bowel ileus. Appendicoliths may obstruct the lumen but are also commonly seen without appendicitis. Ultrasound is first line in paediatric patients, and the 6 mm cutoff needs caution because a normal appendix distended by air or enteric contrast can exceed it.

updates.question_text: Regarding ischaemic colitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Low-flow states can cause colonic ischaemia
The splenic flexure is particularly susceptible in low-flow states
The rectum is commonly affected because it has only one terminal arterial supply
CT suggests ischaemic colitis when there is segmental thickening in a vascular distribution with rectal sparing
If arterial thromboembolism is suspected, aortic atherosclerosis and left atrial thrombus should be assessed
options_after: Low-flow states can cause colonic ischaemia
The splenic flexure is particularly susceptible in low-flow states
The rectum is commonly affected because it has a single terminal arterial supply
CT suggests ischaemic colitis when there is segmental thickening in a vascular distribution with rectal sparing
If arterial thromboembolism is suspected, aortic atherosclerosis and left atrial thrombus should be assessed
updates.explanation: Colonic ischaemia can result from acute arterial thrombus, chronic stenosis, low-flow states and venous thrombosis. The splenic flexure is vulnerable because it is the SMA-IMA watershed. The rectum is almost never affected because it has dual supply from the superior rectal artery plus middle and inferior rectal branches from the internal iliac system. CT features include segmental vascular-distribution thickening with rectal sparing. Suspected arterial thromboembolism should prompt evaluation for aortic atherosclerosis and left atrial thrombus in atrial fibrillation.

updates.question_text: Regarding infectious colitis distribution, which statement is correct?
options_before: Yersinia, Salmonella and colonic tuberculosis usually cause isolated rectal disease
E. coli, CMV and C. difficile most commonly cause right-colon-only disease
Yersinia, Salmonella and colonic tuberculosis tend to affect the right colon
Tuberculosis never involves the ileocaecal valve
All infectious colitides spare the colon wall and affect only the mesentery
options_after: Yersinia, Salmonella and colonic tuberculosis usually cause isolated rectal disease
E. coli, CMV and C. difficile most commonly cause right-colon-predominant disease
Yersinia, Salmonella and colonic tuberculosis tend to affect the right colon
Tuberculosis will not involve the ileocaecal valve
Most infectious colitides spare the colon wall and affect primarily the mesentery
updates.explanation: The source states that Yersinia, Salmonella and colonic tuberculosis tend to affect the right colon. Tuberculosis can involve the ileocaecal valve and cause a desmoplastic reaction that mimics Crohn disease. E. coli, CMV and C. difficile more commonly cause pancolitis. Infectious colitis still shares the general colitis pattern of wall thickening, often with pericolonic stranding and ascites.

updates.question_text: Regarding pseudomembranous colitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is caused by overgrowth of Clostridium difficile, most commonly after alteration of colonic flora from antibiotics
It requires a history of antibiotic use and cannot occur without it
Marked colonic wall thickening with pancolitis is a key imaging finding
The accordion sign is specific to C. difficile colitis
Thumbprinting is a fluoroscopic finding of thickened haustra due to oedema
options_after: It is caused by overgrowth of Clostridium difficile, most commonly after alteration of colonic flora from antibiotics
It requires a history of antibiotic use and will not occur without it
Marked colonic wall thickening with pancolitis is a key imaging finding
The accordion sign is specific to C. difficile colitis
Thumbprinting is a fluoroscopic finding of thickened haustra due to oedema
updates.explanation: Pseudomembranous colitis is caused by C. difficile overgrowth, most commonly after antibiotic-related alteration of bowel flora, but it can occur without antibiotic history, especially in hospital or nursing-home patients and severely immunocompromised transplant patients. Imaging typically shows marked thickening of the colonic wall with pancolitis. The accordion sign reflects severe colonic oedema with undulating enhancing mucosa but is not specific to C. difficile. Thumbprinting is a fluoroscopic manifestation of thickened oedematous haustra.

updates.question_text: Regarding ulcerative colitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It begins distally in the rectum and spreads proximally in a continuous manner
Skip lesions are the defining pattern, unlike Crohn disease
It commonly extends proximally beyond the caecum throughout the small bowel
Patients have increased risk of primary sclerosing cholangitis, cholangiocarcinoma and colon cancer
Backwash ileitis is impossible in ulcerative colitis and therefore never mimics Crohn disease
options_after: It begins distally in the rectum and spreads proximally in a continuous manner
Skip lesions are the defining pattern, unlike Crohn disease
It commonly extends proximally beyond the caecum throughout the small bowel
Patients have increased risk of primary sclerosing cholangitis, cholangiocarcinoma and colon cancer
Backwash ileitis is not considered a realistic possibility in ulcerative colitis and therefore will not mimic Crohn disease
updates.explanation: Ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum and spreads proximally in a continuous fashion, unlike Crohn disease with skip areas. It does not extend beyond the caecum, although backwash ileitis from reflux of inflammatory debris into the ileum can occur and mimic Crohn disease. Patients with UC have increased risks of primary sclerosing cholangitis, cholangiocarcinoma and colon cancer. A treated rectum may appear normal after corticosteroid enemas despite more proximal disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding typhlitis, immunotherapy-related colitis and stercoral colitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Typhlitis is a left-sided colitis seen in immunocompetent patients only
Typhlitis is necrotising inflammatory colitis of the right colon and/or terminal ileum in neutropenic patients
Drug-related colitis may show subtle mild diffuse wall thickening, vasa recta engorgement and fluid-filled colonic distension
Stercoral colitis is caused by pressure from impacted faecal material in the colon or rectum
Stercoral colitis can lead to ischaemia, pressure ulceration and perforation
options_after: Typhlitis is a left-sided colitis seen in immunocompetent patients in typical cases
Typhlitis is necrotising inflammatory colitis of the right colon and/or terminal ileum in neutropenic patients
Drug-related colitis may show subtle mild diffuse wall thickening, vasa recta engorgement and fluid-filled colonic distension
Stercoral colitis is caused by pressure from impacted faecal material in the colon or rectum
Stercoral colitis can lead to ischaemia, pressure ulceration and perforation
updates.explanation: Typhlitis is necrotising inflammatory colitis of the right colon and/or terminal ileum in neutropenic patients, with possible caecal thickening, fat stranding, ileus, obstruction or pneumatosis. Immunotherapy-related colitis can be subtle, with mild diffuse bowel wall thickening, vasa recta engorgement and fluid-filled distension; ipilimumab and pembrolizumab are common culprit agents. Stercoral colitis is pressure-related focal inflammation from impacted faecal material and can progress to ischaemia, stercoral ulcer and perforation.

updates.question_text: Regarding reporting and mimics of diverticulitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Extraluminal gas, fistula, abscess and recurrent diverticulitis history are irrelevant to treatment algorithms
Abscesses from diverticulitis can usually be drained percutaneously with CT guidance
Septic thrombophlebitis may be associated with hepatic abscesses in complicated diverticulitis
Acute diverticulitis can never mimic colon cancer because wall thickening is absent
Follow-up CT or colonoscopy may be recommended after resolution when distinction from colon cancer is uncertain
options_after: Extraluminal gas, fistula, abscess and recurrent diverticulitis history are irrelevant to treatment algorithms
Abscesses from diverticulitis can usually be drained percutaneously with CT guidance
Septic thrombophlebitis may be associated with hepatic abscesses in complicated diverticulitis
Acute diverticulitis will not mimic colon cancer because wall thickening is absent
Follow-up CT or colonoscopy may be recommended after resolution when distinction from colon cancer is uncertain
updates.explanation: Diverticular abscesses can usually be drained percutaneously under CT guidance. Complicated diverticulitis can include mesenteric venous thrombosis or septic thrombophlebitis, with hepatic abscesses as shown in the source example. The report should include extraluminal gas, fistula, abscess and history of recurrent diverticulitis because they may affect treatment. Because extensive colonic wall thickening can make diverticulitis difficult to distinguish from colon cancer, follow-up CT or colonoscopy may be recommended after the acute episode resolves.

updates.question_text: Regarding colorectal carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most colorectal carcinomas arise in the stomach and duodenum
CT colonography is increasingly used as a non-invasive alternative to colonoscopy for screening
CT is most often used for staging and can show nodal involvement or metastases
MRI has no role in rectal cancer staging
Most colorectal carcinomas appear as purely fat-density lesions without luminal narrowing or ulceration
options_after: Most colorectal carcinomas arise in the stomach and duodenum
CT colonography is increasingly used as a non-invasive alternative to colonoscopy for screening
CT is most often used for staging and can show nodal involvement or metastases
MRI has negligible role in rectal cancer staging
Most colorectal carcinomas appear as purely fat-density lesions without luminal narrowing or ulceration
updates.explanation: Colorectal carcinoma is the most common GI tract malignancy and usually arises in the rectosigmoid region, though it can occur from caecum to rectum. CT colonography is increasingly used as a non-invasive screening alternative to colonoscopy. CT is most often used for staging and shows nodal or metastatic disease, while MRI is used for locoregional T and N staging of rectal cancer. Most carcinomas are soft-tissue density masses that can narrow the lumen and ulcerate, not fat-density lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding colorectal carcinoma risk factors and associated syndromes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Inflammatory bowel disease is a risk factor
Low fibre and high fat diet is a risk factor
Obesity, prior radiation and family history are listed risk factors
Familial adenomatous polyposis and Lynch syndrome are associated syndromes
Primary sclerosing cholangitis is listed as the only colorectal cancer syndrome
options_after: Inflammatory bowel disease is a risk factor
Low fibre and high fat diet is a risk factor
Obesity, prior radiation and family history are listed risk factors
Familial adenomatous polyposis and Lynch syndrome are associated syndromes
Primary sclerosing cholangitis is listed as the principal colorectal cancer syndrome
updates.explanation: The source lists inflammatory bowel disease, low fibre/high fat diet, obesity, prior radiation and family history among colorectal carcinoma risk factors. Associated syndromes include FAP, Gardner and Turcot variants, Peutz-Jeghers and HNPCC/Lynch syndrome. Primary sclerosing cholangitis is associated with ulcerative colitis and cholangiocarcinoma in this section, but it is not presented as the only colorectal cancer syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding hamartomatous polyposis syndromes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Peutz-Jeghers has characteristic perioral mucocutaneous blue-brown pigmented spots on the lips and gums
Cowden syndrome is associated with increased risk of thyroid, skin, oral, breast and uterine malignancies
Cronkhite-Canada is autosomal dominant like all other listed polyposis syndromes
Cowden syndrome has multiple hamartomatous polyps, often in skin and external mucous membranes as well as the GI tract
Cronkhite-Canada includes abnormal skin pigmentation, alopecia and onychodystrophy
options_after: Peutz-Jeghers has characteristic perioral mucocutaneous blue-brown pigmented spots on the lips and gums
Cowden syndrome is associated with increased risk of thyroid, skin, oral, breast and uterine malignancies
Cronkhite-Canada is autosomal dominant like most other listed polyposis syndromes
Cowden syndrome has multiple hamartomatous polyps, often in skin and external mucous membranes as well as the GI tract
Cronkhite-Canada includes abnormal skin pigmentation, alopecia and onychodystrophy
updates.explanation: Peutz-Jeghers has characteristic perioral mucocutaneous blue-brown pigmentation on the lips and gums, and is associated with gynaecologic plus gastric, duodenal and colonic malignancies. Cowden syndrome is autosomal dominant with multiple hamartomatous polyps, often in skin and external mucous membranes as well as GI tract, and increased risk of thyroid, skin, oral, breast and uterine cancers. Cronkhite-Canada is the exception in this list: it is non-inherited rather than autosomal dominant, and includes hamartomatous polyps throughout the GI tract with pigmentation, alopecia and nail malformation.

updates.question_text: Regarding toxic megacolon, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is defined by small bowel obstruction from a gallstone
It is specific to infectious colitis and never occurs in ulcerative colitis
It is treated by colonoscopy to decompress the colon in suspected cases
It requires focal thickening limited to the appendiceal tip
It shows colonic dilatation greater than 6 cm with adynamic ileus and colonoscopy is contraindicated
options_after: It is defined by small bowel obstruction from a gallstone
It is specific to infectious colitis and will not occur in ulcerative colitis
It is treated by colonoscopy to decompress the colon in suspected cases
It requires focal thickening limited to the appendiceal tip
It shows colonic dilatation greater than 6 cm with adynamic ileus and colonoscopy is contraindicated
updates.explanation: Toxic megacolon is a severe complication of ulcerative colitis and less commonly Crohn disease, caused by inflammation extending through the muscular layer. Imaging shows colonic dilatation greater than 6 cm with adynamic ileus. Because perforation may occur, colonoscopy is contraindicated when toxic megacolon is suspected. Gallstone ileus and appendiceal tip inflammation belong to other parts of the GI chapter.

updates.question_text: Regarding the CT concept of a misty mesentery, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal mesenteries are usually visible on CT as discrete soft-tissue sheets separate from intra-abdominal fat
A misty mesentery is caused exclusively by neoplastic infiltration
Fluid, inflammatory cells, tumour or fibrosis can increase mesenteric attenuation and make the mesenteric vasculature indistinct
Mesenteric vessels should normally be invisible on CT
The misty mesentery appearance may be the first imaging clue to several pathologies
options_after: Normal mesenteries are usually visible on CT as discrete soft-tissue sheets separate from intra-abdominal fat
A misty mesentery is caused predominantly by neoplastic infiltration
Fluid, inflammatory cells, tumour or fibrosis can increase mesenteric attenuation and make the mesenteric vasculature indistinct
Mesenteric vessels should normally be invisible on CT
The misty mesentery appearance may be the first imaging clue to several pathologies
updates.explanation: The mesenteries are primarily fatty folds and usually blend in with intra-abdominal fat on CT, although their vessels are normally seen. A misty mesentery occurs when the mesentery is infiltrated by fluid, inflammatory cells, tumour or fibrosis, increasing attenuation and making the vessels less distinct. The finding is therefore not specific for neoplasm. It can be the first clue to oedema, inflammation, haemorrhage or tumour infiltration.

updates.question_text: Regarding mesenteric metastases and lymphoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Only carcinoid tumours metastasise to mesenteric lymph nodes in this source
Gastric, ovarian, breast, lung, pancreatic, biliary and colon cancers, as well as melanoma, may metastasise to mesenteric lymph nodes
Mesenteric lymphoma can produce the sandwich sign by engulfing mesenteric fat and vessels between bulky lymphomatous masses
The sandwich sign refers to replacement of omental fat by tumour and fibrosis
Mesenteric lymphoma is primarily identified by peripheral calcification and serotonin-related radiating strands
options_after: Mesenteric nodal metastases are principally associated with carcinoid and are unusual with epithelial primaries.
Gastric, ovarian, breast, lung, pancreatic, biliary and colon cancers, as well as melanoma, may metastasise to mesenteric lymph nodes
Mesenteric lymphoma can produce the sandwich sign by engulfing mesenteric fat and vessels between bulky lymphomatous masses
The sandwich sign refers to replacement of omental fat by tumour and fibrosis
Mesenteric lymphoma is primarily identified by peripheral calcification and serotonin-related radiating strands
updates.explanation: The source lists several malignancies that can metastasise to mesenteric lymph nodes, including gastric, ovarian, breast, lung, pancreatic, biliary and colon cancer, and melanoma. Mesenteric lymphoma may produce the sandwich sign, where mesenteric fat and vessels are engulfed on two sides by bulky lymphomatous masses. Replacement of omental fat by tumour and fibrosis is omental caking. Peripheral calcification with serotonin-related radiating strands describes mesenteric carcinoid involvement.

updates.question_text: Regarding indications for breast ultrasound in this source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is used to characterise palpable abnormalities
It is the first-line evaluation for a breast abnormality in women under age 30, or in pregnant or lactating women
It replaces diagnostic mammography for all women with dense breasts
It can guide interventional breast procedures
It is used in the evaluation of breast implants
options_after: It is used to characterise palpable abnormalities
It is the first-line evaluation for a breast abnormality in women under age 30, or in pregnant or lactating women
It replaces diagnostic mammography for most women with dense breasts
It can guide interventional breast procedures
It is used in the evaluation of breast implants
updates.explanation: The listed indications for breast ultrasound include characterisation of palpable abnormalities, further evaluation of mammographic findings, first-line assessment in young women under age 30 and in pregnant or lactating women, procedural guidance and implant evaluation. It is also used in some settings as supplemental screening in dense breasts or in high-risk women unable to undergo MRI surveillance. The source does not describe ultrasound as replacing diagnostic mammography for all dense-breasted women. Its supplemental screening use is explicitly described as controversial.

updates.question_text: Regarding management implications of ADH diagnosed at core needle biopsy, which statement is correct?
options_before: ADH is usually ignored because it does not increase future breast cancer risk
ADH is managed like a simple cyst if the mammogram shows calcifications
Surgical excision is recommended because the upstage rate is relatively high, up to 20%
ADH always represents invasive ductal carcinoma at the time of core biopsy
The source states that surveillance is mandatory for all ADH because the upstage rate is unknown
options_after: ADH is usually ignored because it does not increase future breast cancer risk
ADH is managed like a simple cyst if the mammogram shows calcifications
Surgical excision is recommended because the upstage rate is relatively high, up to 20%
ADH characteristically represents invasive ductal carcinoma at the time of core biopsy
The source states that surveillance is mandatory for most ADH because the upstage rate is unknown
updates.explanation: Management of high-risk lesions identified at core needle biopsy is related to their upstage rate. The source gives ADH as the example with a relatively high upstage rate, up to 20%, so surgical excision is recommended. FEA and ADH both increase future breast cancer risk, although they are non-obligatory precursor lesions. The source contrasts ADH with other high-risk entities whose upstage rates remain under investigation and may be managed differently by different institutions.

updates.question_text: A mammographic study shows an irregular spiculated mass with associated calcifications and a separate group of calcifications in the same breast. Which of the following statements are correct regarding this image?
options_before: The separate grouped calcifications are described as benign vascular calcifications
The image demonstrates typical Paget disease of the nipple
The irregular spiculated mass with associated calcifications is described as invasive ductal carcinoma
The grouped calcifications in the same breast at a separate location were biopsy-proven DCIS
The source states that no biopsy was required because both findings were stable benign changes
options_after: The separate grouped calcifications are described as benign vascular calcifications
The image demonstrates typical Paget disease of the nipple
The irregular spiculated mass with associated calcifications is described as invasive ductal carcinoma
The grouped calcifications in the same breast at a separate location were biopsy-proven DCIS
Stability of both findings permits a benign assessment without tissue diagnosis.
updates.explanation: The caption identifies the irregular mass with spiculated margins and associated calcifications as invasive ductal carcinoma. It also identifies grouped calcifications in the same breast at a separate location, with biopsy showing DCIS. This image is used to illustrate malignant mammographic findings rather than benign vascular or postsurgical calcification. Paget disease is discussed separately as DCIS infiltrating the epidermis of the nipple.

updates.question_text: Regarding special histologic subtypes of breast cancer discussed in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a common breast cancer subtype accounting for 20% of all cases
Tubular carcinoma is a low-grade cancer that may present as architectural distortion or a small spiculated mass and accounts for less than 2% of invasive ductal cancers
Mucinous carcinoma usually presents only as fine linear branching calcifications without a mass
Mucinous carcinoma is more common in older women and may mimic a benign lesion because of circumscribed mammographic appearance, acoustic enhancement and high T2 MRI signal
Medullary carcinoma is typically seen in younger women, often with BRCA1 mutation, and despite triple-negative basal-like classification has a favourable prognosis
options_after: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a common breast cancer subtype accounting for 20% of cases
Tubular carcinoma is a low-grade cancer that may present as architectural distortion or a small spiculated mass and accounts for less than 2% of invasive ductal cancers
Mucinous carcinoma usually presents primarily as fine linear branching calcifications without a mass
Mucinous carcinoma is more common in older women and may mimic a benign lesion because of circumscribed mammographic appearance, acoustic enhancement and high T2 MRI signal
Medullary carcinoma is typically seen in younger women, often with BRCA1 mutation, and despite triple-negative basal-like classification has a favourable prognosis
updates.explanation: Tubular carcinoma is described as a low-grade cancer, usually architectural distortion or a small spiculated mass, and accounts for less than 2% of invasive ductal cancers. Mucinous carcinoma accounts for approximately 2% of breast cancers, is more common in older women, and can look deceptively benign because it may be circumscribed, show acoustic enhancement and have high T2 signal. Medullary carcinoma accounts for less than 5%, is typically seen in younger women often with BRCA1 mutation, and has favourable prognosis despite basal-like triple-negative classification. Adenoid cystic carcinoma is very rare in the breast, less than 0.1% of all breast cancers.

updates.question_text: Regarding Paget disease and prognostic assessment in breast cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Paget disease is a benign eczema unrelated to ductal carcinoma
Paget disease of the nipple is a form of DCIS infiltrating the epidermis of the nipple
Sentinel lymph node biopsy is routinely performed for all DCIS regardless of necrosis or microinvasion
Axillary lymph node status is irrelevant once a breast cancer is non-metastatic
In non-metastatic invasive breast cancer, axillary lymph node status is the most important prognostic factor
options_after: Paget disease is a benign eczema unrelated to ductal carcinoma
Paget disease of the nipple is a form of DCIS infiltrating the epidermis of the nipple
Sentinel lymph node biopsy is routinely performed for most DCIS despite variation in necrosis or microinvasion
Axillary lymph node status is irrelevant once a breast cancer is non-metastatic
In non-metastatic invasive breast cancer, axillary lymph node status is the most important prognostic factor
updates.explanation: Paget disease of the nipple is described as a form of DCIS that infiltrates the epidermis of the nipple and presents with erythema, ulceration and eczematoid nipple changes. In non-metastatic invasive breast cancer, axillary lymph node status is the most important prognostic factor, and survival worsens with increasing numbers of involved axillary nodes. Sentinel lymph node biopsy is not routinely performed for DCIS unless necrosis or microinvasive disease is present. The source gives surgical sentinel lymph node biopsy a sensitivity of 93%.

updates.question_text: A breast mass appears oval and circumscribed on tomosynthesis and has sonographic features that could be mistaken for benignity, but it also has internal vascularity and rapid growth. Which of the following statements are correct regarding this example?
options_before: The source uses this example to show that all oval circumscribed masses should be assigned BI-RADS 2
The mass is described as HER2/neu overexpressing and therefore expected to respond to trastuzumab
Triple-negative cancers can show imaging features more typical of benign lesions despite aggressive biology
The source states that rapid growth is reassuring when a mass has circumscribed margins
Triple-negative cancers are ER, PR and HER2/neu negative and account for the majority of breast cancers in patients with BRCA1 mutation
options_after: The source uses this example to show that most oval circumscribed masses should be assigned BI-RADS 2
The mass is described as HER2/neu overexpressing and therefore expected to respond to trastuzumab
Triple-negative cancers can show imaging features more typical of benign lesions despite aggressive biology
The source states that rapid growth is reassuring when a mass has circumscribed margins
Triple-negative cancers are ER, PR and HER2/neu negative and account for the majority of breast cancers in patients with BRCA1 mutation
updates.explanation: The example was biopsied as triple-negative invasive ductal carcinoma despite oval circumscribed morphology and benign-leaning sonographic features. The source emphasises that triple-negative cancers are biologically aggressive, have poor prognosis and may show imaging features more typical of benign lesions. They are ER, PR and HER2/neu negative and account for the majority of breast cancers in patients with BRCA1 mutation. Rapid growth and internal vascularity prompted biopsy rather than reassurance.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS reporting structure, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: BI-RADS standardises mammography, ultrasound and MRI reports using a strict lexicon, structured reporting and assessment categories
A mammographic report should include breast composition using the BI-RADS density categories
BI-RADS is described as applying only to screening mammography and not to ultrasound or MRI
A mammographic report should include a clear description of significant findings and an overall impression with assessment category and course of action when appropriate
The fifth BI-RADS edition never allows the course of action to be separated from the assessment category
options_after: BI-RADS standardises mammography, ultrasound and MRI reports using a strict lexicon, structured reporting and assessment categories
A mammographic report should include breast composition using the BI-RADS density categories
BI-RADS is described as applying primarily to screening mammography and not to ultrasound or MRI
A mammographic report should include a clear description of significant findings and an overall impression with assessment category and course of action when appropriate
The fifth BI-RADS edition will not allow the course of action to be separated from the assessment category
updates.explanation: BI-RADS is presented as a system for standardising mammography, ultrasound and MRI reporting through lexicon, structured reporting and assessment categories. A mammographic report includes history and indication, comparisons, breast composition, significant findings including location and an overall impression with category and action when appropriate. The fifth edition allows the course of action to be separated from the assessment category in selected clinical situations. Examples include aspirating a painful simple cyst designated BI-RADS 2, or deferring biopsy for a suspected abscess or haematoma initially designated BI-RADS 4.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS Category 0, which statement is correct?
options_before: It means the breasts are normal and no further action is needed
It is the usual final assessment for diagnostic mammography
It is a known biopsy-proven malignancy category
It indicates that additional imaging or prior mammograms are needed before a final assessment, and it is only appropriate for screening
It is a probably benign category with short-interval follow-up
options_after: It means the breasts are normal without further action is needed
It is the usual final assessment for diagnostic mammography
It is a known biopsy-proven malignancy category
It indicates that additional imaging or prior mammograms are needed before a final assessment, and it is only appropriate for screening
It is a probably benign category with short-interval follow-up
updates.explanation: BI-RADS 0 means that additional imaging evaluation, such as spot compression, magnification, special mammographic views or ultrasound, and/or prior mammograms are required before final assessment. The source states that Category 0 is only appropriate for screening and that all diagnostic mammography must conclude with a final assessment from 1-6. BI-RADS 1 is negative, BI-RADS 2 is benign, BI-RADS 3 is probably benign and BI-RADS 6 is known biopsy-proven malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS Categories 4, 5 and 6, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: BI-RADS 4 indicates suspicious findings with a malignancy probability greater than 2% and less than 95%
BI-RADS 4C is the least suspicious subcategory
BI-RADS 5 indicates a greater than 95% probability of cancer and requires biopsy
BI-RADS 6 is reserved for imaging findings with prior biopsy proof of malignancy
A benign pathology result for a BI-RADS 5 lesion is automatically concordant
options_after: BI-RADS 4 indicates suspicious findings with a malignancy probability greater than 2% and less than 95%
BI-RADS 4C is the least suspicious subcategory
BI-RADS 5 indicates a greater than 95% probability of cancer and requires biopsy
BI-RADS 6 is reserved for imaging findings with prior biopsy proof of malignancy
A benign pathology result for a BI-RADS 5 lesion is ordinarily concordant
updates.explanation: BI-RADS 4 is suspicious, with malignancy probability greater than 2% and less than 95%, and requires biopsy. It may be subdivided into 4A, 4B and 4C, with 4A least suspicious and 4C most suspicious. BI-RADS 5 indicates a probability greater than 95% and also requires biopsy; any pathologic result other than cancer would be discordant. BI-RADS 6 is for known biopsy-proven malignancy, usually with an action plan already in place.

updates.question_text: Regarding screening mammography guideline differences quoted in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All quoted organisations recommend the same starting age and screening interval
ACR and SBI recommendations support annual screening mammography beginning at age 40 for average-risk women
The ACS 2015 recommendation includes annual screening from ages 45-54 and biennial screening at age 55 or older, with an option to start annually at ages 40-44
The USPSTF recommends annual mammography for all women from age 35
The USPSTF 2009 recommendation quoted is biennial mammography between ages 50-74, with the decision to start at ages 40-49 made individually
options_after: Most quoted organisations recommend the same starting age and screening interval
ACR and SBI recommendations support annual screening mammography beginning at age 40 for average-risk women
The ACS 2015 recommendation includes annual screening from ages 45-54 and biennial screening at age 55 or older, with an option to start annually at ages 40-44
The USPSTF recommends annual mammography for most women from age 35
The USPSTF 2009 recommendation quoted is biennial mammography between ages 50-74, with the decision to start at ages 40-49 made individually
updates.explanation: The source explicitly contrasts guideline differences. ACR and SBI support annual screening beginning at age 40 for average-risk women. The ACS 2015 recommendation is annual screening at ages 45-54, biennial screening at 55 or older, with an option to start annual screening at 40-44. The quoted USPSTF 2009 recommendation is biennial mammography between ages 50-74, with the age 40-49 decision made individually.

updates.question_text: Regarding standard screening mammographic views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The two standard screening views are CC and MLO
The CC image plane is approximately 45-60 degrees from the axial plane
The MLO view is primarily used because it captures only the superior-medial breast
The cleavage view is designed to pull lateral tissue into the detector
The MLO plane parallels the course of the pectoralis muscle heading into the axilla and is approximately 45-60 degrees from the axial plane
options_after: The two standard screening views are CC and MLO
The CC image plane is approximately 45-60 degrees from the axial plane
The MLO view is primarily used because it captures primarily the superior-medial breast
The cleavage view is designed to pull lateral tissue into the detector
The MLO plane parallels the course of the pectoralis muscle heading into the axilla and is approximately 45-60 degrees from the axial plane
updates.explanation: The two routine screening mammographic views are cranio-caudal and medial-lateral-oblique. The CC plane is transaxial. The MLO plane is approximately 45-60 degrees from the axial plane and parallels the pectoralis muscle as it heads into the axilla; it is ideal for screening because it captures most breast tissue in a single view. Cleavage view images medial breast tissue of both breasts, while the exaggerated CC view pulls lateral or medial tissue into the detector.

updates.question_text: Regarding diagnostic mammography workflow, which of the following statements are correct?
