options_before: Diagnostic mammography is usually performed for breast symptoms such as pain, lump, skin thickening or nipple discharge
Other indications include annual mammography in an asymptomatic woman with a past history of breast cancer, BI-RADS 3 follow-up and evaluation of a screening abnormality
A mammographic abnormality is first localised in three-dimensional space before problem-solving techniques are used
Ultrasound is never added during diagnostic mammography
Patients wait until imaging is complete before receiving a final summary and recommendations
options_after: Diagnostic mammography is usually performed for breast symptoms such as pain, lump, skin thickening or nipple discharge
Other indications include annual mammography in an asymptomatic woman with a past history of breast cancer, BI-RADS 3 follow-up and evaluation of a screening abnormality
A mammographic abnormality is first localised in three-dimensional space before problem-solving techniques are used
Ultrasound is not added during diagnostic mammography
Patients wait until imaging is complete before receiving a final summary and recommendations
updates.explanation: Diagnostic mammography is used for breast problems such as pain, lump, skin thickening and nipple discharge, and also for women with previous breast cancer, short-interval BI-RADS 3 follow-up and screening abnormalities. The source describes first localising any abnormality in three-dimensional space, then applying special problem-solving techniques. Ultrasound may be added at the radiologist's discretion. The patient remains until all imaging is completed and receives final interpretation and recommendations before leaving.

updates.question_text: Regarding technical adequacy when interpreting a mammogram, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The posterior nipple lines drawn on the CC and MLO views should be within 1 cm of each other
The pectoral muscle must be visible on every CC view or the study is automatically inadequate
On the MLO view, the pectoral muscle should be convex anteriorly and visible at least to the level of the nipple
The nipple of each breast should be in profile in at least one view
Blur is acceptable because it improves the conspicuity of amorphous calcifications
options_after: The posterior nipple lines drawn on the CC and MLO views should be within 1 cm of each other
The pectoral muscle must be visible on most CC views or the study is ordinarily inadequate
On the MLO view, the pectoral muscle should be convex anteriorly and visible at least to the level of the nipple
The nipple of each breast should be in profile in at least one view
Blur is acceptable because it improves the conspicuity of amorphous calcifications
updates.explanation: The source defines the posterior nipple line from the nipple to the pectoralis muscle, or to the film edge on the CC view if pectoralis is not visualised, and states that CC and MLO posterior nipple lines should be within 1 cm. On the MLO view, the pectoral muscle should be convex anteriorly and visible at least to the level of the nipple. The nipple should be in profile in at least one view. Blur and artefact are not acceptable because blur can make benign calcifications look suspicious and can obscure subtle calcifications.

updates.question_text: Regarding skin thickening on mammography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bilateral skin thickening is always malignant
Unilateral skin thickening may be benign or malignant
Benign causes listed include radiation therapy, acute mastitis, focal skin inflammation, and systemic fluid overload states such as CHF, renal failure or liver failure
Inflammatory carcinoma is excluded if there is no mammographic mass
Malignant causes include inflammatory carcinoma, locally advanced carcinoma and lymphatic obstruction from axillary adenopathy
options_after: Bilateral skin thickening is characteristically malignant
Unilateral skin thickening may be benign or malignant
Benign causes listed include radiation therapy, acute mastitis, focal skin inflammation, and systemic fluid overload states such as CHF, renal failure or liver failure
Inflammatory carcinoma is excluded if there is an absence of mammographic mass
Malignant causes include inflammatory carcinoma, locally advanced carcinoma and lymphatic obstruction from axillary adenopathy
updates.explanation: The source states that unilateral skin thickening can be benign or malignant, while bilateral skin thickening is usually benign and systemic. Benign causes include radiation therapy, acute mastitis, skin inflammation and systemic fluid overload or hypoalbuminaemia states including CHF, renal failure and liver failure. Malignant causes include inflammatory carcinoma, locally advanced carcinoma and lymphatic obstruction from axillary adenopathy. In inflammatory carcinoma, a mammographic mass may be present, but the source notes that occasionally no discrete mass is apparent.

updates.question_text: Regarding a mammographic mass versus an asymmetry, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A mammographic mass is a space-occupying lesion with convex borders seen in two different projections
A mammographic mass is defined as any density seen in one view only
A new mass is considered benign if it has any circumscribed component
A malignant-looking mass is disregarded if it has been stable for several years
An asymmetry is seen in one view only
options_after: A mammographic mass is a space-occupying lesion with convex borders seen in two different projections
A mammographic mass is defined as any density seen in one view in typical cases
A new mass is considered benign if it has any circumscribed component
A malignant-looking mass is disregarded if it has been stable for several years
An asymmetry is seen in one view only
updates.explanation: The source distinguishes a mammographic mass from an asymmetry by projection and contour: a mass is a space-occupying lesion with convex borders seen in two different projections, while an asymmetry is seen in one view only. A new mass is suspicious and must be fully evaluated regardless of morphology. A malignant-looking mass should remain suspicious even if unchanged because slow-growing carcinomas, such as tubular carcinoma, can remain stable for years. A stable mass with all benign features is almost always regarded as benign.

updates.question_text: Regarding BI-RADS mammographic mass morphology, which statement is correct?
options_before: A circumscribed fat-containing mass is suspicious until proven otherwise
A spiculated mass is malignant until proven otherwise
Most breast cancers that form a visible mass are lower density than surrounding fibroglandular tissue
An oval mass cannot include any smooth lobulations
Irregular shape is the least suspicious mammographic mass shape
options_after: A circumscribed fat-containing mass is suspicious until proven otherwise
A spiculated mass is malignant until proven otherwise
Most breast cancers that form a visible mass are lower density than surrounding fibroglandular tissue
An oval mass will not include any smooth lobulations
Irregular shape is the least suspicious mammographic mass shape
updates.explanation: The source states that a spiculated mass is malignant until proven otherwise. Most breast cancers that form a visible mass are equal or higher density than surrounding fibroglandular tissue. A circumscribed fat-containing mass is benign. The BI-RADS shape descriptors are round, oval and irregular; an oval mass may include up to two to three smooth lobulations, while an irregular mass is most suspicious for malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding associated mammographic features around a mass or focal abnormality, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Architectural distortion is radiating linear density from a central point without a definite visible mass
If architectural distortion has no history of surgery or trauma, biopsy is appropriate
Nipple inversion and nipple retraction are identical descriptors and always malignant
Skin retraction is most commonly postsurgical but may be due to a desmoplastic tumour
New axillary nodes with replacement of the fatty hilum may warrant evaluation
options_after: Architectural distortion is radiating linear density from a central point without a definite visible mass
If architectural distortion has no history of surgery or trauma, biopsy is appropriate
Nipple inversion and nipple retraction are closely comparable descriptors and characteristically malignant
Skin retraction is most commonly postsurgical but may be due to a desmoplastic tumour
New axillary nodes with replacement of the fatty hilum may warrant evaluation
updates.explanation: Architectural distortion is described as radiating linear densities from a central point without a definite mass, caused by tethering of fibroglandular tissue. Without a history of surgery or trauma, biopsy is appropriate. Skin retraction is most commonly postsurgical but may reflect a desmoplastic tumour. Nipple retraction is tethering or angulation, while inversion means the whole nipple points inward and may be developmental, bilateral and stable. Axillary nodes with loss of the normal fatty hilum, especially if new, may require evaluation.

updates.question_text: A CC mammogram shows an oval anterior inner breast mass that becomes better characterised on spot compression, revealing microlobulated margins. Which of the following statements are correct regarding this example?
options_before: The source describes this as a circumscribed fat-containing mass requiring no further workup
The spot compression view proves that the abnormality was only a one-view asymmetry
Spot compression better demonstrates the microlobulated margins
Biopsy of the mass revealed papilloma with carcinoma in situ
The example is used to show that microlobulation is a typically benign margin descriptor
options_after: The source describes this as a circumscribed fat-containing mass not requiring further workup
The spot compression view proves that the abnormality was primarily a one-view asymmetry
Spot compression better demonstrates the microlobulated margins
Biopsy of the mass revealed papilloma with carcinoma in situ
The example is used to show that microlobulation is a typically benign margin descriptor
updates.explanation: The caption describes an oval mass with partially obscured margins on the CC view that is better evaluated on spot compression, where microlobulated margins are seen. Biopsy revealed papilloma with carcinoma in situ. The teaching point is that additional views can expose a more suspicious margin descriptor. Microlobulation is not treated as a reassuring benign descriptor in this context.

updates.question_text: Regarding the general assessment of mammographic calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Abnormal calcification may be the earliest and sometimes only mammographic manifestation of cancer
Distribution can be ignored if calcification morphology appears suspicious
Both morphology and distribution are essential when characterising calcifications
All calcifications on mammography are considered suspicious unless proven otherwise
Some calcifications can be definitively characterised as benign, while others are highly suspicious or indeterminate
options_after: Abnormal calcification may be the earliest and sometimes only mammographic manifestation of cancer
Distribution can be ignored if calcification morphology appears suspicious
Both morphology and distribution are essential when characterising calcifications
Most calcifications on mammography are considered suspicious unless proven otherwise
Some calcifications can be definitively characterised as benign, while others are highly suspicious or indeterminate
updates.explanation: Most mammograms show calcifications and most are benign, but abnormal calcification can be the earliest or only mammographic sign of cancer. The source emphasises that both morphology and distribution are essential in assessment. Some calcifications have a classic benign appearance, whereas others are highly suspicious or indeterminate. Radiology skill lies in integrating morphology with distribution rather than relying on either alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding mammographic technique for evaluating calcifications, which statement is correct?
options_before: Suspicious calcifications are usually best evaluated only on routine full-field views
Magnification is unnecessary because it increases focal spot size
Spot compression magnification is almost always necessary to characterise indeterminate or suspicious calcifications
Milk of calcium never requires a true lateral view
Air-gap technique is avoided during calcification magnification
options_after: Suspicious calcifications are usually best evaluated primarily on routine full-field views
Magnification is unnecessary because it increases focal spot size
Spot compression magnification is almost always necessary to characterise indeterminate or suspicious calcifications
Milk of calcium will not require a true lateral view
Air-gap technique is avoided during calcification magnification
updates.explanation: The source states that spot compression magnification is almost always necessary to characterise calcifications that are indeterminate or suspicious. Magnification uses air-gap technique and a small 0.1 mm focal spot. Most benign calcifications can be described on routine full-field views, but milk of calcium is an exception because it generally requires a true lateral view with magnification. This reflects the importance of projection-dependent layering.

updates.question_text: Regarding coarse or popcorn-like calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Popcorn-like calcifications are caused by an involuting or hyalinising fibroadenoma
All fibroadenomas calcify early and uniformly
When fibroadenoma calcification begins, it is immediately diagnostic and never mimics cancer
Popcorn-like calcification is the typical appearance of milk of calcium
A benign fibroadenoma can be diagnosed with confidence when calcifications have the classic chunky popcorn-like morphology
options_after: Popcorn-like calcifications are caused by an involuting or hyalinising fibroadenoma
Most fibroadenomas calcify early and uniformly
When fibroadenoma calcification begins, it is immediately diagnostic and will not mimic cancer
Popcorn-like calcification is the typical appearance of milk of calcium
A benign fibroadenoma can be diagnosed with confidence when calcifications have the classic chunky popcorn-like morphology
updates.explanation: Popcorn-like calcifications are caused by involuting or hyalinising fibroadenoma. Not all fibroadenomas calcify, and early peripheral calcifications may resemble malignant calcifications enough to prompt biopsy. Once the chunky popcorn-like morphology is classic, a benign fibroadenoma can be diagnosed confidently. Milk of calcium has a different projection-dependent layering appearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding milk of calcium calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Milk of calcium represents free-floating calcium in tiny benign cysts
The key feature is identical morphology on CC and true lateral views
On CC views, milk of calcium may appear fuzzy, round and amorphous
On a 90-degree lateral view, dependent layering produces more defined semilunar or crescent-shaped calcifications
Milk of calcium is defined by calcium deposited on the surface of a sphere
options_after: Milk of calcium represents free-floating calcium in tiny benign cysts
The key feature is closely comparable morphology on CC and true lateral views
On CC views, milk of calcium may appear fuzzy, round and amorphous
On a 90-degree lateral view, dependent layering produces more defined semilunar or crescent-shaped calcifications
Milk of calcium is defined by calcium deposited on the surface of a sphere
updates.explanation: Milk of calcium is free-floating calcium within tiny benign cysts. Its diagnostic feature is a change in shape between CC and lateral projections. On the CC view it may look indistinct, fuzzy, round or amorphous; on the 90-degree lateral view it layers dependently into semilunar or crescent-shaped deposits. Calcium on the surface of a sphere refers to rim calcification, not milk of calcium.

updates.question_text: Regarding suture, dystrophic, round/punctate and rim calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Suture calcifications are currently common because of modern surgical technique
Dystrophic calcifications may follow surgery, biopsy, trauma or irradiation
Round and punctate calcifications are always BI-RADS 5 when diffusely distributed
A round calcification smaller than 0.5 mm is preferably termed punctate
Rim calcifications represent calcium deposited on the surface of a sphere, often from fat necrosis or a cyst wall
options_after: Suture calcifications are currently common because of modern surgical technique
Dystrophic calcifications may follow surgery, biopsy, trauma or irradiation
Round and punctate calcifications are characteristically BI-RADS 5 when diffusely distributed
A round calcification smaller than 0.5 mm is preferably termed punctate
Rim calcifications represent calcium deposited on the surface of a sphere, often from fat necrosis or a cyst wall
updates.explanation: Suture calcifications are calcium deposited on suture material and are now uncommonly seen because of modern surgical technique. Dystrophic calcifications may occur after surgery, biopsy, trauma or irradiation and often have coarse irregular shapes with lucency from fat necrosis. Round and punctate calcifications are benign when diffuse or random; an isolated baseline group of punctate calcifications may be BI-RADS 3. Rim calcifications reflect calcium on the surface of a sphere, usually fat necrosis or a calcified cyst wall.

updates.question_text: Regarding amorphous calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Amorphous calcifications are large enough to confidently identify as rod-like secretory calcifications
Amorphous calcifications are always benign irrespective of distribution
They are too small or hazy to determine detailed morphology
Their reported positive predictive value is 90%
Grouped, regional, linear or segmental amorphous calcifications are more suspicious and warrant biopsy
options_after: Amorphous calcifications are large enough to confidently identify as rod-like secretory calcifications
Amorphous calcifications are characteristically benign irrespective of distribution
They are too small or hazy to determine detailed morphology
Their reported positive predictive value is 90%
Grouped, regional, linear or segmental amorphous calcifications are more suspicious and warrant biopsy
updates.explanation: Amorphous calcifications are too small or hazy to characterise morphologically. Diffuse amorphous calcifications are usually benign, although magnification may be needed to look for suspicious groups. Grouped, regional, linear or segmental distributions are more suspicious and warrant biopsy. The source reports a positive predictive value of 20%, not 90%.

updates.question_text: Regarding coarse heterogeneous calcifications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are irregular calcifications generally larger than 0.5 mm but smaller than dystrophic calcifications
They may be associated with malignancy and biopsy is warranted
They are the typical benign result of calcium deposited on suture material
Evolving dystrophic calcifications, early fibroadenoma calcifications or fat necrosis cannot mimic coarse heterogeneous calcifications
They are defined by dependent layering on the true lateral view
options_after: They are irregular calcifications generally larger than 0.5 mm but smaller than dystrophic calcifications
They may be associated with malignancy and biopsy is warranted
They are the typical benign result of calcium deposited on suture material
Evolving dystrophic calcifications, early fibroadenoma calcifications or fat necrosis will not mimic coarse heterogeneous calcifications
They are defined by dependent layering on the true lateral view
updates.explanation: Coarse heterogeneous calcifications are irregular, generally larger than 0.5 mm but smaller than dystrophic calcifications. They may be associated with malignancy and warrant biopsy. The source highlights that evolving dystrophic calcifications and early calcifications in hyalinising fibroadenoma or fat necrosis may mimic them, creating a diagnostic challenge. Dependent layering is the key feature of milk of calcium, not coarse heterogeneous morphology.

updates.question_text: Regarding calcification distribution, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Distribution can greatly affect suspicion for malignancy
Diffuse and regional calcifications are always benign regardless of morphology
A regional distribution of suspicious fine pleomorphic or fine-linear branching calcifications may represent cancer
A linear, grouped or segmental distribution of typically benign morphology never needs further workup
Morphology remains important even when distribution is usually benign
options_after: Distribution can greatly affect suspicion for malignancy
Diffuse and regional calcifications are characteristically benign despite variation in morphology
A regional distribution of suspicious fine pleomorphic or fine-linear branching calcifications may represent cancer
A linear, grouped or segmental distribution of typically benign morphology will not need further workup
Morphology remains important even when distribution is usually benign
updates.explanation: The source states that calcification distribution can substantially affect malignancy suspicion. Diffuse and regional distributions are usually benign, but morphology remains important; suspicious fine pleomorphic or fine-linear branching calcifications in a regional distribution may represent cancer. Similarly, a more suspicious distribution such as linear, grouped or segmental can warrant further workup even if the morphology is typically benign. Assessment requires combining both axes of the lexicon.

updates.question_text: Regarding diffuse and regional calcification distributions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diffuse calcifications conform to a single ductal system
Diffuse calcifications are randomly distributed throughout the breast
Regional calcifications must be fewer than five calcifications within 1 cm
Regional calcifications always indicate calcium deposited in one ductal system
Regional calcifications occupy a large area greater than 2 cm and do not conform to a ductal distribution
options_after: Diffuse calcifications conform to a single ductal system
Diffuse calcifications are randomly distributed throughout the breast
Regional calcifications must be fewer than five calcifications within 1 cm
Regional calcifications characteristically indicate calcium deposited in one ductal system
Regional calcifications occupy a large area greater than 2 cm and do not conform to a ductal distribution
updates.explanation: Diffuse calcifications are randomly distributed throughout the breast and are often benign, especially punctate or amorphous calcifications in a scattered bilateral pattern. Regional calcifications are distributed in a large area greater than 2 cm, not conforming to a ductal distribution; because they may involve much of a quadrant or more than one quadrant, malignancy is less likely. Grouped calcifications, not regional calcifications, are defined by at least five small calcifications within 1 cm. Segmental distribution suggests a ductal system.

updates.question_text: Regarding linear and grouped calcification distributions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Linear calcifications are arrayed in a line and raise suspicion by suggesting calcium deposits within a duct
Grouped calcifications are defined as at least five small calcifications within 1 cm, with total extent less than 2 cm
Calcifications extending more than 2 cm are still classified as grouped if they are punctate
Grouped calcifications raise suspicion for malignancy
Large rod-like calcifications cannot be linear in distribution
options_after: Linear calcifications are arrayed in a line and raise suspicion by suggesting calcium deposits within a duct
Grouped calcifications are defined as at least five small calcifications within 1 cm, with total extent less than 2 cm
Calcifications extending more than 2 cm are still classified as grouped if they are punctate
Grouped calcifications raise suspicion for malignancy
Large rod-like calcifications will not be linear in distribution
updates.explanation: Linear calcifications are arranged in a line and increase suspicion because they suggest calcium in a duct. Grouped calcifications require at least five small calcifications within 1 cm, with the extent measuring less than 2 cm; if the extent is greater than 2 cm, the distribution is considered regional. Grouped calcifications raise suspicion for malignancy. The source notes that typically benign large rod-like calcifications are often linear in distribution, so morphology remains essential.

updates.question_text: Regarding segmental calcification distribution, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Segmental calcifications suggest calcium deposited in a ductal system
Segmental distribution is always benign when calcifications are amorphous
When morphology is clearly secretory and rod-like, segmental distribution can be benign
Intermediate-suspicion or typically benign round/punctate calcifications in a segmental distribution should raise concern for malignancy
Fine linear or fine-linear branching calcifications in a segmental distribution are appropriate for BI-RADS 5
options_after: Segmental calcifications suggest calcium deposited in a ductal system
Segmental distribution is characteristically benign when calcifications are amorphous
When morphology is clearly secretory and rod-like, segmental distribution can be benign
Intermediate-suspicion or typically benign round/punctate calcifications in a segmental distribution should raise concern for malignancy
Fine linear or fine-linear branching calcifications in a segmental distribution are appropriate for BI-RADS 5
updates.explanation: Segmental distribution is concerning because it suggests calcium within a ductal system. The source makes an important exception: when morphology is clearly secretory and rod-like, a segmental distribution can be benign. When intermediate-suspicion amorphous or typically benign round/punctate calcifications occur in a segmental distribution, concern for malignancy should be raised. Fine linear or fine-linear branching calcifications in a segmental distribution are highly suggestive of malignancy and are BI-RADS 5.

updates.question_text: Regarding one-view asymmetry, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An asymmetry is a region of breast tissue prominent on one view only
An asymmetry is by definition a mass with convex borders on two views
Asymmetry most commonly represents dermal calcifications
Asymmetry most commonly represents superposition of glandular tissue
Asymmetry is always BI-RADS 5 if seen only on the MLO view
options_after: An asymmetry is a region of breast tissue prominent on one view only
An asymmetry is by definition a mass with convex borders on two views
Asymmetry most commonly represents dermal calcifications
Asymmetry most commonly represents superposition of glandular tissue
Asymmetry is characteristically BI-RADS 5 if seen primarily on the MLO view
updates.explanation: The source defines asymmetry as a region of breast tissue that is prominent on one view only. It most commonly represents superposition of glandular tissue. A mass is different because it is a space-occupying lesion with convex borders seen in two projections. The image example shows an MLO-only asymmetry that represents superimposed fibroglandular tissue on the CC view.

updates.question_text: Regarding focal asymmetry, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A focal asymmetry is seen on one view only
A focal asymmetry involves less than one quadrant and is seen on two views
A focal asymmetry meets criteria for a mass because it has distinct convex borders
Focal asymmetry usually represents a prominent area of normal breast tissue, especially when interspersed fat is present
After complete workup, a nonpalpable focal asymmetry has less than 1% chance of malignancy and may be BI-RADS 3 on a baseline exam
options_after: A focal asymmetry is seen on one view in typical cases
A focal asymmetry involves less than one quadrant and is seen on two views
A focal asymmetry meets criteria for a mass because it has distinct convex borders
Focal asymmetry usually represents a prominent area of normal breast tissue, especially when interspersed fat is present
After complete workup, a nonpalpable focal asymmetry has less than 1% chance of malignancy and may be BI-RADS 3 on a baseline exam
updates.explanation: Focal asymmetry is seen on two views and involves less than one quadrant but does not meet criteria for a mass. A mass has distinct borders and convex contours, whereas focal asymmetry has concave contours. It often represents prominent normal breast tissue, especially with interspersed fat. After a complete workup with additional views and targeted ultrasound, a nonpalpable baseline focal asymmetry has less than 1% malignancy risk and may be BI-RADS 3.

updates.question_text: Regarding stability and management of focal asymmetry after complete workup, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A baseline nonpalpable focal asymmetry is automatically BI-RADS 5
Focal asymmetry cannot be called benign regardless of stability
Additional mammographic views with spot compression and targeted ultrasound are part of complete workup
The source states that MRI is mandatory before any BI-RADS 3 assessment for focal asymmetry
A lesion can be called benign after two to three years of stability
options_after: A baseline nonpalpable focal asymmetry is ordinarily BI-RADS 5
Focal asymmetry will not be called benign despite variation in stability
Additional mammographic views with spot compression and targeted ultrasound are part of complete workup
The source states that MRI is mandatory before any BI-RADS 3 assessment for focal asymmetry
A lesion can be called benign after two to three years of stability
updates.explanation: The source describes complete workup for focal asymmetry as including additional mammographic views with spot compression and targeted ultrasound. If nonpalpable and seen on a baseline exam, the risk of malignancy after workup is less than 1%, and BI-RADS 3 can be used. After two to three years of stability, the lesion can be called benign. MRI is not listed as a mandatory step for this scenario.

updates.question_text: Regarding developing asymmetry, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A developing asymmetry is a focal asymmetry that is new or increased in size
It is suspicious and was shown to represent breast cancer in 12.8% of screening mammography cases
The first workup step is to determine whether it is a true lesion or summation artefact
A typical mammographic workup includes spot compression views and/or repeat standard views
It is benign if no sonographic correlate is seen
options_after: A developing asymmetry is a focal asymmetry that is new or increased in size
It is suspicious and was shown to represent breast cancer in 12.8% of screening mammography cases
The first workup step is to determine whether it is a true lesion or summation artefact
A typical mammographic workup includes spot compression views and/or repeat standard views
It is benign if sonographic correlate is absent
updates.explanation: Developing asymmetry is a focal asymmetry that is new or increasing. It is suspicious, with the source quoting breast cancer rates of 12.8% at screening mammography and 26.7% at diagnostic mammography. The initial task is to confirm whether the finding is real or summation artefact using spot compression and/or repeat standard views. Absence of a sonographic correlate does not make a true developing asymmetry benign; stereotactic biopsy is required.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound and MRI in the evaluation of developing asymmetry, which statement is correct?
options_before: Ultrasound is performed before the developing asymmetry has been localised in three-dimensional space
If no sonographic correlate is seen, the finding is downgraded to BI-RADS 1
Absence of an MRI correlate does not remove the need for biopsy of a suspicious developing asymmetry
MRI is the standard first-line test for every developing asymmetry
A benign sonographic correlate cannot alter BI-RADS assessment
options_after: Ultrasound is performed before the developing asymmetry has been localised in three-dimensional space
If sonographic correlate is absent, the finding is downgraded to BI-RADS 1
Absence of an MRI correlate does not remove the need for biopsy of a suspicious developing asymmetry
MRI is the standard first-line test for a developing asymmetry before targeted mammographic views.
A benign sonographic correlate will not alter BI-RADS assessment
updates.explanation: After diagnostic mammography confirms that a developing asymmetry is real and can be localised in three-dimensional space, ultrasound is performed. If ultrasound shows a mass, it can be targeted for biopsy; if it shows a benign correlate such as a simple cyst, the developing asymmetry may be assessed as BI-RADS 2. If no sonographic correlate exists for a true developing asymmetry, stereotactic biopsy is required because cancer risk remains greater than 2%. MRI generally does not play a standard role, and absence of an MRI correlate would not obviate biopsy.

updates.question_text: Regarding biopsy thresholds for calcification morphology and distribution, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Grouped, regional, linear or segmental amorphous calcifications warrant biopsy
Diffuse amorphous calcifications are always BI-RADS 5
Coarse heterogeneous calcifications may be associated with malignancy and warrant biopsy
Fine pleomorphic calcifications should be biopsied when they could reasonably be identified as pleomorphic
Segmental fine-linear branching calcifications are managed as BI-RADS 2
options_after: Grouped, regional, linear or segmental amorphous calcifications warrant biopsy
Diffuse amorphous calcifications are characteristically BI-RADS 5
Coarse heterogeneous calcifications may be associated with malignancy and warrant biopsy
Fine pleomorphic calcifications should be biopsied when they could reasonably be identified as pleomorphic
Segmental fine-linear branching calcifications are managed as BI-RADS 2
updates.explanation: The source gives biopsy-level concern for grouped, regional, linear or segmental amorphous calcifications, and for coarse heterogeneous calcifications because they may be malignant. It also advises biopsy when a group of calcifications could be pleomorphic. Diffuse amorphous calcifications are usually benign, although magnification may be needed. Fine linear or fine-linear branching calcifications in a segmental distribution are BI-RADS 5, not benign.

updates.question_text: Regarding benign calcification mimics of suspicious disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Early fibroadenoma calcifications can never resemble cancer
Early or incomplete vascular calcifications may resemble fine linear calcifications
Evolving dystrophic calcifications or fat necrosis may resemble coarse heterogeneous calcifications
Milk of calcium is diagnosed by showing no change between CC and lateral projections
Secretory large rod-like calcifications can follow a ductal pattern similar to DCIS but have a classic benign appearance
options_after: Early fibroadenoma calcifications will not resemble cancer
Early or incomplete vascular calcifications may resemble fine linear calcifications
Evolving dystrophic calcifications or fat necrosis may resemble coarse heterogeneous calcifications
Milk of calcium is diagnosed when calcification morphology remains unchanged between CC and lateral projections.
Secretory large rod-like calcifications can follow a ductal pattern similar to DCIS but have a classic benign appearance
updates.explanation: Several benign entities can mimic suspicious calcifications. Early or incomplete vascular calcifications may resemble fine linear calcifications, and evolving dystrophic calcifications, early hyalinising fibroadenoma calcifications or fat necrosis may appear coarse heterogeneous. Large rod-like secretory calcifications can follow a ductal pattern similar to DCIS but have a classic benign morphology. Milk of calcium is recognised because its shape changes between CC and lateral projections, not because it remains unchanged.

updates.question_text: Regarding suspicious distribution despite benign or intermediate morphology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Linear distribution elevates suspicion because it suggests calcium deposits within a duct
Diffuse distribution of punctate calcifications is more suspicious than segmental distribution
Grouped calcifications raise suspicion for malignancy
Regional distribution always means the calcifications conform to a ductal distribution
Segmental round or punctate calcifications should raise concern for malignancy despite typically benign morphology
options_after: Linear distribution elevates suspicion because it suggests calcium deposits within a duct
Diffuse distribution of punctate calcifications is more suspicious than segmental distribution
Grouped calcifications raise suspicion for malignancy
Regional distribution characteristically means the calcifications conform to a ductal distribution
Segmental round or punctate calcifications should raise concern for malignancy despite typically benign morphology
updates.explanation: Linear distribution raises suspicion because it suggests calcium within a duct. Grouped calcifications also raise suspicion. Segmental distribution is worrisome because it suggests a ductal system, and the source specifically says that intermediate or typically benign round/punctate calcifications in a segmental distribution should raise concern. Diffuse punctate or amorphous calcifications are usually benign and often bilateral; regional calcifications do not conform to a ductal distribution.

updates.question_text: Regarding differentiating asymmetry subtypes at the workstation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: One-view prominence is asymmetry and often summation of glandular tissue
Majority-of-one-breast density involving more than one quadrant is global asymmetry
Less-than-one-quadrant abnormality seen on two views without convex mass borders is focal asymmetry
A new or enlarging focal asymmetry is a developing asymmetry
All asymmetries are managed by MRI before mammographic problem-solving
options_after: One-view prominence is asymmetry and often summation of glandular tissue
Majority-of-one-breast density involving more than one quadrant is global asymmetry
Less-than-one-quadrant abnormality seen on two views without convex mass borders is focal asymmetry
A new or enlarging focal asymmetry is a developing asymmetry
Most asymmetries are managed by MRI before mammographic problem-solving
updates.explanation: The source separates asymmetry patterns by number of views, extent and change over time. One-view prominence is asymmetry and commonly represents superposition. Global asymmetry involves most of one breast and more than one quadrant. Focal asymmetry is seen on two views, involves less than one quadrant and lacks convex mass borders. Developing asymmetry is new or increased focal asymmetry and requires mammographic confirmation, targeted ultrasound when localised, and biopsy if needed; MRI is not the standard first step.

updates.question_text: Regarding the cancer risk quoted for developing asymmetry, which statement is correct?
options_before: Cancer risk is less than 1% after diagnostic evaluation in all developing asymmetries
Developing asymmetry represented breast cancer in 12.8% of screening mammography cases and 26.7% of diagnostic mammography cases
Developing asymmetry is considered benign if stable for six months
Developing asymmetry has a malignancy probability below the BI-RADS 3 threshold by definition
The quoted cancer risk is eliminated if targeted ultrasound is negative
options_after: Cancer risk is less than 1% after diagnostic evaluation in most developing asymmetries
Developing asymmetry represented breast cancer in 12.8% of screening mammography cases and 26.7% of diagnostic mammography cases
Developing asymmetry is considered benign if stable for six months
Developing asymmetry has a malignancy probability below the BI-RADS 3 threshold by definition
The quoted cancer risk is eliminated if targeted ultrasound is negative
updates.explanation: The source quotes developing asymmetry as representing breast cancer in 12.8% of cases at screening mammography and 26.7% at diagnostic mammography. That risk makes it a suspicious mammographic finding. Even if there is no sonographic correlate after confirmation of a true developing asymmetry, stereotactic biopsy is required because the risk remains greater than 2%. The less than 1% figure applies to a nonpalpable focal asymmetry after complete workup, not to developing asymmetry.

updates.question_text: Regarding architectural distortion on mammography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It describes lines radiating from a central point with no central mass visible
It is usually ignored if seen only on tomosynthesis
It produces tethering and indentation of breast tissue
It only qualifies as architectural distortion when a central mass is visible
It is only suspicious when associated with coarse popcorn-like calcifications
options_after: It describes lines radiating from a central point with no central mass visible
It is usually ignored if seen primarily on tomosynthesis
It produces tethering and indentation of breast tissue
It primarily qualifies as architectural distortion when a central mass is visible
It is primarily suspicious when associated with coarse popcorn-like calcifications
updates.explanation: Architectural distortion is defined as radiating lines from a central point without a visible central mass, causing tethering and indentation of breast tissue. It is suspicious for malignancy, although benign causes include radial scar/complex sclerosing lesion, post-biopsy scar and fibrocystic change such as sclerosing adenosis. The source image contrasts distortion from a prior excisional biopsy scar with distortion caused by invasive ductal carcinoma on biopsy. Requiring a central mass is the opposite of the definition used here.

updates.question_text: Regarding tomosynthesis and exaggerated CC views, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tomosynthesis worsens lesion detection by increasing the effect of overlapping tissue
Tomosynthesis may decrease the need for additional diagnostic imaging such as spot compression
The lateral XCC view pulls medial breast tissue into the detector
The medial XCC view pulls medial breast tissue into the detector
XCC views are used only for diagnosing milk of calcium
options_after: Tomosynthesis worsens lesion detection by increasing the effect of overlapping tissue
Tomosynthesis may decrease the need for additional diagnostic imaging such as spot compression
The lateral XCC view pulls medial breast tissue into the detector
The medial XCC view pulls medial breast tissue into the detector
XCC views are used primarily for diagnosing milk of calcium
updates.explanation: Compared with full-field digital mammography, tomosynthesis improves lesion detection and characterisation by reducing overlap from breast tissue, and may reduce the need for additional views such as spot compression. The lateral XCC view pulls lateral breast tissue into the detector, while the medial XCC view pulls medial tissue into the detector. Milk of calcium is assessed with true lateral magnification views rather than XCC views.

updates.question_text: Regarding use of the true lateral mammographic view, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is never used for stereotactic procedure planning
It is mainly used to demonstrate skin calcifications with a BB marker
It is the preferred view for routine screening instead of MLO
It is used to diagnose milk of calcium, triangulate an MLO-only lesion and help plan a stereotactic procedure
It is unnecessary if milk of calcium is suspected because the CC view is definitive
options_after: It is not used for stereotactic procedure planning
It is mainly used to demonstrate skin calcifications with a BB marker
It is the preferred view for routine screening instead of MLO
It is used to diagnose milk of calcium, triangulate an MLO-only lesion and help plan a stereotactic procedure
It is unnecessary if milk of calcium is suspected because the CC view is definitive
updates.explanation: The true lateral view may be obtained as ML or LM and is used to diagnose milk of calcium, triangulate a lesion seen on MLO but not CC, and plan stereotactic procedures. When milk of calcium is suspected, magnification spot views should also be obtained in the true lateral projection. On true lateral imaging, calcium layers dependently in small cysts as tiny crescents rather than the fuzzy round CC appearance. The MLO view remains a standard screening projection.

updates.question_text: Regarding diagnostic workup of a screening-detected mass or focal asymmetry, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A screening mammogram can receive BI-RADS 1, 2 or 0 assessments
Concerning screening findings are recalled as BI-RADS 0 for additional evaluation
If diagnostic views show only normal pliable fibroglandular tissue, biopsy is still mandatory
If an abnormality persists on spot compression, it should be localised on two orthogonal views
Once a lesion is localised to a quadrant, targeted ultrasound should be performed
options_after: A screening mammogram can receive BI-RADS 1, 2 or 0 assessments
Concerning screening findings are recalled as BI-RADS 0 for additional evaluation
If diagnostic views show primarily normal pliable fibroglandular tissue, biopsy is still mandatory
If an abnormality persists on spot compression, it should be localised on two orthogonal views
Once a lesion is localised to a quadrant, targeted ultrasound should be performed
updates.explanation: Screening mammography can be assessed as BI-RADS 1, 2 or 0. Concerning findings are recalled as BI-RADS 0 for additional diagnostic evaluation. If additional mammographic views show only normal pliable fibroglandular tissue, no further workup is needed and BI-RADS 1 is appropriate. A persistent abnormality should be localised on two orthogonal views and, once localised to a quadrant, targeted ultrasound should be performed.

updates.question_text: Regarding lesion localisation across mammographic projections, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Correlating lesions on two views does not require any agreement in distance from the nipple
If a lesion is seen only on MLO, rolled CC views are the usual first localisation method
A lesion seen on MLO but not CC may be far lateral, and an XCCL view can better image far lateral tissue
A lesion seen only on CC is always in the lower outer quadrant
Once a lesion is localised to a quadrant, targeted ultrasound should be performed
options_after: Correlating lesions on two views does not require any agreement in distance from the nipple
If a lesion is seen primarily on MLO, rolled CC views are the usual first localisation method
A lesion seen on MLO but not CC may be far lateral, and an XCCL view can better image far lateral tissue
A lesion seen primarily on CC is characteristically in the lower outer quadrant
Once a lesion is localised to a quadrant, targeted ultrasound should be performed
updates.explanation: The source warns that lesions correlated on two views should be at about the same distance from the nipple, within 1 cm, to avoid matching different lesions. An MLO-only lesion should be triangulated with a lateral view and may be far lateral, where XCCL can help. A CC-only lesion may be in the upper-inner quadrant and excluded from the MLO view, for which rolled CC views are typically used. Targeted ultrasound is performed once a lesion is localised to a quadrant.

updates.question_text: Regarding biopsy and problem-solving for difficult mammographic findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI can be helpful when a suspicious single-view finding still cannot be localised despite thorough mammographic and ultrasound evaluation
Stereotactic biopsy is never an option for a one-view finding
A mass with any suspicious feature on either ultrasound or mammography should generally be biopsied
A circumscribed mammographic mass with an indistinct or microlobulated ultrasound margin is still benign because mammography dominates
Most new findings are suspicious, with the notable exception of a circumscribed mammographic mass definitively shown to be a simple cyst on ultrasound
options_after: MRI can be helpful when a suspicious single-view finding still cannot be localised despite thorough mammographic and ultrasound evaluation
Stereotactic biopsy is not an option for a one-view finding
A mass with any suspicious feature on either ultrasound or mammography should generally be biopsied
A circumscribed mammographic mass with an indistinct or microlobulated ultrasound margin is still benign because mammography dominates
Most new findings are suspicious, with the notable exception of a circumscribed mammographic mass definitively shown to be a simple cyst on ultrasound
updates.explanation: MRI can help when a suspicious one-view finding remains unlocalised after full mammographic and ultrasound evaluation. Stereotactic biopsy is also an option for one-view findings, although it is most often used for calcifications. In general, biopsy is recommended when a mass has any suspicious feature on mammography or ultrasound, so a circumscribed mammographic mass with an indistinct or microlobulated ultrasound margin remains suspicious. A new circumscribed mass proven to be a simple cyst on ultrasound is the notable benign exception.

updates.question_text: Regarding palpable breast findings, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The mammographic workup is completely unrelated to workup of an asymptomatic mammographic lesion
All palpable findings are generally evaluated by ultrasound, even if the mammogram is negative
A negative mammogram eliminates the need for ultrasound in all palpable abnormalities
Palpable findings are never assessed with targeted ultrasound in this source
The key difference from asymptomatic screening findings is that ultrasound is generally performed for all palpable findings
options_after: The mammographic workup is completely unrelated to workup of an asymptomatic mammographic lesion
All palpable findings are generally evaluated by ultrasound, even if the mammogram is negative
A negative mammogram eliminates the need for ultrasound in most palpable abnormalities
Palpable findings are not assessed with targeted ultrasound in this source
The key difference from asymptomatic screening findings is that ultrasound is generally performed for all palpable findings
updates.explanation: The source states that mammographic workup for a palpable abnormality is similar to that for an asymptomatic lesion found on mammography. The key difference is that all palpable findings are generally evaluated with ultrasound, even when the mammogram is negative. This ensures that a clinically evident lesion is not dismissed solely because mammography is unrevealing. Describing the workflows as completely unrelated is not supported by the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding grouped punctate calcifications and BI-RADS 3, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Punctate calcifications are a subset of round calcifications that are less than 0.5 mm
Grouped punctate calcifications on a baseline exam can be BI-RADS 3 if morphology is clearly punctate or round and distribution is grouped
Spot-compression magnification views are usually necessary to accurately characterise calcifications
A group of amorphous calcifications is usually BI-RADS 3 if seen on a baseline exam
Round or punctate calcifications in linear or segmental distribution are never suspicious
options_after: Punctate calcifications are a subset of round calcifications that are less than 0.5 mm
Grouped punctate calcifications on a baseline exam can be BI-RADS 3 if morphology is clearly punctate or round and distribution is grouped
Spot-compression magnification views are usually necessary to accurately characterise calcifications
A group of amorphous calcifications is usually BI-RADS 3 if seen on a baseline exam
Round or punctate calcifications in linear or segmental distribution are not suspicious
updates.explanation: Punctate calcifications are round calcifications smaller than 0.5 mm. Grouped punctate calcifications on a baseline mammogram may be BI-RADS 3 if the morphology is clearly punctate or round and the distribution is grouped. Spot-compression magnification is usually needed for accurate calcification characterisation. A group of amorphous calcifications is indeterminate and usually warrants biopsy, and rare linear or segmental round/punctate calcifications would be suspicious.

updates.question_text: Regarding focal asymmetry as a mammographic BI-RADS 3 finding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It may be assessed as probably benign on a baseline exam after thorough imaging workup if no ultrasound correlate is seen
It is automatically BI-RADS 5 because it is seen on two views
It requires no diagnostic workup before being assigned BI-RADS 3
It can be called benign after two to three years of stability
It is the same as developing asymmetry if unchanged from baseline
options_after: It may be assessed as probably benign on a baseline exam after thorough imaging workup if no ultrasound correlate is seen
It is ordinarily BI-RADS 5 because it is seen on two views
It does not require diagnostic workup before being assigned BI-RADS 3
It can be called benign after two to three years of stability
It is the same as developing asymmetry if unchanged from baseline
updates.explanation: A focal asymmetry seen on a baseline exam can be assessed as BI-RADS 3 after thorough imaging workup if no ultrasound correlate is seen. Stability for two to three years allows the lesion to be called benign. It should not be assigned BI-RADS 3 without diagnostic workup. Developing asymmetry is new or increased focal asymmetry, which carries a higher cancer risk and different management.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast ultrasound zonal anatomy and dermal lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The subcutaneous or premammary zone contains skin, dermis, subcutaneous fat and some Cooper ligaments
Dermal lesions are almost always benign and include epidermal inclusion cysts and sebaceous cysts
The mammary zone contains only retromammary fat and no ducts or terminal ductal lobular units
A lesion completely within the echogenic dermis can be confidently diagnosed as a benign epidermal inclusion cyst or sebaceous cyst
Hypodermal lesions are limited to epidermal inclusion cysts and cannot include breast cancer
options_after: The subcutaneous or premammary zone contains skin, dermis, subcutaneous fat and some Cooper ligaments
Dermal lesions are almost always benign and include epidermal inclusion cysts and sebaceous cysts
The mammary zone contains primarily retromammary fat without ducts or terminal ductal lobular units
A lesion completely within the echogenic dermis can be confidently diagnosed as a benign epidermal inclusion cyst or sebaceous cyst
Hypodermal lesions are limited to epidermal inclusion cysts and will not include breast cancer
updates.explanation: The subcutaneous or premammary zone contains skin, dermis, subcutaneous fat and some Cooper ligaments. Dermal lesions are almost always benign and include epidermal inclusion and sebaceous cysts. A lesion fully within the echogenic dermis can be confidently diagnosed as one of these benign skin lesions. Lesions arising from the hypodermis have a broader differential including papilloma, fibroadenoma and breast cancer, so identifying the site of origin is important.

updates.question_text: Regarding epidermal inclusion cysts and sebaceous cysts in the breast, which statement is correct?
options_before: Sebaceous cysts contain keratin debris and therefore are always dense on mammography
Epidermal inclusion cysts are malignant until proven otherwise
Epidermal inclusion cysts arise only from ducts in the mammary zone
Sebaceous cysts are typically lucent on mammography because of fatty sebum, whereas epidermal inclusion cyst keratin debris appears dense
The two entities are always distinguishable clinically and sonographically
options_after: Sebaceous cysts contain keratin debris and therefore are characteristically dense on mammography
Epidermal inclusion cysts are malignant until proven otherwise
Epidermal inclusion cysts arise primarily from ducts in the mammary zone
Sebaceous cysts are typically lucent on mammography because of fatty sebum, whereas epidermal inclusion cyst keratin debris appears dense
The two entities are characteristically distinguishable clinically and sonographically
updates.explanation: Sebaceous cysts are associated with sebaceous ducts and may look similar to epidermal inclusion cysts on clinical examination and ultrasound. The source distinguishes them mammographically: sebaceous cysts are typically lucent because of fatty sebum, while keratin debris in epidermal inclusion cysts appears dense. Epidermal inclusion cysts arise from hair follicle plugging by keratinous debris or traumatic epidermal implantation. Both are benign dermal entities when located completely in the dermis.

updates.question_text: Regarding management implications of suspected epidermal inclusion cyst, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Core needle biopsy is preferred because rupture has no consequence
Rupture of an epidermal inclusion cyst or sebaceous cyst can incite a severe inflammatory reaction with chemical dermatitis
Core needle biopsy should be avoided if an epidermal inclusion cyst is suspected
If tissue sampling is needed, surgical excision is preferable
The source recommends routine stereotactic biopsy for all suspected dermal cysts
options_after: Core needle biopsy is preferred because rupture lacks consequence
Rupture of an epidermal inclusion cyst or sebaceous cyst can incite a severe inflammatory reaction with chemical dermatitis
Core needle biopsy should be avoided if an epidermal inclusion cyst is suspected
If tissue sampling is needed, surgical excision is preferable
The source recommends routine stereotactic biopsy for most suspected dermal cysts
updates.explanation: Rupture of an epidermal inclusion cyst or sebaceous cyst can incite a severe inflammatory reaction, causing chemical dermatitis. Therefore core needle biopsy should be avoided when epidermal inclusion cyst is suspected. If tissue sampling is felt necessary, surgical excision is preferred. This is a practical radiology management point based on the anatomic diagnosis of a dermal lesion.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast ultrasound zones and fat echogenicity, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The mammary zone contains only retromammary fat and no ducts or terminal ductal lobular units
The retromammary zone lies just superficial to pectoralis and contains fat and a few Cooper ligaments
Parenchymal breast fat is hyperechoic, unlike fat elsewhere in the body
Fat in a lymph node hilum, lipoma and fat necrosis may appear hyperechoic
The mammary zone is the site of most breast pathology
options_after: The mammary zone contains primarily retromammary fat without ducts or terminal ductal lobular units
The retromammary zone lies just superficial to pectoralis and contains fat and a few Cooper ligaments
Parenchymal breast fat is hyperechoic, unlike fat elsewhere in the body
Fat in a lymph node hilum, lipoma and fat necrosis may appear hyperechoic
The mammary zone is the site of most breast pathology
updates.explanation: Most breast pathology arises in the mammary zone, which includes ducts, terminal ductal lobular units, fat, fibrous tissue and Cooper ligaments. The retromammary zone is just superficial to pectoralis and contains fat and a few Cooper ligaments. Parenchymal breast fat is hypoechoic in breast ultrasound, unlike fat elsewhere in body imaging. Fat in a lymph node hilum, lipoma or fat necrosis may appear hyperechoic.

updates.question_text: Regarding the BI-RADS lexicon for ultrasound masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A mass should be measured in only one plane because ultrasound is real-time
Position is labelled by mammographic quadrant rather than clockface and nipple distance
Ultrasound mass shape descriptors are round, oval and irregular
The orientation descriptor is unique to ultrasound and refers to the long axis of the mass relative to the skin
Obscured is not a BI-RADS descriptor for ultrasound margins
options_after: A mass should be measured in a single plane because ultrasound is real-time
Position is labelled by mammographic quadrant rather than clockface and nipple distance
Ultrasound mass shape descriptors are round, oval and irregular
The orientation descriptor is unique to ultrasound and refers to the long axis of the mass relative to the skin
Obscured is not a BI-RADS descriptor for ultrasound margins
updates.explanation: The source states that an ultrasound mass should be measured in three orthogonal planes and positioned by clockface and distance from the nipple. Shape descriptors are round, oval and irregular, matching mammography. Orientation is unique to ultrasound and describes the long axis relative to the skin. Obscured is not an ultrasound margin descriptor; non-circumscribed ultrasound margins are described as indistinct, angular, microlobulated or spiculated.

updates.question_text: Regarding posterior acoustic features on breast ultrasound, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Posterior enhancement refers to decreased echogenicity deep to a mass
Posterior enhancement is one characteristic of a simple cyst but is not specific by itself
Shadowing is attenuation of the sound beam as it passes through the lesion
Shadowing excludes fibrosis from neoplastic desmoplastic reaction or surgical scar
A lesion cannot have combined posterior acoustic features
options_after: Posterior enhancement refers to decreased echogenicity deep to a mass
Posterior enhancement is one characteristic of a simple cyst but is not specific by itself
Shadowing is attenuation of the sound beam as it passes through the lesion
Shadowing excludes fibrosis from neoplastic desmoplastic reaction or surgical scar
A lesion will not have combined posterior acoustic features
updates.explanation: Posterior acoustic enhancement is increased echogenicity deep to a mass and is one feature of a simple cyst, but it is not specific alone. Shadowing represents attenuation of the sound beam through the lesion and may be associated with fibrosis from a neoplastic desmoplastic reaction or a surgical scar. A lesion can have no posterior features, enhancement, shadowing or a combined pattern. The source gives fibroadenoma with a large shadowing calcification as an example of combined features.

updates.question_text: Regarding the clinical role and limitation of breast MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Breast MRI plays a complementary role to mammography in breast cancer evaluation
Dynamic contrast enhancement increases accuracy for malignancy detection beyond standard T1- and T2-weighted sequences
MRI has superior sensitivity to mammography for small microcalcifications
Benign and malignant lesions may overlap in morphology and enhancement
Breast MRI does not require a BI-RADS lexicon because enhancement is always specific
options_after: Breast MRI plays a complementary role to mammography in breast cancer evaluation
Dynamic contrast enhancement increases accuracy for malignancy detection beyond standard T1- and T2-weighted sequences
MRI has superior sensitivity to mammography for small microcalcifications
Benign and malignant lesions may overlap in morphology and enhancement
Breast MRI does not require a BI-RADS lexicon because enhancement is characteristically specific
updates.explanation: Breast MRI is complementary to mammography and has high sensitivity for cancer detection. Standard T1- and T2-weighted sequences may not distinguish benign from malignant enhancement, so dynamic contrast enhancement improves detection accuracy. A major challenge is overlap between benign and malignant lesions, addressed using kinetic curves and a stringent BI-RADS lexicon. Mammography remains superior to MRI for detection of small calcifications, although larger calcifications may produce susceptibility artefact.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast MRI for staging known cancer, which statement is correct?
options_before: MRI cannot assess tumour size accurately compared with mammography or ultrasound
MRI cannot evaluate pectoralis or intercostal muscle invasion
MRI has no role in evaluating axillary lymph nodes
Multifocal disease always permits breast conservation regardless of breast size
The presence of cancer in more than one quadrant is multicentric disease and usually requires mastectomy
options_after: MRI will not assess tumour size accurately compared with mammography or ultrasound
MRI will not evaluate pectoralis or intercostal muscle invasion
MRI has negligible role in evaluating axillary lymph nodes
Multifocal disease characteristically permits breast conservation despite variation in breast size
The presence of cancer in more than one quadrant is multicentric disease and usually requires mastectomy
updates.explanation: The source states that cancer in more than one quadrant is multicentric disease and usually requires mastectomy. MRI can evaluate extent of disease, accurately measure tumour size with the highest correlation to pathology among the compared modalities, assess abnormal axillary nodes and evaluate pectoralis or intercostal muscle invasion. Multifocal disease, defined as two or more sites in one quadrant, may preclude breast conservation depending on breast size. The image example shows posterior tumour with loss of the fat plane and pectoralis muscle enhancement.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI assessment of response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Follow-up MRI after one or two cycles of chemotherapy can assess response.
Cytotoxic therapy typically has no effect on lesion enhancement kinetics.
MRI after completion of neoadjuvant therapy can guide surgical planning by showing residual disease extent.
Response assessment is primarily based on silicone-specific implant sequences.
Neoadjuvant therapy is used to reduce the size of large tumours before resection.
options_after: Follow-up MRI after one or two cycles of chemotherapy can assess response.
Cytotoxic therapy typically lacks effect on lesion enhancement kinetics.
MRI after completion of neoadjuvant therapy can guide surgical planning by showing residual disease extent.
Response assessment is primarily based on silicone-specific implant sequences.
Neoadjuvant therapy is used to reduce the size of large tumours before resection.
updates.explanation: The text states that neoadjuvant therapy is used to reduce large tumours prior to resection, and that MRI can assess response even after one or two cycles. After treatment, MRI can detect the location and extent of residual disease to guide surgery. Cytotoxic therapy may alter enhancement kinetics by reducing tumour vascularity. Implant-specific MRI is a separate indication and is not the method for assessing chemotherapy response.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI for diagnostic problem solving and implant assessment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI is first-line for every screening asymmetry before mammographic spot compression.
MRI can be useful when an asymmetry persists after spot compression but remains non-localisable on orthogonal mammography or ultrasound.
Saline implant rupture is best evaluated with non-contrast MRI.
MRI has the highest sensitivity and specificity for silicone implant rupture.
A silicone implant rupture protocol uses gadolinium to evaluate cancer simultaneously.
options_after: MRI is the first-line test for a screening asymmetry before mammographic spot compression.
MRI can be useful when an asymmetry persists after spot compression but remains non-localisable on orthogonal mammography or ultrasound.
Saline implant rupture is best evaluated with non-contrast MRI.
MRI has the highest sensitivity and specificity for silicone implant rupture.
A silicone implant rupture protocol uses gadolinium to evaluate cancer simultaneously.
updates.explanation: MRI is described as a problem-solving tool after a thorough mammographic and ultrasound workup remains indeterminate, such as a persistent asymmetry that cannot be localised by orthogonal view or ultrasound. MRI also has the highest sensitivity and specificity for silicone implant rupture. A silicone implant evaluation does not use gadolinium and does not evaluate for cancer. Saline implants are typically evaluated by physical examination, mammography and ultrasound.

updates.question_text: Regarding the BI-RADS MRI mass lexicon, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A mass is a space-occupying lesion that displaces normal breast parenchyma.
The MRI lexicon for mass shape uses the same shape terms as mammography and ultrasound.
MRI uses irregular only for mass shape and never for mass margin.
MRI mass shape cannot be assessed on postcontrast images.
MRI includes terminology for the internal pattern of enhancement within a mass.
options_after: A mass is a space-occupying lesion that displaces normal breast parenchyma.
The MRI lexicon for mass shape uses the same shape terms as mammography and ultrasound.
In the MRI lexicon, irregular describes mass shape but not mass margin.
MRI mass shape will not be assessed on postcontrast images.
MRI includes terminology for the internal pattern of enhancement within a mass.
updates.explanation: The source defines an MRI mass as a space-occupying lesion that displaces normal parenchyma, and states that MRI mass shape terms match mammography and ultrasound. MRI adds terminology for internal enhancement because dynamic contrast enhancement is part of the technique. Unlike mammography, irregular is used in MRI for both shape and margin. Shape and margin are best evaluated on early postcontrast sequences.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI focus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A focus is a small dot of enhancement less than 5 mm in size.
A focus has definite mass effect on precontrast images.
Margins and internal enhancement cannot be accurately assessed in a focus.
A focus should always be treated as BI-RADS 5.
CAD usually provides reliable enhancement kinetics for a focus.
options_after: A focus is a small dot of enhancement less than 5 mm in size.
A focus has definite mass effect on precontrast images.
Margins and internal enhancement cannot be accurately assessed in a focus.
A focus should characteristically be treated as BI-RADS 5.
CAD usually provides reliable enhancement kinetics for a focus.
updates.explanation: A focus is defined as a dot of enhancement less than 5 mm that lacks mass effect or a precontrast correlate. Because of its small size, margins and internal enhancement are not accurately assessed. Multiple bilateral foci are generally benign, while some authors classify a conspicuous isolated focus as BI-RADS 3. CAD kinetic assessment is generally not possible for a focus.

updates.question_text: Regarding suspicious features in an MRI focus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: If manual measurements suggest washout kinetics, suspicion should be raised.
Multiple bilateral enhancing foci are usually treated as malignant.
A single focus is always indistinguishable from background parenchymal enhancement and should be ignored.
If a focus has suspicious features, it should be described as a mass even when smaller than 5 mm.
A conspicuous isolated focus may be assigned BI-RADS 3 by some authors.
options_after: If manual measurements suggest washout kinetics, suspicion should be raised.
Multiple bilateral enhancing foci are usually treated as malignant.
A single focus is characteristically indistinguishable from background parenchymal enhancement and should be ignored.
If a focus has suspicious features, it should be described as a mass even when smaller than 5 mm.
A conspicuous isolated focus may be assigned BI-RADS 3 by some authors.
updates.explanation: The source notes that kinetic analysis by CAD is generally not possible for a focus, but apparent washout by manual measurement should raise suspicion. A focus with suspicious features should be described as a mass even if it is less than 5 mm. Some authors advocate assigning a conspicuous isolated focus as BI-RADS 3. Multiple bilateral enhancing foci may represent background parenchymal enhancement and are generally considered benign.

updates.question_text: Which statement best defines non-mass enhancement on breast MRI?
options_before: A reniform enhancing mass with a central fatty hilum.
A small dot of enhancement less than 5 mm with no mass effect.
An entirely fat-density circumscribed mass.
An enhancing region that is not a mass or a focus.
A cyst with a solid mural component.
options_after: A reniform enhancing mass with a central fatty hilum.
A small dot of enhancement less than 5 mm without mass effect.
An predominantly fat-density circumscribed mass.
An enhancing region that is not a mass or a focus.
A cyst with a solid mural component.
updates.explanation: Non-mass enhancement is defined as an enhancing region that is not a mass or a focus. A reniform enhancing mass with a fatty hilum describes an intramammary lymph node, while a small enhancing dot describes a focus. Fat-density circumscribed masses and complex cystic and solid masses are separate entities in the mass section.

updates.question_text: Regarding ductal-pattern non-mass enhancement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Focal distribution is the most common distribution of DCIS.
Linear distribution can suggest enhancement associated with a duct.
Regional distribution is defined by a single ductal tree pointing to the nipple.
Diffuse NME is always malignant.
Segmental distribution is the most common distribution of DCIS, present in 42% of cases.
options_after: Focal distribution is the most common distribution of DCIS.
Linear distribution can suggest enhancement associated with a duct.
Regional distribution is defined by a single ductal tree pointing to the nipple.
Diffuse NME is characteristically malignant.
Segmental distribution is the most common distribution of DCIS, present in 42% of cases.
updates.explanation: Linear NME can suggest duct-associated enhancement, and segmental NME is the most common DCIS distribution, present in 42% of DCIS cases. Focal distribution is defined by extent rather than being the commonest DCIS pattern. Regional enhancement involves at least a quadrant and multiple ductal systems. Diffuse NME may represent prominent background parenchymal enhancement, although extensive malignancy is also possible.

updates.question_text: Regarding dynamic contrast-enhanced breast MRI kinetics, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Enhancement curves plot relative enhancement compared with the unenhanced image against time.
The early phase is within the first two minutes.
Early enhancement is characterised as slow, medium or rapid.
The delayed phase is classified only as benign or malignant.
A malignant lesion would be expected to have rapid early enhancement.
options_after: Enhancement curves plot relative enhancement compared with the unenhanced image against time.
The early phase is within the first two minutes.
Early enhancement is characterised as slow, medium or rapid.
The delayed phase is classified primarily as benign or malignant.
A malignant lesion would be expected to have rapid early enhancement.
updates.explanation: Dynamic breast MRI generates curves by plotting percent relative enhancement against time. BI-RADS divides analysis into an early phase within the first two minutes and a delayed phase. Early enhancement is slow, medium or rapid, and malignant lesions are expected to show rapid early enhancement. The delayed phase is classified as persistent, plateau or washout rather than simply benign or malignant.

updates.question_text: Which delayed kinetic curve has the highest positive predictive value for malignancy in the source text?
options_before: Type III washout curve
Type I persistent curve
A curve showing no postcontrast enhancement
A curve generated from a simple cyst
Type II plateau curve
options_after: Type III washout curve
Type I persistent curve
A non-enhancing time-signal curve has the highest positive predictive value for malignancy.
A curve generated from a simple cyst
Type II plateau curve
updates.explanation: The type III washout curve has a reported positive predictive value of 87-92%, higher than the reported 64-77% for type II plateau curves. Type I persistent curves are associated with benign findings in 83% of cases, although malignancy is still possible. Simple cysts and non-enhancing lesions are not described as having the suspicious kinetic pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding limitations of enhancement kinetics, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A type III curve is seen in nearly all malignant lesions.
A type I curve excludes malignancy.
Lymph nodes, adenosis and papillomas may show false-positive washout kinetics.
Morphology is much more important than enhancement pattern when evaluating a lesion.
A spiculated mass with type I kinetics should be downgraded to benign.
options_after: A type III curve is seen in the large majority of malignant lesions.
A type I curve excludes malignancy.
Lymph nodes, adenosis and papillomas may show false-positive washout kinetics.
Morphology is much more important than enhancement pattern when evaluating a lesion.
A spiculated mass with type I kinetics should be downgraded to benign.
