updates.explanation: The source cautions that morphology is much more important than enhancement kinetics. A malignant-looking mass remains suspicious even with type I kinetics. Washout has a high positive predictive value but is seen in only 21% of malignant lesions and may be falsely positive in lymph nodes, adenosis and papillomas. A type I curve does not exclude cancer, as up to 9% of malignant lesions may show it.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI BI-RADS assessment with type II or type III kinetics, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A benign-appearing intramammary lymph node is a notable exception to automatic biopsy despite type III kinetics.
A type II or III kinetic curve with benign morphology is usually BI-RADS 2.
Type II or III kinetics with malignant morphology may be classified as BI-RADS 4 or 5.
Type I kinetics with malignant morphology is generally BI-RADS 4.
Type III kinetics always requires biopsy, regardless of a typical reniform mass adjacent to a vessel.
options_after: A benign-appearing intramammary lymph node is a notable exception to automatic biopsy despite type III kinetics.
A type II or III kinetic curve with benign morphology is usually BI-RADS 2.
Type II or III kinetics with malignant morphology may be classified as BI-RADS 4 or 5.
Type I kinetics with malignant morphology is generally BI-RADS 4.
Type III kinetics characteristically requires biopsy, despite variation in a typical reniform mass adjacent to a vessel.
updates.explanation: A mass or NME with type II or III kinetics and malignant morphology may be BI-RADS 4 or 5, while type I kinetics with malignant morphology is generally BI-RADS 4. The text gives a specific exception: a benign intramammary lymph node adjacent to a vessel with reniform shape can show type III kinetics and should not be biopsied. Benign morphology with type II or III kinetics is otherwise BI-RADS 4 rather than BI-RADS 2.

updates.question_text: Regarding fatty breast masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All entirely fat-density circumscribed masses are benign.
A lipoma is usually diagnosed only after core biopsy.
A lipoma is expected to show peripheral calcification like an oil cyst.
Ultrasound is required whenever a mammographic lipoma is diagnostic.
A lipoma may appear as an oval isoechoic or hyperechoic circumscribed mass on ultrasound.
options_after: All entirely fat-density circumscribed masses are benign.
A lipoma is usually diagnosed primarily after core biopsy.
A lipoma is expected to show peripheral calcification like an oil cyst.
Ultrasound is required whenever a mammographic lipoma is diagnostic.
A lipoma may appear as an oval isoechoic or hyperechoic circumscribed mass on ultrasound.
updates.explanation: The source states that all entirely fat-density circumscribed masses are benign. A lipoma is a benign lesion of mature adipocytes and appears mammographically as a radiolucent mass, sometimes with a thin rim but without peripheral calcification. Ultrasound is unnecessary when mammography is diagnostic, but if used it may show an oval circumscribed isoechoic or hyperechoic mass.

updates.question_text: Which feature most specifically supports an oil cyst rather than a lipoma in the source text?
options_before: Oval circumscribed hyperechoic mass on ultrasound
Entirely fat-density circumscribed mass with no rim
Palpable soft breast lump
Mature adipocyte composition
Radiolucent mass with a fine peripherally calcified rim
options_after: Oval circumscribed hyperechoic mass on ultrasound
Predominantly fat-density circumscribed mass without rim
Palpable soft breast lump
Mature adipocyte composition
Radiolucent mass with a fine peripherally calcified rim
updates.explanation: An oil cyst is a form of fat necrosis and has the distinctive mammographic appearance of a circumscribed lucent lesion that can peripherally calcify. The source contrasts this with lipoma, which does not exhibit peripheral calcification. Mature adipocyte composition and an oval isoechoic or hyperechoic ultrasound appearance describe lipoma rather than the specific oil cyst clue.

updates.question_text: Regarding intramammary lymph nodes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most occur in the lower inner quadrant.
They should never have a fatty hilum on mammography.
On mammography, a characteristic node has a reniform shape with a lucent fatty hilum.
Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic mass with central echogenicity representing the fatty hilum.
Colour Doppler should not demonstrate vessels entering the hilum.
options_after: Most occur in the lower inner quadrant.
They should not have a fatty hilum on mammography.
On mammography, a characteristic node has a reniform shape with a lucent fatty hilum.
Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic mass with central echogenicity representing the fatty hilum.
Colour Doppler should not demonstrate vessels entering the hilum.
updates.explanation: Intramammary lymph nodes are benign normal structures and the vast majority occur in the upper outer quadrant, not the lower inner quadrant. Mammography should show a reniform shape with a lucent fatty hilum, while ultrasound shows a hypoechoic mass with central echogenicity from the fatty hilum. Doppler may demonstrate vessels coursing into the hilum. If the hilum is not visible, a full workup is recommended, especially if the location is atypical.

updates.question_text: Regarding axillary lymph node enlargement in breast imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bilateral enlarged axillary nodes are most likely ipsilateral breast cancer.
Unilateral axillary lymph node enlargement or abnormal morphology should raise concern for ipsilateral breast cancer.
Bilateral enlarged axillary nodes may be due to systemic inflammatory or neoplastic disease.
Axillary nodes are almost never normally present.
Lymphoma is listed as a possible cause of bilateral enlarged axillary nodes.
options_after: Bilateral enlarged axillary nodes are most likely ipsilateral breast cancer.
Unilateral axillary lymph node enlargement or abnormal morphology should raise concern for ipsilateral breast cancer.
Bilateral enlarged axillary nodes may be due to systemic inflammatory or neoplastic disease.
Normal axillary lymph nodes are generally not visible on breast imaging.
Lymphoma is listed as a possible cause of bilateral enlarged axillary nodes.
updates.explanation: The text notes that lymph nodes are almost always present in the axilla, unlike intramammary nodes which are only sometimes seen. Unilateral axillary lymph node enlargement or abnormal morphology should raise concern for ipsilateral breast cancer. Bilateral enlarged axillary nodes are unlikely to be due to breast cancer and may reflect systemic inflammatory or neoplastic disease, including lymphoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding PASH on MRI and follow-up, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI features of PASH are pathognomonic.
Washout kinetics are the defining MRI feature of PASH.
High T2 signal slit-like spaces and cystic components favour PASH.
PASH usually requires mastectomy because recurrence after excision is impossible to monitor.
Persistent type I enhancement is often associated with PASH.
options_after: MRI features of PASH are pathognomonic.
Washout kinetics are the defining MRI feature of PASH.
High T2 signal slit-like spaces and cystic components favour PASH.
PASH usually requires mastectomy because recurrence after excision is not considered a realistic possibility to monitor.
Persistent type I enhancement is often associated with PASH.
updates.explanation: MRI features of PASH are nonspecific, but high T2 signal slit-like spaces and cystic components favour the diagnosis. Persistent type I enhancement is often associated with PASH. The source states that PASH has no malignant potential, although growth and recurrence after excision are not uncommon. Most patients undergo follow-up imaging because clinical management remains controversial.

updates.question_text: Which management statement is directly supported for papilloma in this source?
options_before: All benign papillomas without atypia require mandatory mastectomy.
All papillomas should be ignored after biopsy regardless of atypia.
Surgical excision is recommended for papillomas with atypia or other suspicious features.
Papillomas are treated with antibiotics after galactography.
Papillomas with atypia are managed only with annual mammography.
options_after: Most benign papillomas without atypia require mandatory mastectomy.
Most papillomas should be ignored after biopsy despite variation in atypia.
Surgical excision is recommended for papillomas with atypia or other suspicious features.
Papillomas are treated with antibiotics after galactography.
Papillomas with atypia are managed primarily with annual mammography.
updates.explanation: The source states that follow-up of biopsied benign papilloma without atypia is controversial. For papillomas with atypia or other suspicious features, surgical excision is recommended. It does not support mandatory mastectomy, antibiotics, or ignoring atypical lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding round or oval circumscribed malignant breast masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Breast carcinoma is uncommonly circumscribed.
A new circumscribed mass is reassuring in a post-menopausal woman and requires no workup.
Triple-negative, medullary, mucinous and papillary carcinoma can present as round or oval circumscribed masses.
Circumscribed morphology excludes breast metastasis.
A haematogenous metastasis most commonly presents as a circumscribed round mass.
options_after: Breast carcinoma is uncommonly circumscribed.
A new circumscribed mass is reassuring in a post-menopausal woman and does not require workup.
Triple-negative, medullary, mucinous and papillary carcinoma can present as round or oval circumscribed masses.
Circumscribed morphology excludes breast metastasis.
A haematogenous metastasis most commonly presents as a circumscribed round mass.
updates.explanation: The source cautions that breast carcinoma is uncommon as a circumscribed mass, but a new circumscribed mass should raise suspicion, especially in a post-menopausal woman. Several cancer subtypes can present this way, including triple-negative, medullary, mucinous and papillary carcinoma. Haematogenous metastasis most commonly presents as a circumscribed round mass. Circumscription therefore does not exclude malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding metastasis to the breast, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Multiple metastases are much more common than solitary metastasis.
Melanoma has a propensity to metastasise to the breast.
Renal cell carcinoma never metastasises to the breast.
Breast metastases typically present with popcorn-like calcification.
Renal cell carcinoma has a propensity to metastasise to the breast.
options_after: Multiple metastases are much more common than solitary metastasis.
Melanoma has a propensity to metastasise to the breast.
Renal cell carcinoma will not metastasise to the breast.
Breast metastases typically present with popcorn-like calcification.
Renal cell carcinoma has a propensity to metastasise to the breast.
updates.explanation: The source states that solitary breast metastasis is much more frequent than multiple metastases. Melanoma and renal cell carcinoma have a propensity to metastasise to the breast. Popcorn-like calcification is instead the classic benign appearance of a hyalinising fibroadenoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding lactating adenoma, haematoma and seroma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A lactating adenoma usually requires excision after benign biopsy.
A lactating adenoma is typically seen only after menopause.
Lactating adenomas are seen in the second or third trimester of pregnancy or postpartum period.
A lactating adenoma regresses after the patient is no longer lactating.
Haematoma and seroma should decrease in size over time.
options_after: A lactating adenoma usually requires excision after benign biopsy.
A lactating adenoma is typically seen primarily after menopause.
Lactating adenomas are seen in the second or third trimester of pregnancy or postpartum period.
A lactating adenoma regresses after the patient is no longer lactating.
Haematoma and seroma should decrease in size over time.
updates.explanation: Lactating adenomas occur in the second or third trimester or postpartum period, and they regress once the patient is no longer lactating. After biopsy, they are benign and do not need excision. Haematoma and seroma can be iatrogenic or post-traumatic, appear as round or oval masses, and should decrease in size over time.

updates.question_text: Regarding multiple intraductal papillomas, DCIS and metastases as causes of multiple masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Multiple intraductal papillomas tend to occur in younger patients than solitary papillomas.
Multiple intraductal papillomas are usually central and always unilateral.
DCIS can present as multiple masses, typically in a segmental distribution.
Multiple new masses in a non-ductal distribution favour DCIS rather than haematogenous metastases.
Multiple papillomas are frequently associated with pathologic nipple discharge.
options_after: Multiple intraductal papillomas tend to occur in younger patients than solitary papillomas.
Multiple intraductal papillomas are usually central and characteristically unilateral.
DCIS can present as multiple masses, typically in a segmental distribution.
Multiple new masses in a non-ductal distribution favour DCIS rather than haematogenous metastases.
Multiple papillomas are frequently associated with pathologic nipple discharge.
updates.explanation: Multiple intraductal papillomas occur in younger patients than solitary papillomas and tend to be peripheral and bilateral. They are infrequently associated with pathologic nipple discharge, unlike solitary papillomas. DCIS can present as multiple masses in a segmental distribution. Multiple new masses in a non-ductal distribution are concerning for haematogenous metastases from a non-breast primary.

updates.question_text: Which statement is directly supported for typical invasive ductal carcinoma in this section?
options_before: IDC usually contains no malignant-type calcifications.
IDC is the rarest form of breast cancer.
IDC has a typical mammographic appearance of a high-density spiculated mass.
IDC has only one imaging presentation.
IDC is usually indistinguishable from steatocystoma multiplex.
options_after: IDC usually lacks malignant-type calcifications.
IDC is the rarest form of breast cancer.
IDC has a typical mammographic appearance of a high-density spiculated mass.
IDC has a single imaging presentation.
IDC is usually indistinguishable from steatocystoma multiplex.
updates.explanation: The source describes invasive ductal carcinoma as the most common form of breast cancer and gives a typical mammographic appearance of a high-density spiculated mass. Malignant-type calcifications may be present within the mass. IDC can also have variable appearances, including round mass, isolated calcifications, architectural distortion, or combinations of findings.

updates.question_text: Regarding post-lumpectomy or post-excisional biopsy scar, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A post-surgical scar is always easy to distinguish from cancer without clinical history.
A post-surgical scar should enlarge over time if benign.
Volume loss and skin retraction can help support a post-surgical diagnosis.
Radiation-treated scars never show dystrophic calcification.
Unlike recurrent tumour, a post-surgical scar should not get larger over time.
options_after: A post-surgical scar is characteristically easy to distinguish from cancer without clinical history.
A post-surgical scar should enlarge over time if benign.
Volume loss and skin retraction can help support a post-surgical diagnosis.
Radiation-treated scars will not show dystrophic calcification.
Unlike recurrent tumour, a post-surgical scar should not get larger over time.
updates.explanation: A post-surgical scar can be indistinguishable from cancer on mammography when clinical history is absent. Helpful supporting findings include volume loss in the treated breast and skin retraction. A benign post-surgical scar should not enlarge over time, unlike recurrent tumour. After radiation, dystrophic calcification and skin thickening/retraction may also be present.

updates.question_text: Which axillary mass statement is directly supported by the source?
options_before: The axillary tail of Spence is always malignant when palpable.
Accessory breast tissue cannot occur in the axilla.
The axillary tail of Spence is a normal extension of fibroglandular tissue into the axilla.
Sebaceous cysts occur only in the retroareolar breast.
Epidermal inclusion cysts are excluded from the axillary differential.
options_after: The axillary tail of Spence is characteristically malignant when palpable.
Accessory breast tissue will not occur in the axilla.
The axillary tail of Spence is a normal extension of fibroglandular tissue into the axilla.
Sebaceous cysts occur primarily in the retroareolar breast.
Epidermal inclusion cysts are excluded from the axillary differential.
updates.explanation: The source states that the axillary tail of Spence is normal extension of fibroglandular tissue into the axilla, and accessory breast tissue can also occur there. Both can be mistaken for a mass on physical examination. Benign and malignant breast processes may occur in this tissue, and epidermal inclusion or sebaceous cysts are also common in the axilla and inframammary fold.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast angiosarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It may be primary or secondary to prior breast conservation therapy with radiation.
Radiation-associated angiosarcoma arises only in the pectoralis muscle.
Radiation-associated angiosarcoma can mimic bruising with skin thickening and ecchymosis.
Mammography and ultrasound findings are highly specific for radiation-associated angiosarcoma.
On MRI, angiosarcoma is T2 hyperintense and intensely enhancing.
options_after: It may be primary or secondary to prior breast conservation therapy with radiation.
Radiation-associated angiosarcoma arises primarily in the pectoralis muscle.
Radiation-associated angiosarcoma can mimic bruising with skin thickening and ecchymosis.
Mammography and ultrasound findings are highly specific for radiation-associated angiosarcoma.
On MRI, angiosarcoma is T2 hyperintense and intensely enhancing.
updates.explanation: Angiosarcoma is rare and aggressive, and may be primary or secondary to prior breast conservation therapy with radiation. Radiation-associated angiosarcoma arises in the dermis and subcutis and presents with skin thickening and ecchymosis that can mimic bruising. Mammography and ultrasound are nonspecific, while MRI shows T2 hyperintensity and intense enhancement.

updates.question_text: Regarding fibrocystic change and sclerosing adenosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fibrocystic change is an essentially normal pattern of breast physiology.
Fibrocystic change is diagnosed on imaging alone.
Fibrocystic change is almost always seen in post-menopausal women.
Sclerosing adenosis can mimic DCIS with microcalcifications.
Sclerosing adenosis is caused by infection with Staphylococcus aureus.
options_after: Fibrocystic change is an essentially normal pattern of breast physiology.
Fibrocystic change is diagnosed on imaging alone.
Fibrocystic change is typically seen in post-menopausal women.
Sclerosing adenosis can mimic DCIS with microcalcifications.
Sclerosing adenosis is caused by infection with Staphylococcus aureus.
updates.explanation: Fibrocystic change is described as an essentially normal pattern of breast physiology, usually in pre-menopausal women, and the diagnosis is never made on imaging alone. Its imaging importance is that cysts and calcifications may trigger further workup. Sclerosing adenosis is a benign proliferative lesion that can mimic DCIS with microcalcifications; Staphylococcus aureus is instead discussed with mastitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding mastitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Imaging is routinely required before antibiotic treatment in every patient.
Mastitis is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
It is typically seen in nursing mothers or diabetic patients.
Inflammatory carcinoma is not a relevant differential diagnosis.
If clinical or imaging differentiation from inflammatory carcinoma is not possible, skin punch biopsy can be performed.
options_after: Imaging is routinely required before antibiotic treatment in most patients.
Mastitis is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
It is typically seen in nursing mothers or diabetic patients.
Inflammatory carcinoma is not a relevant differential diagnosis.
If clinical or imaging differentiation from inflammatory carcinoma is not possible, skin punch biopsy can be performed.
updates.explanation: Mastitis is infection of the breast, most commonly by Staphylococcus aureus, and is typically seen in nursing mothers or diabetic patients. It is treated with antibiotics, and imaging is usually not performed unless symptoms persist after treatment. Inflammatory carcinoma is the primary differential, and skin punch biopsy can be performed if the entities cannot be differentiated clinically or on imaging.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast abscess imaging and treatment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Breast abscess is most commonly subareolar.
Treatment is ultrasound-guided aspiration in addition to antibiotics.
Ultrasound should show a purely anechoic simple cyst in all cases.
Mammography can show a mass, asymmetry or architectural distortion with skin thickening.
The periphery of the mass is often avascular.
options_after: Breast abscess is most commonly subareolar.
Treatment is ultrasound-guided aspiration in addition to antibiotics.
Ultrasound should show a purely anechoic simple cyst in more than 90% of cases.
Mammography can show a mass, asymmetry or architectural distortion with skin thickening.
The periphery of the mass is often avascular.
updates.explanation: A breast abscess is a walled-off purulent collection, most commonly subareolar. Mammography may show mass, asymmetry or architectural distortion with overlying skin thickening, and ultrasound often shows an oval or irregular complex cystic and solid mass with indistinct margins and an echogenic halo. The periphery is often hypervascular, not avascular. Treatment is ultrasound-guided aspiration plus antibiotics.

updates.question_text: Which statement about breast abscess clinical presentation is directly supported by the source?
options_before: Breast abscess presents only as painless diffuse breast enlargement.
Breast abscess is always occult on mammography.
Breast abscess presents with focal pain, erythema, fluctuance and fever.
Breast abscess is a sterile fat-containing lesion.
Breast abscess is managed by surveillance alone.
options_after: Breast abscess presents primarily as painless diffuse breast enlargement.
Breast abscess is characteristically occult on mammography.
Breast abscess presents with focal pain, erythema, fluctuance and fever.
Breast abscess is a sterile fat-containing lesion.
Breast abscess is managed by surveillance alone.
updates.explanation: The source describes breast abscess as a walled-off purulent collection that clinically presents with focal breast pain, erythema, fluctuance and fever. The illustrated lactating patient had pain, skin erythema and a palpable lump, with aspiration growing Staphylococcus aureus. Treatment is aspiration plus antibiotics, not surveillance.

updates.question_text: Regarding clinically important mimics in this breast mass section, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radial scar can be confidently dismissed when it shows architectural distortion with central lucency.
Inflammatory carcinoma is the primary differential diagnosis when mastitis cannot be resolved clinically or by imaging.
Post-surgical scar should be considered when volume loss and skin retraction are present in the treated breast.
Mucinous carcinoma is the main mimic of steatocystoma multiplex in this section.
A new circumscribed mass in a post-menopausal woman is reassuring and needs no further assessment.
options_after: Radial scar can be confidently dismissed when it shows architectural distortion with central lucency.
Inflammatory carcinoma is the primary differential diagnosis when mastitis cannot be resolved clinically or by imaging.
Post-surgical scar should be considered when volume loss and skin retraction are present in the treated breast.
Mucinous carcinoma is the main mimic of steatocystoma multiplex in this section.
A new circumscribed mass in a post-menopausal woman is reassuring and can be followed without additional assessment.
updates.explanation: Several benign or inflammatory entities in this section mimic malignancy. Radial scar requires biopsy because even classic central lucency is not diagnostically reliable. Mastitis is primarily differentiated from inflammatory carcinoma, and skin punch biopsy may be used if uncertainty remains. Post-surgical scar is supported by treatment-related features such as volume loss and skin retraction. A new circumscribed mass remains suspicious in a post-menopausal woman and should not be dismissed.

updates.question_text: Regarding periductal mastitis and diabetic mastopathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Periductal mastitis is a disease of young lactating women and never calcifies.
Periductal mastitis produces large rod-like secretory calcifications on mammography.
Diabetic mastopathy is caused by acute Staphylococcus aureus infection.
Diabetic mastopathy can mimic scirrhous breast cancer on ultrasound.
Diabetic mastopathy can be dismissed without biopsy when bilateral.
options_after: Periductal mastitis is a disease of young lactating women and will not calcify.
Periductal mastitis produces large rod-like secretory calcifications on mammography.
Diabetic mastopathy is caused by acute Staphylococcus aureus infection.
Diabetic mastopathy can mimic scirrhous breast cancer on ultrasound.
Diabetic mastopathy can be dismissed without biopsy when bilateral.
updates.explanation: Periductal mastitis, also called plasma cell mastitis, is seen in post-menopausal women and produces large rod-like secretory calcifications. Diabetic mastopathy is related to long-term insulin-dependent diabetes and can show hypoechoic masses or regional shadowing that mimics scirrhous carcinoma. Because it can mimic cancer on mammography and ultrasound, core biopsy is required.

updates.question_text: Regarding breast implants and implant imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Implants may be used for cosmetic reasons or reconstruction after mastectomy.
Silicone implants contain a valve that permits filling during surgery.
A fibrous capsule gradually forms as a reaction to the foreign body.
All implants must be placed retropectoral.
Silicone implants are identified on mammography by a saline valve.
options_after: Implants may be used for cosmetic reasons or reconstruction after mastectomy.
Silicone implants contain a valve that permits filling during surgery.
A fibrous capsule gradually forms as a reaction to the foreign body.
Most implants must be placed retropectoral.
Silicone implants are identified on mammography by a saline valve.
updates.explanation: The source states that implants are used cosmetically or for reconstruction and may be filled with silicone or saline. A fibrous capsule forms as a foreign-body reaction and may calcify. The filling valve is a feature of saline implants, whereas silicone implants are uniformly dense and have no valve. Implant location may be retropectoral or prepectoral/retroglandular rather than universally retropectoral.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI and ultrasound evaluation of implants, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Specific MRI protocols can include silicone-only and silicone-suppression sequences.
MRI is less sensitive than mammography for silicone implant rupture.
Ultrasound probes optimised for breast tissue always penetrate sufficiently to evaluate posterior implants.
A single fixed ultrasound probe is advantageous because implant evaluation never requires altered penetration.
MRI has higher sensitivity and specificity than mammogram and ultrasound for silicone implant rupture.
options_after: Specific MRI protocols can include silicone-only and silicone-suppression sequences.
MRI is less sensitive than mammography for silicone implant rupture.
Ultrasound probes optimised for breast tissue characteristically penetrate sufficiently to evaluate posterior implants.
A single fixed ultrasound probe is advantageous because implant evaluation will not require altered penetration.
MRI has higher sensitivity and specificity than mammogram and ultrasound for silicone implant rupture.
updates.explanation: MRI implant protocols include silicone-only and silicone-suppression sequences. MRI has higher sensitivity and specificity for silicone implant rupture than mammography or ultrasound. The source notes that probes optimised for breast tissue may not penetrate enough for posterior implants, so multiple probe choices can be advantageous. It does not support a single fixed probe or mammography as more sensitive than MRI for silicone rupture.

updates.question_text: Regarding implant rupture categories, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Intracapsular rupture is contained within the fibrous capsule.
Extracapsular rupture extends outside the fibrous capsule.
The distinction between intra- and extracapsular rupture is only important for saline implants.
Saline implant contents remain contained if the fibrous capsule is intact.
Partial herniation through the capsule is itself diagnostic of implant rupture.
options_after: Intracapsular rupture is contained within the fibrous capsule.
Extracapsular rupture extends outside the fibrous capsule.
The distinction between intra- and extracapsular rupture is primarily important for saline implants.
Saline implant contents remain contained if the fibrous capsule is intact.
Partial herniation through the capsule is itself diagnostic of implant rupture.
updates.explanation: Implant rupture can be intracapsular, contained within the fibrous capsule, or extracapsular, extending out of it. The distinction is important for silicone implants. With saline implants, the contents leak out even if the capsule is intact. Separately, an implant may partially herniate through the capsule without rupture, producing a palpable contour deformity.

updates.question_text: Which ultrasound appearance is classic for extracapsular silicone implant rupture?
options_before: A fan-shaped retroareolar hypoechoic region.
A stepladder pattern of collapsed shell within intracapsular silicone.
A fat-fluid level in a circumscribed mass.
An echogenic shadowing mass with snowstorm appearance.
A bead-like tubular structure with no Doppler flow.
options_after: A fan-shaped retroareolar hypoechoic region.
A stepladder pattern of collapsed shell within intracapsular silicone.
A fat-fluid level in a circumscribed mass.
An echogenic shadowing mass with snowstorm appearance.
A bead-like tubular structure without Doppler flow.
updates.explanation: Extracapsular silicone rupture releases free silicone into breast parenchyma, producing the classic snowstorm appearance on ultrasound. The stepladder pattern is used for intracapsular rupture. A fan-shaped retroareolar region describes gynecomastia, a fat-fluid level suggests galactocele, and a bead-like avascular tubular structure describes Mondor disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding extracapsular rupture and silicone migration, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Silicone uptake by regional nodes is commonest with intact implants and never occurs after rupture.
Implant-displaced views cannot show the extent of intraparenchymal silicone granulomas.
Silicone uptake by regional nodes cannot occur after free silicone injection.
Silicone uptake by regional nodes can occur with extracapsular rupture.
Mammography may show high-density silicone extending beyond the capsule into breast parenchyma.
options_after: Silicone uptake by regional nodes is commonest with intact implants and will not occur after rupture.
Implant-displaced views will not show the extent of intraparenchymal silicone granulomas.
Silicone uptake by regional nodes will not occur after free silicone injection.
Silicone uptake by regional nodes can occur with extracapsular rupture.
Mammography may show high-density silicone extending beyond the capsule into breast parenchyma.
updates.explanation: Extracapsular silicone rupture can be visible mammographically as high-density silicone outside the capsule in the breast parenchyma. Implant-displaced views may better show intraparenchymal silicone granulomas, so saying they cannot show the extent is incorrect. Silicone uptake by regional nodes can occur with free silicone injection, extracapsular rupture, and less commonly with intracapsular rupture or gel bleed through an intact weakened shell. It is not described as commonest with intact implants.

updates.question_text: Regarding saline implant rupture and reduction mammoplasty, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Saline implant rupture is usually evident clinically.
Saline rupture causes sudden collapse and instantaneous decrease in breast size.
Reduction mammoplasty removes inferior breast parenchyma and skin and relocates the nipple superiorly.
Reduction mammoplasty produces no mammographic architectural distortion.
Fat necrosis, suture and dermal calcifications may be present after reduction mammoplasty.
options_after: Saline implant rupture is usually evident clinically.
Saline rupture causes sudden collapse and instantaneous decrease in breast size.
Reduction mammoplasty removes inferior breast parenchyma and skin and relocates the nipple superiorly.
Reduction mammoplasty fails to produce mammographic architectural distortion.
Fat necrosis, suture and dermal calcifications may be present after reduction mammoplasty.
updates.explanation: Saline rupture is usually clinically evident because it causes sudden collapse and rapid decrease in breast size as saline is absorbed. Reduction mammoplasty removes inferior breast parenchyma and skin and relocates the nipple superiorly. Mammographic findings include nipple elevation, redistribution of tissue, lower-breast curvilinear architectural distortion, post-surgical skin thickening, and possible fat necrosis, suture or dermal calcifications.

updates.question_text: Regarding gynecomastia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gynecomastia is benign development of glandular tissue in a male.
It is the most common diagnosis in males evaluated for a focal breast complaint.
The typical mammographic appearance is an eccentric high-density irregular mass with nipple retraction.
Ultrasound often shows a central disc- or fan-shaped hypoechoic or heterogeneous region behind the nipple.
It is never associated with drugs or endocrine dysfunction.
options_after: Gynecomastia is benign development of glandular tissue in a male.
It is the most common diagnosis in males evaluated for a focal breast complaint.
The typical mammographic appearance is an eccentric high-density irregular mass with nipple retraction.
Ultrasound often shows a central disc- or fan-shaped hypoechoic or heterogeneous region behind the nipple.
It is not associated with drugs or endocrine dysfunction.
updates.explanation: Gynecomastia is benign male glandular breast development and is the most common diagnosis in males evaluated for a focal breast complaint. Mammography usually shows a flame-shaped or triangular subareolar density with interspersed fat, and ultrasound may show a central disc- or fan-shaped hypoechoic or heterogeneous region. Eccentric irregular mass and nipple retraction are more concerning for male breast cancer. Causes include cirrhosis, drugs, marijuana, pituitary dysfunction and hormone-producing tumours.

updates.question_text: Regarding age-based initial imaging of pathologic nipple discharge, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Women under 30 should initially undergo ultrasound.
Women aged 30 or older and all men should initially undergo mammography and ultrasound.
Ultrasound alone can be considered in women aged 30-39.
MRI replaces mammography and ultrasound as the first test after age 30.
Men with pathologic discharge are initially evaluated with ultrasound only.
options_after: Women under 30 should initially undergo ultrasound.
Women aged 30 or older and all men should initially undergo mammography and ultrasound.
Ultrasound alone can be considered in women aged 30-39.
MRI replaces mammography and ultrasound as the first test after age 30.
Men with pathologic discharge are initially evaluated with ultrasound in typical cases.
updates.explanation: For women under 30, ultrasound is the initial imaging test for pathologic discharge. For women aged 30 or older and all men, initial evaluation should be mammography and ultrasound, although ultrasound alone can be considered in women aged 30-39. MRI is reserved for further assessment when mammography and ultrasound are negative, not for the initial evaluation.

updates.question_text: Regarding palpable breast mass evaluation in younger women and men, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In women under 30 with suspicious ultrasound findings, mammography should be considered and biopsy performed.
In women under 30 with negative ultrasound, mammography should always be added even for a minimal clinical finding.
Clearly benign or probably benign ultrasound findings in young women do not require mammographic assessment.
Men under 25 with an indeterminate mass not classic for gynecomastia should initially undergo ultrasound.
Men aged 25 or older are never evaluated with mammography.
options_after: In women under 30 with suspicious ultrasound findings, mammography should be considered and biopsy performed.
In women under 30 with negative ultrasound, mammography should characteristically be added even for a minimal clinical finding.
Clearly benign or probably benign ultrasound findings in young women do not require mammographic assessment.
Men under 25 with an indeterminate mass not classic for gynecomastia should initially undergo ultrasound.
Men aged 25 or older are not evaluated with mammography.
updates.explanation: In women under 30, suspicious ultrasound findings should prompt biopsy and consideration of mammography. If ultrasound is negative, mammography is added only if the clinical finding is striking; otherwise clinical follow-up is appropriate. Clearly benign or probably benign ultrasound findings in young women do not require mammography. Men under 25 with an indeterminate mass not classic for gynecomastia start with ultrasound, while men 25 or older can undergo mammography and ultrasound as initial options.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiology-pathology correlation after breast biopsy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radiology-pathology correlation is only needed after surgical excision.
Every biopsy requires correlation to ensure pathology is concordant with imaging.
Discordant findings typically require further workup such as repeat core or excisional biopsy.
Benign fibroadenoma fragments from a highly suspicious spiculated mass are an example of concordance.
Discordant findings should be ignored if the pathology is benign.
options_after: Radiology-pathology correlation is primarily needed after surgical excision.
Every biopsy requires correlation to ensure pathology is concordant with imaging.
Discordant findings typically require further workup such as repeat core or excisional biopsy.
Benign fibroadenoma fragments from a highly suspicious spiculated mass are an example of concordance.
Discordant findings should be ignored if the pathology is benign.
updates.explanation: The radiologist must perform radiology-pathology correlation for every biopsy case. Discordant results require further workup, typically repeat core or excisional biopsy. Benign pathology such as fibroadenoma fragments from a highly suspicious spiculated mass is the source's example of discordance, not concordance.

updates.question_text: Which statement about ultrasound-guided breast biopsy technique is directly supported by the source?
options_before: Posterior lesions require a shorter distance between entry site and lesion to keep the needle vertical.
Needle position within the target should be documented in an orthogonal plane for at least 1-2 passes.
Local anaesthetic should never be administered under ultrasound guidance.
Far posterior lesions cannot be sampled with ultrasound guidance.
A steep perpendicular approach is preferred for every lesion.
options_after: Posterior lesions require a shorter distance between entry site and lesion to keep the needle vertical.
Needle position within the target should be documented in an orthogonal plane for at least 1-2 passes.
Local anaesthetic should not be administered under ultrasound guidance.
Far posterior lesions will not be sampled with ultrasound guidance.
A steep perpendicular approach is preferred for most lesions.
updates.explanation: The source states that each needle pass should be documented and needle position within the target demonstrated in an orthogonal plane for at least 1-2 passes. Posterior lesions require a larger entry-site-to-lesion distance to maintain a nearly parallel course. Cutaneous and subcutaneous anaesthesia are given under ultrasound guidance, and far posterior lesions can be lifted anteriorly off the chest wall before sampling.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound-guided cyst aspiration and stereotactic biopsy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cyst aspiration uses a standard syringe attached to a 20- or 18-gauge needle.
Bloody aspirate can be discarded if the cyst collapses completely.
Benign-appearing green, grey, yellow or cloudy fluid must always be sent for cytology.
A complex cystic and solid mass should be aspirated only and never biopsied.
Stereotactic guidance is most commonly used to biopsy calcifications.
options_after: Cyst aspiration uses a standard syringe attached to a 20- or 18-gauge needle.
Bloody aspirate can be discarded if the cyst collapses completely.
Benign-appearing green, grey, yellow or cloudy fluid must characteristically be sent for cytology.
A complex cystic and solid mass should be managed with aspiration rather than core biopsy.
Stereotactic guidance is most commonly used to biopsy calcifications.
updates.explanation: Cyst aspiration uses a syringe on a 20- or 18-gauge needle. Bloody or clear aspirate is sent for cytology, while benign-appearing green, grey, yellow or cloudy fluid can be discarded. Only benign-appearing cysts should be aspirated; complex cystic and solid masses require core biopsy targeting the solid component. Stereotactic guidance is most commonly used for calcification biopsy.

updates.question_text: Which statement about MRI-guided biopsy is directly supported by the source?
options_before: MRI-guided biopsy is mainly used for lesions visible on mammography but not MRI.
Second-look ultrasound is avoided because it never finds an MRI correlate.
MRI-guided biopsy almost always requires intravenous gadolinium.
MRI-guided biopsy is performed with the patient supine and the needle parallel to the breast.
Delayed parenchymal enhancement makes targeting easier over time.
options_after: MRI-guided biopsy is mainly used for lesions visible on mammography but not MRI.
Second-look ultrasound is avoided because it will not find an MRI correlate.
MRI-guided biopsy almost always requires intravenous gadolinium.
MRI-guided biopsy is performed with the patient supine and the needle parallel to the breast.
Delayed parenchymal enhancement makes targeting easier over time.
updates.explanation: MRI-guided biopsy is performed for lesions seen only on MRI and almost always requires intravenous gadolinium. A second-look ultrasound is commonly performed first because a correlate is found in 56-57% of cases, particularly for masses and larger lesions. The patient lies prone, and targeting must be rapid before washout or delayed parenchymal enhancement obscures the lesion.

updates.question_text: Regarding clinical applications and high-risk findings on myocardial perfusion imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A negative myocardial perfusion examination can allow safe discharge in selected patients with ambiguous chest pain and negative ECG/troponins
A normal myocardial perfusion examination carries a high annual cardiac-event rate even when pre-test CAD likelihood is high
Large severe defects, multivessel-territory defects, significant lung uptake and low gated EF are high-risk findings after myocardial infarction
Myocardial perfusion imaging has no role in preoperative assessment before intermediate-to-high-risk non-cardiac surgery
Myocardial perfusion imaging cannot be used to assess revascularisation status after CABG
options_after: A negative myocardial perfusion examination can allow safe discharge in selected patients with ambiguous chest pain and negative ECG/troponins
A normal myocardial perfusion examination carries a high annual cardiac-event rate even when pre-test CAD likelihood is high
Large severe defects, multivessel-territory defects, significant lung uptake and low gated EF are high-risk findings after myocardial infarction
Myocardial perfusion imaging has negligible role in preoperative assessment before intermediate-to-high-risk non-cardiac surgery
Myocardial perfusion imaging will not be used to assess revascularisation status after CABG
updates.explanation: The source states that myocardial perfusion imaging can be a gatekeeper in selected ambiguous acute chest pain presentations, and a negative study may allow safe discharge. A normal myocardial perfusion examination is associated with a low annual cardiac-event rate. High-risk post-MI findings include large severe defects, stress-induced or peri-infarct ischaemia, defects in multiple vascular territories, significant lung uptake, LV aneurysm and low gated EF. The text also lists preoperative risk assessment and post-CABG assessment as clinical applications.

updates.question_text: Regarding exercise stress myocardial perfusion testing, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A diagnostic exercise study requires achieving the target heart rate calculated from maximal predicted heart rate
Beta-blockers should always be continued in patients without known CAD because they help the patient reach target heart rate
Calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers should be administered immediately before exercise to help the patient reach target heart rate
Acute myocardial infarction within 48 hours, high-risk unstable angina, acute aortic dissection and severe symptomatic aortic stenosis are listed contraindications
Left bundle branch block is an indication to prefer exercise stress because it removes false-positive septal defects
options_after: A diagnostic exercise study requires achieving the target heart rate calculated from maximal predicted heart rate
Beta-blockers should characteristically be continued in patients without known CAD because they help the patient reach target heart rate
Calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers should be administered immediately before exercise to help the patient reach target heart rate
Acute myocardial infarction within 48 hours, high-risk unstable angina, acute aortic dissection and severe symptomatic aortic stenosis are listed contraindications
Left bundle branch block is an indication to prefer exercise stress because it removes false-positive septal defects
updates.explanation: Exercise stress requires adequate physiologic stress, including reaching the target heart rate. The source notes that calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers may be held in patients without known CAD so the target heart rate can be achieved; giving them immediately beforehand would work against this goal. Several acute cardiovascular conditions are contraindications to exercise stress. Left bundle branch block can cause false-positive reversible septal defects with exercise, so pharmacologic stress is an alternative.

updates.question_text: Regarding Tc-99m sestamibi/tetrofosmin SPECT protocols, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Because sestamibi redistributes rapidly, imaging must always begin immediately after injection
In a single-day rest-stress study, rest images are obtained first and stress images after background activity clears
Gated SPECT wall motion always reflects wall motion at the exact time of peak stress injection
A two-day protocol is often used in obese patients to optimise image quality and reduce residual-activity interference
A normal stress-first study always requires a rest study for confirmation
options_after: Because sestamibi redistributes rapidly, imaging must characteristically begin immediately after injection
In a single-day rest-stress study, rest images are obtained first and stress images after background activity clears
Gated SPECT wall motion characteristically reflects wall motion at the exact time of peak stress injection
A two-day protocol is often used in obese patients to optimise image quality and reduce residual-activity interference
A normal stress-first study characteristically requires a rest study for confirmation
updates.explanation: Sestamibi and tetrofosmin do not redistribute, so imaging can be delayed after tracer administration. A common single-day protocol acquires rest images first, then stress images after background activity clears. Two-day protocols improve image quality and reduce residual-activity interference, especially in obese patients. Gated SPECT wall motion reflects the time of imaging, whereas perfusion reflects the time of injection; a normal stress-first study may allow omission of the rest study.

updates.question_text: Regarding thallium redistribution and PET viability imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Thallium rest-redistribution can be used to assess myocardial viability before revascularisation
Thallium is currently preferred over FDG PET for myocardial viability because it never underestimates viable myocardium
FDG uptake is seen only in non-viable scar tissue
Delayed thallium uptake due to redistribution indicates viable myocardium
FDG PET requires preparation that shifts myocardium toward glucose metabolism
options_after: Thallium rest-redistribution can be used to assess myocardial viability before revascularisation
Thallium is currently preferred over FDG PET for myocardial viability because it will not underestimate viable myocardium
FDG uptake is seen primarily in non-viable scar tissue
Delayed thallium uptake due to redistribution indicates viable myocardium
FDG PET requires preparation that shifts myocardium toward glucose metabolism
updates.explanation: Rest-redistribution thallium imaging is a viability technique, and delayed thallium uptake indicates viable myocardium. The source states that FDG PET is preferred over thallium for myocardial viability and that thallium can underestimate viability. FDG PET requires metabolic preparation to encourage myocardial glucose utilisation. Viable myocardium takes up FDG; scar does not.

updates.question_text: Which pattern best indicates hibernating myocardium on combined perfusion and FDG PET imaging?
options_before: Normal perfusion with normal FDG uptake and reduced contractility
Matched reduction of perfusion and FDG uptake
Reduced perfusion with preserved or increased FDG uptake
A reversible stress defect with no resting abnormality
Fixed perfusion defect with no metabolic activity
options_after: Normal perfusion with normal FDG uptake and reduced contractility
Matched reduction of perfusion and FDG uptake
Reduced perfusion with preserved or increased FDG uptake
A reversible stress defect without resting abnormality
Fixed perfusion defect without metabolic activity
updates.explanation: Hibernating myocardium is viable but chronically hypoperfused, so the key pattern is a perfusion/metabolic mismatch: reduced perfusion with preserved or increased FDG uptake. A matched reduction in perfusion and FDG uptake indicates non-viable scar. Normal perfusion with impaired contractility fits stunned myocardium. A reversible stress defect represents inducible ischaemia rather than chronic hibernation.

updates.question_text: Regarding SPECT/CT and perfusion study quality control, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Attenuation-correction CT reduces diagnostic accuracy by creating unavoidable artefacts
Attenuation-corrected and uncorrected images should be compared to look for artefacts
A single-day rest-stress study should usually have higher signal-to-noise stress images because more stress tracer is administered
The raw rotating SPECT data and sinogram have no role in identifying motion artefact
Misregistration between SPECT and CT images can be ignored if attenuation-corrected images look diagnostic
options_after: Attenuation-correction CT reduces diagnostic accuracy by creating unavoidable artefacts
Attenuation-corrected and uncorrected images should be compared to look for artefacts
A single-day rest-stress study should usually have higher signal-to-noise stress images because more stress tracer is administered
The raw rotating SPECT data and sinogram have negligible role in identifying motion artefact
Misregistration between SPECT and CT images can be ignored if attenuation-corrected images look diagnostic
updates.explanation: The source emphasises systematic quality control before interpretation. Stress images in a single-day rest-stress protocol should usually have better signal-to-noise because more tracer is administered; if not, dose infiltration should be considered. Attenuation-corrected and uncorrected images should be compared specifically because misregistration and attenuation correction can create artefacts. Raw rotating projections and sinograms can reveal motion artefact, as illustrated by horizontal breaks in the sinogram.

updates.question_text: Regarding characterisation of myocardial perfusion defects, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A reversible defect signifies ischaemia
A fixed defect can be confidently labelled scar without any functional or metabolic information
Transient ischaemic dilatation implies left main or three-vessel disease and a worse prognosis only when there is a focal defect
Exercise-induced reversible septal defects in left bundle branch block follow a coronary artery territory and prove CAD
Right ventricular uptake implies right heart disease or pulmonary hypertension
options_after: A reversible defect signifies ischaemia
A fixed defect can be confidently labelled scar without any functional or metabolic information
Transient ischaemic dilatation implies left main or three-vessel disease and a worse prognosis primarily when there is a focal defect
Exercise-induced reversible septal defects in left bundle branch block follow a coronary artery territory and prove CAD
Right ventricular uptake implies right heart disease or pulmonary hypertension
updates.explanation: A reversible stress defect signifies ischaemia. A fixed defect may represent infarct/scar or hibernating myocardium, and functional or metabolic information is needed to separate possibilities. Transient ischaemic dilatation implies left main or three-vessel disease and poor prognosis even when there is no focal defect. Reversible septal defects from exercise in left bundle branch block are false-positive and do not follow a coronary artery territory. Right ventricular uptake suggests right heart disease or pulmonary hypertension.

updates.question_text: Regarding myocardial reconstruction axes and vascular territories, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Short-axis images are the traditional donut views from apex to base
The polar plot represents only the right ventricle
VLA and HLA are long-axis U-shaped views
Perfusion defect size is assessed using 12 standard LV segments in this source
The 17-segment model is evaluated on short-axis views, although coronary supply varies between patients
options_after: Short-axis images are the traditional donut views from apex to base
The polar plot represents primarily the right ventricle
VLA and HLA are long-axis U-shaped views
Perfusion defect size is assessed using 12 standard LV segments in this source
The 17-segment model is evaluated on short-axis views, although coronary supply varies between patients
updates.explanation: The source describes short-axis images as the donut views from apex through base, with VLA and HLA as long-axis U-shaped views. The polar plot unfolds the three-dimensional left ventricle onto a two-dimensional map. Defect size is assessed using 17 standard left ventricular segments on short-axis views, while recognising that vascular supply varies between patients. This supports precise reporting of defect size and coronary territory.

updates.question_text: Regarding potential pitfalls in E-RNA/MUGA LVEF calculation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Including part of an enlarged left atrium in the background region of interest can falsely elevate the calculated LVEF
Including extracardiac activity such as spleen in the background region can falsely elevate the calculated LVEF
E-RNA cannot provide visual evaluation of cardiac size, shape or wall motion
In vitro RBC labelling is preferred
MUGA is synonymous with pulmonary perfusion scanning
options_after: Including part of an enlarged left atrium in the background region of interest can falsely elevate the calculated LVEF
Including extracardiac activity such as spleen in the background region can falsely elevate the calculated LVEF
E-RNA will not provide visual evaluation of cardiac size, shape or wall motion
In vitro RBC labelling is preferred
MUGA is synonymous with pulmonary perfusion scanning
updates.explanation: The source warns that the selected background region can falsely elevate LVEF if it includes part of an enlarged left atrium or extracardiac activity such as the spleen. In vitro RBC labelling is preferred for E-RNA. E-RNA can provide visual and functional assessment of cardiac performance. MUGA is gated blood pool ventriculography, not a pulmonary perfusion scan.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET interpretation in cardiac sarcoidosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cardiac sarcoidosis typically presents as focal or patchy myocardial FDG uptake
Diffuse myocardial uptake may reflect incompletely suppressed physiologic uptake
Lateral LV wall uptake is always diagnostic of active sarcoid inflammation
A perfusion defect matching focal FDG uptake can suggest fibrosis/scarring from advanced sarcoidosis when obstructive CAD has been excluded
Perfusion imaging is abnormal in all early-stage cardiac sarcoidosis
options_after: Cardiac sarcoidosis typically presents as focal or patchy myocardial FDG uptake
Diffuse myocardial uptake may reflect incompletely suppressed physiologic uptake
Lateral LV wall uptake is characteristically diagnostic of active sarcoid inflammation
A perfusion defect matching focal FDG uptake can suggest fibrosis/scarring from advanced sarcoidosis when obstructive CAD has been excluded
Perfusion imaging is abnormal in most early-stage cardiac sarcoidosis
updates.explanation: Cardiac sarcoidosis typically appears as focal or patchy myocardial FDG uptake. Diffuse myocardial uptake is a pitfall from incomplete physiologic suppression, and isolated lateral LV wall uptake can be a normal variant. The source notes that combined perfusion and FDG imaging can identify sarcoid-induced tissue damage: a perfusion defect corresponding to focal FDG uptake suggests advanced sarcoid fibrosis or scarring, provided obstructive CAD has been excluded. Perfusion imaging may be normal in early disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding distinguishing cardiac sarcoid inflammation from coronary disease on FDG/perfusion imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A perfusion defect with focal FDG uptake may also represent hibernating myocardium and CAD
Coronary artery disease should be excluded before interpreting this mismatch as focal myocardial inflammation
Stress perfusion imaging, CT angiography or invasive angiography can help exclude obstructive CAD
Myocardial FDG uptake outside the coronary territories is impossible in sarcoidosis
The source describes FDG PET as useful for monitoring treatment response
options_after: A perfusion defect with focal FDG uptake may also represent hibernating myocardium and CAD
Coronary artery disease should be excluded before interpreting this mismatch as focal myocardial inflammation
Stress perfusion imaging, CT angiography or invasive angiography can help exclude obstructive CAD
Myocardial FDG uptake outside the coronary territories is not considered a realistic possibility in sarcoidosis
The source describes FDG PET as useful for monitoring treatment response
updates.explanation: The source explicitly warns that a perfusion defect with focal FDG uptake may represent hibernating myocardium from CAD rather than inflammation. Obstructive CAD should be excluded by CT, invasive angiography or stress perfusion imaging before interpreting the pattern as focal myocardial inflammation. FDG PET is also described as a method for diagnosis and monitoring treatment response in cardiac sarcoidosis. Sarcoidosis can produce patchy uptake patterns rather than being constrained to coronary distributions.

updates.question_text: Regarding the clinical context for cardiac amyloidosis imaging in this source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis is recognised as a common cause of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in elderly patients
Cardiac amyloid involvement is a benign incidental finding with no prognostic implication
Cardiac amyloidosis may lead to angina, arrhythmias, restrictive cardiomyopathy and heart failure
Amyloid-specific PET agents such as F-18 florbetapir and C-11 PiB are currently undergoing investigation
The source says amyloid deposits are confined to the myocardium and cannot affect other organs
options_after: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis is recognised as a common cause of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in elderly patients
Cardiac amyloid involvement is a benign incidental finding without prognostic implication
Cardiac amyloidosis may lead to angina, arrhythmias, restrictive cardiomyopathy and heart failure
Amyloid-specific PET agents such as F-18 florbetapir and C-11 PiB are currently undergoing investigation
The source says amyloid deposits are confined to the myocardium and will not affect other organs
updates.explanation: Amyloidosis is systemic and cardiac involvement has poor prognosis. Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis is recognised as a common cause of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in elderly patients. Cardiac involvement may cause angina, arrhythmias, restrictive cardiomyopathy and heart failure. The source also notes investigational amyloid-specific PET agents, including F-18 florbetapir and C-11 PiB.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET/CT and leukocyte scintigraphy for endocarditis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: FDG PET/CT is less reliable for native valve endocarditis than for prosthetic valve endocarditis
The typical appearance is diffuse uniform physiologic myocardial uptake without focal valvular uptake
FDG PET can be combined with CT angiography to increase sensitivity
Radiolabelled leukocyte scintigraphy with SPECT/CT is more specific than FDG PET/CT but has limited sensitivity
FDG PET/CT cannot assess systemic complications of prosthetic valve endocarditis
options_after: FDG PET/CT is less reliable for native valve endocarditis than for prosthetic valve endocarditis
The typical appearance is diffuse uniform physiologic myocardial uptake without focal valvular uptake
FDG PET can be combined with CT angiography to increase sensitivity
Radiolabelled leukocyte scintigraphy with SPECT/CT is more specific than FDG PET/CT but has limited sensitivity
FDG PET/CT will not assess systemic complications of prosthetic valve endocarditis
updates.explanation: FDG PET/CT can accurately diagnose prosthetic valve endocarditis and its systemic complications, but it is less reliable for native valve endocarditis. The typical appearance on FDG PET or leukocyte scintigraphy is focal valvular uptake, as in the illustrated prosthetic aortic valve case. Combining FDG PET with CT angiography can increase sensitivity. Leukocyte scintigraphy with SPECT/CT is more specific but has limited sensitivity because of weak signal and lower resolution.

updates.question_text: Which CCTA acquisition strategy provides cine reconstructions for cardiac and valvular functional assessment according to the source?
options_before: Prospective ECG triggering at a single selected phase
Non-gated calcium scoring only
Retrospective ECG gating
Delayed venous-phase chest CT
Static noncontrast axial reconstruction
options_after: Prospective ECG triggering at a single selected phase
Non-gated calcium scoring in typical cases
Retrospective ECG gating
Delayed venous-phase chest CT
Static noncontrast axial reconstruction
updates.explanation: The source states that retrospective ECG gating allows cine reconstructions to evaluate cardiac and valvular function, typically with multiple frames per cardiac cycle. The trade-off is a significantly increased radiation dose compared with a prospectively gated study. Prospective gating has lower dose but does not provide cine reconstructions because only a selected phase is acquired.

updates.question_text: Regarding temporal resolution and heart-rate control for CCTA, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Dual-source CT can improve temporal resolution because only a 90-degree rotation is needed for reconstruction
Single-source CT temporal resolution is calculated as four times the gantry rotation time
Oral beta-blocker gives better heart-rate control and less heart-rate variability than intravenous beta-blocker in the source
Dual-source CT makes nitroglycerin unnecessary because vessel dilatation is no longer useful
With dual-source CT, scanning without heart-rate control may be possible even in arrhythmia
options_after: Dual-source CT can improve temporal resolution because only a 90-degree rotation is needed for reconstruction
Single-source CT temporal resolution is calculated as four times the gantry rotation time
Oral beta-blocker gives better heart-rate control and less heart-rate variability than intravenous beta-blocker in the source
Dual-source CT makes nitroglycerin unnecessary because vessel dilatation is not currently useful
With dual-source CT, scanning without heart-rate control may be possible even in arrhythmia
updates.explanation: Dual-source CT improves temporal resolution by using two X-ray sources 90 degrees apart, requiring only a 90-degree rotation for reconstruction. The source states that scanning without heart-rate control may be possible with dual-source CT even in patients with arrhythmias. Single-source CT temporal resolution is approximately half the gantry rotation time, not four times it. Oral beta-blockers are described as giving better heart-rate control and less variability than IV beta-blocker.

updates.question_text: Regarding coronary artery origins and normal anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The RCA arises from the right coronary sinus, which is located anteriorly
The left main coronary artery arises from the noncoronary sinus
The noncoronary sinus is located right-posterior and straddles the interatrial septum
The left main coronary artery courses between the pulmonary artery and the left atrial appendage before bifurcating into LAD and LCx
A ramus branch, when present, means the left main coronary artery cannot trifurcate
options_after: The RCA arises from the right coronary sinus, which is located anteriorly
The left main coronary artery arises from the noncoronary sinus
The noncoronary sinus is located right-posterior and straddles the interatrial septum
The left main coronary artery courses between the pulmonary artery and the left atrial appendage before bifurcating into LAD and LCx
A ramus branch, when present, means the left main coronary artery will not trifurcate
updates.explanation: The source describes the right coronary sinus as anterior and giving rise to the RCA. The left main coronary artery arises from the left coronary sinus, courses between the pulmonary artery and left atrial appendage, and bifurcates into LAD and LCx; a ramus may be present to form a trifurcation. The noncoronary sinus is right-posterior and straddles the interatrial septum. These relationships are central to CCTA anatomy interpretation.

updates.question_text: Regarding malignant coronary artery anomalies, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Either anomalous left or right coronary artery can take a malignant interarterial course
Exercise-related aortic dilatation may compress the anomalous interarterial vessel
An anomalous interarterial course has no association with sudden death
Treatment of malignant interarterial course is medical reassurance only
Anomalous intramural coronary artery can be treated by bypass, reimplantation or unroofing
options_after: Either anomalous left or right coronary artery can take a malignant interarterial course
Exercise-related aortic dilatation may compress the anomalous interarterial vessel
An anomalous interarterial course lacks association with sudden death
Treatment of malignant interarterial course is medical reassurance in typical cases
Anomalous intramural coronary artery can be treated by bypass, reimplantation or unroofing
updates.explanation: The source states that anomalous left or right coronary arteries can take a malignant interarterial course. Risk is linked to exercise-related aortic dilatation compressing the anomalous vessel, potentially causing myocardial infarction and sudden death. Treatment of interarterial malignant course is surgical bypass grafting. Intramural coronary artery can be treated with bypass, reimplantation or unroofing.

updates.question_text: Regarding coronary artery calcium scoring, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A gated noncontrast cardiac CT can be obtained for coronary calcium scoring
The Agatston score represents the total calcium in the coronary tree and can guide preventive therapy
Calcium scoring is appropriate for all symptomatic high-risk acute coronary syndrome presentations as first-line triage
Coronary calcification excludes CAD because only non-calcified plaque is clinically relevant
Calcium scoring is appropriate for asymptomatic patients without known CAD and intermediate 10-year ASCVD risk, or low-risk patients with family history of premature CAD
options_after: A gated noncontrast cardiac CT can be obtained for coronary calcium scoring
The Agatston score represents the total calcium in the coronary tree and can guide preventive therapy
Calcium scoring is appropriate for most symptomatic high-risk acute coronary syndrome presentations as first-line triage
Coronary calcification excludes clinically relevant CAD because significant plaques are expected to be non-calcified.
Calcium scoring is appropriate for asymptomatic patients without known CAD and intermediate 10-year ASCVD risk, or low-risk patients with family history of premature CAD
updates.explanation: Calcium scoring uses gated noncontrast cardiac CT, and the Agatston score summarises calcium burden in the coronary tree. It can predict future major adverse cardiovascular events and guide preventive therapy. The source positions calcium scoring for risk stratification in asymptomatic patients without known CAD when ASCVD risk is intermediate, or when family history of premature CAD exists despite low estimated risk. Acute high-risk coronary syndrome belongs to functional assessment or invasive angiography rather than calcium-score triage.

updates.question_text: Regarding CAD-RADS stenosis categories and management implications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CAD-RADS 0, 1 and 2 represent non-obstructive CAD with stenosis less than 50%
CAD-RADS 3 corresponds to moderate stenosis of 50-69% and consideration of functional testing plus preventive therapy
CAD-RADS 4 includes 70-99% stenosis or greater than 50% left main stenosis
Coronary segments smaller than 1.5 mm are not classifiable by CAD-RADS
Any non-evaluable segment automatically makes the study CAD-RADS 5
options_after: CAD-RADS 0, 1 and 2 represent non-obstructive CAD with stenosis less than 50%
CAD-RADS 3 corresponds to moderate stenosis of 50-69% and consideration of functional testing plus preventive therapy
CAD-RADS 4 includes 70-99% stenosis or greater than 50% left main stenosis
Coronary segments smaller than 1.5 mm are not classifiable by CAD-RADS
Any non-evaluable segment ordinarily makes the study CAD-RADS 5
updates.explanation: CAD-RADS 0-2 are non-obstructive categories below 50% stenosis. CAD-RADS 3 is moderate 50-69% stenosis, with functional testing and preventive therapy considered. CAD-RADS 4 includes severe 70-99% stenosis or greater than 50% left main stenosis, with functional testing or invasive angiography and possible revascularisation. Segments below 1.5 mm are not classifiable. CAD-RADS N is used for non-evaluable segments when the evaluable remainder shows less than 50% stenosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding vulnerable plaque, coronary stents and bypass grafts on CCTA, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: High-risk plaque features include low attenuation plaque, spotty calcification, positive remodelling and the napkin-ring sign
In-stent restenosis occurs by neointimal hyperplasia and appears as low-attenuation material within the stent lumen
CCTA evaluation of coronary stents is always straightforward and independent of stent diameter, location or artefact
A completely occluded bypass graft can be difficult to discern, with an outpouching at the graft-aortic anastomosis as a clue
Beam hardening and streak artefacts from surgical clips are irrelevant to bypass graft assessment
options_after: High-risk plaque features include low attenuation plaque, spotty calcification, positive remodelling and the napkin-ring sign
In-stent restenosis occurs by neointimal hyperplasia and appears as low-attenuation material within the stent lumen
CCTA evaluation of coronary stents is characteristically straightforward and independent of stent diameter, location or artefact
A completely occluded bypass graft can be difficult to discern, with an outpouching at the graft-aortic anastomosis as a clue
Beam hardening and streak artefacts from surgical clips are irrelevant to bypass graft assessment
updates.explanation: High-risk plaque features include low attenuation plaque, spotty calcification, positive remodelling and the napkin-ring sign. In-stent restenosis is a late complication due to neointimal hyperplasia, seen as low-attenuation material within the stent lumen. CCTA evaluation of stents is difficult and depends on stent type, diameter, location, motion and blooming artefacts. Bypass grafts can be assessed by CCTA, but surgical clip artefacts may obscure findings; a completely occluded graft may only be suggested by an outpouching at the graft-aortic anastomosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding coronary artery aneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Coronary artery aneurysm is common and is usually managed by a fixed imaging algorithm regardless of symptoms
Atherosclerosis is the most common cause in the United States
The usual presentation is always acute coronary syndrome, rather than incidental detection
Kawasaki disease is described as an important cause of coronary artery aneurysm in the United States
Kawasaki disease is the most common cause worldwide
options_after: Coronary artery aneurysm is common and is usually managed by a fixed imaging algorithm despite variation in symptoms
Atherosclerosis is the most common cause in the United States
The usual presentation is characteristically acute coronary syndrome, rather than incidental detection
Kawasaki disease is described as an important cause of coronary artery aneurysm in the United States
Kawasaki disease is the most common cause worldwide
updates.explanation: The source states that coronary artery aneurysmal dilatation is rare. Atherosclerosis is the most common cause in the United States, whereas Kawasaki disease is the most common cause worldwide. These aneurysms may be found incidentally in asymptomatic patients or present with angina or acute coronary syndrome. Management varies according to clinical presentation and risk assessment, rather than following a single fixed pathway.

updates.question_text: Regarding cardiac MRI pulse sequences, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Spin echo is used for anatomy
Spin echo is the fastest sequence and is preferred for perfusion and angiography
Spoiled gradient recalled echo is more susceptible to metal artefact than spin echo
Spoiled gradient recalled echo is used for quantitative measurements, perfusion and angiography
Balanced SSFP is primarily a dark-blood sequence for static morphology only
options_after: Spin echo is used for anatomy
Spin echo is the fastest sequence and is preferred for perfusion and angiography
Spoiled gradient recalled echo is more susceptible to metal artefact than spin echo
Spoiled gradient recalled echo is used for quantitative measurements, perfusion and angiography
Balanced SSFP is primarily a dark-blood sequence for static morphology in typical cases
updates.explanation: Spin echo has a longer acquisition time but provides high spatial resolution, excellent contrast and little metal artefact, so it is used for anatomy. Spoiled gradient recalled echo is faster but more susceptible to metal artefact and is used for quantitative measurements, perfusion and angiography. Balanced SSFP is described as a bright-blood gradient echo technique rather than a dark-blood sequence.

updates.question_text: Regarding phase contrast velocity-encoded cardiac MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It measures blood flow parallel to the imaging plane
Stationary tissue appears white while forward flow appears grey
