options_after: Stage 0 is end-stage fibrosis.
Stage 1 is hilar or mediastinal adenopathy only, without lung changes.
Stage 4 sarcoidosis consists of hilar or mediastinal adenopathy without pulmonary parenchymal change.
Patients necessarily progress through stages 0 to 4 in order.
The historical staging system applies to radiographic findings rather than CT.
updates.explanation: The source states that sarcoidosis staging is a historical radiographic system and that patients do not necessarily progress through the stages. Stage 1 is adenopathy only without lung changes, while stage 4 is end-stage fibrosis. Stage 0 is a normal radiograph, not end-stage disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding thoracic sarcoidosis imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Sarcoid fibrosis usually has mid and upper-lung predominance, unlike IPF.
Symmetric adenopathy is the most common radiographic finding, but sarcoidosis can be present without lymph-node enlargement.
The most common CT finding in addition to adenopathy is upper-lobe predominant perilymphatic nodules.
Perilymphatic sarcoid nodules occur only along the pleural surface and do not involve bronchovascular bundles.
Sarcoidosis lymph nodes never calcify.
options_after: Sarcoid fibrosis usually has mid and upper-lung predominance, unlike IPF.
Symmetric adenopathy is the most common radiographic finding, but sarcoidosis can be present without lymph-node enlargement.
The most common CT finding in addition to adenopathy is upper-lobe predominant perilymphatic nodules.
Perilymphatic sarcoid nodules occur primarily along the pleural surface and do not involve bronchovascular bundles.
Sarcoidosis lymph nodes will not calcify.
updates.explanation: Sarcoid fibrosis is typically mid and upper-lung predominant, unlike IPF. Symmetric adenopathy is the commonest radiographic finding, but lymph-node enlargement is not required. The common CT pattern, in addition to adenopathy, is upper-lobe predominant perilymphatic nodules along peribronchovascular, subpleural, and septal lymphatic pathways, not pleural-only disease. Lymph nodes may show stippled or eggshell calcification in up to 50%.

updates.question_text: Regarding pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is almost always seen in adult non-smokers.
Nearly 100% of adults with PLCH are smokers.
It may present with spontaneous pneumothorax.
The natural progression is nodules to cavitary nodules to irregular cysts.
Radiographic and CT findings include upper-lobe predominant cysts and irregular peribronchovascular nodules sparing the costophrenic sulci.
options_after: It is typically seen in adult non-smokers.
Nearly 100% of adults with PLCH are smokers.
It may present with spontaneous pneumothorax.
The natural progression is nodules to cavitary nodules to irregular cysts.
Radiographic and CT findings include upper-lobe predominant cysts and irregular peribronchovascular nodules sparing the costophrenic sulci.
updates.explanation: PLCH is a smoking-related lung disease and nearly all affected adults are smokers. It can present with spontaneous pneumothorax. Disease evolves from airway-associated nodules to cavitary nodules and finally irregular cysts, so patients may show nodules, nodules plus cysts, or cysts alone. The typical distribution is upper-lobe predominant cysts and irregular peribronchovascular nodules sparing the costophrenic sulci.

updates.question_text: Regarding the cystic lung disease summary table, which of the following pairings are correct?
options_before: LAM - diffuse distribution with many cysts and possible pneumothorax or pleural effusion.
PLCH - lower-lobe distribution with no nodules.
LIP - diffuse distribution with many cysts and pleural effusion.
BHD - lower-lobe distribution, few cysts, and pneumothorax association.
LAM - no pleural effusion association and few cysts.
options_after: LAM - diffuse distribution with many cysts and possible pneumothorax or pleural effusion.
PLCH - lower-lobe distribution without nodules.
LIP - diffuse distribution with many cysts and pleural effusion.
BHD - lower-lobe distribution, few cysts, and pneumothorax association.
LAM typically consists of few cysts and is unrelated to pleural effusion.
updates.explanation: The summary table lists LAM as diffuse with many cysts and possible pneumothorax or pleural effusion. BHD is lower-lobe predominant with few cysts and pneumothorax. LIP is lower-lobe predominant with few cysts and possible nodules, but the table does not list pneumothorax or pleural effusion. PLCH is upper-zone predominant and may have nodules and pneumothorax.

updates.question_text: Regarding paratracheal and paraspinal mediastinal landmarks, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The right paratracheal stripe is rarely visible on normal PA radiographs.
The posterior tracheal stripe is primarily a frontal radiographic interface and is not seen on the lateral radiograph.
Paraspinal line abnormalities suggest a prevascular mediastinal mass only.
Thickening of the right paratracheal stripe is most commonly due to a paratracheal mass including adenopathy or thyroid/tracheal neoplasm.
Paraspinal line abnormalities can be caused by haematoma, neurogenic tumour, aortic aneurysm, extramedullary haematopoiesis, oesophageal mass, or osteophyte.
options_after: The right paratracheal stripe is rarely visible on normal PA radiographs.
The posterior tracheal stripe is primarily a frontal radiographic interface and is not seen on the lateral radiograph.
Paraspinal line abnormalities suggest a prevascular mediastinal mass in typical cases.
Thickening of the right paratracheal stripe is most commonly due to a paratracheal mass including adenopathy or thyroid/tracheal neoplasm.
Paraspinal line abnormalities can be caused by haematoma, neurogenic tumour, aortic aneurysm, extramedullary haematopoiesis, oesophageal mass, or osteophyte.
updates.explanation: The right paratracheal stripe is the most commonly seen paratracheal landmark, visible in up to 97% of normal PA radiographs. Its thickening is most commonly due to a paratracheal mass such as adenopathy or thyroid/tracheal neoplasm. Paraspinal abnormalities suggest paravertebral disease and have a broad differential including haematoma, neurogenic tumour, aneurysm, extramedullary haematopoiesis, oesophageal mass, and osteophyte. The posterior tracheal stripe is actually the only interface seen on the lateral radiograph.

updates.question_text: Which statement is correct regarding the left superior intercostal vein?
options_before: It forms the azygoesophageal recess on the lateral radiograph.
It is the most common cause of a posterior mediastinal mass.
It is always pathologic when visible.
When visible, it may produce the aortic nipple as a small round shadow left of the aortic knob and can dilate as a collateral pathway in SVC obstruction.
It indicates malignant pleural effusion.
options_after: It forms the azygoesophageal recess on the lateral radiograph.
It is the most common cause of a posterior mediastinal mass.
It is characteristically pathologic when visible.
When visible, it may produce the aortic nipple as a small round shadow left of the aortic knob and can dilate as a collateral pathway in SVC obstruction.
It indicates malignant pleural effusion.
updates.explanation: The left superior intercostal vein is a normal vein that is not often seen on radiography. When visible, it produces the aortic nipple to the left of the aortic knob. It may dilate as a collateral pathway in SVC obstruction. It is not the azygoesophageal recess and does not itself diagnose pleural malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding mediastinal lymphadenopathy and Castleman disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lymph node calcification, low attenuation, and avid enhancement are typical features of lymphoma.
Low-attenuation lymph nodes exclude active TB and should be treated as typical lymphoma.
Castleman disease is also called angiofollicular lymph node hyperplasia and is characterised by avidly enhancing lymph nodes.
Unicentric Castleman disease is a single enlarged node in children or young adults and is usually cured by surgical resection.
Multicentric Castleman disease is almost always seen in AIDS with HHV8 and is typically treated with surgery alone.
options_after: Lymph node calcification, low attenuation, and avid enhancement are typical features of lymphoma.
Low-attenuation lymph nodes exclude active TB and should be treated as typical lymphoma.
Castleman disease is also called angiofollicular lymph node hyperplasia and is characterised by avidly enhancing lymph nodes.
Unicentric Castleman disease is a single enlarged node in children or young adults and is usually cured by surgical resection.
Multicentric Castleman disease is typically seen in AIDS with HHV8 and is typically treated with surgery alone.
updates.explanation: Calcification, low attenuation, and avid enhancement are unusual for lymphoma and should prompt consideration of alternatives. Low attenuation raises concern for active TB but can also occur in fungal infection, lymphoma, and metastatic disease; it does not exclude TB. Castleman disease is angiofollicular lymph node hyperplasia with avid enhancement. Unicentric disease is usually surgically curable, while multicentric disease is usually AIDS/HHV8-associated and treated with chemotherapy rather than surgery alone.

updates.question_text: Which statement is correct regarding thyroid lesions extending into the mediastinum?
options_before: They always arise in the paravertebral compartment.
The key diagnostic feature is absence of continuity with the thyroid.
They cannot contain coarse calcification.
Inferior extension occurs only through the oesophageal hiatus.
The key to diagnosis is showing superior continuity with the thyroid; a goitre may extend inferiorly into the middle mediastinum.
options_after: They characteristically arise in the paravertebral compartment.
The key diagnostic feature is absence of continuity with the thyroid.
They will not contain coarse calcification.
Inferior extension occurs primarily through the oesophageal hiatus.
The key to diagnosis is showing superior continuity with the thyroid; a goitre may extend inferiorly into the middle mediastinum.
updates.explanation: The source states that benign and malignant thyroid masses may extend into the mediastinum and that the key to diagnosis is showing continuity superiorly with the thyroid. Goitre may extend inferiorly into the middle mediastinum because of an embryologic fascial plane created by the inferior thyroidal artery. The illustrated goitre is heterogeneous and coarsely calcified.

updates.question_text: Regarding paraganglioma in the visceral mediastinum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It arises only from thymic epithelium and is never neuroendocrine.
Cardiac or aortopulmonary paragangliomas may arise from phrenic, vagus, or recurrent laryngeal nerves.
Visceral mediastinal paraganglioma tends to be thymic epithelial in origin.
MRI shows a T1 intermediate, T2 hyperintense mass with homogeneous enhancement.
Malignancy cannot occur in extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma.
options_after: It arises primarily from thymic epithelium and is not neuroendocrine.
Cardiac or aortopulmonary paragangliomas may arise from phrenic, vagus, or recurrent laryngeal nerves.
Visceral mediastinal paraganglioma tends to be thymic epithelial in origin.
MRI shows a T1 intermediate, T2 hyperintense mass with homogeneous enhancement.
Malignancy will not occur in extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma.
updates.explanation: Paragangliomas are highly vascular neuroendocrine tumours from embryonic neural crest cells and may arise in the cardiac or AP window region from phrenic, vagus, or recurrent laryngeal nerves. Visceral mediastinal paraganglioma tends to be parasympathetic rather than thymic epithelial in origin. MRI shows T1 intermediate and T2 hyperintense signal with homogeneous enhancement. Malignancy can occur in up to 10% of extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas.

updates.question_text: Which statement is correct regarding the schwannoma example in the source?
options_before: The lesion enhances avidly and is centred in the prevascular mediastinum.
The frontal radiograph shows a right hilar opacity with the hilum overlay sign corresponding to a paravertebral abnormality on the lateral radiograph.
The CT shows a fat-fluid level diagnostic of teratoma.
The MRI shows T1 hyperintensity from haemorrhage only.
The lesion is a malignant sympathetic ganglion tumour of early childhood.
options_after: The lesion enhances avidly and is centred in the prevascular mediastinum.
The frontal radiograph shows a right hilar opacity with the hilum overlay sign corresponding to a paravertebral abnormality on the lateral radiograph.
The CT shows a fat-fluid level diagnostic of teratoma.
The MRI shows T1 hyperintensity from haemorrhage in typical cases.
The lesion is a malignant sympathetic ganglion tumour of early childhood.
updates.explanation: The schwannoma example shows a round opacity over the right hilum with the hilum overlay sign, localised to a paravertebral abnormality on the lateral radiograph. CT shows a low-density lesion without significant enhancement, and MRI shows heterogeneous T2 hyperintensity in the cystic lesion. The fat-fluid level belongs to teratoma, and neuroblastoma is the malignant sympathetic ganglion tumour of early childhood.

updates.question_text: Regarding bronchial carcinoid and enhancing endobronchial masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Carcinoid almost always arises in the cervical trachea above the carina.
Carcinoid almost always occurs distal to the carina.
Carcinoid tumours do not calcify and do not enhance avidly.
Carcinoid tumours tend to have a larger endobronchial component than extrinsic component.
The differential diagnosis of an enhancing endobronchial mass includes carcinoid, mucoepidermoid carcinoma, haemangioma, and glomus tumour.
options_after: Carcinoid typically arises in the cervical trachea above the carina.
Carcinoid almost always occurs distal to the carina.
Carcinoid tumours do not calcify and do not enhance avidly.
Carcinoid tumours tend to have a larger endobronchial component than extrinsic component.
The differential diagnosis of an enhancing endobronchial mass includes carcinoid, mucoepidermoid carcinoma, haemangioma, and glomus tumour.
updates.explanation: The source states that carcinoid almost always occurs distal to the carina. On CT it is an endoluminal bronchial mass that may calcify and often enhances avidly, with a larger extrinsic than endobronchial component. The enhancing endobronchial mass differential includes mucoepidermoid carcinoma and rare haemangioma or glomus tumour. A cervical tracheal location and absent enhancement are not the described carcinoid pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding endobronchial metastasis, direct airway invasion, and benign endobronchial lesions, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: The commonest airway metastases arise from ovarian, pancreatic, prostatic, and colonic primary tumours.
Papilloma is a benign lesion with no recognised premalignant potential.
A single papilloma is usually caused by HPV acquired at birth.
Laryngotracheal papillomatosis is usually centred in the peripheral lung and rarely involves the larynx.
Direct central airway invasion by aggressive laryngeal, thyroid, oesophageal, and lung cancer occurs more commonly than endobronchial metastases.
options_after: The commonest airway metastases arise from ovarian, pancreatic, prostatic, and colonic primary tumours.
Papilloma is a benign lesion without recognised premalignant potential.
A single papilloma is usually caused by HPV acquired at birth.
Laryngotracheal papillomatosis is usually centred in the peripheral lung and rarely involves the larynx.
Direct central airway invasion by aggressive laryngeal, thyroid, oesophageal, and lung cancer occurs more commonly than endobronchial metastases.
updates.explanation: The source states that direct central airway invasion occurs more commonly than endobronchial metastases and lists laryngeal, thyroid, oesophageal, and lung cancers as adjacent aggressive tumours that may invade the airway. Common endobronchial metastases are remembered by BReTh Lung: breast, renal cell, thyroid, and lung; melanoma and sarcoma are also listed. Papilloma is benign but potentially premalignant. A single papilloma is usually due to chronic irritation, while multiple papillomas are HPV-related and usually centred in the larynx.

updates.question_text: Regarding smoking-related emphysema and related lung disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Respiratory bronchiolitis, RB-ILD, DIP, PLCH, and emphysema may lie on a spectrum of smoking-related lung disease.
Panacinar emphysema is mainly due to chronic aspiration and affects only the central bronchi.
Centrilobular emphysema, like RB-ILD, primarily affects the centre of the secondary pulmonary lobule.
Paraseptal emphysema is usually smoking-related and is often seen in combination with other forms of emphysema.
In smokers, alveolar macrophages and neutrophils produce less elastase, protecting alveolar walls from destruction.
options_after: Respiratory bronchiolitis, RB-ILD, DIP, PLCH, and emphysema may lie on a spectrum of smoking-related lung disease.
Panacinar emphysema is mainly due to chronic aspiration and affects primarily the central bronchi.
Centrilobular emphysema, like RB-ILD, primarily affects the centre of the secondary pulmonary lobule.
Paraseptal emphysema is usually smoking-related and is often seen in combination with other forms of emphysema.
In smokers, alveolar macrophages and neutrophils produce less elastase, protecting alveolar walls from destruction.
updates.explanation: The source frames respiratory bronchiolitis, RB-ILD, DIP, PLCH, and emphysema as possibly belonging to the same smoking-related macrophage-mediated spectrum. Centrilobular emphysema, like RB-ILD, affects the centre of the secondary pulmonary lobule. Paraseptal emphysema is usually smoking-related and usually coexists with other emphysema. Smoking increases macrophages and neutrophils and therefore elastase burden rather than reducing it.

updates.question_text: Regarding pleural malignancy and malignant pleural effusion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mesothelioma is the most common cause of pleural malignancy.
Metastatic disease is the most common cause of pleural malignancy, including lung and breast cancer, gastrointestinal and genitourinary adenocarcinoma, and invasive thymoma.
The split pleura sign is characteristic of malignant pleural effusion.
Extrapleural soft-tissue components from myeloma or plasmacytoma cannot secondarily invade the pleura.
Features suggesting malignant effusion include nodular pleural thickening, a large or recurrent effusion without another aetiology, and mediastinal pleural thickening.
options_after: Mesothelioma is the most common cause of pleural malignancy.
Metastatic disease is the most common cause of pleural malignancy, including lung and breast cancer, gastrointestinal and genitourinary adenocarcinoma, and invasive thymoma.
The split pleura sign is characteristic of malignant pleural effusion.
Extrapleural soft-tissue components from myeloma or plasmacytoma will not secondarily invade the pleura.
Features suggesting malignant effusion include nodular pleural thickening, a large or recurrent effusion without another aetiology, and mediastinal pleural thickening.
updates.explanation: Metastatic disease is stated to be the most common cause of pleural malignancy, with lung, breast, gastrointestinal, genitourinary adenocarcinoma, and invasive thymoma listed. Malignant effusion is suggested by nodular pleural thickening, large or recurrent effusion without another cause, and mediastinal pleural thickening. The split pleura sign is characteristic of empyema. Myeloma or plasmacytoma osseous metastases may have extrapleural components that secondarily invade the pleura.

updates.question_text: Regarding mesothelioma, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: The epithelial subtype is the least common subtype and has the worst prognosis.
Most cases are unrelated to asbestos exposure and occur with latency under 2 years.
CT typically shows nodular concentric pleural thickening, often with an associated pleural effusion, and most cases are due to prior asbestos exposure with latency over 20 years.
Surgery has no evolving role because mesothelioma is treated only with systemic antibiotics.
The split pleura sign is pathognomonic for mesothelioma.
options_after: The epithelial subtype is the least common subtype and has the worst prognosis.
Most cases are unrelated to asbestos exposure and occur with latency under 2 years.
CT typically shows nodular concentric pleural thickening, often with an associated pleural effusion, and most cases are due to prior asbestos exposure with latency over 20 years.
Surgery lacks evolving role because mesothelioma is treated primarily with systemic antibiotics.
The split pleura sign is pathognomonic for mesothelioma.
updates.explanation: Mesothelioma is a highly aggressive pleural neoplasm; the source states that most cases are due to asbestos exposure with a latency greater than 20 years. CT usually shows nodular concentric pleural thickening, often with effusion. The epithelial subtype is more common and has a slightly better prognosis than sarcomatoid or mixed subtypes. Surgery has an evolving role with visible tumour resection, and trimodality therapy may benefit a subset. The split pleura sign belongs to empyema.

updates.question_text:
Coronal T2, coronal postcontrast T1 fat-saturated, and axial precontrast T1 fat-saturated MRI demonstrate a complex cystic right upper pole renal mass with internal T1 hyperintense foci, and a large inferior retroperitoneal collection containing similar T1 bright signal. Subtraction images confirm no enhancement within either structure.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this case?
options_before: Retroperitoneal bleeds are unlikely to explain acute anaemia when there is no identifiable source of bleeding on physical examination.
Absence of enhancement on postcontrast and subtraction images completely excludes haemorrhage in this region.
A ruptured haemorrhagic renal cyst is not a recognised cause of retroperitoneal haemorrhage.
The T1 hyperintensity within the collection represents methemoglobin in evolving blood products.
On MRI, foci of T1 shortening within a haematoma should be interpreted as active contrast extravasation.
options_after: Retroperitoneal bleeds are unlikely to explain acute anaemia when there is an absence of identifiable source of bleeding on physical examination.
Absence of enhancement on postcontrast and subtraction images completely excludes haemorrhage in this region.
A ruptured haemorrhagic renal cyst is not a recognised cause of retroperitoneal haemorrhage.
The T1 hyperintensity within the collection represents methemoglobin in evolving blood products.
On MRI, foci of T1 shortening within a haematoma should be interpreted as active contrast extravasation.
updates.explanation: The correct option is d. The source explains that the T1-bright foci represent methemoglobin in evolving blood products. Option e is incorrect because the text specifically warns not to confuse T1 shortening with active extravasation. Option c is incorrect because the illustrated retroperitoneal haematoma is due to a ruptured haemorrhagic renal cyst. Option b is incorrect because lack of enhancement excludes active extravasation at the time of imaging, not prior haemorrhage. Option a is incorrect because retroperitoneal bleeding may explain acute anaemia without an identifiable external source.

updates.question_text: Regarding the imaging diagnosis of adrenal adenoma on CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adrenal protocol CT uses a delayed phase at 5 minutes after contrast injection.
An adrenal adenoma characteristically demonstrates absolute washout of greater than 60% on adrenal protocol CT.
An adrenal nodule measuring ?10 HU on noncontrast CT can be reliably diagnosed as an adenoma.
All adrenal adenomas have lipid-poor characteristics on noncontrast CT and require washout calculation for diagnosis.
Approximately 70-80% of adrenal adenomas measure less than 10 HU on noncontrast CT.
options_after: Adrenal protocol CT uses a delayed phase at 5 minutes after contrast injection.
An adrenal adenoma characteristically demonstrates absolute washout of greater than 60% on adrenal protocol CT.
An adrenal nodule measuring ?10 HU on noncontrast CT can be reliably diagnosed as an adenoma.
Most adrenal adenomas have lipid-poor characteristics on noncontrast CT and require washout calculation for diagnosis.
Approximately 70-80% of adrenal adenomas measure less than 10 HU on noncontrast CT.
updates.explanation: The correct options are b, c and e. A nodule measuring ?10 HU on noncontrast CT can be diagnosed as adenoma, and 70-80% of adenomas meet this lipid-rich threshold. Lipid-poor adenomas require washout assessment, and absolute washout greater than 60% is diagnostic of adenoma. Option d is incorrect because only 20-30% are lipid-poor. Option a is incorrect because the source adrenal protocol uses unenhanced imaging, a 60-second enhanced phase and a 15-minute delayed phase, not a 5-minute delayed phase.

updates.question_text:
Opposed-phase MRI of a left adrenal mass shows a crescentic posterolateral lesion with signal dropout, consistent with an adenoma component. An additional anteromedial lesion shows no OOP suppression and demonstrates central necrosis with enhancement on postcontrast imaging.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this case?
options_before: If tissue diagnosis is required in a patient with lung cancer and an indeterminate adrenal mass, FDG PET/CT and adrenal mass biopsy may be helpful adjuncts.
When an apparent adenoma appears heterogeneous or enlarges in a patient with known primary malignancy, a collision tumour should be considered.
An indeterminate adrenal nodule in a patient without known malignancy most likely represents a lipid-poor adenoma, and advanced imaging is usually not required.
This appearance is consistent with a collision tumour comprising co-existing adenoma and a second distinct adrenal lesion.
In a patient with known primary malignancy, a lesion measuring <10 HU on noncontrast CT definitively excludes metastatic disease regardless of morphology.
options_after: If tissue diagnosis is required in a patient with lung cancer and an indeterminate adrenal mass, FDG PET/CT and adrenal mass biopsy may be helpful adjuncts.
When an apparent adenoma appears heterogeneous or enlarges in a patient with known primary malignancy, a collision tumour should be considered.
An indeterminate adrenal nodule in a patient without known malignancy most likely represents a lipid-poor adenoma, and advanced imaging is usually not required.
This appearance is consistent with a collision tumour comprising co-existing adenoma and a second distinct adrenal lesion.
In a patient with known primary malignancy, a lesion measuring <10 HU on noncontrast CT definitively excludes metastatic disease despite variation in morphology.
updates.explanation: A collision tumour represents co-existence of two distinct tumours within a single adrenal mass — here, an adenoma (OOP signal dropout) and a second enhancing lesion with central necrosis coexist. In a patient with known primary malignancy, even an apparent adenoma component should not lead to dismissal if the mass is heterogeneous or enlarging, as collision tumour must be considered. An indeterminate nodule in a patient without known malignancy most likely represents a lipid-poor adenoma, and advanced imaging is usually unnecessary. FDG PET/CT and biopsy are useful when tissue diagnosis is required in the context of known malignancy.

updates.question_text:
Paired axial MRI of a right adrenal mass demonstrates signal on in-phase imaging (left) and signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging (right).

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this finding?
options_before: Signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging indicates intracytoplasmic lipid within the lesion, consistent with a lipid-rich adenoma.
The drop in signal on out-of-phase images results from cancellation of fat and water proton signals when both are contained within the same voxel.
Adrenal metastases generally demonstrate signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging in the same manner as adenomas.
MRI chemical shift imaging cannot detect intracytoplasmic lipid that is undetectable by CT density measurement.
Chemical shift imaging uses paired spin-echo sequences rather than gradient-echo in-phase and out-of-phase imaging.
options_after: Signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging indicates intracytoplasmic lipid within the lesion, consistent with a lipid-rich adenoma.
The drop in signal on out-of-phase images results from cancellation of fat and water proton signals when both are contained within the same voxel.
Adrenal metastases generally demonstrate signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging in the same manner as adenomas.
MRI chemical shift imaging will not detect intracytoplasmic lipid that is undetectable by CT density measurement.
Chemical shift imaging uses paired spin-echo sequences rather than gradient-echo in-phase and out-of-phase imaging.
updates.explanation: The correct options are a and b. Out-of-phase signal dropout reflects intracytoplasmic lipid, typical of lipid-rich adrenal adenoma, and occurs because fat and water signal cancel when both are present in the same voxel. Option d is incorrect because MRI can detect small amounts of lipid that may be undetectable by CT. Option c is incorrect because metastases generally do not suppress on out-of-phase imaging. Option e is incorrect because chemical shift imaging uses paired gradient-echo in-phase and out-of-phase sequences.

updates.question_text: Regarding malignant adrenal masses that may demonstrate signal loss on out-of-phase MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All malignant adrenal masses consistently demonstrate signal loss on out-of-phase imaging.
Well-differentiated adrenocortical carcinoma can very rarely demonstrate signal loss on out-of-phase MRI.
Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma is a recognised cause of signal dropout on out-of-phase adrenal MRI.
Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma may occasionally show signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging.
Liposarcoma is a recognised entity that may rarely show signal loss on out-of-phase imaging, though it is typically a large mass unlikely to be confused with adenoma.
options_after: Most malignant adrenal masses consistently demonstrate signal loss on out-of-phase imaging.
Well-differentiated adrenocortical carcinoma can very rarely demonstrate signal loss on out-of-phase MRI.
Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma is a recognised cause of signal dropout on out-of-phase adrenal MRI.
Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma may occasionally show signal dropout on out-of-phase imaging.
Liposarcoma is a recognised entity that may rarely show signal loss on out-of-phase imaging, though it is typically a large mass unlikely to be confused with adenoma.
updates.explanation: The majority of adrenal masses with OOP signal loss are lipid-rich adenomas; however, rare malignant exceptions exist. These include well-differentiated adrenocortical carcinoma, metastatic clear cell RCC, metastatic HCC, and liposarcoma — all of which may contain intracytoplasmic lipid. Most adrenal metastases do NOT suppress on OOP imaging, making signal loss a generally reliable but not absolute indicator of adenoma. Liposarcoma typically presents as a large predominantly fatty mass and is rarely confused with adrenal adenoma given its morphology and location.

updates.question_text:
Fused axial PET-CT in a patient with lung cancer demonstrates an FDG-avid left adrenal mass. An intraprocedural CT-guided biopsy image shows the deployed biopsy needle traversing the mass.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this case?
options_before: Biopsy is indicated for any incidentally discovered adrenal nodule in a patient without known malignancy, regardless of CT characteristics.
FDG-avidity on PET-CT can support the decision to proceed to adrenal biopsy in equivocal cases.
Biopsy is particularly indicated for adrenal masses that remain indeterminate after comprehensive imaging workup in the context of underlying malignancy.
Adrenal mass biopsy is very accurate in providing a definitive histological diagnosis.
Percutaneous adrenal biopsy is a safe procedure frequently performed under CT guidance.
options_after: Biopsy is indicated for any incidentally discovered adrenal nodule in a patient without known malignancy, despite variation in CT characteristics.
FDG-avidity on PET-CT can support the decision to proceed to adrenal biopsy in equivocal cases.
Biopsy is particularly indicated for adrenal masses that remain indeterminate after comprehensive imaging workup in the context of underlying malignancy.
Adrenal mass biopsy is very accurate in providing a definitive histological diagnosis.
Percutaneous adrenal biopsy is a safe procedure frequently performed under CT guidance.
updates.explanation: Percutaneous adrenal biopsy under CT guidance is a safe and accurate procedure for providing definitive histological diagnosis. It is indicated when an adrenal mass remains indeterminate after comprehensive imaging workup, particularly in patients with underlying malignancy where distinguishing metastasis from adenoma is clinically important. FDG-avidity on PET-CT, as in this lung cancer patient, supports the indication for biopsy. Biopsy is not indicated for every incidentally discovered adrenal nodule — CT density and washout criteria usually suffice in patients without known malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding the absent nephrogram on CT urography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A surgically absent kidney is a recognised cause of unilateral absent nephrogram.
Chronic ureteral obstruction always causes a bilateral absent nephrogram.
An ectopic kidney located outside the renal fossa may produce a unilateral absent nephrogram.
Acute renal artery or vein occlusion can produce an absent nephrogram on the affected side.
Bilateral absent nephrogram is a recognised cause of acute tubular necrosis.
options_after: A surgically absent kidney is a recognised cause of unilateral absent nephrogram.
Chronic ureteral obstruction characteristically causes a bilateral absent nephrogram.
An ectopic kidney located outside the renal fossa may produce a unilateral absent nephrogram.
Acute renal artery or vein occlusion can produce an absent nephrogram on the affected side.
Bilateral absent nephrogram is a recognised cause of acute tubular necrosis.
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, c and d. A unilateral absent nephrogram may reflect renal agenesis, ectopic kidney, surgically absent kidney, or a present but non-enhancing kidney from renal artery/vein occlusion or chronic obstruction. Option e is incorrect because absent nephrogram is an imaging pattern, not a cause of acute tubular necrosis. Option b is incorrect because chronic ureteral obstruction is listed as a cause of an absent nephrogram on the affected side, not necessarily bilateral disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal variants of renal morphology that may simulate a renal mass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Persistent fetal lobulation produces a focal bulge of the renal contour, whereas a hypertrophied column of Bertin produces a cortical indentation.
A hypertrophied column of Bertin represents normal cortical tissue that anchors the renal cortex to the hilum and creates separations between the renal pyramids.
A dromedary hump is a focal bulge at the lateral left kidney, thought to result from splenic compression of the superolateral kidney.
Persistent fetal lobulation is suggested when septa of Bertin are absent on both sides of the cortical indentation.
A hypertrophied column of Bertin cannot mimic a renal mass on imaging.
options_after: Persistent fetal lobulation produces a focal bulge of the renal contour, whereas a hypertrophied column of Bertin produces a cortical indentation.
A hypertrophied column of Bertin represents normal cortical tissue that anchors the renal cortex to the hilum and creates separations between the renal pyramids.
A dromedary hump is a focal bulge at the lateral left kidney, thought to result from splenic compression of the superolateral kidney.
Persistent fetal lobulation is suggested when septa of Bertin are absent on both sides of the cortical indentation.
A hypertrophied column of Bertin will not mimic a renal mass on imaging.
updates.explanation: The correct options are b and c. A hypertrophied column of Bertin is normal cortical tissue that may mimic a mass, and a dromedary hump is a left lateral renal bulge thought to reflect splenic impression. Option d is incorrect because persistent fetal lobulation is distinguished from a mass by septa of Bertin on either side of the indentation, not absence of these septa. Option a reverses the described morphology. Option e is incorrect because a hypertrophied column of Bertin may mimic a renal mass.

updates.question_text:
Coronal excretory phase CT urography shows bilateral blunted, rounded calyces in a patient with chronic analgesic use and diabetes mellitus.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this condition?
options_before: The signet ring sign describes contrast filling only the periphery of the papilla.
On excretory phase CT, sloughed papillae may appear as filling defects in the calyces, renal pelvis, or ureter.
On ultrasound, papillary necrosis is not associated with focal areas of increased papillary echogenicity.
The most common causes include NSAIDs, sickle cell anaemia, diabetes mellitus, and renal vein thrombosis.
The POSTCARD mnemonic includes pyelonephritis, obstruction, sickle cell disease, tuberculosis, cirrhosis, analgesics, renal vein thrombosis, and diabetes mellitus.
options_after: The signet ring sign describes contrast filling primarily the periphery of the papilla.
On excretory phase CT, sloughed papillae may appear as filling defects in the calyces, renal pelvis, or ureter.
On ultrasound, papillary necrosis is not associated with focal areas of increased papillary echogenicity.
The most common causes include NSAIDs, sickle cell anaemia, diabetes mellitus, and renal vein thrombosis.
The POSTCARD mnemonic includes pyelonephritis, obstruction, sickle cell disease, tuberculosis, cirrhosis, analgesics, renal vein thrombosis, and diabetes mellitus.
updates.explanation: The correct options are b, d and e. The source lists NSAIDs/analgesics, sickle cell disease, diabetes and renal vein thrombosis among common causes, and the POSTCARD mnemonic covers the wider list. Sloughed papillae may appear as filling defects on excretory phase CT. Option a is incorrect because the lobster claw sign describes peripheral papillary contrast filling, while the signet ring sign describes contrast surrounding a sloughed papilla. Option c is incorrect because ultrasound may show focal increased papillary echogenicity.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT features of renal vascular injury following trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Traumatic renal artery thrombosis results from external compression of the artery without intimal tearing.
Permanent loss of renal function occurs after approximately six hours of ischaemia following traumatic renal artery thrombosis.
Active haemorrhage and pseudoaneurysm cannot be differentiated on CT, as both show identical attenuation changes on delayed phase imaging.
Active renal haemorrhage increases in attenuation and/or size on delayed phase imaging.
Renal artery pseudoaneurysm and arteriovenous fistula appear as a hyperattenuating focus with density similar to the aorta that decreases in attenuation on delayed phase imaging.
options_after: Traumatic renal artery thrombosis results from external compression of the artery without intimal tearing.
Long-term loss of renal function occurs after approximately six hours of ischaemia following traumatic renal artery thrombosis.
Active haemorrhage and pseudoaneurysm will not be differentiated on CT, as both show closely comparable attenuation changes on delayed phase imaging.
Active renal haemorrhage increases in attenuation and/or size on delayed phase imaging.
Renal artery pseudoaneurysm and arteriovenous fistula appear as a hyperattenuating focus with density similar to the aorta that decreases in attenuation on delayed phase imaging.
updates.explanation: The correct options are d and e. Pseudoaneurysm and AV fistula appear as a hyperattenuating focus similar to the aorta that decreases on delayed imaging, whereas active haemorrhage increases in attenuation and/or size on delayed imaging. Option a is incorrect because traumatic renal artery thrombosis occurs with tearing of the intima, initiating thrombosis. Option b is incorrect because permanent functional loss occurs after approximately two hours of ischaemia. Option c is incorrect because delayed phase behaviour helps distinguish active bleeding from pseudoaneurysm/AV fistula.

updates.question_text: Regarding Page kidney, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Page kidney is a rare cause of secondary hypertension due to extrinsic compression of the kidney by a subcapsular collection, usually following trauma.
Hypertension typically develops within hours of the initial subcapsular haematoma.
Imaging demonstrates diffuse renal enlargement without subcapsular deformation.
The mechanism involves decreased renal blood flow leading to increased renin secretion and consequent hypertension.
Percutaneous drainage of the subcapsular haematoma is never an effective treatment.
options_after: Page kidney is a rare cause of secondary hypertension due to extrinsic compression of the kidney by a subcapsular collection, usually following trauma.
Hypertension typically develops within hours of the initial subcapsular haematoma.
Imaging demonstrates diffuse renal enlargement without subcapsular deformation.
The mechanism involves decreased renal blood flow leading to increased renin secretion and consequent hypertension.
Percutaneous drainage of the subcapsular haematoma is not an effective treatment.
updates.explanation: The correct options are a and d. Page kidney is secondary hypertension caused by external renal compression from a subcapsular collection, usually after trauma, with reduced renal blood flow triggering increased renin secretion. Option b is incorrect because hypertension usually takes several months to develop. Option c is incorrect because imaging shows a subcapsular haematoma causing deformation and flattening of the kidney. Option e is incorrect because percutaneous drainage may be effective.

updates.question_text: Regarding the resistive index (RI) in Doppler ultrasound evaluation of renal obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A RI of >0.7 on the affected side, or a difference of >0.1 between kidneys, suggests acute obstruction.
The resistive index is useful for diagnosing chronic obstruction.
The resistive index is measured using Doppler of the main renal artery only.
The resistive index is calculated as RI = (PSV ? EDV) / PSV, where PSV is peak systolic velocity and EDV is end-diastolic velocity.
Bilateral elevated resistive indices (>0.7) are specific for bilateral ureteral obstruction.
options_after: A RI of >0.7 on the affected side, or a difference of >0.1 between kidneys, suggests acute obstruction.
The resistive index is useful for diagnosing chronic obstruction.
The resistive index is measured using Doppler of the main renal artery in typical cases.
The resistive index is calculated as RI = (PSV ? EDV) / PSV, where PSV is peak systolic velocity and EDV is end-diastolic velocity.
Bilateral elevated resistive indices (>0.7) are specific for bilateral ureteral obstruction.
updates.explanation: The correct options are a and d. RI is calculated as (PSV ? EDV) / PSV, and RI >0.7 on the affected side or a side-to-side difference >0.1 suggests acute obstruction. Option e is incorrect because bilateral elevated RI is nonspecific and may reflect medical renal disease. Option b is incorrect because RI is not used to diagnose chronic obstruction. Option c is incorrect because RI is measured in renal segmental or arcuate arteries.

updates.question_text:
Axial and coronal contrast-enhanced CT demonstrates an enlarged left kidney with delayed and striated enhancement in a febrile patient with loin pain and positive urinalysis.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this condition?
options_before: Mild hydronephrosis on the affected side in pyelonephritis should be assumed to represent an obstructing calculus.
On ultrasound, focal pyelonephritis characteristically appears as a hyperechoic mass with a well-defined wall.
CT findings of pyelonephritis never include perinephric stranding.
Infection typically ascends from the bladder.
CT imaging can appear normal in up to 75% of cases.
options_after: Mild hydronephrosis on the affected side in pyelonephritis should be assumed to represent an obstructing calculus.
On ultrasound, focal pyelonephritis characteristically appears as a hyperechoic mass with a well-defined wall.
CT findings of pyelonephritis will not include perinephric stranding.
Infection typically ascends from the bladder.
CT imaging can appear normal in up to 75% of cases.
updates.explanation: The correct options are d and e. CT may appear normal in up to 75% of pyelonephritis cases, and infection usually ascends from the bladder. Option b is incorrect because focal pyelonephritis is classically a hypoechoic mass lacking a distinct wall. Option a is incorrect because mild hydronephrosis may reflect endotoxin-related reduced ureteral peristalsis and should not automatically be confused with obstruction. Option c is incorrect because perinephric stranding is listed among additional CT findings.

updates.question_text:
Sequential ultrasound images of the kidney show marked hydronephrosis with echogenic dependent material and a fluid-debris level within the dilated collecting system, in a patient with a malpositioned ureteral stent.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this condition?
options_before: Treatment requires emergent relief of obstruction via percutaneous nephrostomy or ureteral stent.
Ultrasound of pyonephrosis should show an entirely anechoic collecting system without debris.
Pyonephrosis is colloquially referred to as sterile urine under pressure.
Pyonephrosis is defined as infection of an obstructed collecting system.
On ultrasound, pyonephrosis characteristically demonstrates a thick-walled multiloculated lesion with a distinct wall.
options_after: Treatment requires emergent relief of obstruction via percutaneous nephrostomy or ureteral stent.
Ultrasound of pyonephrosis should show an predominantly anechoic collecting system without debris.
Pyonephrosis is colloquially referred to as sterile urine under pressure.
Pyonephrosis is defined as infection of an obstructed collecting system.
On ultrasound, pyonephrosis characteristically demonstrates a thick-walled multiloculated lesion with a distinct wall.
updates.explanation: The correct options are a and d. Pyonephrosis is infection of an obstructed collecting system and requires emergent drainage by percutaneous nephrostomy or ureteral stent. Option e describes the ultrasound appearance of renal abscess rather than pyonephrosis. Option b is incorrect because pyonephrosis shows nonshadowing echogenic material and may show a fluid-fluid level. Option c is incorrect because it is colloquially pus under pressure.

updates.question_text: Regarding the evaluation of enhancement in a renal mass, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The presence of intralesional calcification with fat is almost always diagnostic of benign angiomyolipoma
On MRI, definite enhancement requires a signal intensity increase of ?20%
A non-fat-containing renal mass <1 cm carries the same malignancy risk as one >3 cm
On CT, 10-19 HU is classified as equivocal enhancement
On CT, an absolute increase of ?20 HU represents definite enhancement
options_after: The presence of intralesional calcification with fat is typically diagnostic of benign angiomyolipoma
On MRI, definite enhancement requires a signal intensity increase of ?20%
A non-fat-containing renal mass <1 cm carries the same malignancy risk as one >3 cm
On CT, 10-19 HU is classified as equivocal enhancement
On CT, an absolute increase of ?20 HU represents definite enhancement
updates.explanation: The correct options are b, d and e. CT enhancement is definite at ?20 HU and equivocal at 10-19 HU, while MRI definite enhancement requires a signal intensity increase of ?20%. Option a is incorrect because intralesional fat alone is almost always diagnostic of benign AML, but calcification should raise concern for RCC with macroscopic fat. Option c is incorrect because the malignancy risk rises with size: many solid masses <1 cm are benign, while masses >3 cm are more often malignant.

updates.question_text: Regarding the Bosniak classification of cystic renal masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Category III carries approximately 50% risk of malignancy
Category IIF carries a 0-38% risk of malignancy and requires imaging follow-up
The 2019 update formally incorporates MRI into the classification
Category IV mandates surgical excision regardless of patient comorbidities
Calcification is a major independent criterion in the 2019 Bosniak classification
options_after: Category III carries approximately 50% risk of malignancy
Category IIF carries a 0-38% risk of malignancy and requires imaging follow-up
The 2019 update formally incorporates MRI into the classification
Category IV mandates surgical excision despite variation in patient comorbidities
Calcification is a major independent criterion in the 2019 Bosniak classification
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, b and c. The 2019 Bosniak update incorporates MRI, category IIF has a 0-38% malignancy risk and needs follow-up, and category III carries roughly 50% risk. Option d is incorrect because category IV usually requires surgical excision unless significant comorbidities exist. Option e is incorrect because isolated calcification has limited predictive value and is no longer a major independent criterion.

updates.question_text:
A patient presents with progressive renal failure and hypertension. An axial contrast-enhanced CT is shown, demonstrating bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts of varying attenuation and hepatic cysts.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this image and the underlying condition?
options_before: Approximately 70% of patients have multiple hepatic cysts
Saccular cerebral aneurysms occur in approximately 15% of patients
The condition is responsible for about half of patients on long-term dialysis
ADPKD is known to markedly increase the risk of renal cell carcinoma in all patients
The cysts demonstrate varying attenuation due to haemorrhage
options_after: Approximately 70% of patients have multiple hepatic cysts
Saccular cerebral aneurysms occur in approximately 15% of patients
The condition is responsible for about half of patients on long-term dialysis
ADPKD is known to markedly increase the risk of renal cell carcinoma in most patients
The cysts demonstrate varying attenuation due to haemorrhage
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, b and e. ADPKD kidneys contain multiple cysts of varying attenuation due to haemorrhage, about 70% have hepatic cysts, and about 15% have saccular cerebral aneurysms. Option c is incorrect because ADPKD accounts for 10% of long-term dialysis patients, not half. Option d is incorrect because ADPKD is not known to clearly increase RCC risk in all patients, though some authors propose a slight increase.

updates.question_text:
Sagittal ultrasound and colour Doppler images of the kidney are shown, demonstrating a solid renal mass.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding renal cell carcinoma (RCC)?
options_before: Venous invasion by RCC does not alter the surgical approach
On ultrasound, RCC is always hyperechoic
RCC arises from renal tubular epithelium
RCC represents 2–3% of all cancers
Risk factors include smoking, acquired cystic kidney disease, and von Hippel-Lindau
options_after: Venous invasion by RCC does not alter the surgical approach
On ultrasound, RCC is characteristically hyperechoic
RCC arises from renal tubular epithelium
RCC represents 2–3% of all cancers
Risk factors include smoking, acquired cystic kidney disease, and von Hippel-Lindau
updates.explanation: RCC arises from renal tubular epithelium and accounts for 2–3% of all cancers. Risk factors include smoking, acquired cystic kidney disease, von Hippel-Lindau disease, and tuberous sclerosis. On ultrasound, RCC is usually isoechoic to the renal cortex but can be hypo- or hyperechoic — it is not always hyperechoic. RCC has a propensity for venous invasion, which significantly alters the surgical approach.

updates.question_text: Regarding non-neoplastic solid renal masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Follow-up imaging is not required after antibiotic treatment for focal pyelonephritis
Asymmetric enhancement of the renal vein on the affected side excludes a renal AVM
Focal pyelonephritis can mimic a solid renal mass on imaging
Renal abscess can always be reliably differentiated from cystic RCC on imaging alone
A renal arteriovenous malformation (AVM) will avidly enhance and can mimic a hypervascular renal mass
options_after: Follow-up imaging is not required after antibiotic treatment for focal pyelonephritis
Asymmetric enhancement of the renal vein on the affected side excludes a renal AVM
Focal pyelonephritis can mimic a solid renal mass on imaging
Renal abscess can characteristically be reliably differentiated from cystic RCC on imaging alone
A renal arteriovenous malformation (AVM) will avidly enhance and can mimic a hypervascular renal mass
updates.explanation: The correct options are c and e. Focal pyelonephritis can mimic a solid renal mass, and a renal AVM can avidly enhance and mimic a hypervascular mass. Option b is incorrect because asymmetric enhancement of the ipsilateral renal vein is a clue to AVM from early venous shunting. Option d is incorrect because renal abscess may be difficult to distinguish from cystic RCC. Option a is incorrect because follow-up imaging is usually performed to confirm resolution after antibiotics.

updates.question_text: Regarding medical complications and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Renal PTLD demonstrates no Doppler flow on ultrasound, distinguishing it from fluid collections
PTLD is thought to result from immune suppression and Epstein-Barr virus proliferation
Acute rejection occurs after three months of transplant; chronic rejection occurs earlier
Acute tubular necrosis (ATN) is usually a sequela of pre-implantation ischaemia
Hyperacute rejection occurs within the first few hours of transplant and is due to ABO blood type incompatibility
options_after: Renal PTLD lacks Doppler flow on ultrasound, distinguishing it from fluid collections
PTLD is thought to result from immune suppression and Epstein-Barr virus proliferation
Acute rejection occurs after three months of transplant; chronic rejection occurs earlier
Acute tubular necrosis (ATN) is usually a sequela of pre-implantation ischaemia
Hyperacute rejection occurs within the first few hours of transplant and is due to ABO blood type incompatibility
updates.explanation: The correct options are b, d and e. Hyperacute rejection occurs within hours and relates to ABO incompatibility, ATN is usually due to pre-implantation ischaemia, and PTLD is linked to immune suppression and EBV proliferation. Option c is incorrect because acute rejection occurs within three months and chronic rejection after three months. Option a is incorrect because PTLD may simulate a fluid collection on greyscale, but unlike fluid it demonstrates Doppler flow.

updates.question_text:
A CT urogram demonstrates a bladder mass and a proximal ureteric filling defect.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding this appearance?
options_before: The bladder should be evaluated for a synchronous mass because TCC has a propensity for multifocal disease
A typical CTU appearance is a short segment of wall thickening, stricture or filling defect at the excretory phase
Transitional cell carcinoma is the most common ureteral neoplasm
Upper tract malignancy is common and accounts for most urothelial cancers
Multiple ureteral filling defects are never seen in transitional cell carcinoma
options_after: The bladder should be evaluated for a synchronous mass because TCC has a propensity for multifocal disease
A typical CTU appearance is a short segment of wall thickening, stricture or filling defect at the excretory phase
Transitional cell carcinoma is the most common ureteral neoplasm
Upper tract malignancy is common and accounts for most urothelial cancers
Multiple ureteral filling defects are not seen in transitional cell carcinoma
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, b and c. TCC is the commonest ureteral neoplasm, typically appears on CTU as short-segment wall thickening, stricture or filling defect, and the bladder should be checked because TCC is often multifocal. Option e is incorrect because multiple filling defects may be seen in 40%. Option d is incorrect because upper tract malignancy is relatively rare.

updates.question_text: Regarding benign and inflammatory ureteral lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fibroepithelial polyps typically affect the proximal ureter and may appear as elongated smooth tubular lesions
Fibroepithelial polyp is the most common benign tumour of the ureter
Ureteritis cystica has malignant potential and requires radical surgery
Ureteritis cystica is a malignant response to chronic urinary tract inflammation
Leukoplakia always indicates premalignant change when it involves the renal collecting system
options_after: Fibroepithelial polyps typically affect the proximal ureter and may appear as elongated smooth tubular lesions
Fibroepithelial polyp is the most common benign tumour of the ureter
Ureteritis cystica has malignant potential and requires radical surgery
Ureteritis cystica is a malignant response to chronic urinary tract inflammation
Leukoplakia characteristically indicates premalignant change when it involves the renal collecting system
updates.explanation: The correct options are a and b. Fibroepithelial polyp is the commonest benign ureteral tumour and usually affects the proximal ureter as an elongated smooth tubular lesion. Option d is incorrect because ureteritis cystica is a benign response to chronic urinary tract inflammation. Option c is incorrect because it has no malignant potential. Option e is incorrect because collecting-system leukoplakia is not thought to be premalignant, although bladder leukoplakia is associated with squamous cell carcinoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding bladder transitional cell carcinoma and its imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Transitional cell carcinoma is by far the most common bladder cancer
Complete bladder opacification is unnecessary because bladder masses are always conspicuous on CTU
Non-muscle-invasive organ-confined disease accounts for approximately 70% and is treated with radical cystectomy/nodal dissection
Bladder TCC typically presents with painless haematuria in older males with risk factors such as smoking and aromatic amines
If bladder cancer is clinically suspected with macroscopic haematuria, cystoscopy and urine cytology are warranted even if CTU does not show a lesion
options_after: Transitional cell carcinoma is by far the most common bladder cancer
Complete bladder opacification is unnecessary because bladder masses are characteristically conspicuous on CTU
Non-muscle-invasive organ-confined disease accounts for approximately 70% and is treated with radical cystectomy/nodal dissection
Bladder TCC typically presents with painless haematuria in older males with risk factors such as smoking and aromatic amines
If bladder cancer is clinically suspected with macroscopic haematuria, cystoscopy and urine cytology are warranted even if CTU does not show a lesion
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, d and e. Transitional cell carcinoma is the commonest bladder cancer, typically presenting with painless haematuria in older men with risk factors such as smoking and aromatic amines. If macroscopic haematuria raises clinical suspicion, cystoscopy and urine cytology are warranted even if CTU is negative. Option c is incorrect because non-muscle-invasive disease is typically resected endoscopically; muscle-invasive disease is treated with cystectomy and nodal dissection. Option b is incorrect because bladder masses can be subtle without complete opacification.

updates.question_text: Regarding utricle cysts and prostatitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Utricle cysts communicate freely with the urethra and may cause post-void dribbling
Acute bacterial prostatitis typically presents only with indolent local symptoms in older men
Utricle cysts are usually off-midline lesions diagnosed in patients aged 30-40 years
Chronic prostatitis usually occurs in older men with undertreated or recurrent acute prostatitis or lower urinary tract obstruction
A utricle cyst is usually a midline cystic structure within the prostate posterior to the urethra
options_after: Utricle cysts communicate freely with the urethra and may cause post-void dribbling
Acute bacterial prostatitis typically presents primarily with indolent local symptoms in older men
Utricle cysts are usually off-midline lesions diagnosed in patients aged 30-40 years
Chronic prostatitis usually occurs in older men with undertreated or recurrent acute prostatitis or lower urinary tract obstruction
A utricle cyst is usually a midline cystic structure within the prostate posterior to the urethra
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, d and e. Utricle cysts are midline cystic structures posterior to the urethra that freely communicate with it and can cause post-void dribbling. Chronic prostatitis usually occurs in older men with undertreated/recurrent acute prostatitis or lower urinary tract obstruction. Option c is incorrect because off-midline lesions in patients aged 30-40 years are more typical of Mullerian duct cysts. Option b is incorrect because acute bacterial prostatitis usually presents with local and systemic symptoms in young men.

updates.question_text: Regarding prostate cancer MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Prostate cancer typically shows restricted diffusion, low T2 signal and early enhancement relative to the surrounding peripheral zone
Prostatitis and prostate cancer can be reliably distinguished because prostatitis never enhances early
Low Gleason grade (<7) prostate cancers are typically conspicuous on MRI
Most prostate cancers (90%) occur in the peripheral zone
MRI spectroscopy is routinely performed in most centres for prostate cancer
options_after: Prostate cancer typically shows restricted diffusion, low T2 signal and early enhancement relative to the surrounding peripheral zone
Prostatitis and prostate cancer can be reliably distinguished because prostatitis will not enhance early
Low Gleason grade (<7) prostate cancers are typically conspicuous on MRI
Most prostate cancers (90%) occur in the peripheral zone
MRI spectroscopy is routinely performed in most centres for prostate cancer
updates.explanation: The correct options are a and d. Most prostate cancers occur in the peripheral zone, and prostate cancer typically shows restricted diffusion, low T2 signal and early enhancement. Option c is incorrect because low Gleason grade cancers are typically not detectable on MRI. Option b is incorrect because prostatitis and prostate cancer may both show increased and early enhancement. Option e is incorrect because MR spectroscopy is not routinely performed in most centres.

updates.question_text: Regarding Fournier gangrene and the general approach to testicular masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fournier gangrene is highly morbid and surgically emergent
Fournier gangrene is necrotising fasciitis of the scrotum and perineum
Most extratesticular masses in adults are malignant
Intratesticular masses are usually benign, with only 5-10% being malignant
The key CT finding in Fournier gangrene is subcutaneous gas
options_after: Fournier gangrene is highly morbid and surgically emergent
Fournier gangrene is necrotising fasciitis of the scrotum and perineum
Most extratesticular masses in adults are malignant
The malignancy rate of intratesticular masses is approximately 5-10%.
The key CT finding in Fournier gangrene is subcutaneous gas
updates.explanation: The correct options are a, b and e. Fournier gangrene is surgically emergent necrotising fasciitis of the scrotum and perineum, and CT key finding is subcutaneous gas. Option d is incorrect because intratesticular masses are usually malignant, 90-95%. Option c is incorrect because most adult extratesticular masses are benign.

updates.question_text: Regarding malignant germ cell tumours of the testis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Choriocarcinoma is the most common NSGCT and has the best prognosis
Seminoma is the most common testicular malignancy and has a favourable prognosis
It is possible to distinguish all NSGCT subtypes reliably on ultrasound
Seminoma accounts for about half of all germ cell tumours and is usually more homogeneous than NSGCT
Mixed germ cell tumour is the most common NSGCT and the second most common primary testicular malignancy after seminoma
options_after: Choriocarcinoma is the most common NSGCT and has the best prognosis
Seminoma is the most common testicular malignancy and has a favourable prognosis
It is possible to distinguish most NSGCT subtypes reliably on ultrasound
Seminoma accounts for about half of all germ cell tumours and is usually more homogeneous than NSGCT
Mixed germ cell tumour is the most common NSGCT and the second most common primary testicular malignancy after seminoma
updates.explanation: The correct options are b, d and e. Seminoma is the commonest testicular malignancy, accounts for about half of GCTs and is usually more homogeneous than NSGCT; mixed GCT is the commonest NSGCT and second commonest primary testicular malignancy after seminoma. Option a is incorrect because choriocarcinoma is rare and aggressive, with early metastases. Option c is incorrect because NSGCT subtypes cannot be reliably distinguished on ultrasound.

updates.question_text: Regarding testicular microlithiasis, metastases and benign tumours, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Current guidelines support routine ultrasound and tumour-marker screening for all patients with microlithiasis
An epidermoid is a keratin-filled cyst with an onion-skin appearance
At least 50 microcalcifications per image are required to call microlithiasis; fewer than 50 is limited microlithiasis
Testicular microlithiasis is multiple punctate intratesticular calcifications
Leukaemia and lymphoma are the most common metastases to the testes
options_after: Current guidelines support routine ultrasound and tumour-marker screening for most patients with microlithiasis
An epidermoid is a keratin-filled cyst with an onion-skin appearance
At least 50 microcalcifications per image are required to call microlithiasis; fewer than 50 is limited microlithiasis
Testicular microlithiasis is multiple punctate intratesticular calcifications
Leukaemia and lymphoma are the most common metastases to the testes
updates.explanation: The correct options are b, d and e. Testicular microlithiasis is multiple punctate intratesticular calcifications; leukaemia and lymphoma are the commonest metastases to the testes; and epidermoid is a keratin-filled cyst with onion-skin appearance. Option c is incorrect because at least 5, not 50, microcalcifications per image are required. Option a is incorrect because current guidelines do not support routine ultrasound or tumour-marker screening for all patients with microlithiasis.

updates.question_text: Regarding uterine anatomy and position, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The fundus is superior to the ostia of the fallopian tubes
The uterine body is the lower third of the uterus
Version refers to the angle between the cervix and vagina
Retroflexion improves transabdominal visualisation of the fundus and cannot mimic a fibroid
Flexion refers to the angle between the cervix and vagina
options_after: The fundus is superior to the ostia of the fallopian tubes
The uterine body is the lower third of the uterus
Version refers to the angle between the cervix and vagina
Retroflexion improves transabdominal visualisation of the fundus and will not mimic a fibroid
Flexion refers to the angle between the cervix and vagina
updates.explanation: The fundus is superior to the tubal ostia, and version is the angle between the cervix and vagina. Flexion is the angle between the uterine body and cervix, not another term for version. The uterine body forms the upper two-thirds of the uterus. Retroversion and retroflexion can impair transabdominal visualisation; retroflexion can also mimic an intramural fibroid.

updates.question_text: Regarding endometrial polyp and endometrial hyperplasia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Endometrial polyps are always asymptomatic and do not cause intermenstrual bleeding
Larger polyps >1.5 cm in postmenopausal patients may have malignant potential
Sonohysterography is more definitive than routine ultrasound for diagnosing a polyp
Endometrial hyperplasia results from unopposed oestrogen stimulation
Endometrial hyperplasia is driven by progesterone excess rather than oestrogenic stimulation
options_after: Endometrial polyps are characteristically asymptomatic and do not cause intermenstrual bleeding
Larger polyps >1.5 cm in postmenopausal patients may have malignant potential
Sonohysterography is more definitive than routine ultrasound for diagnosing a polyp
Endometrial hyperplasia results from unopposed oestrogen stimulation
Endometrial hyperplasia is driven by progesterone excess rather than oestrogenic stimulation
updates.explanation: Endometrial polyps can cause mucous discharge or irregular intermenstrual bleeding, so they are not always asymptomatic. Larger polyps over 1.5 cm in postmenopausal patients may have malignant potential. Sonohysterography is more definitive than routine ultrasound for diagnosing a polyp. Endometrial hyperplasia reflects unopposed oestrogen stimulation, and imaging cannot reliably distinguish hyperplasia, metaplasia and carcinoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding postmenopausal endometrial thickness management in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Postmenopausal bleeding with endometrial thickness >=5 mm needs workup in the chart, noting ACOG uses 4 mm
Endometrial thickness <5 mm with bleeding mandates workup in all patients according to the chart
Focal endometrial thickening requires workup regardless of thickness
Tamoxifen use lowers the risk of endometrial cancer and raises the threshold for workup
The management approach applies only if the entire endometrial lining is visualised
options_after: Postmenopausal bleeding with endometrial thickness >=5 mm needs workup in the chart, noting ACOG uses 4 mm
Endometrial thickness <5 mm with bleeding mandates workup in most patients according to the chart
Focal endometrial thickening requires workup regardless of thickness
Tamoxifen use lowers the risk of endometrial cancer and raises the threshold for workup
The management approach applies only if the entire endometrial lining is visualised
updates.explanation: The chart uses >=5 mm as a workup threshold for postmenopausal bleeding, while noting that ACOG uses 4 mm. If bleeding is present but the endometrium is <5 mm, malignancy risk is low and bleeding is likely due to atrophy rather than automatically mandating workup. Focal thickening requires workup regardless of thickness. Tamoxifen increases endometrial cancer risk, and the chart explicitly applies only when the entire endometrial lining is visualised.

updates.question_text:
Sagittal T2 and postcontrast fat-suppressed T1 MRI show an endometrial mass with myometrial invasion >50% and no definite cervical stromal invasion.

Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In a postmenopausal patient, an intact junctional zone reliably confirms no myometrial invasion
MRI can be used for staging after endometrial carcinoma is confirmed histologically
Presence and depth of myometrial invasion are key for staging
Depth of myometrial invasion has no relationship to lymph node metastasis
FIGO staging considers spread to cervix, vagina, serosa/adnexa, bladder/bowel, nodes and distant sites
options_after: In a postmenopausal patient, an intact junctional zone reliably confirms absent myometrial invasion
MRI can be used for staging after endometrial carcinoma is confirmed histologically
Presence and depth of myometrial invasion are key for staging
Depth of myometrial invasion lacks relationship to lymph node metastasis
FIGO staging considers spread to cervix, vagina, serosa/adnexa, bladder/bowel, nodes and distant sites
updates.explanation: MRI is used for staging once the diagnosis has been confirmed histologically. Endometrial FIGO staging includes cervix, vagina, serosa, adnexa, adjacent bladder/bowel, inguinal nodes and distant metastases. Myometrial invasion is central to staging, and its depth correlates strongly with nodal metastasis. The junctional zone can confirm absence of myometrial invasion in premenopausal patients; it cannot be distinguished in postmenopausal patients.

updates.question_text: Regarding endometrial cavity fluid, infection and haemorrhage, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Trace endometrial fluid can be normal, particularly in premenopausal patients
Pyometra is common and is usually unrelated to outflow obstruction
In postmenopausal women, endometrial fluid can be due to cervical stenosis and should prompt careful evaluation for cervical malignancy
Gas in the uterus within the first three weeks postpartum is always suspicious for endometritis
Endometritis is commonly seen postpartum and uncomplicated cases may have normal imaging
options_after: Trace endometrial fluid can be normal, particularly in premenopausal patients
Pyometra is common and is usually unrelated to outflow obstruction
In postmenopausal women, endometrial fluid can be due to cervical stenosis and should prompt careful evaluation for cervical malignancy
Gas in the uterus within the first three weeks postpartum is characteristically suspicious for endometritis
Endometritis is commonly seen postpartum and uncomplicated cases may have normal imaging
updates.explanation: Trace endometrial canal fluid may be normal, especially in premenopausal patients. In postmenopausal women it may be due to cervical stenosis, and cervical malignancy should be excluded. Endometritis is commonly postpartum and imaging can be normal in uncomplicated cases. Gas in the uterus can be seen up to three weeks postpartum in normal cases; gas more than three weeks postpartum is suspicious. Pyometra is very rare and usually reflects outflow obstruction, often from cervical malignancy.

updates.question_text:
An enhancing anterior abdominal wall lesion is shown at a Caesarean section scar.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding endometriosis?
options_before: Superficial endometriotic implants are typically large and readily visible on MRI
Endometriosis is ectopic endometrial tissue outside the endometrial cavity
Deep infiltrating endometriosis is defined by invasion at least 5 mm beyond the peritoneal surface
Ovarian endometrioma is typically T1 hyperintense and T2 hypointense on MRI
Endometriosis never occurs in surgical scars or outside the pelvis
options_after: Superficial endometriotic implants are typically large and readily visible on MRI
Endometriosis is ectopic endometrial tissue outside the endometrial cavity
Deep infiltrating endometriosis is defined by invasion at least 5 mm beyond the peritoneal surface
Ovarian endometrioma is typically T1 hyperintense and T2 hypointense on MRI
Endometriosis will not occur in surgical scars or outside the pelvis
updates.explanation: Endometriosis is ectopic endometrial tissue outside the endometrial cavity. It may occur as superficial implants, ovarian endometriomas or deep infiltrating disease. Deep infiltrating disease extends at least 5 mm beyond the peritoneal surface. Endometriomas are typically T1 hyperintense and T2 hypointense. Superficial implants are usually small and not visible on MRI, and less common sites include Caesarean scars and distant organs.

updates.question_text: Regarding adenomyosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adenomyosis is ectopic endometrial tissue outside the uterus with no myometrial involvement
Adenomyosis is ectopic endometrial tissue within the myometrium
Borderline junctional zone thickening of 8-12 mm is diagnostic of adenomyosis
Ultrasound classically shows a sharply marginated focal myometrial mass with a lobular external uterine contour
T2-weighted MRI shows diffuse or focal junctional zone thickening >12 mm
options_after: Adenomyosis is ectopic endometrial tissue outside the uterus without myometrial involvement
Adenomyosis is ectopic endometrial tissue within the myometrium
Borderline junctional zone thickening of 8-12 mm is diagnostic of adenomyosis
Ultrasound classically shows a sharply marginated focal myometrial mass with a lobular external uterine contour
T2-weighted MRI shows diffuse or focal junctional zone thickening >12 mm
updates.explanation: Adenomyosis is endometriosis interna, with ectopic endometrial tissue in the myometrium. MRI shows diffuse or focal junctional zone thickening >12 mm, often with small T2-hyperintense foci. Borderline thickening of 8-12 mm may be due to adenomyosis but is not diagnostic. Ultrasound may show an enlarged uterus with heterogeneous myometrium and no focal mass; a well-defined focal mass with lobular contour is more typical of leiomyoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian and fallopian tube anatomy and physiology, which of the following statements are correct?
