options_before: The ampulla is the narrowest fallopian tube segment
The ovarian artery arises directly from the aorta and supplies the lateral aspect of the ovary
The uterine artery branch arises from the internal iliac artery and supplies the medial aspect of the ovary
The fallopian tube segments from proximal to distal are interstitial, isthmus, ampulla and infundibulum
The ovary has a single arterial supply exclusively from the internal iliac artery
options_after: The ampulla is the narrowest fallopian tube segment
The ovarian artery arises directly from the aorta and supplies the lateral aspect of the ovary
The uterine artery branch arises from the internal iliac artery and supplies the medial aspect of the ovary
The fallopian tube segments from proximal to distal are interstitial, isthmus, ampulla and infundibulum
The ovary has a single arterial supply predominantly from the internal iliac artery
updates.explanation: The ovary has dual blood supply: the ovarian artery arises directly from the aorta and supplies the lateral ovary, while a uterine artery branch from the internal iliac supplies the medial ovary. The fallopian tube segments from proximal to distal are interstitial/intramural, isthmus, ampulla and infundibulum. The interstitial/intramural segment is the narrowest, not the ampulla.

updates.question_text:
MRI shows an enlarged right ovary displaced into the pouch of Douglas with oedematous central stroma and peripheral follicles.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding adnexal torsion?
options_before: It results from twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle
It occurs mainly in reproductive-age women and commonly occurs in pregnancy
Lack of colour Doppler flow must always be present to diagnose torsion
A large adnexal mass, most commonly ovarian dermoid, may act as a lead point
It is more common on the right because the sigmoid colon inhibits free rotation of the left adnexa
options_after: It results from twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle
It occurs mainly in reproductive-age women and commonly occurs in pregnancy
Lack of colour Doppler flow must characteristically be present to diagnose torsion
A large adnexal mass, most commonly ovarian dermoid, may act as a lead point
It is more common on the right because the sigmoid colon inhibits free rotation of the left adnexa
updates.explanation: Adnexal torsion is twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle causing pain and possible vascular compromise. It mainly affects reproductive-age women, can occur in pregnancy, and is more common on the right because the sigmoid colon limits left adnexal mobility. A large adnexal mass, particularly an ovarian dermoid, is a common lead point. Doppler flow may persist because of dual ovarian blood supply or intermittent torsion/detorsion.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging features of adnexal torsion, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Twisting of the ovarian pedicle is common but has no diagnostic significance on CT or MRI
Whirlpool sign is very specific but not often seen
Enlarged ovary >4 cm is a common but nonspecific finding
Lack of Doppler flow is always present before torsion can be diagnosed
Follicles may be pushed to the ovarian periphery
options_after: Twisting of the ovarian pedicle is common but lacks diagnostic significance on CT or MRI
Whirlpool sign is very specific but not often seen
Enlarged ovary >4 cm is a common but nonspecific finding
Lack of Doppler flow is characteristically present before torsion can be diagnosed
Follicles may be pushed to the ovarian periphery
updates.explanation: The classic ultrasound pattern includes an enlarged oedematous ovary, abnormal Doppler and free fluid. Whirlpool sign is very specific but uncommon. Less specific common features include ovary >4 cm, abnormal position and peripheral follicles. Doppler findings are variable and flow may persist. On CT or MRI, twisting of the pedicle is uncommon but pathognomonic when identified.

updates.question_text: Regarding follow-up of ovarian cysts in the SRU consensus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In postmenopausal women, indeterminate but probably benign cysts require no follow-up or surgical consideration
A cyst stable in size for two years can be considered benign with no further imaging follow-up
A cyst decreasing in size by >10-15% in average linear dimension can be considered benign with no further follow-up
If a presumed haemorrhagic cyst does not resolve, endometrioma is considered
Haemorrhagic cysts >5 cm are ignored if colour Doppler shows no internal flow
options_after: A postmenopausal patient with an indeterminate but probably benign cyst can be discharged from imaging follow-up.
A cyst stable in size for two years can be considered benign with no further imaging follow-up
A cyst decreasing in size by >10-15% in average linear dimension can be considered benign with no further follow-up
If a presumed haemorrhagic cyst does not resolve, endometrioma is considered
Haemorrhagic cysts >5 cm are ignored if colour Doppler fails to show internal flow
updates.explanation: On follow-up, stability for two years or decrease by >10-15% in average linear dimension supports benignity and no further imaging. Haemorrhagic cysts >5 cm require short-term ultrasound follow-up at 6-12 weeks, and failure to resolve raises consideration of endometrioma. Indeterminate but probably benign cysts in postmenopausal women should be considered for surgical evaluation.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian neoplasm histology and risk stratification, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: O-RADS provides a definitive histological classification of ovarian neoplasms
Primary ovarian neoplasms include epithelial, germ cell and sex cord-stromal tumours
Meigs syndrome is the triad of benign ovarian fibroma, ascites and right pleural effusion
Tumours containing thecal cells may produce oestrogen and cause endometrial carcinoma
Surface epithelial tumours account for only 10% of ovarian cancers
options_after: O-RADS provides a definitive histological classification of ovarian neoplasms
Primary ovarian neoplasms include epithelial, germ cell and sex cord-stromal tumours
Meigs syndrome is the triad of benign ovarian fibroma, ascites and right pleural effusion
Tumours containing thecal cells may produce oestrogen and cause endometrial carcinoma
Surface epithelial tumours account for approximately 10% of ovarian cancers
updates.explanation: Primary ovarian neoplasms include epithelial, germ cell and sex cord-stromal tumours. Surface epithelial tumours account for 70% of ovarian neoplasms overall and more than 90% of ovarian cancers. Meigs syndrome is benign ovarian fibroma with ascites and right pleural effusion. Tumours containing thecal cells may produce oestrogen and cause endometrial carcinoma. O-RADS is a risk-stratification system, not a definitive histological classification.

updates.question_text: Regarding ovarian cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mucinous cystadenocarcinomas are usually bilateral and smaller than serous cystadenocarcinomas
Approximately 90% of malignant ovarian tumours are epithelial in origin
Serous tumours are the most common epithelial subtype
Endometrioid and clear cell carcinoma have no association with endometriosis
Ovarian cancer ranks fifth in cancer deaths among women
options_after: Mucinous cystadenocarcinomas are usually bilateral and smaller than serous cystadenocarcinomas
Approximately 90% of malignant ovarian tumours are epithelial in origin
Serous tumours are the most common epithelial subtype
Endometrioid and clear cell carcinoma lack association with endometriosis
Ovarian cancer ranks fifth in cancer deaths among women
updates.explanation: Ovarian cancer is the tenth most common female malignancy but ranks fifth in cancer deaths among women because it often presents late. Approximately 90% of malignant tumours are epithelial, with serous the most common subtype followed by mucinous, endometrioid and clear cell. Mucinous cystadenocarcinomas are large, most commonly unilateral, and occur in older patients compared with serous tumours. Clear cell and less commonly endometrioid carcinoma are linked to endometriosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding metastatic ovarian disease and Krukenberg tumour, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Endometrial cancer never metastasises to the ovaries
Ovarian metastases may arise from gastric, colon, pancreatic, breast cancer and melanoma
Ovarian metastases are usually unilateral and this helps distinguish them from primary tumours
A Krukenberg tumour is an ovarian metastasis of a mucin-producing tumour, typically gastric or colonic adenocarcinoma
Metastases to the ovary are common and account for most ovarian masses
options_after: Endometrial cancer will not metastasise to the ovaries
Ovarian metastases may arise from gastric, colon, pancreatic, breast cancer and melanoma
Ovarian metastases are usually unilateral and this helps distinguish them from primary tumours
A Krukenberg tumour is an ovarian metastasis of a mucin-producing tumour, typically gastric or colonic adenocarcinoma
Metastases to the ovary are common and account for most ovarian masses
updates.explanation: The source says ovarian metastases are uncommon but may arise from gastric, colon, pancreatic, breast cancer and melanoma, and are often bilateral. Krukenberg tumour is an ovarian metastasis from a mucin-producing tumour, usually gastric or colonic adenocarcinoma. Endometrial cancer may also metastasise to the ovaries.

updates.question_text: Regarding paraovarian cyst and peritoneal inclusion cyst, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A paraovarian cyst is a simple cyst separate from the ovary
Surgery is recommended for peritoneal inclusion cyst because it prevents additional adhesions
Ovarian cysts should be reported and followed if >3 cm, while paraovarian cysts need no follow-up unless >5 cm
A peritoneal inclusion cyst is a septated fluid collection formed by adhesions, almost always related to prior surgery
Paraovarian cysts are considered normal only if <3 cm
options_after: A paraovarian cyst is a simple cyst separate from the ovary
Surgery is recommended for peritoneal inclusion cyst because it prevents additional adhesions
Ovarian cysts should be reported and followed if >3 cm, while paraovarian cysts need no follow-up unless >5 cm
A peritoneal inclusion cyst is a septated fluid collection formed by adhesions, almost always related to prior surgery
Paraovarian cysts are considered normal primarily if <3 cm
updates.explanation: Paraovarian cysts are simple cysts separate from the ovary and are considered normal if <5 cm. The source contrasts them with ovarian cysts, which should be reported and followed if >3 cm, whereas paraovarian cysts are not followed unless >5 cm. Peritoneal inclusion cysts are septated fluid collections related to adhesions, usually after surgery, with the ovary trapped in or adjacent to the collection. Surgery should not be recommended because it can create further adhesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging of sinus disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI is the primary modality for bony detail of the sinuses.
Imaging is routinely appropriate for acute uncomplicated rhinosinusitis.
CT is the primary modality for evaluating bony sinus detail.
Routine sinus MRI is reliable because inspissated secretions always remain high signal.
MRI can distinguish enhancing mucosal lesions from obstructed secretions when a sinonasal mass or complication is suspected.
options_after: MRI is the primary modality for bony detail of the sinuses.
Imaging is routinely appropriate for acute uncomplicated rhinosinusitis.
CT is the primary modality for evaluating bony sinus detail.
Routine sinus MRI is reliable because inspissated secretions characteristically remain high signal.
MRI can distinguish enhancing mucosal lesions from obstructed secretions when a sinonasal mass or complication is suspected.
updates.explanation: CT is the main modality for evaluating bony sinus anatomy and preoperative detail. MRI is most useful when orbital or intracranial complications or a sinonasal mass are suspected, because enhancement helps distinguish mucosal lesions from obstructed secretions. MRI is unreliable for routine sinus disease because sinus contents can have variable signal and low signal inspissated secretions can mimic aeration.

updates.question_text: Regarding complications of rhinosinusitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Orbital spread may cause preseptal cellulitis, orbital cellulitis, orbital abscess or subperiosteal abscess.
Cranial spread is limited to extradural disease and cannot cause brain abscess.
The temporal lobe is stated to be the typical site of sinogenic brain abscess.
Acute frontal sinusitis complicated by osteomyelitis and subgaleal/subperiosteal abscess is Pott's puffy tumour.
Cranial spread may cause meningitis, cerebritis or suppurative collections.
options_after: Orbital spread may cause preseptal cellulitis, orbital cellulitis, orbital abscess or subperiosteal abscess.
Cranial spread is limited to extradural disease and will not cause brain abscess.
The temporal lobe is stated to be the typical site of sinogenic brain abscess.
Acute frontal sinusitis complicated by osteomyelitis and subgaleal/subperiosteal abscess is Pott's puffy tumour.
Cranial spread may cause meningitis, cerebritis or suppurative collections.
updates.explanation: Orbital complications include preseptal cellulitis, orbital cellulitis, orbital abscess, subperiosteal abscess and septic venous thrombosis. Intracranial spread can produce meningitis, cerebritis, epidural abscess, subdural empyema or brain abscess, with the frontal lobe being the typical site for sinogenic brain abscess. Pott's puffy tumour is frontal sinusitis complicated by osteomyelitis and subgaleal or subperiosteal abscess.

updates.question_text: Regarding sinonasal and anterior skull base malignancies, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignant neoplasm in the sinonasal tract.
Imaging can usually predict exact histology with confidence for most sinonasal malignancies.
Imaging should localise the tumour and evaluate extent of disease because this affects treatment approach.
Sinonasal malignancies usually remodel bone without destruction and show no enhancement.
Many sinonasal malignancies have intermediate T2 signal and restricted diffusion owing to high cellularity.
options_after: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignant neoplasm in the sinonasal tract.
Imaging can usually predict exact histology with confidence for most sinonasal malignancies.
Imaging should localise the tumour and evaluate extent of disease because this affects treatment approach.
Sinonasal malignancies usually remodel bone without destruction and fail to show enhancement.
Many sinonasal malignancies have intermediate T2 signal and restricted diffusion owing to high cellularity.
updates.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma is the commonest sinonasal malignancy, but a broad range of other histologies exists. Imaging often cannot confidently predict histology, so its key role is localisation and disease extent assessment. Aggressive bony destruction, heterogeneous enhancement, intermediate T2 signal and restricted diffusion are important malignant features.

updates.question_text: Regarding selected sinonasal malignancy subtypes, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a surface epithelial tumour most strongly associated with wood dust exposure.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma is the most common sinonasal tumour of minor salivary gland origin.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma has the highest risk of perineural spread and commonly affects CN V2 in the sinonasal tract.
Intestinal-type adenocarcinoma is strongly associated with occupational wood dust exposure.
Sinonasal adenocarcinomas are divided only into viral and post-traumatic types.
options_after: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a surface epithelial tumour most strongly associated with wood dust exposure.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma is the most common sinonasal tumour of minor salivary gland origin.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma has the highest risk of perineural spread and commonly affects CN V2 in the sinonasal tract.
Intestinal-type adenocarcinoma is strongly associated with occupational wood dust exposure.
Sinonasal adenocarcinomas are divided primarily into viral and post-traumatic types.
updates.explanation: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is the commonest sinonasal tumour of minor salivary gland origin and carries the highest risk of perineural tumour spread, often along CN V2. Sinonasal adenocarcinomas arise from surface epithelial glands and are divided into intestinal and nonintestinal types. Intestinal-type adenocarcinoma is strongly linked to occupational wood dust exposure.

updates.question_text: Regarding olfactory neuroblastoma and mucosal melanoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Olfactory neuroblastoma arises from olfactory epithelium in the superior nasal cavity.
Olfactory neuroblastoma arises from the inferior turbinate and never extends intracranially.
Cysts at the margin of an intracranial component argue strongly against olfactory neuroblastoma.
Mucosal melanoma is commoner than cutaneous melanoma.
The head and neck, most commonly the sinonasal tract, is the most common site for mucosal melanoma.
options_after: Olfactory neuroblastoma arises from olfactory epithelium in the superior nasal cavity.
Olfactory neuroblastoma arises from the inferior turbinate and will not extend intracranially.
Cysts at the margin of an intracranial component argue strongly against olfactory neuroblastoma.
Mucosal melanoma is commoner than cutaneous melanoma.
The head and neck, most commonly the sinonasal tract, is the most common site for mucosal melanoma.
updates.explanation: Olfactory neuroblastoma is a malignant neural crest-derived tumour arising from olfactory epithelium in the superior nasal cavity. When it extends intracranially, cysts at the tumour-brain interface are highly suggestive. Mucosal melanoma is uncommon compared with cutaneous melanoma; in the mucosal category, the head and neck, particularly the sinonasal tract, is the most common site.

updates.question_text: Post-contrast MRI and diffusion imaging show rim-enhancing extra-axial collections complicating acute frontal sinusitis. Which statement is supported by the source?
options_before: Sinogenic infection cannot spread intracranially.
Restricted diffusion excludes empyema.
The typical sinogenic brain abscess site is the cerebellum.
Acute frontal sinusitis may be complicated by epidural abscess and subdural empyema.
Orbital spread is limited to isolated preseptal swelling.
options_after: Sinogenic infection will not spread intracranially.
Restricted diffusion excludes empyema.
The typical sinogenic brain abscess site is the cerebellum.
Acute frontal sinusitis may be complicated by epidural abscess and subdural empyema.
Orbital spread is limited to isolated preseptal swelling.
updates.explanation: The source illustrates acute frontal sinusitis complicated by epidural and subdural empyemas with rim enhancement and restricted diffusion. Intracranial complications also include meningitis, cerebritis and brain abscess, with the frontal lobe being the typical sinogenic brain abscess location. Orbital complications include several postseptal entities, not only preseptal cellulitis.

updates.question_text: A child has a midline nasal lesion on MRI/CT. Which of the following statements are correct regarding congenital nasal masses?
options_before: Nasal glioma should demonstrate continuity with intracranial contents on MRI.
Frontoethmoidal encephalocele is excluded if the mass lies near the glabella or nasal cavity.
MRI best demonstrates whether an encephalocele is contiguous with intracranial contents.
Dermoid cysts always lack fat density or signal.
Epidermoid cysts may show restricted diffusion.
options_after: Nasal glioma should demonstrate continuity with intracranial contents on MRI.
Frontoethmoidal encephalocele is excluded if the mass lies near the glabella or nasal cavity.
MRI best demonstrates whether an encephalocele is contiguous with intracranial contents.
Dermoid cysts characteristically lack fat density or signal.
Epidermoid cysts may show restricted diffusion.
updates.explanation: MRI is the key modality for showing continuity of an encephalocele with intracranial contents. Frontoethmoidal encephaloceles may protrude at the glabella, nasal cavity or medial orbit depending on the skull base defect. Dermoids may contain fat, epidermoids may restrict diffusion, and nasal glial heterotopia lacks intracranial communication.

updates.question_text: Regarding the orbital apex and orbital fissures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The optic canal transmits the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery.
The maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve passes through the superior orbital fissure before entering the orbit.
The inferior orbital fissure contains all cavernous sinus cranial nerves except V2.
The superior orbital fissure transmits CN III, CN IV, CN V1, CN VI and the superior ophthalmic vein.
The annulus of Zinn is unrelated to the orbital apex.
options_after: The optic canal transmits the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery.
The maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve passes through the superior orbital fissure before entering the orbit.
The inferior orbital fissure contains most cavernous sinus cranial nerves except V2.
The superior orbital fissure transmits CN III, CN IV, CN V1, CN VI and the superior ophthalmic vein.
The annulus of Zinn is unrelated to the orbital apex.
updates.explanation: The optic canal contains the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery. The superior orbital fissure contains the cavernous sinus cranial nerves other than V2, including CN III, IV, V1 and VI, as well as venous drainage including the superior ophthalmic vein. CN V2 passes through foramen rotundum and gives branches that reach the inferior orbital fissure via the pterygopalatine fossa. The orbital apex is defined around the optic canal, superior and inferior orbital fissures and the annulus of Zinn.

updates.question_text: Regarding thyroid-associated orbitopathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It occurs only in patients who are biochemically hyperthyroid.
It is usually associated with Graves disease.
It can occur in patients with euthyroid or hypothyroid autoimmune thyroiditis.
Its pathogenesis includes glycosaminoglycan overproduction by fibroblasts and adipogenesis.
Severe muscle enlargement can crowd the orbital apex and cause dysthyroid optic neuropathy.
options_after: It occurs primarily in patients who are biochemically hyperthyroid.
It is usually associated with Graves disease.
It can occur in patients with euthyroid or hypothyroid autoimmune thyroiditis.
Its pathogenesis includes glycosaminoglycan overproduction by fibroblasts and adipogenesis.
Severe muscle enlargement can crowd the orbital apex and cause dysthyroid optic neuropathy.
updates.explanation: Thyroid-associated orbitopathy is usually linked to Graves disease but may also occur with euthyroid or hypothyroid autoimmune thyroiditis. The source attributes the orbital changes to inflammation, fibroblast overproduction of glycosaminoglycans and adipogenesis. Severe muscle enlargement can crowd the orbital apex, causing dysthyroid optic neuropathy that may require decompression if steroid treatment fails.

updates.question_text: Regarding causes and imaging evolution of optic neuritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Optic neuritis is limited to multiple sclerosis and has no other inflammatory causes.
NMOSD and MOG antibody-associated disease are not included among the source causes.
The chronic phase is characterised by persistent optic nerve enlargement without atrophy.
Acutely, the optic nerve may enlarge and show T2 prolongation and contrast enhancement.
Chronically, the optic nerve may atrophy.
options_after: Optic neuritis is limited to multiple sclerosis and lacks other inflammatory causes.
NMOSD and MOG antibody-associated disease are not included among the source causes.
The chronic phase is characterised by persistent optic nerve enlargement without atrophy.
Acutely, the optic nerve may enlarge and show T2 prolongation and contrast enhancement.
Chronically, the optic nerve may atrophy.
updates.explanation: The source lists several causes of optic neuritis, including MS, NMOSD, MOG antibody-associated disease, ischaemic optic neuropathy, viral infection, sarcoidosis, lupus and CRION. Acute imaging may show enlargement, T2 prolongation and contrast enhancement. Chronic disease may lead to optic nerve atrophy.

updates.question_text: Regarding compartment-based localisation of orbital masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The lacrimal gland is an extraconal structure.
The ocular compartment is the conal compartment formed by rectus muscles.
The intraconal compartment contains the optic nerve-sheath complex and fat central to the myofascial cone.
All orbital lesions obey strict fascial boundaries between intraconal and extraconal spaces.
The extraconal compartment excludes fat and contains only bone.
options_after: The lacrimal gland is an extraconal structure.
The ocular compartment is the conal compartment formed by rectus muscles.
The intraconal compartment contains the optic nerve-sheath complex and fat central to the myofascial cone.
Most orbital lesions obey strict fascial boundaries between intraconal and extraconal spaces.
The extraconal compartment excludes fat and contains primarily bone.
updates.explanation: The lacrimal gland is located in the extraconal compartment. The intraconal space contains the optic nerve-sheath complex, central neurovascular structures and fat within the myofascial cone. The ocular compartment is the globe. The source emphasises that real orbital fascial planes are more complex than the classic intraconal/extraconal model and may be crossed by pathology.

updates.question_text: Regarding cavernous venous malformation and orbital varix, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Venous malformations are encapsulated slow-flow vascular malformations and are the most common orbital mass in adults.
Orbital varices are isolated solid tumours without connection to the normal circulation.
Cavernous venous malformations are usually extraconal and never intraconal.
Orbital varices commonly present with intermittent positional or stress proptosis.
Orbital varices can be distinguished by dynamic distension during Valsalva manoeuvre or prone positioning.
options_after: Venous malformations are encapsulated slow-flow vascular malformations and are the most common orbital mass in adults.
Orbital varices are isolated solid tumours without connection to the normal circulation.
An intraconal location effectively excludes a cavernous venous malformation.
Orbital varices commonly present with intermittent positional or stress proptosis.
Orbital varices can be distinguished by dynamic distension during Valsalva manoeuvre or prone positioning.
updates.explanation: Cavernous venous malformations are encapsulated slow-flow lesions and are described as the most common orbital mass in adults, usually intraconal though not exclusively. Orbital varices are distended veins connected to normal circulation. Their key diagnostic behaviour is dynamic enlargement with increased venous pressure, such as Valsalva or prone positioning, and they often present with intermittent positional or stress proptosis.

updates.question_text: Axial contrast-enhanced CT shows a large posterior globe outpouching in the region of the optic disc. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The main diagnosis is globe rupture because all posterior outpouchings are acute open-globe injuries.
The finding is compatible with an ocular coloboma.
The lesion may be associated with microphthalmia and a retrobulbar cyst.
The expected syndrome association is isolated Graves disease.
Colobomas are associated with syndromes including trisomies 13 and 18 and CHARGE syndrome.
options_after: The main diagnosis is globe rupture because most posterior outpouchings are acute open-globe injuries.
The finding is compatible with an ocular coloboma.
The lesion may be associated with microphthalmia and a retrobulbar cyst.
The expected syndrome association is isolated Graves disease.
Colobomas are associated with syndromes including trisomies 13 and 18 and CHARGE syndrome.
updates.explanation: The captioned CT demonstrates a posterior ocular coloboma. Posterior colobomas are congenital outpouchings near the optic disc and can be associated with microphthalmia and retrobulbar cysts. The source lists associated syndromes including trisomies 13 and 18 and CHARGE. Coloboma is also specifically named as a nonacute mimic of globe rupture.

updates.question_text: Regarding retinal detachment and choroidal detachment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Complete retinal detachment forms an hourglass configuration that spares the posterior pole.
Retinal detachment fluid occupies the suprachoroidal space between choroid and sclera.
Extensive retinal detachment forms a V configuration converging on the optic disc and extending to the ora serrata.
Choroidal detachment diverges towards the optic disc, sparing the posterior pole, and may form the kissing choroid sign.
Retinal detachment is never related to retinal tears.
options_after: Complete retinal detachment forms an hourglass configuration that spares the posterior pole.
Retinal detachment fluid occupies the suprachoroidal space between choroid and sclera.
Extensive retinal detachment forms a V configuration converging on the optic disc and extending to the ora serrata.
Choroidal detachment diverges towards the optic disc, sparing the posterior pole, and may form the kissing choroid sign.
Retinal detachment is not related to retinal tears.
updates.explanation: Retinal detachment forms a V-shaped configuration that converges on the optic disc and extends to the ora serrata, with fluid in the subretinal space between retina and choroid. Choroidal detachment instead occupies the suprachoroidal space, often has an hourglass configuration, diverges near the optic disc and may create kissing choroids. Retinal tears are the commonest cause of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT assessment and reporting of complex facial fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Complex facial trauma is best reported as a simple list of every fractured bone, with regional fracture patterns avoided.
Regional fracture patterns are useful because treatment is influenced by form and function rather than bone names alone.
Displacement, fragmentation, bone loss and region-specific anatomy are important descriptors.
Plain radiography is preferred over CT for surgical planning in complex facial trauma.
Multiplanar reformatted and 3D volume-rendered CT images can help diagnosis and surgical planning.
options_after: Complex facial trauma is best reported as an inventory of individual fractures rather than regional fracture patterns.
Regional fracture patterns are useful because treatment is influenced by form and function rather than bone names alone.
Displacement, fragmentation, bone loss and region-specific anatomy are important descriptors.
Plain radiography is preferred over CT for surgical planning in complex facial trauma.
Multiplanar reformatted and 3D volume-rendered CT images can help diagnosis and surgical planning.
updates.explanation: The source emphasises describing complex facial fractures by regional patterns, with attention to form and function. Displacement, fragmentation, bone loss and regional anatomy all influence treatment strategy. Multiplanar reformatted and 3D volume-rendered CT images are often useful for diagnosis and surgical planning. A laundry list of bones is specifically discouraged.

updates.question_text: Regarding frontal sinus and panfacial fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A panfacial fracture involves all thirds of the face: frontal bone, midface and mandible.
Posterior table frontal sinus involvement is clinically irrelevant if the anterior table is fractured.
Frontal recess disruption reduces the risk of delayed frontal sinus mucocele.
Posterior table involvement confers risk of CSF leak and intracranial infection.
Frontal sinus fracture management depends only on whether the anterior table is involved.
options_after: A panfacial fracture involves all thirds of the face: frontal bone, midface and mandible.
Posterior table frontal sinus involvement is clinically irrelevant if the anterior table is fractured.
Frontal recess disruption reduces the risk of delayed frontal sinus mucocele.
Posterior table involvement confers risk of CSF leak and intracranial infection.
Frontal sinus fracture management depends primarily on whether the anterior table is involved.
updates.explanation: A panfacial fracture involves the frontal bone, midface and mandible. Frontal sinus fracture management depends on the anterior table, posterior table, frontal recess, displacement and comminution. Posterior table involvement carries risk of CSF leak and intracranial infection. Disruption of the frontal recess or frontonasal duct raises risk of frontal sinus mucocele or mucopyocele.

updates.question_text: Regarding the Le Fort fracture classification, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Le Fort fractures spare the pterygoid plates by definition.
Le Fort I fractures cause craniofacial dissociation with free movement of the entire midface.
Le Fort II fractures are defined only by zygomatic arch fracture and do not involve the orbit.
Le Fort III fractures allow free movement of the hard palate only, with the nose fixed to the skull base.
All Le Fort fractures involve the pterygoid plates and maxillary sinus walls.
options_after: Le Fort fractures spare the pterygoid plates by definition.
Le Fort I fractures cause craniofacial dissociation with free movement of the entire midface.
Le Fort II fractures are defined primarily by zygomatic arch fracture and do not involve the orbit.
Le Fort III fractures allow free movement of the hard palate primarily, with the nose fixed to the skull base.
All Le Fort fractures involve the pterygoid plates and maxillary sinus walls.
updates.explanation: All Le Fort fractures involve the pterygoid plates and maxillary sinus walls. Le Fort I involves the lateral margin of the pyriform aperture and allows free movement of the hard palate. Le Fort II is pyramidal and involves the inferior orbital rim, floor and medial wall. Le Fort III includes the zygomatic arch and lateral/medial orbital walls and produces craniofacial dissociation.

updates.question_text: Regarding Le Fort II and III fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are irrelevant to vascular screening because only mandibular condyle fractures warrant neck CTA.
Le Fort II fractures involve the inferior orbital rim, orbital floor and medial orbital wall.
Le Fort III fractures are limited to the lateral margin of the pyriform aperture.
Le Fort II and III fractures are included among Denver screening criteria for blunt cerebrovascular injury.
Upper-level Le Fort fracture components can overlap with NOE, ZMC and orbital fracture patterns.
options_after: Mandibular condyle fractures are the principal indication for neck CTA; Le Fort II and III fractures are irrelevant to vascular screening.
Le Fort II fractures involve the inferior orbital rim, orbital floor and medial orbital wall.
Le Fort III fractures are limited to the lateral margin of the pyriform aperture.
Le Fort II and III fractures are included among Denver screening criteria for blunt cerebrovascular injury.
Upper-level Le Fort fracture components can overlap with NOE, ZMC and orbital fracture patterns.
updates.explanation: Le Fort II fractures follow a pyramidal pattern involving the inferior orbital rim, orbital floor and medial wall. Le Fort III fractures include zygomatic arch and orbital wall components and can cause craniofacial dissociation. Reporting Le Fort II and III fractures remains important because they are included in Denver screening criteria for blunt cerebrovascular injury, warranting CTA of the neck arteries and circle of Willis. Their upper non-occlusion components overlap with NOE, ZMC and orbital injuries.

updates.question_text: Regarding zygomaticomaxillary complex fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A complete ZMC fracture liberates a tripod fragment at only three zygomatic articulations.
The zygomaticosphenoid suture is not useful for judging ZMC alignment.
A complete ZMC fracture involves the zygomaticofrontal, zygomaticomaxillary, zygomaticotemporal and zygomaticosphenoid articulations.
Classic ZMC fractures never involve the orbital floor.
ZMC fractures with significant orbital volume expansion can cause late enophthalmos.
options_after: A complete ZMC fracture liberates a tripod fragment at primarily three zygomatic articulations.
The zygomaticosphenoid suture is not useful for judging ZMC alignment.
A complete ZMC fracture involves the zygomaticofrontal, zygomaticomaxillary, zygomaticotemporal and zygomaticosphenoid articulations.
Classic ZMC fractures will not involve the orbital floor.
ZMC fractures with significant orbital volume expansion can cause late enophthalmos.
updates.explanation: A complete ZMC fracture liberates a tetrapod fragment at four zygomatic articulations: zygomaticofrontal, zygomaticomaxillary, zygomaticotemporal and zygomaticosphenoid. The zygomaticosphenoid suture is a sensitive landmark for overall alignment. Classic ZMC fractures include the orbital floor, so they are sometimes called orbitozygomatic fractures. Marked orbital volume expansion can lead to late enophthalmos.

updates.question_text: Regarding submandibular and sublingual gland anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The submandibular gland is entirely confined to the nasal cavity.
The sublingual gland normally drains through Stensen duct over the masseter.
A Stafne bone cavity/cyst is caused by remodelling of the outer table of the frontal sinus.
Wharton duct opens on the side of the frenulum of the tongue.
A mylohyoid boutonniere prevents sublingual gland herniation into the submandibular space.
options_after: The submandibular gland is predominantly confined to the nasal cavity.
The sublingual gland normally drains through Stensen duct over the masseter.
A Stafne bone cavity/cyst is caused by remodelling of the outer table of the frontal sinus.
Wharton duct opens on the side of the frenulum of the tongue.
A mylohyoid boutonniere prevents sublingual gland herniation into the submandibular space.
updates.explanation: Wharton duct is the submandibular duct and opens on the side of the frenulum of the tongue. The submandibular gland straddles the floor of mouth and neck, wrapping around the posterior mylohyoid margin. Remodelling by the gland may cause a Stafne bone cavity at the mandibular angle. A mylohyoid boutonniere is a normal variant discontinuity through which the sublingual gland can herniate.

updates.question_text: A parotid MRI shows a well-defined, T2-hyperintense, T1-hypointense, enhancing circumscribed mass with bosselated margins in a middle-aged woman. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The imaging and demographic pattern support pleomorphic adenoma.
Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common salivary gland tumour and accounts for 70% of salivary tumours.
The typical patient for this tumour is an elderly male smoker.
Malignant transformation risk is absent, so no treatment is needed.
Superficial parotidectomy is the standard treatment for parotid pleomorphic adenoma.
options_after: The imaging and demographic pattern support pleomorphic adenoma.
Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common salivary gland tumour and accounts for 70% of salivary tumours.
The typical patient for this tumour is an elderly male smoker.
Given its absent malignant potential, pleomorphic adenoma is managed with imaging surveillance rather than parotidectomy.
Superficial parotidectomy is the standard treatment for parotid pleomorphic adenoma.
updates.explanation: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common salivary gland tumour, accounting for 70% of all salivary tumours, and is most common in the parotid. The typical patient is a middle-aged female. MRI shows a well-defined, very T2-hyperintense, strongly enhancing mass with bosselated margins. Although benign, it carries malignant transformation risk and standard parotid treatment is superficial parotidectomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding Warthin tumour, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the second most common benign parotid neoplasm.
It is the most common epithelial malignancy of the lacrimal gland.
The typical patient is an elderly male smoker.
It has a strong predilection for the sublingual gland and almost never affects the parotid tail.
It usually shows stronger enhancement and higher T2 signal than pleomorphic adenoma.
options_after: It is the second most common benign parotid neoplasm.
It is the most common epithelial malignancy of the lacrimal gland.
The typical patient is an elderly male smoker.
It has a strong predilection for the sublingual gland and almost will not affect the parotid tail.
It usually shows stronger enhancement and higher T2 signal than pleomorphic adenoma.
updates.explanation: Warthin tumour is the second most common benign parotid neoplasm. The typical patient is an elderly male, and most are smokers. It may be multifocal or bilateral in up to 20% of cases, making it the most common multifocal or bilateral parotid neoplasm, and it has a predilection for the parotid tail. Imaging tends to show a heterogeneous mass with weak enhancement and sometimes complicated cystic components.

updates.question_text: Regarding mucoepidermoid carcinoma and adenoid cystic carcinoma of the salivary glands, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is primarily a benign salivary neoplasm with no infiltrative high-grade form.
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the most common primary salivary gland malignancy, especially in the parotid gland.
Low-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma may be MRI-indistinguishable from pleomorphic adenoma.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma is the most common primary malignancy of the submandibular, sublingual and minor salivary glands.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma has the highest risk of perineural spread among head and neck malignancies.
options_after: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is primarily a benign salivary neoplasm without infiltrative high-grade form.
Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the most common primary salivary gland malignancy, especially in the parotid gland.
Low-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma may be MRI-indistinguishable from pleomorphic adenoma.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma is the most common primary malignancy of the submandibular, sublingual and minor salivary glands.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma has the highest risk of perineural spread among head and neck malignancies.
updates.explanation: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the most common primary salivary malignancy, especially in the parotid. Low-grade lesions can appear well-defined, enhancing and T2-hyperintense, making them indistinguishable from pleomorphic adenoma on MRI; high-grade lesions are more infiltrative and lower on T2. Adenoid cystic carcinoma is the commonest primary malignancy of the submandibular, sublingual and minor salivary glands and has the highest perineural spread risk among head and neck malignancies.

updates.question_text: Regarding carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It occurs when Warthin tumour transforms into lymphoma.
The risk occurs only in childhood pleomorphic adenomas.
It remains very T2-hyperintense with high ADC values and sharp margins, like uncomplicated pleomorphic adenoma.
A typical presentation is an elderly person with a long-standing parotid mass that develops rapid enlargement, pain or facial nerve palsy.
Compared with pleomorphic adenoma, it is T2-hypointense, has low ADC values and may extend beyond the gland.
options_after: It occurs when Warthin tumour transforms into lymphoma.
The risk occurs primarily in childhood pleomorphic adenomas.
It remains very T2-hyperintense with high ADC values and sharp margins, like uncomplicated pleomorphic adenoma.
A typical presentation is an elderly person with a long-standing parotid mass that develops rapid enlargement, pain or facial nerve palsy.
Compared with pleomorphic adenoma, it is T2-hypointense, has low ADC values and may extend beyond the gland.
updates.explanation: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma is malignant transformation of pleomorphic adenoma, with risk accumulating over many years. The source describes the typical patient as elderly with a long-standing parotid mass that newly enlarges rapidly or becomes painful, or develops facial nerve palsy. Imaging differs from benign pleomorphic adenoma by lower T2 signal, low ADC values, ill-defined infiltrative borders and possible extension beyond gland parenchyma.

updates.question_text: Regarding iodine-related salivary gland disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radioiodine sialadenitis is a common dose-dependent side effect of iodine-131 therapy for thyroid cancer.
Iodide sialadenitis is an allergic contrast reaction that always requires lifelong iodinated contrast avoidance.
Iodide sialadenitis is also known as iodide mumps.
Iodide sialadenitis is a rare idiosyncratic non-allergic adverse reaction to iodinated contrast media.
Iodide sialadenitis may cause self-limited painless salivary gland swelling minutes to days after contrast-enhanced CT or angiography.
options_after: Radioiodine sialadenitis is a common dose-dependent side effect of iodine-131 therapy for thyroid cancer.
Iodide sialadenitis is an allergic contrast reaction that characteristically requires lifelong iodinated contrast avoidance.
Iodide sialadenitis is also known as iodide mumps.
Iodide sialadenitis is a rare idiosyncratic non-allergic adverse reaction to iodinated contrast media.
Iodide sialadenitis may cause self-limited painless salivary gland swelling minutes to days after contrast-enhanced CT or angiography.
updates.explanation: Radioiodine sialadenitis is described as a common dose-dependent side effect of iodine-131 therapy, causing transient gland swelling, pain and decreased salivary flow. Iodide sialadenitis, or iodide mumps, is a rare idiosyncratic non-allergic reaction to iodinated contrast, not a true allergic reaction. It causes self-limited painless salivary gland swelling minutes to days after contrast-enhanced CT or angiography.

updates.question_text: A middle-aged woman has parotid MRI showing numerous small T2-hyperintense lesions with minimal peripheral enhancement and a salt-and-pepper or honeycomb parotid appearance. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: This appearance is characteristic of a Le Fort II fracture pattern.
The disease is always secondary to HIV infection.
The imaging pattern supports Sjögren syndrome.
The MRI appearance reflects benign lymphoepithelial lesions with fibrosis, punctate calcifications and fatty infiltration.
The source states that the typical patient is a middle-aged female.
options_after: This appearance is characteristic of a Le Fort II fracture pattern.
The disease is characteristically secondary to HIV infection.
The imaging pattern supports Sjögren syndrome.
The MRI appearance reflects benign lymphoepithelial lesions with fibrosis, punctate calcifications and fatty infiltration.
The source states that the typical patient is a middle-aged female.
updates.explanation: Sjögren syndrome is an autoimmune salivary and lacrimal gland disorder, typically affecting middle-aged women. MRI can show a salt-and-pepper or honeycomb appearance of bilateral parotid glands. The mixed signal pattern reflects benign lymphoepithelial lesions with fibrosis, punctate calcifications and fatty infiltration. Sjögren may be primary or secondary to another autoimmune disease such as rheumatoid arthritis or systemic lupus erythematosus.

updates.question_text: Regarding vascular imaging implications of facial fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Displaced or complex mandibular fractures, especially involving the condyles, warrant neck CTA because of increased blunt vascular injury risk.
Le Fort II and III fractures should never trigger vascular imaging because they are purely dental injuries.
Panfacial fractures are limited to the maxillary alveolus and never involve the mandible.
Isolated enamel-only tooth fractures are a Denver screening criterion for blunt cerebrovascular injury.
Le Fort II and III fractures are among the Denver screening criteria and warrant CTA of the neck arteries and circle of Willis.
options_after: Displaced or complex mandibular fractures, especially involving the condyles, warrant neck CTA because of increased blunt vascular injury risk.
Le Fort II and III fractures should not trigger vascular imaging because they are purely dental injuries.
Panfacial fractures are limited to the maxillary alveolus and will not involve the mandible.
Isolated enamel-predominant tooth fractures are a Denver screening criterion for blunt cerebrovascular injury.
Le Fort II and III fractures are among the Denver screening criteria and warrant CTA of the neck arteries and circle of Willis.
updates.explanation: The source specifically notes that displaced or complex mandibular fractures, particularly those involving the condyles, are associated with increased blunt vascular injury risk and warrant neck CTA. It also states that Le Fort II and III fractures are included among Denver screening criteria, warranting CTA of the neck arteries and circle of Willis. Dental crown fractures and panfacial descriptors are separate issues.

updates.question_text: Regarding salivary gland ducts and variant spaces, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Stensen duct is the sublingual duct draining into the Wharton duct.
Accessory parotid tissue may lie along Stensen duct superficial to the masseter.
The submandibular gland cannot remodel adjacent bone.
Rivinus ducts drain the sublingual gland and may form Bartholin duct, which empties into Wharton duct.
The parotid tail is the deep lobe extension through the stylomandibular tunnel.
options_after: Stensen duct is the sublingual duct draining into the Wharton duct.
Accessory parotid tissue may lie along Stensen duct superficial to the masseter.
The submandibular gland will not remodel adjacent bone.
Rivinus ducts drain the sublingual gland and may form Bartholin duct, which empties into Wharton duct.
The parotid tail is the deep lobe extension through the stylomandibular tunnel.
updates.explanation: Accessory parotid glands may lie along Stensen duct superficial to the masseter. The sublingual glands drain via multiple Rivinus ducts, which may form Bartholin duct emptying into Wharton duct. Stensen duct is the parotid duct, while Wharton duct is the submandibular duct. The submandibular gland can remodel the mandible to create a Stafne bone cavity, and the parotid tail is an inferior superficial-lobe projection over the mandibular angle.

updates.question_text: Regarding the posterior pituitary bright spot and ectopic posterior pituitary, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The normal posterior pituitary is T1 hyperintense because of stored ADH.
Loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot has been associated with central diabetes insipidus.
Loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot is always pathological and never seen in normal patients.
Ectopic posterior pituitary commonly lies at the median eminence when normal descent is halted.
Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome combines ectopic posterior pituitary with absent or hypoplastic infundibulum and anterior pituitary.
options_after: The normal posterior pituitary is T1 hyperintense because of stored ADH.
Loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot has been associated with central diabetes insipidus.
Loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot is specific for pituitary disease.
Ectopic posterior pituitary commonly lies at the median eminence when normal descent is halted.
Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome combines ectopic posterior pituitary with absent or hypoplastic infundibulum and anterior pituitary.
updates.explanation: The posterior bright spot is best seen sagittally on T1-weighted MRI and reflects stored ADH. Its absence can occur with central diabetes insipidus but is not entirely specific because it may also occur in normal patients. Ectopic posterior pituitary usually lies at the median eminence when descent from the diencephalon is arrested. The source defines pituitary stalk interruption syndrome by ectopic posterior pituitary plus absent or hypoplastic stalk and anterior pituitary.

updates.question_text: Regarding dynamic enhancement of the pituitary gland, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The infundibulum and posterior pituitary enhance first.
The anterior pituitary enhances before the infundibulum because it has direct arterial supply only.
The anterior pituitary is supplied by the hypophyseal portal system.
The entire pituitary gland enhances homogeneously between 30 and 60 seconds and then washes out.
Dynamic enhancement is unrelated to pituitary blood supply.
options_after: The infundibulum and posterior pituitary enhance first.
The anterior pituitary enhances before the infundibulum because it has direct arterial supply in typical cases.
The anterior pituitary is supplied by the hypophyseal portal system.
The entire pituitary gland enhances homogeneously between 30 and 60 seconds and then washes out.
Dynamic enhancement is unrelated to pituitary blood supply.
updates.explanation: Pituitary enhancement follows its vascular supply. The infundibulum and posterior pituitary enhance first, followed by the anterior gland supplied through the hypophyseal portal system. The whole gland then enhances homogeneously between 30 and 60 seconds before washout. This timing underpins dynamic MRI detection of some microadenomas.

updates.question_text: Regarding cavernous sinus cranial nerve anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: V3 traverses the cavernous sinus and exits through the superior orbital fissure.
The optic nerve is located within the cavernous sinus wall.
CN VI travels only in the lateral cavernous sinus wall.
V2 exits via the superior orbital fissure with V1.
CN VI and sympathetic fibres around the carotid artery lie centrally within the cavernous sinus.
options_after: V3 traverses the cavernous sinus and exits through the superior orbital fissure.
The optic nerve is located within the cavernous sinus wall.
CN VI travels primarily in the lateral cavernous sinus wall.
V2 exits via the superior orbital fissure with V1.
CN VI and sympathetic fibres around the carotid artery lie centrally within the cavernous sinus.
updates.explanation: The source emphasises that CN VI and sympathetic fibres around the carotid artery are central within the cavernous sinus, while CN III, IV, V1 and V2 run in the lateral wall. V3 is the trigeminal division that does not traverse the cavernous sinus and exits Meckel cave via foramen ovale. V2 is the cavernous sinus nerve that does not exit through the superior orbital fissure; it exits through foramen rotundum.

updates.question_text: Regarding cavernous sinus drainage and clinical syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The cavernous sinus drains only the frontal sinus and has no ophthalmic venous connection.
The cavernous sinus drains the superior and inferior ophthalmic veins and the sphenoparietal sinus.
Inferior petrosal sinus sampling via the internal jugular vein may demonstrate pituitary ACTH hypersecretion in suspected Cushing disease.
The lateral cavernous sinus wall is normally convex; straight or concave contour suggests disease.
Cavernous sinus syndrome can include ophthalmoplegia, facial sensory loss, Horner syndrome, chemosis and proptosis.
options_after: The cavernous sinus drains primarily the frontal sinus and lacks ophthalmic venous connection.
The cavernous sinus drains the superior and inferior ophthalmic veins and the sphenoparietal sinus.
Inferior petrosal sinus sampling via the internal jugular vein may demonstrate pituitary ACTH hypersecretion in suspected Cushing disease.
The lateral cavernous sinus wall is normally convex; straight or concave contour suggests disease.
Cavernous sinus syndrome can include ophthalmoplegia, facial sensory loss, Horner syndrome, chemosis and proptosis.
updates.explanation: The cavernous sinus receives the superior/inferior ophthalmic veins and sphenoparietal sinus and drains through petrosal pathways with other plexus connections. Inferior petrosal sinus sampling is used in suspected Cushing disease to show pituitary ACTH hypersecretion. The normal lateral wall is concave or straight, and outward bulging suggests lesion involvement. Cavernous sinus syndrome combines cranial nerve and sympathetic deficits with orbital venous congestion.

updates.question_text: Regarding the suprasellar cistern, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The suprasellar cistern is posterior to the interpeduncular cistern.
The suprasellar cistern contains no major neurovascular structures.
The suprasellar cistern contains the optic nerves/chiasm, infundibulum and circle of Willis.
Spontaneous intracranial hypertension increases the height of the suprasellar cistern in the source description.
Uncal herniation from supratentorial mass effect can efface the suprasellar cistern.
options_after: The suprasellar cistern is posterior to the interpeduncular cistern.
The suprasellar cistern lacks major neurovascular structures.
The suprasellar cistern contains the optic nerves/chiasm, infundibulum and circle of Willis.
Spontaneous intracranial hypertension increases the height of the suprasellar cistern in the source description.
Uncal herniation from supratentorial mass effect can efface the suprasellar cistern.
updates.explanation: The suprasellar cistern is above the sella, below the hypothalamus, between the temporal unci and anterior to the interpeduncular cistern. It contains the optic pathways, infundibulum and circle of Willis. Supratentorial mass effect with uncal herniation effaces it from the involved side. The source links reduced height of the suprasellar cistern to spontaneous intracranial hypotension.

updates.question_text: Regarding pituitary adenomas, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pituitary adenomas are by far the most common intrinsic pituitary mass.
Microadenomas are less than 10 mm, while macroadenomas are 10 mm or larger.
The most common hormonal classes are lactotroph and nonfunctioning adenomas.
Macroadenomas can present with visual field deficits due to optic pathway compression.
All pituitary adenomas arise from Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
options_after: Pituitary adenomas are by far the most common intrinsic pituitary mass.
Microadenomas are less than 10 mm, while macroadenomas are 10 mm or larger.
The most common hormonal classes are lactotroph and nonfunctioning adenomas.
Macroadenomas can present with visual field deficits due to optic pathway compression.
Most pituitary adenomas arise from Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
updates.explanation: Pituitary adenomas dominate the intrinsic pituitary mass differential. The source classifies them by size into microadenomas under 10 mm and macroadenomas at least 10 mm. Lactotroph and nonfunctioning adenomas are the common hormonal categories. Larger adenomas may cause mass effect with visual field deficits from optic pathway compression and headache.

updates.question_text: A pituitary MRI shows a subcentimetre T2-hyperintense, hypoenhancing central pituitary lesion. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The lesion is compatible with a pituitary microadenoma.
The lesion is a macroadenoma because all pituitary adenomas under 10 mm are macroadenomas.
Contrast-enhanced sequences reduce sensitivity for pituitary microadenoma detection.
Most microadenomas show delayed enhancement relative to the normal pituitary.
Dynamic early and delayed imaging is needed to detect a small subset of microadenomas.
options_after: The lesion is compatible with a pituitary microadenoma.
The lesion is a macroadenoma because most pituitary adenomas under 10 mm are macroadenomas.
Contrast-enhanced sequences reduce sensitivity for pituitary microadenoma detection.
Most microadenomas show delayed enhancement relative to the normal pituitary.
Dynamic early and delayed imaging is needed to detect a small subset of microadenomas.
updates.explanation: A subcentimetre pituitary lesion fits the microadenoma size category. Microadenomas may be subtle on conventional sequences, and contrast-enhanced imaging improves sensitivity. Most appear hypoenhancing relative to normal pituitary on routine timing because they enhance later. Dynamic imaging with early and delayed phases is needed for a small subset of lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding pituitary apoplexy and Sheehan syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pituitary apoplexy usually means slow enlargement of a Rathke cleft cyst without haemorrhage.
Pituitary apoplexy is a syndrome of severe headache, visual impairment and hypopituitarism caused by sudden haemorrhage into the pituitary.
Sheehan syndrome refers to pituitary apoplexy in postpartum women associated with hypopituitarism.
Acute pituitary apoplexy always produces a normal-sized, completely empty sella on imaging.
The typical cause of pituitary apoplexy is Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
options_after: Pituitary apoplexy usually means slow enlargement of a Rathke cleft cyst without haemorrhage.
Pituitary apoplexy is a syndrome of severe headache, visual impairment and hypopituitarism caused by sudden haemorrhage into the pituitary.
Sheehan syndrome refers to pituitary apoplexy in postpartum women associated with hypopituitarism.
Acute pituitary apoplexy characteristically produces a normal-sized, completely empty sella on imaging.
The typical cause of pituitary apoplexy is Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
updates.explanation: Pituitary apoplexy is the acute clinical syndrome of severe headache, visual symptoms and hypopituitarism from sudden pituitary haemorrhage, most often into an adenoma. Acute imaging may show an enlarged pituitary gland with intrinsic T1 hyperintensity due to haemorrhage. Over time the gland may atrophy and leave a partially empty sella. Sheehan syndrome is the postpartum hypopituitarism form described in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding pituitary macroadenoma invasion and morphology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Macroadenomas usually narrow the internal carotid artery before they remodel the sella.
Complete internal carotid artery encasement is an early screening sign that excludes cavernous sinus invasion.
The snowman sign is created by calcification of Rathke cleft cyst fluid.
A macroadenoma extending laterally beyond the tangent line between supraclinoid and cavernous carotid lateral walls predicts high risk of cavernous sinus invasion.
Meningiomas and metastases never narrow adjacent carotid arteries.
options_after: Macroadenomas usually narrow the internal carotid artery before they remodel the sella.
Complete internal carotid artery encasement is an early screening sign that excludes cavernous sinus invasion.
The snowman sign is created by calcification of Rathke cleft cyst fluid.
A macroadenoma extending laterally beyond the tangent line between supraclinoid and cavernous carotid lateral walls predicts high risk of cavernous sinus invasion.
Meningiomas and metastases will not narrow adjacent carotid arteries.
updates.explanation: Preoperative coronal MRI predicts a high risk of cavernous sinus invasion when tumour extends laterally beyond the line connecting the lateral walls of the supraclinoid and cavernous ICA segments. Complete ICA encasement indicates invasion but occurs late. Macroadenomas are typically slow-growing and can remodel the sella; their softness allows indentation by the diaphragma sellae, producing the snowman or dumbbell configuration. The source contrasts adenomas with meningiomas or metastases, which can narrow the carotid.

updates.question_text: A pituitary MRI shows complete replacement of the gland by an enhancing mass with superior displacement of the optic chiasm. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The appearance is compatible with pituitary macroadenoma.
Macroadenomas may be heterogeneous from cystic change, necrosis or haemorrhage.
This appearance excludes optic pathway compression because the chiasm is superiorly displaced.
A haemorrhagic adenoma is never intrinsically T1 hyperintense.
Haemorrhagic pituitary adenoma is the most common sellar-region lesion with intrinsic T1 hyperintensity, especially with a fluid level.
options_after: The appearance is compatible with pituitary macroadenoma.
Macroadenomas may be heterogeneous from cystic change, necrosis or haemorrhage.
This appearance excludes optic pathway compression because the chiasm is superiorly displaced.
A haemorrhagic adenoma is not intrinsically T1 hyperintense.
Haemorrhagic pituitary adenoma is the most common sellar-region lesion with intrinsic T1 hyperintensity, especially with a fluid level.
updates.explanation: The captioned images show macroadenoma replacing the pituitary and displacing the optic chiasm superiorly. Macroadenomas can be heterogeneous due to cystic change, necrosis or haemorrhage, and haemorrhagic adenoma is the commonest sellar lesion with intrinsic T1 hyperintensity, especially when a fluid level is present. Chiasmal displacement is clinically relevant because macroadenomas can produce visual field deficits.

updates.question_text: Regarding pituitary hyperplasia and hypophysitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Physiological pituitary hyperplasia can occur during adolescence, pregnancy and perimenopause.
Pituitary hyperplasia always appears as an eccentric cyst with an intracystic nodule.
Pathological pituitary hyperplasia is usually related to end-organ insufficiency, especially primary hypothyroidism.
Lymphocytic hypophysitis is unrelated to the peripartum period and checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
Plasmacytic hypophysitis is the most common histological subtype.
options_after: Physiological pituitary hyperplasia can occur during adolescence, pregnancy and perimenopause.
Pituitary hyperplasia characteristically appears as an eccentric cyst with an intracystic nodule.
Pathological pituitary hyperplasia is usually related to end-organ insufficiency, especially primary hypothyroidism.
Lymphocytic hypophysitis is unrelated to the peripartum period and checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
Plasmacytic hypophysitis is the most common histological subtype.
updates.explanation: The source notes wide normal pituitary size variation and physiological hyperplasia in hormonally active periods such as adolescence, pregnancy and perimenopause. Pathological hyperplasia usually reflects end-organ insufficiency, especially primary hypothyroidism. Hyperplasia appears as a homogeneously enlarged gland with convex superior margin. Hypophysitis is inflammatory, with lymphocytic type most common and recognised in the peripartum period and after checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

updates.question_text: Regarding idiopathic intracranial hypertension and empty sella, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Empty sella is one imaging feature in idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
Typical clinical features include headache, transient visual obscurations and/or pulsatile tinnitus in obese female patients.
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is caused by an intracranial mass or hydrocephalus in the source definition.
The only imaging finding is isolated enlargement of the cavernous carotid artery.
Associated imaging findings can include papilloedema/posterior scleral flattening, optic nerve sheath dilation and transverse sinus stenosis.
options_after: Empty sella is one imaging feature in idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
Typical clinical features include headache, transient visual obscurations and/or pulsatile tinnitus in obese female patients.
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is caused by an intracranial mass or hydrocephalus in the source definition.
The principal imaging finding is isolated enlargement of the cavernous carotid artery.
Associated imaging findings can include papilloedema/posterior scleral flattening, optic nerve sheath dilation and transverse sinus stenosis.
updates.explanation: The source describes idiopathic intracranial hypertension as elevated CSF pressure without intracranial mass or hydrocephalus. Empty sella is part of a constellation of findings, alongside papilloedema or posterior scleral flattening, optic nerve sheath dilation, bilateral transverse sinus stenosis, tonsillar ectopia and meningoceles. The clinical profile given is typically obese female patients with headache, transient visual obscurations and/or pulsatile tinnitus.

updates.question_text: Regarding parasellar meningioma and aneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Meningiomas do not arise from skull base meninges around the sella.
CTA or MRA is diagnostic for aneurysm and helps avoid catastrophic biopsy of an aneurysm mistaken for tumour.
Parasellar meningiomas never narrow adjacent vasculature.
Aneurysms in this region never show flow void or pulsation artefact on conventional MRI.
The suprasellar/parasellar region is the least common site of giant intracranial aneurysms.
options_after: Meningiomas do not arise from skull base meninges around the sella.
CTA or MRA is diagnostic for aneurysm and helps avoid catastrophic biopsy of an aneurysm mistaken for tumour.
Parasellar meningiomas will not narrow adjacent vasculature.
Aneurysms in this region will not show flow void or pulsation artefact on conventional MRI.
The suprasellar/parasellar region is the least common site of giant intracranial aneurysms.
updates.explanation: The source highlights aneurysm as an important mimic of suprasellar/parasellar tumour because biopsy could be catastrophic. Conventional MRI may show pulsation artefact or a flow void, while CTA or MRA establishes the diagnosis. Meningiomas can arise from multiple skull base dural sites around the sella, enhance intensely with dural tail, cause hyperostosis and may encase or narrow the cavernous/supraclinoid ICA.

updates.question_text: A suprasellar mass contains coarse calcifications on CT and shows avid heterogeneous enhancement on post-contrast MRI. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The appearance excludes craniopharyngioma because calcification is never seen.
Craniopharyngioma is a benign WHO grade I neoplasm arising from Rathke pouch remnants.
Most craniopharyngiomas are suprasellar, although they may extend into or rarely arise within the sella.
In children, the adamantinomatous subtype is typically complex cystic and calcified with proteinaceous T1-hyperintense cyst fluid.
Adult papillary craniopharyngioma is usually a cystic calcified lobulated mass.
options_after: The appearance excludes craniopharyngioma because calcification is not seen.
Craniopharyngioma is a benign WHO grade I neoplasm arising from Rathke pouch remnants.
Most craniopharyngiomas are suprasellar, although they may extend into or rarely arise within the sella.
In children, the adamantinomatous subtype is typically complex cystic and calcified with proteinaceous T1-hyperintense cyst fluid.
Adult papillary craniopharyngioma is usually a cystic calcified lobulated mass.
updates.explanation: The captioned mass fits craniopharyngioma. Craniopharyngiomas are WHO grade I neoplasms from Rathke pouch remnants and are usually suprasellar. In children the adamantinomatous subtype is common and tends to be complex cystic, lobulated and calcified, with proteinaceous machine-oil cyst fluid that is T1 hyperintense. In adults the papillary subtype is more common and is typically predominantly solid, enhancing, spherical and non-calcified.

updates.question_text: A suprasellar MRI shows a mass involving the optic chiasm with avid heterogeneous enhancement. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: This imaging pattern is diagnostic of an arterial aneurysm without vascular imaging.
Optic pathway glioma can involve the optic chiasm and optic tracts.
Hypothalamic gliomas may be considered with optic pathway gliomas because the site of origin can be hard to distinguish in the suprasellar region.
This tumour group is always T2 hypointense and dark on ADC due to hypercellularity.
These lesions are excluded if the mass enhances.
options_after: This imaging pattern is diagnostic of an arterial aneurysm without vascular imaging.
Optic pathway glioma can involve the optic chiasm and optic tracts.
Hypothalamic gliomas may be considered with optic pathway gliomas because the site of origin can be hard to distinguish in the suprasellar region.
This tumour group is characteristically T2 hypointense and dark on ADC due to hypercellularity.
These lesions are excluded if the mass enhances.
updates.explanation: The source groups optic pathway and hypothalamic gliomas because suprasellar origin can be difficult to distinguish. Optic pathway gliomas can involve the optic nerves, chiasm and tracts, are T1 isointense, T2 hyperintense and usually enhance. T2 hypointensity and dark ADC from hypercellularity describe germinoma rather than glioma. Aneurysm remains an important mimic, but vascular imaging is needed for that diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal clival anatomy and variants, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The clivus is formed by the frontal bone and hard palate.
The sphenoid body and basiocciput form the sloping midline clivus.
A persistent hypophyseal canal is less than 1.5 mm, while a craniopharyngeal canal is greater than 1.5 mm.
Normal ageing changes clival marrow from low T1 haematopoietic marrow to high T1 fatty marrow.
Low T1 clival marrow signal in an older adult is always normal fatty marrow.
options_after: The clivus is formed by the frontal bone and hard palate.
The sphenoid body and basiocciput form the sloping midline clivus.
A persistent hypophyseal canal is less than 1.5 mm, while a craniopharyngeal canal is greater than 1.5 mm.
Normal ageing changes clival marrow from low T1 haematopoietic marrow to high T1 fatty marrow.
Low T1 clival marrow signal in an older adult is characteristically normal fatty marrow.
updates.explanation: The clivus is the sloping midline central skull base formed by the sphenoid body and basiocciput, which meet at the spheno-occipital synchondrosis. A persistent hypophyseal canal is under 1.5 mm, while a craniopharyngeal canal is over 1.5 mm and connects the nasopharynx and sella. With age, clival marrow normally becomes T1-bright fatty marrow. Low T1 signal in an older adult is abnormal and may reflect neoplasm or systemic disease.

updates.question_text: A small T2-hyperintense retroclival lesion projects from the dorsum of the clivus into the prepontine cistern, has no significant enhancement, and is stable over time. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The lesion is an aggressive chondrosarcoma because all retroclival lesions enhance intensely.
The lesion is a pituitary macroadenoma because it is located in the prepontine cistern.
The appearance supports ecchordosis physaliphora.
The lesion is diagnostic of a direct carotid-cavernous fistula.
The finding is a normal Stafne bone cavity.
options_after: The lesion is an aggressive chondrosarcoma because most retroclival lesions enhance intensely.
The lesion is a pituitary macroadenoma because it is located in the prepontine cistern.
The appearance supports ecchordosis physaliphora.
The lesion is diagnostic of a direct carotid-cavernous fistula.
The finding is a normal Stafne bone cavity.
updates.explanation: Ecchordosis physaliphora is a benign ectopic notochordal remnant projecting from the clival dorsum into the posterior fossa. It appears as a small T2-hyperintense retroclival lesion without enhancement and may have a stalk or small adjacent clival defect. Stability over time supports the diagnosis and helps distinguish it from chordoma. The other entities have different locations and imaging behaviours.

updates.question_text: Regarding chordoma and chondrosarcoma at the skull base, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chordomas tend to be midline.
Chondrosarcomas most commonly arise at the petroclival synchondrosis within the skull base.
Chordomas and chondrosarcomas have no imaging overlap, so location is irrelevant.
Chondrosarcomas can show rings-and-arcs calcifications on CT.
Chondrosarcomas are cartilage-derived adult malignancies with high T2 signal and markedly elevated ADC values.
options_after: Chordomas tend to be midline.
Chondrosarcomas most commonly arise at the petroclival synchondrosis within the skull base.
Chordomas and chondrosarcomas lack imaging overlap, so location is irrelevant.
Chondrosarcomas can show rings-and-arcs calcifications on CT.
Chondrosarcomas are cartilage-derived adult malignancies with high T2 signal and markedly elevated ADC values.
updates.explanation: Chordomas and chondrosarcomas can overlap on imaging, so location is a major discriminator. Chordomas tend to be midline clival lesions, whereas chondrosarcomas are usually off-midline and centred at the petroclival synchondrosis. Chondrosarcomas are cartilage-derived, high T2 lesions with markedly elevated ADC values, and CT can show chondroid rings-and-arcs calcification.

updates.question_text: Regarding pterygopalatine fossa disease spread, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Obliteration or infiltration of pterygopalatine fossa fat by soft tissue is the earliest imaging sign of pathological involvement.
The pterygopalatine fossa can only be involved by benign congenital cysts, not malignancy or inflammation.
Contrast enhancement and enlargement of neural foramina or canals leading to the fossa indicate perineural tumour spread.
Later signs include spontaneous restoration of fat and narrowing of all bony walls.
Primary sites that can spread to the fossa are limited to pituitary macroadenoma and Rathke cleft cyst.
