The surgical threshold for most ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms is 4.5 cm despite variation in cause
Annual growth greater than 1 cm per year is an indication for surgical repair
updates.explanation: The source states that atherosclerotic thoracic aortic aneurysm more commonly affects the descending thoracic aorta and that almost one-third of these patients have an associated abdominal aortic aneurysm. Bicuspid aortic valve-associated aortopathy is explicitly listed among non-atherosclerotic causes. The lower 4.5 cm surgical threshold applies to selected patients with connective tissue disorders and bicuspid valve aortopathy meeting criteria for valve replacement, not to every ascending aneurysm. Rapid growth greater than 1 cm per year, or greater than 5 mm in 6 months, is an indication for repair.

updates.question_text: Regarding large-vessel vasculitis involving the aorta and great vessels, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Giant cell arteritis typically affects patients older than 50 years
Giant cell arteritis commonly involves the aorta, whereas Takayasu arteritis rarely does
Temporal artery biopsy is always positive when aortic involvement is present
FDG-PET/CT may help diagnose large-vessel vasculitis by demonstrating moderate to intense uptake in involved vessels
Takayasu arteritis often involves the aorta and is commonly associated with occlusions
options_after: Giant cell arteritis typically affects patients older than 50 years
Giant cell arteritis commonly involves the aorta, whereas Takayasu arteritis rarely does
Temporal artery biopsy is characteristically positive when aortic involvement is present
FDG-PET/CT may help diagnose large-vessel vasculitis by demonstrating moderate to intense uptake in involved vessels
Takayasu arteritis often involves the aorta and is commonly associated with occlusions
updates.explanation: Giant cell arteritis tends to affect older patients, typically over 50 years, whereas Takayasu arteritis occurs in younger patients. FDG-PET/CT can support the diagnosis of large-vessel vasculitis when involved vessels show moderate to intense uptake. The source contrasts the two entities by noting that Takayasu arteritis often involves the aorta and is commonly associated with occlusions, while aortic involvement is rare in giant cell arteritis. Temporal artery biopsy can be false negative because of skip lesions or isolated aortic involvement.

updates.question_text: Regarding infectious aortitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It most commonly presents as a smooth long stenosis without aneurysm formation
The most common pathogens are restricted to viral causes
Focal crescentic aortic wall thickening with periaortic soft-tissue accumulation is a key imaging feature
Rapid progression of a saccular or mycotic aneurysm supports the diagnosis
Syphilitic aortitis usually affects only the infrarenal abdominal aorta
options_after: It most commonly presents as a smooth long stenosis without aneurysm formation
The most common pathogens are restricted to viral causes
Focal crescentic aortic wall thickening with periaortic soft-tissue accumulation is a key imaging feature
Rapid progression of a saccular or mycotic aneurysm supports the diagnosis
Syphilitic aortitis usually affects primarily the infrarenal abdominal aorta
updates.explanation: The source describes infectious aortitis as most commonly presenting as a mycotic aneurysm, although non-aneurysmal infection can occur. Key imaging features include focal crescentic wall thickening, periaortic soft-tissue accumulation, and rapid progression of a saccular or mycotic aneurysm or pseudoaneurysm. Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella, Pneumococcus and E. coli are listed among common pathogens, so viral restriction is wrong. Syphilitic aortitis is described as usually limited to the thoracic aorta.

updates.question_text: Regarding associated anomalies and mimics of aortic coarctation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most common associated cardiovascular anomaly is patent ductus arteriosus
Bicuspid aortic valve is the most common associated anomaly and is present in 75-80%
Pseudocoarctation is defined by a pressure differential with prominent collateral vessels
Shone syndrome consists only of supravalvular mitral membrane and coarctation
Aortic coarctation is one of the four components of Shone syndrome
options_after: The most common associated cardiovascular anomaly is patent ductus arteriosus
Bicuspid aortic valve is the most common associated anomaly and is present in 75-80%
Pseudocoarctation is defined by a pressure differential with prominent collateral vessels
Shone syndrome consists primarily of supravalvular mitral membrane and coarctation
Aortic coarctation is one of the four components of Shone syndrome
updates.explanation: The source states that bicuspid aortic valve is the most common associated anomaly, present in 75-80% of patients with coarctation. Aortic coarctation is also one component of Shone syndrome, along with supravalvular mitral membrane, subvalvular aortic stenosis and parachute mitral valve. Pseudocoarctation resembles true coarctation morphologically but lacks a pressure differential and collateral vessels. Patent ductus arteriosus is listed as an association but not as the most common one.

updates.question_text: Regarding superior vena cava obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chronic SVC occlusion is always a vascular emergency even if asymptomatic
Acute SVC syndrome presents with facial and upper extremity oedema and cyanosis
Common causes include thoracic malignancy, catheter-associated thrombosis and mediastinal fibrosis after histoplasmosis exposure
Increased enhancement of hepatic segment IVa can occur through collateral opacification of the vein of Sappey
Collateral formation is independent of whether the occlusion is above or below the azygos vein
options_after: Chronic SVC occlusion is characteristically a vascular emergency even if asymptomatic
Acute SVC syndrome presents with facial and upper extremity oedema and cyanosis
Common causes include thoracic malignancy, catheter-associated thrombosis and mediastinal fibrosis after histoplasmosis exposure
Increased enhancement of hepatic segment IVa can occur through collateral opacification of the vein of Sappey
Collateral formation is independent of whether the occlusion is above or below the azygos vein
updates.explanation: Acute SVC obstruction causes SVC syndrome with facial and upper extremity oedema and cyanosis and is a vascular emergency. The source lists thoracic malignancy, catheter-associated thrombosis and mediastinal fibrosis after histoplasmosis exposure as common causes. A classic abdominal imaging finding is increased enhancement of segment IVa due to collateral opacification of the vein of Sappey. Chronic occlusion may be asymptomatic, and collateral patterns depend on the level of occlusion relative to the azygos vein.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital anomalies of the superior vena cava, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A left-sided SVC is due to persistence of the embryological left anterior cardinal vein with regression of the right anterior cardinal vein
A left-sided SVC most commonly drains directly into the left atrium
A duplicated SVC is caused by regression of both anterior cardinal veins
Persistent left-sided SVC is the most common congenital venous anomaly in the chest
Left-sided SVC has no association with congenital heart disease
options_after: A left-sided SVC is due to persistence of the embryological left anterior cardinal vein with regression of the right anterior cardinal vein
A left-sided SVC most commonly drains directly into the left atrium
A duplicated SVC is caused by regression of both anterior cardinal veins
Persistent left-sided SVC is the most common congenital venous anomaly in the chest
Left-sided SVC lacks association with congenital heart disease
updates.explanation: A left-sided SVC results from persistence of the left anterior cardinal vein and regression of the right anterior cardinal vein, and it is the most common congenital venous anomaly in the chest. It usually drains into the coronary sinus and then the right atrium; direct drainage into the left atrium is rare and causes a right-to-left shunt. Duplicated SVC results from persistence of both right and left anterior cardinal veins. The source notes a weak association between left-sided SVC and congenital heart disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Open repair is preferred for all patients regardless of surgical risk
Endovascular repair has worse early morbidity and longer hospital stay than open repair
Endovascular repair is preferred for all patients regardless of surgical risk when anatomy permits
Long-term outcomes are clearly inferior after endovascular repair compared with open repair
Complications of endovascular repair include endoleak, endotension, stent migration, delayed rupture, infection, end-organ ischaemia and aorto-enteric fistula
options_after: Open repair is preferred for most patients despite variation in surgical risk
Endovascular repair has worse early morbidity and longer hospital stay than open repair
Endovascular repair is preferred for all patients regardless of surgical risk when anatomy permits
Long-term outcomes are clearly inferior after endovascular repair compared with open repair
Complications of endovascular repair include endoleak, endotension, stent migration, delayed rupture, infection, end-organ ischaemia and aorto-enteric fistula
updates.explanation: The source says endovascular repair is preferred for all patients regardless of surgical risk and is associated with reduced major morbidity and hospital time. Open repair is considered when endovascular repair is not possible, usually because of aneurysm shape. Long-term outcomes are equivalent between endovascular and open repair, although endovascular repair often requires repeat interventions. Listed endovascular complications include endoleak, endotension, stent migration or limb breakdown, delayed rupture, infection, end-organ ischaemia and aorto-enteric fistula.

updates.question_text: Regarding celiac axis and hepatic arterial anatomy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The usual celiac trunk branches are the left gastric, common hepatic and splenic arteries
The right gastroepiploic artery arises from the splenic artery
The cystic artery usually arises from the left hepatic artery
The proper hepatic artery is the continuation of the common hepatic artery after the gastroduodenal artery takeoff
Normal celiac arterial anatomy is present in only about 25% of patients
options_after: The usual celiac trunk branches are the left gastric, common hepatic and splenic arteries
The right gastroepiploic artery arises from the splenic artery
The cystic artery usually arises from the left hepatic artery
The proper hepatic artery is the continuation of the common hepatic artery after the gastroduodenal artery takeoff
Normal celiac arterial anatomy is present in approximately 25% of patients
updates.explanation: Approximately 75% of patients have normal celiac anatomy, with left gastric, common hepatic and splenic arteries as the three main branches. The proper hepatic artery continues beyond the gastroduodenal artery takeoff and divides into the right and left hepatic arteries. The right gastroepiploic artery arises from the gastroduodenal artery, while the left gastroepiploic artery arises from the splenic artery. The cystic artery arises from the right hepatic artery in the source description.

updates.question_text: A selective superior mesenteric angiogram shows numerous tiny peripheral visceral aneurysms. Regarding this appearance, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The source diagnosis is polyarteritis nodosa
It is best treated by coil embolisation of every microaneurysm as first-line therapy
It usually affects only large elastic arteries such as the thoracic aorta
Renal, hepatic and mesenteric end-arterioles are typical targets
Invasive angiography is ideal because the microaneurysms are small
options_after: The source diagnosis is polyarteritis nodosa
It is best treated by coil embolisation of most microaneurysms as first-line therapy
It usually affects primarily large elastic arteries such as the thoracic aorta
Renal, hepatic and mesenteric end-arterioles are typical targets
Invasive angiography is ideal because the microaneurysms are small
updates.explanation: The angiographic pattern of multiple tiny peripheral visceral aneurysms is described in the source as polyarteritis nodosa. PAN is a systemic necrotising vasculitis of small- and medium-sized arteries, typically affecting renal, hepatic and mesenteric end-arterioles. Invasive angiography is ideal because of the small size of the multiple microaneurysms, although CTA can now depict some of these lesions. Treatment is with steroids, not procedural embolisation of each aneurysm as primary therapy.

updates.question_text: Regarding CTA technique for suspected mesenteric ischaemia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CTA is the ideal imaging modality to assess acute or chronic mesenteric ischaemia
Only a single portal venous phase should be acquired for proper diagnosis
The arterial phase is acquired at approximately 30 seconds or with bolus tracking
The delayed or venous phase is acquired at approximately 90 seconds
MRA is the preferred first-line test in acute mesenteric ischaemia regardless of contrast status
options_after: CTA is the ideal imaging modality to assess acute or chronic mesenteric ischaemia
A portal venous phase alone is sufficient when bowel enhancement is the primary concern.
The arterial phase is acquired at approximately 30 seconds or with bolus tracking
The delayed or venous phase is acquired at approximately 90 seconds
MRA is the preferred first-line test in acute mesenteric ischaemia despite variation in contrast status
updates.explanation: CTA is described as the ideal modality for both acute and chronic mesenteric ischaemia. The protocol includes non-contrast, arterial and delayed/venous phases; the arterial phase is at about 30 seconds or bolus tracking, and the delayed/venous phase at about 90 seconds. MRA has a limited role in acute mesenteric ischaemia but can identify proximal stenosis or occlusion when iodinated contrast allergy is present. A single venous phase would miss key arterial and temporal findings.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute and chronic mesenteric ischaemia mechanisms, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An SMA embolus distal to the middle colic artery is low risk because distal collaterals are abundant
Acute in situ thrombosis is usually superimposed on existing atherosclerosis
Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is described as intestinal necrosis with a patent arterial tree
Chronic mesenteric ischaemia usually produces symptoms when only one mesenteric artery is diseased
Chronic mesenteric ischaemia can be treated endovascularly with angioplasty and stenting
options_after: An SMA embolus distal to the middle colic artery is low risk because distal collaterals are abundant
Acute in situ thrombosis is usually superimposed on existing atherosclerosis
Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is described as intestinal necrosis with a patent arterial tree
Chronic mesenteric ischaemia usually produces symptoms when a single mesenteric artery is diseased
Chronic mesenteric ischaemia can be treated endovascularly with angioplasty and stenting
updates.explanation: The source states that acute in situ thrombosis is usually superimposed on atherosclerosis. Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is described as intestinal necrosis with a patent arterial tree, although mesenteric arteries are diffusely attenuated on CTA from vasospasm. Chronic mesenteric ischaemia can be treated with angioplasty and stenting. An embolus distal to the middle colic artery is high risk because there are few native distal collaterals, and chronic symptoms usually require at least two of the celiac, SMA and IMA to be diseased.

updates.question_text: Regarding neurofibromatosis-related renal artery disease and renal AVF/AVM, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Neurofibromatosis may cause hypertension in children due to renal artery stenosis
NF1 renal artery stenosis may be angiographically indistinguishable from Takayasu arteritis
Renal AVFs are almost always acquired, secondary to trauma or renal biopsy
Renal AVMs are rare congenital entities and almost always have a vascular nidus
CTA cannot assess renal AVF or AVM because arterial and venous phases are indistinguishable
options_after: Neurofibromatosis may cause hypertension in children due to renal artery stenosis
NF1 renal artery stenosis may be angiographically indistinguishable from Takayasu arteritis
Renal AVFs are almost always acquired, secondary to trauma or renal biopsy
Renal AVMs are rare congenital entities and almost always have a vascular nidus
CTA will not assess renal AVF or AVM because arterial and venous phases are indistinguishable
updates.explanation: The source states that neurofibromatosis may cause childhood hypertension from renal artery stenosis, and that NF1-related stenosis may resemble Takayasu arteritis angiographically. Renal AVFs are direct artery-vein communications that are almost always acquired after trauma or renal biopsy. Renal AVMs are rare congenital lesions with a vascular nidus. CTA is described as an ideal modality for AVF or AVM, showing a large renal artery, aneurysmal dilatation near the venous communication and early renal vein opacification.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging diagnosis of gastrointestinal bleeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Upper GI bleeding is distal to the ligament of Treitz and accounts for approximately 85% of GI bleeding
Lower GI bleeding always presents with haematemesis and never with melena
Colonoscopy is not considered a first-line modality for lower GI bleeding
CTA performed within 4 hours or as soon as possible after the last bleeding episode has a higher positivity rate for extravasation
Intermittent bleeding is the most common cause of false-negative CTA results
options_after: Upper GI bleeding is distal to the ligament of Treitz and accounts for approximately 85% of GI bleeding
Lower GI bleeding characteristically presents with haematemesis and not with melena
Colonoscopy is not considered a first-line modality for lower GI bleeding
CTA performed within 4 hours or as soon as possible after the last bleeding episode has a higher positivity rate for extravasation
Intermittent bleeding is the most common cause of false-negative CTA results
updates.explanation: The source defines upper GI bleeding as proximal to the ligament of Treitz and lower GI bleeding as distal, with lower GI bleeding making up about 85%. Lower GI bleeding may present with haematochezia or melena; upper GI bleeding presents with haematemesis or melena. Colonoscopy is the first-line modality for diagnosing lower GI bleeding. CTA positivity for extravasation is higher when performed within 4 hours or as soon as possible after the last episode, and intermittent bleeding is the commonest cause of false-negative CTA.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging findings and modalities for active GI bleeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CTA protocol includes non-contrast, arterial and delayed or venous phases
Intraluminal contrast extravasation is the main criterion used to locate the bleeding point on CTA
Changing morphology of extravasated contrast on delayed images confirms the diagnosis
CTA and tagged red blood cell scintigraphy have comparable sensitivity to locate the bleeding point
CTA detects bleeding only at rates lower than 0.1 mL/min
options_after: CTA protocol includes non-contrast, arterial and delayed or venous phases
Intraluminal contrast extravasation is the main criterion used to locate the bleeding point on CTA
Changing morphology of extravasated contrast on delayed images confirms the diagnosis
CTA and tagged red blood cell scintigraphy have comparable sensitivity to locate the bleeding point
CTA detects bleeding primarily at rates lower than 0.1 mL/min
updates.explanation: The CTA protocol for GI bleeding includes non-contrast, arterial and delayed/venous phases. Intraluminal contrast extravasation is the main criterion for locating the bleeding point, and change in morphology over time on delayed images confirms active bleeding. CTA and tagged RBC scintigraphy have comparable sensitivities for detection, but CTA is more sensitive for localisation. The source lists tagged RBC scintigraphy as detecting less than 0.1 mL/min, while CTA detects approximately 0.3-0.5 mL/min.

updates.question_text: Regarding diverticular bleeding and angiodysplasia, which statement is correct?
options_before: Angiodysplasia should always stop the search for any other bleeding source
Diverticulosis is the most common cause of lower GI bleeding in young adults
Diverticular bleeding is diagnosed on CTA only when no diverticulosis is present
Angiodysplasia is typically located in the left colon and is never incidental
Most diverticular bleeds respond to conservative management, but angiography can be used when medical management fails
options_after: Angiodysplasia should characteristically stop the search for any other bleeding source
Diverticulosis is the most common cause of lower GI bleeding in young adults
Diverticular bleeding on CTA requires active extravasation arising from bowel without visible diverticulosis.
Angiodysplasia is typically located in the left colon and is not incidental
Most diverticular bleeds respond to conservative management, but angiography can be used when medical management fails
updates.explanation: The source states that diverticulosis is the most common cause of lower GI bleeding in older adults, and CTA shows active bleeding within extensive diverticulosis. Most patients respond to conservative management, but angiography is used for stable or unstable patients who fail medical management, with possible superselective embolisation or vasopressin infusion. Angiodysplasia is a common cause of chronic intermittent lower GI bleeding, most typically in the right colon or caecum, but its incidental prevalence means it should not stop the search for other sources.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal abdominopelvic venous anatomy and MR venography in this source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The portal venous system is the primary structure displayed on the illustrated normal MR venogram
The illustrated coronal MIP MR venogram demonstrates the renal veins, IVC and common iliac veins
Contrast MR venography is acquired as a single breath-hold arterial phase only
The protocol described uses multiplanar spoiled gradient-echo acquisition during three breath holds
The normal MR venogram image is primarily intended to demonstrate the hepatic arteries
options_after: The portal venous system is the primary structure displayed on the illustrated normal MR venogram
The illustrated coronal MIP MR venogram demonstrates the renal veins, IVC and common iliac veins
Contrast MR venography is acquired as a single breath-hold arterial phase in typical cases
The protocol described uses multiplanar spoiled gradient-echo acquisition during three breath holds
The normal MR venogram image is primarily intended to demonstrate the hepatic arteries
updates.explanation: The caption describes a coronal MIP MR venogram showing the renal veins, IVC and common iliac veins. It explicitly notes that the portal venous system is not portrayed. The described contrast MR venography technique uses multiplanar spoiled gradient-echo acquisitions during three breath holds to obtain arterial, first delayed and second delayed imaging. The image is venous rather than hepatic arterial.

updates.question_text: Regarding duplicated IVC and filter placement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Duplicated IVC is irrelevant to filter placement because a clot cannot bypass an infrarenal filter
A single filter may be placed above the IVC confluence
Alternatively, one filter can be placed in each duplicated IVC
On initial cavography, duplicated IVC is suggested by reflux into the portal venous system
Absence of iliac vein influx contralateral to the side injected is a clue when pre-procedural imaging is unavailable
options_after: Duplicated IVC is irrelevant to filter placement because a clot will not bypass an infrarenal filter
A single filter may be placed above the IVC confluence
Alternatively, one filter can be placed in each duplicated IVC
On initial cavography, duplicated IVC is suggested by reflux into the portal venous system
Absence of iliac vein influx contralateral to the side injected is a clue when pre-procedural imaging is unavailable
updates.explanation: The source states that duplicated IVC matters because a clot can circumnavigate a filter. To prevent this, either a single filter is placed above the IVC confluence or a filter is placed in each duplicated IVC. If pre-procedural imaging is absent, the lack of iliac vein influx contralateral to the injected side on initial cavography is a clue. Portal venous reflux is not described as the diagnostic clue.

updates.question_text: Regarding IVC imaging pitfalls, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pseudolipoma at the diaphragm results from volume averaging of prominent pericaval fat above the caudate lobe
Pseudolipoma is a true fat-containing IVC tumour requiring biopsy
Admixture artefact occurs only in the portal vein and not in the IVC
Admixture artefact can occur when enhanced renal venous blood mixes with non-opacified blood from the lower extremities
Contrast injection faster than 3 mL/sec prevents admixture artefact
options_after: Pseudolipoma at the diaphragm results from volume averaging of prominent pericaval fat above the caudate lobe
Pseudolipoma is a true fat-containing IVC tumour requiring biopsy
Admixture artefact occurs primarily in the portal vein and not in the IVC
Admixture artefact can occur when enhanced renal venous blood mixes with non-opacified blood from the lower extremities
Contrast injection faster than 3 mL/sec prevents admixture artefact
updates.explanation: Pseudolipoma is described as a common mimic at the diaphragmatic IVC due to volume averaging of prominent pericaval fat above the caudate lobe, especially in cirrhosis. Admixture artefact occurs where contrast-enhanced and non-opacified blood mix, including at the renal veins where renal venous blood mixes with lower-extremity venous return. It can also occur with retrograde flow in right heart failure and with fast contrast injection over 3 mL/sec. The source does not describe pseudolipoma as a true tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding nutcracker syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is compression of the left renal vein between the aorta and the SMA
The posterior variant compresses the duodenum between the SMA and the aorta
Symptoms may include pain, haematuria, orthostatic proteinuria, pelvic congestion and male varicocele
Narrowing of the renal vein alone is sufficient for diagnosis regardless of intravascular volume status
Prominent collateral flow, particularly through the left gonadal vein, supports the diagnosis
options_after: It is compression of the left renal vein between the aorta and the SMA
The posterior variant compresses the duodenum between the SMA and the aorta
Symptoms may include pain, haematuria, orthostatic proteinuria, pelvic congestion and male varicocele
Narrowing of the renal vein alone is sufficient for diagnosis despite variation in intravascular volume status
Prominent collateral flow, particularly through the left gonadal vein, supports the diagnosis
updates.explanation: Nutcracker syndrome is left renal vein compression between the aorta and SMA; the posterior variant involves compression of a retroaortic or circumaortic renal vein between the aorta and vertebral body. Symptoms include pain, haematuria, orthostatic proteinuria, pelvic congestion and varicocele in males. Ultrasound, CTA or MRA can assess the aorta-SMA angle, stenosis, upstream dilatation and left gonadal collateral pathways. The source warns that vein narrowing alone varies with intravascular volume status, so other findings should be included.

updates.question_text: Regarding nutcracker phenomenon and treatment, which statement is correct?
options_before: Nutcracker phenomenon means symptomatic left renal vein compression with haematuria
All patients require immediate renal vein stenting
Most cases of haematuria require nephrectomy within two years
Asymptomatic left renal vein compression is called nutcracker phenomenon
Observation is contraindicated because haematuria never resolves spontaneously
options_after: Nutcracker phenomenon means symptomatic left renal vein compression with haematuria
Most patients require immediate renal vein stenting
Most cases of haematuria require nephrectomy within two years
Asymptomatic left renal vein compression is called nutcracker phenomenon
Observation is contraindicated because haematuria will not resolve spontaneously
updates.explanation: The source defines asymptomatic compression as nutcracker phenomenon. Treatment depends on symptoms, and most cases of haematuria resolve within two years of observation. When treatment is desired, angioplasty and stenting of the renal vein can be performed. The source does not describe nephrectomy or mandatory immediate stenting as standard management.

updates.question_text: Regarding May-Thurner syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is chronic compression of the left common iliac vein by the crossing right common iliac artery against the lumbar vertebrae
It may occur with or without deep venous thrombosis
Chronic compression leads to fibrous adhesion in the vein, predisposing to thrombosis
The source recommends treatment with long-term anticoagulation alone and no endovascular therapy
CT venography or MR venography can diagnose compression and associated DVT
options_after: It is chronic compression of the left common iliac vein by the crossing right common iliac artery against the lumbar vertebrae
It may occur with or without deep venous thrombosis
Chronic compression leads to fibrous adhesion in the vein, predisposing to thrombosis
The source recommends treatment with long-term anticoagulation alone without endovascular therapy
CT venography or MR venography can diagnose compression and associated DVT
updates.explanation: May-Thurner syndrome is chronic compression of the left common iliac vein by the right common iliac artery against the lumbar vertebrae, and it may occur with or without DVT. Chronic compression causes a fibrous adhesion that predisposes to thrombosis. CT or MR venography can diagnose compression and thrombosis. The treatment described is endovascular thrombolysis followed by stenting, not anticoagulation alone as the definitive approach in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding superficial and deep venous anatomy of the arm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The superficial veins arise from the plantar venous arch and drain only to the deep veins
The cephalic vein drains the radial or lateral side and connects with the subclavian vein
The basilic vein drains the radial side and connects directly with the subclavian vein
The ulnar and radial deep veins do not accompany their corresponding arteries
The brachial vein is renamed the axillary vein at the axilla
options_after: The superficial veins arise from the plantar venous arch and drain primarily to the deep veins
The cephalic vein drains the radial or lateral side and connects with the subclavian vein
The basilic vein drains the radial side and connects directly with the subclavian vein
The ulnar and radial deep veins do not accompany their corresponding arteries
The brachial vein is renamed the axillary vein at the axilla
updates.explanation: The superficial veins arise from the dorsal venous arch of the hand and drain into the cephalic and basilic veins. The cephalic vein drains the radial/lateral side and connects with the subclavian vein. The basilic vein drains the ulnar/medial side and connects with the brachial or axillary vein. Deep venous drainage occurs through the ulnar and radial veins accompanying their arteries, and the brachial vein is renamed the axillary vein at the axilla.

updates.question_text: Regarding subclavian artery compression in thoracic outlet syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The typical clinical presentation is facial oedema that improves with standing
Symptoms include hand or finger pain, numbness, paraesthesias or coolness
Adson's manoeuvre may reduce the radial pulse in arterial thoracic outlet syndrome
Mechanical compression is usually absent and cannot be provoked by hyperabduction
Potential complications include mural thrombus, aneurysm and distal embolisation
options_after: The typical clinical presentation is facial oedema that improves with standing
Symptoms include hand or finger pain, numbness, paraesthesias or coolness
Adson's manoeuvre may reduce the radial pulse in arterial thoracic outlet syndrome
Mechanical compression is usually absent and will not be provoked by hyperabduction
Potential complications include mural thrombus, aneurysm and distal embolisation
updates.explanation: Subclavian artery compression presents with hand or finger pain, numbness, paraesthesias or coolness. Adson's manoeuvre can reduce the radial pulse in arterial thoracic outlet syndrome. Mechanical compression is almost always present and is exaggerated by hyperabduction; over 70% have a cervical rib. Complications include mural thrombus, aneurysm and distal embolisation, so the hands should be evaluated for distal emboli. Facial oedema improving with standing belongs to chronic SVC obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding hypothenar hammer syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It represents injury to the ulnar artery as it crosses the hamate bone
The classic history is acute facial and upper extremity oedema after central venous catheter placement
The radial artery is chronically traumatised at the scaphoid, producing first and second digit ischaemia
Ultrasound is used initially, followed by CTA or MRA
Treatment is medical observation because angiography always shows the full extent of ulnar artery injury
options_after: It represents injury to the ulnar artery as it crosses the hamate bone
The classic history is acute facial and upper extremity oedema after central venous catheter placement
The radial artery is chronically traumatised at the scaphoid, producing first and second digit ischaemia
Ultrasound is used initially, followed by CTA or MRA
Treatment is medical observation because angiography characteristically shows the full extent of ulnar artery injury
updates.explanation: Hypothenar hammer syndrome is ulnar artery injury where it crosses the hamate, caused by chronic repetitive trauma. The classic clinical history is a jackhammer operator with ischaemia of the fourth and fifth digits. Ultrasound is the initial imaging modality, followed by CTA or MRA. Imaging may show corkscrew or tortuous distal ulnar artery at the hook of hamate, aneurysmal dilatation and distal embolic occlusions. Treatment is surgical because ulnar artery injury may not be apparent on angiography.

updates.question_text: Regarding small-vessel hand ischaemia differentials in this source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Buerger disease is a non-inflammatory vasospastic disorder triggered only by cold temperature
Raynaud disease most commonly causes distal corkscrew collaterals and fixed thrombotic occlusions
Buerger disease is thromboangiitis obliterans and is seen in adult male smokers
Raynaud disease shows decreased distal digital arterial perfusion with improvement on warming or vasodilator administration
Distal thromboembolic disease is characterised by occlusion of distal small arteries of the hand
options_after: Buerger disease is a non-inflammatory vasospastic disorder triggered primarily by cold temperature
Raynaud disease most commonly causes distal corkscrew collaterals and fixed thrombotic occlusions
Buerger disease is thromboangiitis obliterans and is seen in adult male smokers
Raynaud disease shows decreased distal digital arterial perfusion with improvement on warming or vasodilator administration
Distal thromboembolic disease is characterised by occlusion of distal small arteries of the hand
updates.explanation: Buerger disease, or thromboangiitis obliterans, is a chronic inflammatory thrombotic arteritis, usually seen in adult male smokers, with small-vessel occlusions and distal corkscrew collaterals. Raynaud disease is small arterial vasospasm triggered by cold and associated with scleroderma and other connective tissue disorders; imaging shows distal perfusion reduction that improves with warming or vasodilators. Thromboembolic disease causes occlusion of distal small arteries of the hand. The first two statements swap the described features between Buerger and Raynaud disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding CTA, MRA and non-contrast MRA in chronic lower extremity PAD, which statement is correct?
options_before: CTA is unable to detect occlusion from calcified plaque
Blooming artefact from calcified plaque improves below-knee arterial assessment
Time-resolved MRA is not useful in calf arterial assessment
QISS non-contrast MRA has high diagnostic accuracy compared with DSA and is less prone to artefact than CTA
MRA has no role after abnormal ABI or ultrasound findings
options_after: CTA is unable to detect occlusion from calcified plaque
Blooming artefact from calcified plaque improves below-knee arterial assessment
Time-resolved MRA is not useful in calf arterial assessment
QISS non-contrast MRA has high diagnostic accuracy compared with DSA and is less prone to artefact than CTA
MRA has negligible role after abnormal ABI or ultrasound findings
updates.explanation: The source states that non-contrast quiescent interval single-shot MRA has been used clinically with high diagnostic accuracy compared with DSA and is less prone to artefact than CTA. CTA can detect luminal narrowing, irregularity and occlusion from calcified and non-calcified plaque, although blooming from calcified plaque can limit below-knee assessment. Time-resolved MRA through the calves can demonstrate stenosis or occlusion and complements conventional MRA. CTA or MRA can be used for anatomical mapping and to confirm ABI or ultrasound findings.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute thromboembolic lower limb disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute limb ischaemia presents with acute onset pain, pallor, poikilothermia, pulselessness and paraesthesias
Blue toe syndrome is acute thromboembolism in the toes
The most common embolic source is a left atrial thrombus, with atrial fibrillation as a significant risk factor
Significant atherosclerotic disease must always be present for the diagnosis
Treatment options include surgical embolectomy, bypass graft and endovascular thrombolysis
options_after: Acute limb ischaemia presents with acute onset pain, pallor, poikilothermia, pulselessness and paraesthesias
Blue toe syndrome is acute thromboembolism in the toes
The most common embolic source is a left atrial thrombus, with atrial fibrillation as a significant risk factor
Significant atherosclerotic disease must characteristically be present for the diagnosis
Treatment options include surgical embolectomy, bypass graft and endovascular thrombolysis
updates.explanation: Acute thromboembolic limb disease differs from chronic atherosclerotic PAD by abrupt onset with pain, pallor, poikilothermia, pulselessness and paraesthesias. Blue toe syndrome is acute thromboembolism in the toes. The common embolic source is a left atrial thrombus, with atrial fibrillation a major risk factor, and echocardiography is indicated in the workup. CTA or MRA shows an acute vessel cutoff with a filling defect at a bifurcation; significant atherosclerosis may be absent. Treatment options include surgical embolectomy, bypass and endovascular thrombolysis.

updates.question_text: Regarding popliteal artery aneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Popliteal aneurysm is defined only when diameter exceeds 2 cm
Popliteal aneurysms are almost always due to atherosclerosis and are associated with other atherosclerotic aneurysms
Rupture is the typical presenting symptom
Cross-sectional imaging is unnecessary because mural thrombus never alters luminal calibre
Treatment is recommended for symptomatic aneurysms and asymptomatic aneurysms greater than 2 cm
options_after: Popliteal aneurysm is defined primarily when diameter exceeds 2 cm
Popliteal aneurysms are almost always due to atherosclerosis and are associated with other atherosclerotic aneurysms
Rupture is the typical presenting symptom
Cross-sectional imaging is unnecessary because mural thrombus will not alter luminal calibre
Treatment is recommended for symptomatic aneurysms and asymptomatic aneurysms greater than 2 cm
updates.explanation: The source defines popliteal artery aneurysm as diameter of 8 mm or more. These aneurysms are almost always atherosclerotic and associated with other atherosclerotic aneurysms; about 20% of patients also have an aortic aneurysm and up to half have bilateral popliteal aneurysms. They are usually asymptomatic, and distal ischaemia from embolism is the typical symptomatic presentation, while rupture is rare. CTA or MRA is important because mural thrombus can narrow the lumen and obscure true aneurysm size.

updates.question_text: Regarding carotid ultrasound conventions and plaque assessment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In sagittal carotid images, the patient's head is conventionally on the left side of the image and the feet on the right
Carotid plaque morphology is evaluated only with spectral Doppler and never with grayscale imaging
Less than 50% cross-sectional area plaque is expected to be haemodynamically significant
The carotid exam includes plaque morphology, haemodynamic evaluation and waveform analysis
Normal arterial flow is usually optimised to appear below the baseline
options_after: In sagittal carotid images, the patient's head is conventionally on the left side of the image and the feet on the right
Carotid plaque morphology is evaluated primarily with spectral Doppler and not with grayscale imaging
Less than 50% cross-sectional area plaque is expected to be haemodynamically significant
The carotid exam includes plaque morphology, haemodynamic evaluation and waveform analysis
Normal arterial flow is usually optimised to appear below the baseline
updates.explanation: For sagittal carotid images, the head is conventionally displayed on the left and the feet on the right. The carotid examination includes plaque morphology, haemodynamic evaluation and waveform analysis. Plaque morphology is assessed on grayscale imaging and described by absolute percent stenosis. Less than 50% cross-sectional plaque is not expected to be haemodynamically significant, while more than 50% luminal plaque should elevate PSV. The source notes that arterial flow is optimised so normal arterial flow is above the baseline.

updates.question_text: Regarding DVT diagnosis and chronic thrombus features, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Colour Doppler is necessary for diagnosing all DVTs and compression is optional
Normal colour Doppler flow in a noncompressible vein excludes non-obstructing thrombus
Echogenicity of clot is a reliable way to determine thrombus age
The hallmark sonographic finding is a noncompressible vein with or without intraluminal clot
Chronic thrombus may show clot retraction, thickened echogenic vein walls, partial compressibility and collateral veins
options_after: Colour Doppler is necessary for diagnosing most DVTs and compression is optional
Normal colour Doppler flow in a noncompressible vein excludes non-obstructing thrombus
Echogenicity of clot is a reliable way to determine thrombus age
The hallmark sonographic finding is a noncompressible vein with or without intraluminal clot
Chronic thrombus may show clot retraction, thickened echogenic vein walls, partial compressibility and collateral veins
updates.explanation: The hallmark DVT finding is a noncompressible vein, with or without visible intraluminal clot. A partially thrombosed vein may be partially compressible, while complete thrombosis is noncompressible. Colour Doppler helps localise veins but is not necessary for diagnosis, and normal colour flow in a noncompressible vein is suspicious for non-obstructing thrombus. Echogenicity is unreliable for clot age; chronic features include retraction, poor visualisation, partial compressibility, irregular thickened echogenic walls and collateral veins.

updates.question_text: Regarding abdominal aortic aneurysm ultrasound screening and assessment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Screening ultrasound is performed for patients aged 65 years or older
Screening is also performed for patients aged 50 years or older with positive family history or personal history of aortic or peripheral vascular aneurysm
Transverse and longitudinal images of the proximal, mid and distal aorta and common iliac arteries are obtained
Colour or spectral Doppler is not useful because it cannot document intraluminal thrombus or endoleaks
A 5.6 cm infrarenal aortic aneurysm with mural thrombus is below the source definition of aneurysm
options_after: Screening ultrasound is performed for patients aged 65 years or older
Screening is also performed for patients aged 50 years or older with positive family history or personal history of aortic or peripheral vascular aneurysm
Transverse and longitudinal images of the proximal, mid and distal aorta and common iliac arteries are obtained
Colour or spectral Doppler is not useful because it will not document intraluminal thrombus or endoleaks
A 5.6 cm infrarenal aortic aneurysm with mural thrombus is below the source definition of aneurysm
updates.explanation: The source states that screening ultrasound is performed for patients aged 65 years or older, or 50 years or older with a positive family history or personal history of aortic or peripheral vascular aneurysm. The exam obtains transverse and longitudinal images of proximal, mid and distal aorta and common iliac arteries. Colour Doppler or spectral waveform analysis helps confirm patency, detect intraluminal thrombus and document endoleaks. A 5.6 cm infrarenal aneurysm with mural thrombus is clearly aneurysmal in the source caption.

updates.question_text: Regarding pre-procedure preparation for interventional radiology procedures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: NPO fasting is required before procedures performed using local anaesthetic alone
The consultation should include a directed history and physical examination, discussion of risks and benefits, formal signed consent, and safety review
The choice of anaesthesia is determined only by operator preference rather than by patient factors or procedure invasiveness
Moderate procedural sedation may be delivered with intravenous midazolam and fentanyl by non-anaesthesiologist procedural staff under continuous monitoring
ASA fasting guidance includes longer fasting for full meals, shorter fasting for light meals, and the shortest interval for clear liquids
options_after: NPO fasting is required before procedures performed using local anaesthetic alone
The consultation should include a directed history and physical examination, discussion of risks and benefits, formal signed consent, and safety review
The choice of anaesthesia is determined primarily by operator preference rather than by patient factors or procedure invasiveness
Moderate procedural sedation may be delivered with intravenous midazolam and fentanyl by non-anaesthesiologist procedural staff under continuous monitoring
ASA fasting guidance includes longer fasting for full meals, shorter fasting for light meals, and the shortest interval for clear liquids
updates.explanation: The source emphasises that pre-procedure planning includes clinical assessment, consent, discussion of risks and benefits, and review of safety concerns. Moderate procedural sedation can use midazolam and fentanyl under continuous monitoring by procedural staff, with reversal agents available for opioids and benzodiazepines. NPO fasting is not needed for local anaesthesia alone, while ASA fasting guidance is graduated by meal type: full meals require the longest interval, light meals less, and clear liquids the shortest.

updates.question_text: Regarding embolization technique and complications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Coiling a vessel preserves distal access for retreatment, which is the main advantage of coils
Non-target embolization is limited to uterine fibroid embolization and is not a recognised risk during bronchial artery embolization
When coiling a specific lesion, the general technique is to coil distal to the lesion and then proximal to it
Post-embolization syndrome typically occurs within the first day and may present with pain, cramping, fever, nausea, and vomiting
Absorbable gelatin sponge is classified as a permanent embolic agent
options_after: Coiling a vessel preserves distal access for retreatment, which is the main advantage of coils
Non-target embolization is limited to uterine fibroid embolization and is not a recognised risk during bronchial artery embolization
When coiling a specific lesion, the general technique is to coil distal to the lesion and then proximal to it
Post-embolization syndrome typically occurs within the first day and may present with pain, cramping, fever, nausea, and vomiting
Absorbable gelatin sponge is classified as a long-term embolic agent
updates.explanation: For a specific lesion, the source describes coiling distal to the lesion first and then proximal to it, reducing recurrent bleeding from retrograde collaterals. Post-embolization syndrome usually occurs within the first day, with pain, cramping, fever, nausea, and vomiting, and is treated supportively with NSAIDs, opioids when appropriate, and IV fluids. Coiling sacrifices distal access rather than preserving it. Non-target embolization is a broader complication, including ovarian embolization during fibroid embolization and cerebral or spinal embolization during bronchial artery embolization.

updates.question_text: Regarding arteriovenous fistula and air embolism after vascular access, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Low femoral arterial puncture increases the risk of iatrogenic arteriovenous fistula because the femoral vein may pass deep to the artery distally
Iatrogenic arteriovenous fistulas are always immediately symptomatic and require emergency treatment
Doppler features of arteriovenous fistula include arterial flow within a vein and increased diastolic flow in the artery proximal to the fistula
If air embolism is suspected during catheter insertion into a peel-away sheath, the patient should be placed left side down and given 100% oxygen
Catheter aspiration is mandatory for every suspected air embolism regardless of bubble size
options_after: Low femoral arterial puncture increases the risk of iatrogenic arteriovenous fistula because the femoral vein may pass deep to the artery distally
Iatrogenic arteriovenous fistulas are characteristically immediately symptomatic and require emergency treatment
Doppler features of arteriovenous fistula include arterial flow within a vein and increased diastolic flow in the artery proximal to the fistula
If air embolism is suspected during catheter insertion into a peel-away sheath, the patient should be placed left side down and given 100% oxygen
Catheter aspiration is mandatory whenever intravascular air is suspected, independent of bubble volume.
updates.explanation: A low femoral arterial puncture increases AVF risk because the femoral vein may pass deep to the artery distal to the standard puncture site. Doppler shows arterial flow in a vein, loss of normal triphasic arterial waveform, and increased diastolic flow in the feeding artery. For suspected air embolism during insertion into a peel-away sheath, immediate left-lateral decubitus positioning and 100% oxygen are recommended. Catheter aspiration is only considered when the air bubble is large and practical to treat.

updates.question_text: Regarding replaced right hepatic artery anatomy, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It arises from the left gastric artery and supplies the left hepatic lobe
It is always clinically irrelevant because the portal vein completely protects the right lobe from ischaemia
It may be advantageous in a living right hepatic donor because it is longer and larger than a regular right hepatic artery
It is defined as an additional artery from the SMA in the presence of a normal right hepatic artery
It is present in fewer than 1% of patients
options_after: It arises from the left gastric artery and supplies the left hepatic lobe
It is characteristically clinically irrelevant because the portal vein completely protects the right lobe from ischaemia
It may be advantageous in a living right hepatic donor because it is longer and larger than a regular right hepatic artery
It is defined as an additional artery from the SMA in the presence of a normal right hepatic artery
It is present in fewer than 1% of patients
updates.explanation: The source notes that a replaced right hepatic artery can be beneficial in a living right hepatic donor because it is longer and larger than a usual right hepatic artery, allowing better recipient anastomosis. It arises from the SMA and replaces the usual right hepatic artery rather than being additional to it. An additional artery from the SMA with a normal right hepatic artery is an accessory right hepatic artery. The source also states that SMA stenosis may theoretically predispose the right lobe to ischaemia, although this is usually not clinically relevant.

updates.question_text: Regarding general management principles for traumatic vascular injury in interventional radiology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conservative management is preferred for unstable patients with CT contrast extravasation from high-grade solid organ injuries
Trauma accounts for the majority of interventional radiology emergencies
Stable patients with low-grade solid organ injury are best managed with resuscitation, monitoring, serial laboratory values, and serial examinations
Stable patients with moderate-to-high-grade injuries and CT contrast extravasation or pseudoaneurysm are appropriate candidates for angiography and embolization
IR embolization is only applicable to contained haemorrhage and cannot be used for uncontained bleeding
options_after: Conservative management is preferred for unstable patients with CT contrast extravasation from high-grade solid organ injuries
Trauma accounts for the majority of interventional radiology emergencies
Stable patients with low-grade solid organ injury are best managed with resuscitation, monitoring, serial laboratory values, and serial examinations
Stable patients with moderate-to-high-grade injuries and CT contrast extravasation or pseudoaneurysm are appropriate candidates for angiography and embolization
IR embolization is primarily applicable to contained haemorrhage and will not be used for uncontained bleeding
updates.explanation: The source states that trauma accounts for most IR emergencies. Stable patients with low-grade solid organ injury are generally managed conservatively with resuscitation, vital and laboratory monitoring, and serial examinations. Angiography and embolization are best for stable patients with moderate-to-high-grade injury plus CT evidence of active extravasation or pseudoaneurysm. Embolization may be applied to contained or uncontained haemorrhage to avoid surgery.

updates.question_text: Regarding traumatic aortic and renal injury, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CTA is the gold standard for evaluation of suspected traumatic aortic injury
Endovascular repair remains contraindicated for acute traumatic aortic injury because open repair is the only treatment described
Renal trauma is most commonly penetrating rather than blunt
Haematuria is rarely present in renal trauma regardless of mechanism
A horseshoe kidney is particularly susceptible to trauma because it is not protected by the inferior ribs and may be compressed against the vertebral column
options_after: CTA is the gold standard for evaluation of suspected traumatic aortic injury
Endovascular repair remains contraindicated for acute traumatic aortic injury because open repair is the principal treatment described
Renal trauma is most commonly penetrating rather than blunt
Haematuria is rarely present in renal trauma despite variation in mechanism
A horseshoe kidney is particularly susceptible to trauma because it is not protected by the inferior ribs and may be compressed against the vertebral column
updates.explanation: CTA is described as the gold standard for evaluating suspected traumatic aortic injury. Open surgical repair is the gold standard treatment, but endovascular stent-graft repair is increasingly performed. Renal trauma is more often blunt than penetrating, and haematuria is usually present regardless of aetiology. A horseshoe kidney is vulnerable because of reduced rib protection and possible compression against the vertebral column.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal trauma classification and endovascular treatment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Grades I-III renal injuries include non-expanding haematomas or parenchymal laceration without collecting system injury and are usually managed conservatively
OIS grade IV renal injury always requires nephrectomy as first-line treatment
OIS grade V renal injury is a minor contusion with no collecting system or vascular injury
Endovascular treatment indications include active extravasation, dissection, or pseudoaneurysm
Superselective coil embolization is the usual endovascular treatment for suitable renal trauma
options_after: Grades I-III renal injuries include non-expanding haematomas or parenchymal laceration without collecting system injury and are usually managed conservatively
OIS grade IV renal injury characteristically requires nephrectomy as first-line treatment
OIS grade V renal injury is a minor contusion without collecting system or vascular injury
Endovascular treatment indications include active extravasation, dissection, or pseudoaneurysm
Superselective coil embolization is the usual endovascular treatment for suitable renal trauma
updates.explanation: The source states that renal OIS grades I-III are non-expanding haematomas or parenchymal lacerations without collecting system injury and are usually conservative. Grade IV includes deep laceration into the collecting system or vascular injury with contained haemorrhage, and may be treated endovascularly. Grade V is the most severe injury, with shattered kidney or hilar avulsion, and is surgical. Endovascular indications include active extravasation, dissection, and pseudoaneurysm, usually treated with superselective coil embolization.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal arteriovenous fistulas, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: They are usually congenital rather than acquired
Angiography shows venous opacification during the arterial phase
The majority present with high-output cardiac failure
Treatment is always nephrectomy rather than endovascular embolization
They are most commonly caused by portal hypertension
options_after: They are usually congenital rather than acquired
Angiography shows venous opacification during the arterial phase
The majority present with high-output cardiac failure
Treatment is characteristically nephrectomy rather than endovascular embolization
They are most commonly caused by portal hypertension
updates.explanation: The source states that renal AVFs are almost always acquired, usually secondary to trauma or renal biopsy. Most are asymptomatic and often heal spontaneously, although haematuria is the most common symptom when they are symptomatic. Angiography shows early venous opacification during the arterial phase. Treatment, when needed, is embolization with coils, glue, or alcohol rather than nephrectomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding pelvic vascular trauma and embolization strategy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A 3 cm pubic symphysis diastasis doubles potential intrapelvic volume to approximately 8 litres
In active pelvic bleeding with pelvic fractures, angiography is usually performed before orthopaedic surgery
Initial treatment should begin with superselective catheterisation of every visible distal bleeding branch before any overview angiogram
The first angiographic step is a nonselective pelvic arteriogram followed by selective bilateral internal iliac arteriograms
Rapid nonselective gelfoam embolization of an entire anterior or posterior internal iliac division may be acceptable in life-threatening haemorrhage because of rich pelvic collateral supply
options_after: A 3 cm pubic symphysis diastasis doubles potential intrapelvic volume to approximately 8 litres
In active pelvic bleeding with pelvic fractures, angiography is usually performed before orthopaedic surgery
Initial treatment should begin with superselective catheterisation of most visible distal bleeding branches before any overview angiogram
The first angiographic step is a nonselective pelvic arteriogram followed by selective bilateral internal iliac arteriograms
Rapid nonselective gelfoam embolization of an entire anterior or posterior internal iliac division may be acceptable in life-threatening haemorrhage because of rich pelvic collateral supply
updates.explanation: The source emphasises that pelvic bleeding can be catastrophic, with 3 cm symphyseal diastasis doubling intrapelvic volume to about 8 litres. In the setting of active bleeding and pelvic fracture, angiography usually precedes orthopaedic surgery because surgical control is difficult. The angiographic sequence starts with nonselective pelvic arteriography, followed by selective bilateral internal iliac arteriography. In life-threatening haemorrhage, time-consuming superselective embolization may be avoided in favour of rapid nonselective gelfoam embolization of the relevant internal iliac division.

updates.question_text: Regarding localisation and causes of haemoptysis before embolization, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Pre-procedure bronchoscopy and CTA are not useful because angiography alone is always diagnostic
Pre-procedure bronchoscopy or CTA can help localise the bleeding site
Worldwide, cystic fibrosis and thoracic malignancy are more common causes than tuberculosis or fungal infection
If bronchial and pulmonary arterial evaluation is negative, no other systemic vessels should be assessed
If bleeding persists after bronchial and pulmonary arterial evaluation, the subclavian, internal mammary, inferior phrenic, and celiac arteries may need assessment
options_after: Pre-procedure bronchoscopy and CTA are not useful because angiography alone is characteristically diagnostic
Pre-procedure bronchoscopy or CTA can help localise the bleeding site
Worldwide, cystic fibrosis and thoracic malignancy are more common causes than tuberculosis or fungal infection
After negative bronchial and pulmonary arterial evaluation, assessment of additional systemic arteries adds little.
If bleeding persists after bronchial and pulmonary arterial evaluation, the subclavian, internal mammary, inferior phrenic, and celiac arteries may need assessment
updates.explanation: The source states that bronchoscopy or CTA before the procedure can localise the site of bleeding. Most haemoptysis involves bronchial arteries, but pulmonary arteries and occasionally other systemic arteries may be involved. If bleeding continues after evaluating bronchial and pulmonary arterial circulation, systemic sources such as subclavian, internal mammary, inferior phrenic, and celiac arteries should be considered. In the United States cystic fibrosis and thoracic malignancy are common causes, whereas worldwide tuberculosis and fungal infection are more common.

updates.question_text: Regarding clinical associations of pulmonary arteriovenous malformations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is also known as Kawasaki disease
HHT-related pulmonary AVMs are expected to cause only left-to-right shunting and pulmonary oedema
HHT may present clinically with brain abscess, stroke, or recurrent epistaxis
Nasal mucosal telangiectasia is unrelated to recurrent epistaxis in HHT
Patients with HHT may have multiple pulmonary AVMs
options_after: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is also known as Kawasaki disease
HHT-related pulmonary AVMs are expected to cause primarily left-to-right shunting and pulmonary oedema
HHT may present clinically with brain abscess, stroke, or recurrent epistaxis
Nasal mucosal telangiectasia is unrelated to recurrent epistaxis in HHT
Patients with HHT may have multiple pulmonary AVMs
updates.explanation: The source equates hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia with Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome and notes that these patients may have multiple pulmonary AVMs. Clinical presentations include brain abscess, stroke, or recurrent epistaxis due to nasal mucosal telangiectasia. The shunt through a pulmonary AVM is right-to-left, explaining paradoxical embolic or septic complications rather than pulmonary oedema from a left-to-right shunt.

updates.question_text: Regarding embolization of pulmonary arteriovenous malformations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Coils must be used to embolize a pulmonary AVM
Particles are contraindicated because the right-to-left shunt can cause brain emboli and infarction
Most pulmonary AVMs require complete embolization of the entire nidus from multiple systemic arterial feeders
Most pulmonary AVMs have a single feeding artery, and coiling the inflow artery via a pulmonary arterial approach is usually sufficient
Asymptomatic pulmonary AVMs should never be treated regardless of feeding artery size
options_after: Coils must be used to embolize a pulmonary AVM
Particles are contraindicated because the right-to-left shunt can cause brain emboli and infarction
Most pulmonary AVMs require complete embolization of the entire nidus from multiple systemic arterial feeders
Most pulmonary AVMs have a single feeding artery, and coiling the inflow artery via a pulmonary arterial approach is usually sufficient
Asymptomatic pulmonary AVMs should not be treated despite variation in feeding artery size
updates.explanation: The source states that coils must be used for pulmonary AVM embolization and particles are contraindicated because right-to-left shunting can produce cerebral emboli and infarction. Most pulmonary AVMs have a single feeding artery, so coiling the inflow artery through a pulmonary arterial approach is usually sufficient. This differs from peripheral limb AVMs, where the entire nidus often needs treatment. An asymptomatic lesion with a feeding artery larger than 3 mm is an indication for treatment.

updates.question_text: Regarding the difference between pulmonary and peripheral arteriovenous malformation treatment, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Pulmonary AVM treatment requires liquid sclerosant injection into the venous drainage limb rather than feeding artery occlusion
Peripheral limb AVMs are treated like most pulmonary AVMs by coiling only a single inflow artery
Particles are preferred for pulmonary AVMs because they pass safely through right-to-left shunts
Peripheral AVM treatment generally requires elimination of the entire nidus, which is often supplied by multiple arterial branches
Pulmonary AVMs are never treated if the patient has had brain abscess or infarct
options_after: Pulmonary AVM treatment requires liquid sclerosant injection into the venous drainage limb rather than feeding artery occlusion
Peripheral limb AVMs are treated like most pulmonary AVMs by coiling primarily a single inflow artery
Particles are preferred for pulmonary AVMs because they pass safely through right-to-left shunts
Peripheral AVM treatment generally requires elimination of the entire nidus, which is often supplied by multiple arterial branches
Pulmonary AVMs are not treated if the patient has had brain abscess or infarct
updates.explanation: The source explicitly contrasts pulmonary AVMs with peripheral AVMs. Most pulmonary AVMs have a single feeding artery, where coiling the inflow artery is usually sufficient. Peripheral AVMs, such as those in a limb, generally require elimination of the entire nidus, often fed by multiple arterial branches. Particles are contraindicated in pulmonary AVMs because of the right-to-left shunt, and symptomatic lesions such as those associated with prior infarct or brain abscess are treatment indications.

updates.question_text: Regarding obstetric haemorrhage and uterine artery pseudoaneurysm, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Antepartum haemorrhage causes listed in the source are usually treated first with bronchial artery embolization
Antepartum haemorrhage can be caused by placenta previa, placental abruption, and uterine rupture
Postpartum haemorrhage may be caused by uterine inversion, uterine atony, and genital tract trauma
Uterine artery pseudoaneurysms typically present immediately during delivery and are never diagnosed by ultrasound or CT
Interventional radiology can interrogate the internal iliac arteries diagnostically and therapeutically for postpartum haemorrhage, often identifying the uterine artery as the source
options_after: Antepartum haemorrhage causes listed in the source are usually treated first with bronchial artery embolization
Antepartum haemorrhage can be caused by placenta previa, placental abruption, and uterine rupture
Postpartum haemorrhage may be caused by uterine inversion, uterine atony, and genital tract trauma
Uterine artery pseudoaneurysms typically present immediately during delivery and are not diagnosed by ultrasound or CT
Interventional radiology can interrogate the internal iliac arteries diagnostically and therapeutically for postpartum haemorrhage, often identifying the uterine artery as the source
updates.explanation: The source lists placenta previa, placental abruption, and uterine rupture as causes of antepartum haemorrhage, usually managed with urgent Caesarean section or hysterectomy, with IR support such as balloon catheter placement and haemorrhage control. Postpartum haemorrhage causes include uterine inversion, uterine atony, and genital tract trauma. IR can interrogate the internal iliac arteries for diagnosis and treatment, often targeting the uterine artery. Uterine artery pseudoaneurysms typically present several weeks after delivery and are usually diagnosed by ultrasound or CT before embolization.

updates.question_text: Regarding diverticular lower GI bleeding, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Diverticulosis is a rare cause of lower GI bleeding in older adults
Angiography is reserved only for unstable patients and is never used in stable patients
If active extravasation is seen, treatment options include superselective embolization, most commonly with coils, or vasopressin infusion
Diverticular bleeding is treated by empiric nonselective embolization even when no active extravasation is present
Surgery is always required before any endovascular treatment attempt
options_after: Diverticulosis is a rare cause of lower GI bleeding in older adults
Angiography is reserved primarily for unstable patients and is not used in stable patients
If active extravasation is seen, treatment options include superselective embolization, most commonly with coils, or vasopressin infusion
Empiric nonselective embolization is appropriate when CTA shows absent active extravasation.
Surgery is characteristically required before any endovascular treatment attempt
updates.explanation: Diverticulosis is the most common cause of lower GI bleeding in older adults. Most patients respond to conservative treatment, but angiography can be used in stable or unstable patients who fail medical management. When active extravasation is seen, superselective embolization, most commonly with coils, or vasopressin infusion are potential therapies. The example shows selective and superselective angiography guiding a treatment decision when the bleed was distal and difficult to reach.

updates.question_text: Regarding angiodysplasia and haemorrhoidal bleeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Angiodysplasia is a small age-related vascular malformation and a common cause of unexplained GI bleeding and anaemia
Heyde syndrome is the association of aortic valve stenosis and bleeding from angiodysplasia
Angiodysplasia is confined to the oesophagus and never occurs in the colon
Haemorrhoidal embolization requires excision of the haemorrhoidal tissue to preserve continence
Endovascular occlusion of distal superior rectal artery branches can preserve anal continence and avoid creation of rectal wounds
options_after: Angiodysplasia is a small age-related vascular malformation and a common cause of unexplained GI bleeding and anaemia
Heyde syndrome is the association of aortic valve stenosis and bleeding from angiodysplasia
Angiodysplasia is confined to the oesophagus and will not occur in the colon
Haemorrhoidal embolization requires excision of the haemorrhoidal tissue to preserve continence
Endovascular occlusion of distal superior rectal artery branches can preserve anal continence and avoid creation of rectal wounds
updates.explanation: The source describes angiodysplasia as an age-related vascular malformation and a common cause of otherwise unexplained GI bleeding and anaemia. It is most common in the caecum and ascending colon but can occur anywhere in the GI tract. Heyde syndrome links aortic stenosis with bleeding from angiodysplasia. Haemorrhoidal embolization leaves the haemorrhoidal tissue in place, preserves continence, and avoids rectal wounds.

updates.question_text: Regarding endovascular haemorrhoid embolization, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The target vessel is usually the inferior pulmonary artery
Only liquid glue is described as an acceptable embolic agent
Particle embolization is avoided because it always causes anal incontinence
Coil occlusion of distal superior rectal artery branches can be used
Particles may involve more distal branches and decrease recurrence risk
options_after: The target vessel is usually the inferior pulmonary artery
Liquid embolic agents are preferred because coils do not reach distal superior rectal branches.
Particle embolization is avoided because it characteristically causes anal incontinence
Coil occlusion of distal superior rectal artery branches can be used
Particles may involve more distal branches and decrease recurrence risk
updates.explanation: The source describes endovascular coil occlusion of distal superior rectal artery branches for haemorrhoidal bleeding. It also states that coil or particle embolization may be used, with particles potentially reaching more distal branches and decreasing recurrence risk. The advantage of the endovascular approach is preserving haemorrhoidal tissue and continence without creating rectal wounds.

updates.question_text: Regarding endovascular therapy and nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Endovascular thrombolysis or suction embolectomy may be performed in selected acute embolic cases without peritoneal signs or clinical findings of bowel necrosis
Endovascular therapy is first-line for all acute mesenteric ischaemia regardless of peritoneal findings
Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is also known as intestinal necrosis with an occluded arterial tree
Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is low mortality and usually managed with observation
Direct arterial infusion of papaverine is the primary treatment of nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia
options_after: Endovascular thrombolysis or suction embolectomy may be performed in selected acute embolic cases without peritoneal signs or clinical findings of bowel necrosis
Endovascular therapy is first-line for most acute mesenteric ischaemia despite variation in peritoneal findings
Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is also known as intestinal necrosis with an occluded arterial tree
Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is low mortality and usually managed with observation
Direct arterial infusion of papaverine is the primary treatment of nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia
updates.explanation: The source limits endovascular therapy for acute embolic mesenteric ischaemia to selected patients without peritoneal signs or clinical evidence of bowel necrosis. Nonocclusive mesenteric ischaemia is a highly lethal form of acute mesenteric ischaemia, also called intestinal necrosis with a patent arterial tree, and features spasm and narrowing of multiple mesenteric arterial branches. The source gives direct arterial papaverine infusion as the primary treatment.

updates.question_text: Regarding aneurysm terminology, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Aneurysm is defined when an artery is twice the size of the normal vessel
A true aneurysm involves all three arterial wall layers: intima, media, and adventitia
A pseudoaneurysm contains all three arterial wall layers
Pseudoaneurysm is limited to congenital connective-tissue disease and is not associated with trauma, malignancy, or infection
Management decisions are based only on whether the aneurysm is fusiform or saccular
options_after: Aneurysm is defined when an artery is twice the size of the normal vessel
A true aneurysm involves all three arterial wall layers: intima, media, and adventitia
A pseudoaneurysm contains most three arterial wall layers
Pseudoaneurysm is limited to congenital connective-tissue disease and is not associated with trauma, malignancy, or infection
Management decisions are based primarily on whether the aneurysm is fusiform or saccular
updates.explanation: The source defines aneurysm as an artery measuring 1.5 times the normal vessel size. A true aneurysm involves intima, media, and adventitia.
