A pseudoaneurysm contains only one to two wall layers and occurs in settings such as trauma, malignancy, or infection. Management is based on rupture risk rather than morphology alone.

updates.question_text: Regarding endoleak types after EVAR, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Type I endoleak results from failure of the stent graft to seal at proximal or distal attachment sites
Type II endoleak is the most common type and results from retrograde sac filling by branch vessels such as the IMA and lumbar arteries
Type II endoleaks always require prompt intervention regardless of sac behaviour
Type III endoleak results from loss of device integrity
Type III endoleak requires prompt management by deploying a new stent graft over the defect with angioplasty to obtain a seal
options_after: Type I endoleak results from failure of the stent graft to seal at proximal or distal attachment sites
Type II endoleak is the most common type and results from retrograde sac filling by branch vessels such as the IMA and lumbar arteries
Type II endoleaks characteristically require prompt intervention despite variation in sac behaviour
Type III endoleak results from loss of device integrity
Type III endoleak requires prompt management by deploying a new stent graft over the defect with angioplasty to obtain a seal
updates.explanation: Type I endoleaks reflect inadequate proximal or distal seal and require prompt treatment. Type II endoleaks are the most common and arise from retrograde branch-vessel filling, often from the IMA or lumbar arteries; management is controversial because many thrombose or remain stable, with treatment considered for persistent endoleak or sac enlargement over 5 mm. Type III endoleak reflects device integrity failure and is managed promptly with a new stent graft over the defect plus angioplasty to obtain a good seal.

updates.question_text: Regarding visceral artery aneurysm embolization technique, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Proximal splenic artery embolization better preserves splenic function because collateral blood supply can be maintained
Distal splenic embolization is less painful and preserves splenic tissue better than proximal embolization
Right hepatic artery embolization distal to the cystic artery is preferred to reduce the risk of ischaemic cholecystitis
Hepatic artery aneurysm is described as the most common visceral aneurysm
Pancreatic complications are minimised by placing coils in the distal splenic hilum beyond all pancreatic branches
options_after: Proximal splenic artery embolization better preserves splenic function because collateral blood supply can be maintained
Distal splenic embolization is less painful and preserves splenic tissue better than proximal embolization
Right hepatic artery embolization distal to the cystic artery is preferred to reduce the risk of ischaemic cholecystitis
Hepatic artery aneurysm is described as the most common visceral aneurysm
Pancreatic complications are minimised by placing coils in the distal splenic hilum beyond most pancreatic branches
updates.explanation: The source states that proximal splenic embolization is less painful and better at preserving splenic function because collateral blood supply can remain. Embolization should be in the mid splenic artery between the dorsal pancreatic and pancreatica magna arteries to reduce pancreatic complications. Hepatic artery aneurysm is the second most common visceral aneurysm. For right hepatic artery embolization, distal embolization beyond the cystic artery is preferred because proximal embolization increases the risk of ischaemic cholecystitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging assessment and treatment strategy for Paget-Schroetter syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diagnostic venography should evaluate the arm in both neutral and abducted positions
Only the symptomatic side should be evaluated because contralateral compression is not expected
Treatment is thrombolysis followed subsequently by surgical thoracic outlet decompression
Stents should generally be used early because mechanical obstruction protects against device failure
If residual stenosis remains after thrombolysis, angioplasty should always precede decompression regardless of pre-procedure imaging
options_after: Diagnostic venography should evaluate the arm in both neutral and abducted positions
Contralateral venography adds little because venous compression is expected to be unilateral.
Treatment is thrombolysis followed subsequently by surgical thoracic outlet decompression
Stents should generally be used early because mechanical obstruction protects against device failure
If residual stenosis remains after thrombolysis, angioplasty should characteristically precede decompression despite variation in pre-procedure imaging
updates.explanation: The source states that diagnostic venography should assess the arm in neutral and abducted positions, and both sides should be evaluated because both subclavian veins are often compressed. Treatment is thrombolysis followed by surgical thoracic outlet decompression. If residual stenosis remains after thrombolysis, decompression should generally precede angioplasty unless pre-procedure imaging shows no mechanical cause. Stents are generally avoided, especially with mechanical obstruction, because of high device failure risk.

updates.question_text: Regarding May-Thurner syndrome, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It is thrombosis of the right renal vein caused by compression between the aorta and SMA
It is caused by compression of the right common iliac vein by the left common iliac artery
It is venous thrombosis of the left common iliac vein caused by compression from the crossing right common iliac artery
It affects only women according to the source
It is treated primarily with permanent IVC filter placement alone
options_after: It is thrombosis of the right renal vein caused by compression between the aorta and SMA
It is caused by compression of the right common iliac vein by the left common iliac artery
It is venous thrombosis of the left common iliac vein caused by compression from the crossing right common iliac artery
It affects primarily women according to the source
It is treated primarily with long-term IVC filter placement alone
updates.explanation: May-Thurner syndrome is venous thrombosis of the left common iliac vein caused by compression from the crossing right common iliac artery. Chronic compression leads to fibrous adhesions, intimal proliferation, and spur formation, predisposing to thrombosis. The source states that both genders are equally affected. Diagnosis and treatment are directed at the iliac venous lesion, not at renal vein compression or filter-only management.

updates.question_text: Regarding May-Thurner diagnosis, treatment, and complications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conventional venography with intravascular ultrasound is the gold standard for diagnosis
Treatment is anticoagulation only, because catheter-directed thrombolysis is contraindicated
Treatment is initial catheter-directed thrombolysis for acute thrombus followed by stenting
Balloon-expandable stents are preferred because they are rigid and resist pelvic motion
Post-thrombotic syndrome can include oedema, pain, ulceration, discolouration, and varicose veins
options_after: Conventional venography with intravascular ultrasound is the gold standard for diagnosis
Treatment is anticoagulation primarily, because catheter-directed thrombolysis is contraindicated
Treatment is initial catheter-directed thrombolysis for acute thrombus followed by stenting
Balloon-expandable stents are preferred because they are rigid and resist pelvic motion
Post-thrombotic syndrome can include oedema, pain, ulceration, discolouration, and varicose veins
updates.explanation: The source identifies conventional venography with IVUS as the diagnostic gold standard. Treatment is catheter-directed thrombolysis for acute clot followed by stenting, with self-expanding stents preferred. Post-thrombotic syndrome can occur in up to half of DVT patients and includes oedema, pain, ulceration, discolouration, and varicose veins.

updates.question_text: Regarding superior vena cava syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute SVC obstruction is usually asymptomatic and requires no urgent management
Acute SVC syndrome presents with facial and upper extremity oedema and cyanosis and is a vascular emergency
Chronic SVC occlusion invariably causes severe cyanosis and never improves with standing
Common causes include thoracic malignancy, catheter-associated thrombosis, and mediastinal fibrosis after histoplasmosis exposure
The classic abdominal imaging finding is absent enhancement of hepatic segment IVa because the vein of Sappey is occluded
options_after: Acute SVC obstruction is usually asymptomatic and does not require urgent management
Acute SVC syndrome presents with facial and upper extremity oedema and cyanosis and is a vascular emergency
Chronic SVC occlusion invariably causes severe cyanosis and will not improve with standing
Common causes include thoracic malignancy, catheter-associated thrombosis, and mediastinal fibrosis after histoplasmosis exposure
The classic abdominal imaging finding is absent enhancement of hepatic segment IVa because the vein of Sappey is occluded
updates.explanation: The source describes acute SVC syndrome as a vascular emergency causing facial and upper extremity oedema and cyanosis. Chronic SVC stenosis or occlusion may be asymptomatic; when symptomatic, facial oedema improving with standing is characteristic. Common causes are thoracic malignancy, catheter-associated thrombosis, and post-histoplasmosis mediastinal fibrosis. The classic abdominal imaging finding is increased enhancement of segment IVa from collateral opacification of the vein of Sappey.

updates.question_text: Regarding duplicated IVC and megacava considerations for filter placement, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A duplicated IVC allows standard single infrarenal filter placement in one limb because clot cannot cross the confluence
If a duplicated IVC is present, one option is placing a single filter above the IVC confluence
Another option in duplicated IVC is placing a filter in each duplicated IVC
Absence of iliac vein influx contralateral to the injected side on initial cavography can suggest duplicated IVC if pre-procedure imaging is unavailable
Most IVC filters are suitable for vessel diameters larger than 40 mm
options_after: A duplicated IVC allows standard single infrarenal filter placement in one limb because clot will not cross the confluence
If a duplicated IVC is present, one option is placing a single filter above the IVC confluence
Another option in duplicated IVC is placing a filter in each duplicated IVC
Absence of iliac vein influx contralateral to the injected side on initial cavography can suggest duplicated IVC if pre-procedure imaging is unavailable
Most IVC filters are suitable for vessel diameters larger than 40 mm
updates.explanation: In duplicated IVC, clot can bypass a filter placed in only one limb. The source gives two strategies: place one filter above the confluence or place a filter in each duplicated IVC. When pre-procedure imaging is unavailable, absence of iliac vein influx from the contralateral side during cavography is a clue. Most filters are suitable for diameters smaller than 28-30 mm; larger megacava may require a Bird's Nest filter or separate common iliac filters.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal vein variants and IVC filter position, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The preferred IVC filter location is immediately inferior to the lowest renal vein, including variant renal veins
A retroaortic left renal vein usually joins the IVC more superiorly than the right renal vein
Circumaortic left renal vein consists of a single left renal vein passing posterior to the aorta
Placing the filter above all renal veins is the routine preferred position in patients without IVC thrombus
Placement below the lowest renal vein prevents an anomalous renal vein from acting as a conduit for clot propagation
options_after: The preferred IVC filter location is immediately inferior to the lowest renal vein, including variant renal veins
A retroaortic left renal vein usually joins the IVC more superiorly than the right renal vein
Circumaortic left renal vein consists of a single left renal vein passing posterior to the aorta
Placing the filter above most renal veins is the routine preferred position in patients without IVC thrombus
Placement below the lowest renal vein prevents an anomalous renal vein from acting as a conduit for clot propagation
updates.explanation: The source states that the preferred IVC filter position is immediately below the lowest renal vein, including circumaortic or retroaortic variants. This prevents an anomalous vein from acting as a clot-propagation conduit. Circumaortic left renal vein has two components, one anterior and one posterior to the aorta. Retroaortic left renal vein is a single vein behind the aorta and usually joins the IVC more inferiorly than the right renal vein.

updates.question_text: Regarding phlegmasia cerulea dolens, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It is chronic asymptomatic venous reflux treated electively with compression stockings alone
It is a vascular emergency consisting of acute limb swelling, cyanosis, and severe pain from complete thrombotic occlusion of venous drainage
It occurs only in patients with congenital interrupted IVC
It should not be anticoagulated because venous thrombosis is not part of its pathophysiology
The source recommends observation because ischaemia and gangrene do not occur
options_after: It is chronic asymptomatic venous reflux treated electively with compression stockings alone
It is a vascular emergency consisting of acute limb swelling, cyanosis, and severe pain from complete thrombotic occlusion of venous drainage
It occurs primarily in patients with congenital interrupted IVC
It should not be anticoagulated because venous thrombosis is not part of its pathophysiology
The source recommends observation because ischaemia and gangrene do not occur
updates.explanation: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens is a vascular emergency caused by complete thrombotic occlusion of venous drainage, producing acute limb swelling, cyanosis, and severe pain. It occurs most often with malignancy, trauma, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, or other prothrombotic states. Untreated massive swelling can progress to capillary hypertension, ischaemia, and gangrene. Treatment requires IV heparin plus angioplasty, catheter-directed thrombolysis, or surgical thrombectomy.

updates.question_text: Regarding varicocele treatment and access, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Treatment is indicated for all incidentally detected asymptomatic varicoceles regardless of fertility or testicular size
Indications for treatment include pain, infertility, or testicular atrophy
Coil embolization is inferior to surgical ligation in all patients and is not described as an equivalent option
Right femoral or right internal jugular access is preferred for right-sided varicocele embolization
Coil embolization or surgical ligation of the gonadal vein have been shown to be equivalent in outcome
options_after: Treatment is indicated for most incidentally detected asymptomatic varicoceles despite variation in fertility or testicular size
Indications for treatment include pain, infertility, or testicular atrophy
Coil embolization is inferior to surgical ligation in most patients and is not described as an equivalent option
Right femoral or right internal jugular access is preferred for right-sided varicocele embolization
Coil embolization or surgical ligation of the gonadal vein have been shown to be equivalent in outcome
updates.explanation: The source lists pain, infertility, and testicular atrophy as treatment indications. It states that coil embolization and surgical ligation of the gonadal vein have equivalent outcomes. For left-sided varicocele, right femoral or right internal jugular access is preferred; for right-sided varicocele, internal jugular or basilic vein access is preferred. Incidental asymptomatic varicoceles are not given as automatic treatment indications.

updates.question_text: Regarding lower extremity venous insufficiency treatment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It most commonly results from venous hypertension secondary to incompetent valves, but can also follow prior DVT
Treatment options include thermal endovascular ablation with laser or radiofrequency
Thermal ablation works by preserving the endothelium and increasing venous compliance
Tumescent anaesthesia acts as both local anaesthetic and heat sink to protect the overlying skin
Post-procedure compression stockings are avoided after all venous ablation options
options_after: It most commonly results from venous hypertension secondary to incompetent valves, but can also follow prior DVT
Treatment options include thermal endovascular ablation with laser or radiofrequency
Thermal ablation works by preserving the endothelium and increasing venous compliance
Tumescent anaesthesia acts as both local anaesthetic and heat sink to protect the overlying skin
Post-procedure compression stockings are avoided after most venous ablation options
updates.explanation: Lower-extremity venous insufficiency most commonly results from venous hypertension due to incompetent valves and can also occur after DVT. Treatment options include thermal ablation using laser or radiofrequency and non-thermal ablation with sclerosing agents. These interventions damage the endothelium to cause fibrosis and irreversible occlusion. Tumescent anaesthesia provides local anaesthesia and a heat sink to prevent skin burns, and compression stockings are used post-procedure.

updates.question_text: Regarding causes and initial management of chylous leaks, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chylous leaks are caused only by congenital lymphatic malformation and not by surgery or malignancy
Initial treatment before attempted thoracic duct embolization is a high-fat diet to increase lymphatic flow
Chylous leaks can result from thoracic duct or tributary rupture after thoracic surgery such as oesophagectomy
Thoracic duct embolization does not require consent for pancreatitis or non-target embolization
Initial treatment includes dietary modification with a non-fat diet for 2-3 days before attempting thoracic duct embolization
options_after: Chylous leaks are caused primarily by congenital lymphatic malformation and not by surgery or malignancy
Initial treatment before attempted thoracic duct embolization is a high-fat diet to increase lymphatic flow
Chylous leaks can result from thoracic duct or tributary rupture after thoracic surgery such as oesophagectomy
Thoracic duct embolization does not require consent for pancreatitis or non-target embolization
Initial treatment includes dietary modification with a non-fat diet for 2-3 days before attempting thoracic duct embolization
updates.explanation: The source lists thoracic surgery such as oesophagectomy, abdominal surgery, malignancy including lymphoma, and idiopathic causes as causes of chylous leak. Initial treatment is dietary modification with a non-fat diet for 2-3 days before attempting thoracic duct embolization. Patients should be consented for pancreatitis and non-target embolization.

updates.question_text: Regarding thoracic duct embolization technique, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lipiodol is injected into each leg followed by a saline push for lymphangiography
The cisterna chyli is visualised at approximately L1-L3 once lymphographic dye reaches the abdomen
After direct puncture, a wire is extended to the thorax
The thoracic duct is coiled along its entirety to provide a matrix for glue polymerisation
The procedure deliberately avoids glue because only coils are used
options_after: Lipiodol is injected into each leg followed by a saline push for lymphangiography
The cisterna chyli is visualised at approximately L1-L3 once lymphographic dye reaches the abdomen
After direct puncture, a wire is extended to the thorax
The thoracic duct is coiled along its entirety to provide a matrix for glue polymerisation
Coils are preferred to glue during BRTO because migration of liquid embolic is negligible.
updates.explanation: The source describes injecting lipiodol into each leg followed by saline push. Once the dye reaches the abdomen, the cisterna chyli is visualised at L1-L3. After direct puncture with a long spinal needle, a wire is advanced to the thorax. The thoracic duct is coiled to provide a matrix for glue polymerisation using a glue-lipiodol mixture, so glue is part of the described procedure.

updates.question_text: Regarding non-target embolization during thoracic duct embolization, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Glue embolization to pulmonary arteries is impossible because lymphatic access never crosses venous structures
Glue should be injected without fluoroscopic monitoring once the thoracic duct is accessed
If glue enters the IVC it is trapped in the liver and cannot reach the lungs
If the IVC is transgressed, glue can embolize to the pulmonary arteries and cause acute pulmonary embolus
Non-target embolization is prevented by avoiding lipiodol entirely
options_after: Glue embolization to pulmonary arteries is not considered a realistic possibility because lymphatic access will not cross venous structures
Glue should be injected without fluoroscopic monitoring once the thoracic duct is accessed
If glue enters the IVC it is trapped in the liver and will not reach the lungs
If the IVC is transgressed, glue can embolize to the pulmonary arteries and cause acute pulmonary embolus
Non-target embolization is prevented by avoiding lipiodol predominantly
updates.explanation: The source explicitly warns that glue must be watched carefully during injection to identify non-target embolization. If the IVC is transgressed, glue can embolize to the pulmonary arteries and cause acute pulmonary embolus. The illustrated CTA shows glue embolization to a right lower lobe segmental pulmonary artery.

updates.question_text: Regarding complications to discuss before thoracic duct embolization, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Transgression of visceral organs with the puncture needle is expected and never clinically relevant
Rare complications include visceral organ transgression causing peritonitis or bleeding
Pulmonary artery embolization may occur and may or may not be symptomatic
Long-term complications are limited to immediate pancreatitis and do not include lower-extremity or abdominal symptoms
Rare long-term complications include chronic lower-extremity oedema, chronic diarrhoea, and abdominal ascites
options_after: Transgression of a visceral organ is clinically inconsequential when immediate bleeding is absent.
Rare complications include visceral organ transgression causing peritonitis or bleeding
Pulmonary artery embolization may occur and may or may not be symptomatic
Long-term complications are limited to immediate pancreatitis and do not include lower-extremity or abdominal symptoms
Rare long-term complications include chronic lower-extremity oedema, chronic diarrhoea, and abdominal ascites
updates.explanation: The source lists rare procedural complications including visceral organ transgression with the puncture needle, which can result in peritonitis or bleeding. Pulmonary artery embolization is another complication and may be symptomatic or asymptomatic. Rare long-term complications to consent for include chronic lower-extremity oedema, chronic diarrhoea, and abdominal ascites.

updates.question_text: Regarding biliary drain management after placement, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Routine aspiration is recommended to reduce cholangitis risk
All institutions agree that biliary drains should be forward-flushed daily
A biliary drain should never be aspirated because aspiration may draw bowel contents into the biliary system and risk cholangitis
Preventative maintenance is unnecessary once the drain enters the small bowel
Extra sideholes should never be manually cut because they prevent drainage
options_after: Routine aspiration is recommended to reduce cholangitis risk
Most institutions agree that biliary drains should be forward-flushed daily
A biliary drain should never be aspirated because aspiration may draw bowel contents into the biliary system and risk cholangitis
Preventative maintenance is unnecessary once the drain enters the small bowel
Extra sideholes should not be manually cut because they prevent drainage
updates.explanation: The source states that the role of regular flushing is controversial, with different institutional practices. Regardless of flushing policy, a biliary drain should never be aspirated because this can draw bowel contents into the biliary system and predispose to cholangitis. Extra sideholes may be manually cut when needed to allow drainage from the biliary puncture site to the bowel. Three-month preventative maintenance is recommended.

updates.question_text: Regarding biliary stents, drains, and contraindications to PTC, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Metallic stents for biliary strictures are usually reserved for patients with life expectancy under six months
Most metallic biliary stents are easily removed and exchanged at regular intervals
Plastic stents are placed endoscopically and allow regular exchange
Ascites is an absolute contraindication to PTC that cannot be modified before the procedure
An internal-external biliary drain can be used as an alternative to stent placement, though it is less comfortable because of the external drain
options_after: Metallic stents for biliary strictures are usually reserved for patients with life expectancy under six months
Most metallic biliary stents are easily removed and exchanged at regular intervals
Plastic stents are placed endoscopically and allow regular exchange
Ascites is an absolute contraindication to PTC that will not be modified before the procedure
An internal-external biliary drain can be used as an alternative to stent placement, though it is less comfortable because of the external drain
updates.explanation: The source states that metallic stents are usually placed only when life expectancy is less than six months, because most cannot be removed and have median patency of 6-8 months. Plastic stents are endoscopic and exchangeable. An internal-external drain is an alternative but is less comfortable due to the external component. Most contraindications are relative: ascites may be managed with therapeutic paracentesis, and an intrahepatic tumour should not be traversed if a direct duct target is available.

updates.question_text: Regarding complications and bile duct injury management in biliary intervention, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Percutaneous biliary drainage has no risk of sepsis because antibiotics are always administered
Complications include sepsis, haemorrhage, bile leak, haemobilia, and abscess
Haemobilia in this context is due only to venous-venous fistula formation
The most common cause of bile duct injury is iatrogenic injury from laparoscopic cholecystectomy
Bile duct injury is treated by immediate TIPS creation to decompress the portal system
options_after: Percutaneous biliary drainage lacks risk of sepsis because antibiotics are characteristically administered
Complications include sepsis, haemorrhage, bile leak, haemobilia, and abscess
Haemobilia in this context is due primarily to venous-venous fistula formation
The most common cause of bile duct injury is iatrogenic injury from laparoscopic cholecystectomy
Bile duct injury is treated by immediate TIPS creation to decompress the portal system
updates.explanation: The source lists sepsis, haemorrhage, bile leak, haemobilia due to arterial-biliary fistula, and abscess as complications of percutaneous biliary drainage. The most common cause of bile duct injury is iatrogenic injury during laparoscopic cholecystectomy, with orthotopic liver transplant a less common cause. Treatment is biliary diversion to a drainage bag to allow the leak to heal, not portal decompression with TIPS.

updates.question_text: Regarding multifocal biliary strictures and malignant biliary obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Multifocal biliary strictures are specific for sclerosing cholangitis and have no meaningful differential diagnosis
The differential for multifocal biliary strictures includes primary biliary cirrhosis
The differential includes multifocal cholangiocarcinoma and chronic bacterial cholangitis
AIDS cholangitis is listed as a differential diagnosis and is usually associated with papillary stenosis
Unilateral biliary obstruction always requires bilateral right and left biliary drains
options_after: Multifocal biliary strictures are specific for sclerosing cholangitis and lack meaningful differential diagnosis
The differential for multifocal biliary strictures includes primary biliary cirrhosis
The differential includes multifocal cholangiocarcinoma and chronic bacterial cholangitis
AIDS cholangitis is listed as a differential diagnosis and is usually associated with papillary stenosis
Unilateral biliary obstruction characteristically requires bilateral right and left biliary drains
updates.explanation: The source gives a differential for multifocal biliary strictures including sclerosing cholangitis, primary biliary cirrhosis, multifocal cholangiocarcinoma, chronic bacterial cholangitis, and AIDS cholangitis, the latter usually associated with papillary stenosis. Unilateral obstruction of a right or left hepatic ductal system is usually treated on the affected side only. Hilar obstruction, often due to Klatskin tumour, more often requires separate right and left drains.

updates.question_text: Regarding hilar malignant biliary obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hilar obstruction is most commonly due to hilar cholangiocarcinoma, also known as Klatskin tumour
Hilar obstruction can always be completely drained with one left-sided drain because right and left systems communicate freely
Pre-procedure MRCP is unnecessary because biliary anatomy is never variant
Hilar obstruction is unrelated to cholangiocarcinoma and usually reflects gallbladder stones
It often requires two biliary drains, one in the right and one in the left ducts
options_after: Hilar obstruction is most commonly due to hilar cholangiocarcinoma, also known as Klatskin tumour
Hilar obstruction can characteristically be completely drained with one left-sided drain because right and left systems communicate freely
Pre-procedure MRCP is unnecessary because biliary anatomy is not variant
Hilar obstruction is unrelated to cholangiocarcinoma and usually reflects gallbladder stones
It often requires two biliary drains, one in the right and one in the left ducts
updates.explanation: The source states that hilar obstruction is most commonly due to hilar cholangiocarcinoma, or Klatskin tumour. It most often requires two biliary drains, one in the right ducts and one in the left ducts. Occasionally, an anatomic anomaly such as anomalous right duct drainage into the left duct may allow single-drain decompression. MRCP may be helpful to delineate biliary anatomy before the procedure.

updates.question_text: Regarding percutaneous cholecystostomy for acute cholecystitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is indicated for acute calculous or acalculous cholecystitis in patients who are not surgical candidates
It is contraindicated in acute acalculous cholecystitis because surgery is always required
Cultures are positive in essentially all cases of acute cholecystitis
It is a temporising measure for calculous cholecystitis before cholecystectomy
It may cure acalculous cholecystitis without surgery
options_after: It is indicated for acute calculous or acalculous cholecystitis in patients who are not surgical candidates
It is contraindicated in acute acalculous cholecystitis because surgery is characteristically required
Cultures are positive in more than 90% of cases of acute cholecystitis
It is a temporising measure for calculous cholecystitis before cholecystectomy
It may cure acalculous cholecystitis without surgery
updates.explanation: The source states that percutaneous gallbladder drainage is used for acute calculous or acalculous cholecystitis in patients who are not surgical candidates. It is a temporising measure before cholecystectomy for calculous disease, but may cure acalculous cholecystitis without surgery. Cultures are negative in 40% of acute cholecystitis, so culture negativity does not exclude the diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding percutaneous cholecystostomy approaches, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: The transperitoneal approach decreases peritoneal bile leak risk compared with the transhepatic approach
The transhepatic approach has decreased risk of peritoneal bile leak but increased risk of liver laceration
The transhepatic approach avoids liver traversal entirely
The transperitoneal approach is more commonly performed because it creates the most reliable tract
The transperitoneal approach avoids the gallbladder fundus because the fundus is immobile
options_after: The transperitoneal approach decreases peritoneal bile leak risk compared with the transhepatic approach
The transhepatic approach has decreased risk of peritoneal bile leak but increased risk of liver laceration
The transhepatic approach avoids liver traversal predominantly
The transperitoneal approach is more commonly performed because it creates the most reliable tract
The transperitoneal approach avoids the gallbladder fundus because the fundus is immobile
updates.explanation: The source describes two approaches. The transhepatic approach traverses liver into the bare area of the gallbladder fossa and is more commonly performed; it decreases peritoneal bile leak risk but increases risk of liver laceration. The transperitoneal approach avoids the liver and has less risk of liver injury, but carries greater bile leak risk and requires puncturing the mobile gallbladder fundus.

updates.question_text: Regarding BRTO for gastric variceal bleeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: BRTO is used for gastric variceal bleeding due to portal hypertension
In the United States and Europe, BRTO is usually performed when endoscopic therapy fails and TIPS is not an option
BRTO can be performed even when there is no spontaneous gastrorenal or gastrocaval shunt
The procedure injects sclerosant directly into the varix while variceal outflow is occluded by an inflated balloon
BRTO works by creating a new low-resistance shunt between portal and hepatic veins
options_after: BRTO is used for gastric variceal bleeding due to portal hypertension
In the United States and Europe, BRTO is usually performed when endoscopic therapy fails and TIPS is not an option
BRTO can be performed even when there is an absence of spontaneous gastrorenal or gastrocaval shunt
The procedure injects sclerosant directly into the varix while variceal outflow is occluded by an inflated balloon
BRTO works by creating a new low-resistance shunt between portal and hepatic veins
updates.explanation: BRTO is an endovascular treatment for gastric variceal bleeding from portal hypertension. In the United States and Europe it is generally used when endoscopic therapy fails and TIPS is not an option. It requires a spontaneous gastrorenal or gastrocaval shunt, and without such a shunt BRTO is not a treatment option. The outflow is balloon-occluded and sclerosant is injected into the varix. Creating a portal-hepatic shunt describes TIPS rather than BRTO.

updates.question_text: Regarding the physiologic trade-off of BRTO compared with TIPS, which of the following statement is correct?
options_before: BRTO reduces portal pressure by creating a direct portosystemic stent, so it cannot worsen ascites
BRTO is contraindicated for gastric variceal bleeding because it always worsens hepatic encephalopathy
BRTO has substantially worse rebleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and mortality rates than TIPS according to the source
BRTO can improve liver function and lower liver failure or encephalopathy risk by obstructing a major gastrorenal shunt, but may worsen ascites and oesophageal varices
BRTO is identical to TIPS except that femoral arterial access is used instead of jugular venous access
options_after: BRTO reduces portal pressure by creating a direct portosystemic stent, so it will not worsen ascites
BRTO is contraindicated for gastric variceal bleeding because it characteristically worsens hepatic encephalopathy
BRTO has substantially worse rebleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and mortality rates than TIPS according to the source
BRTO can improve liver function and lower liver failure or encephalopathy risk by obstructing a major gastrorenal shunt, but may worsen ascites and oesophageal varices
BRTO is closely comparable to TIPS except that femoral arterial access is used instead of jugular venous access
updates.explanation: The source explains the key trade-off: by obstructing a major gastrorenal shunt, BRTO increases portal venous pressure. This may improve liver function and lower liver failure or encephalopathy risk, but can worsen ascites and oesophageal varices. The source also states that BRTO has comparable efficacy to TIPS and is associated with lower rates of rebleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and mortality.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiofrequency ablation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The ablation zone is well monitored in real time during RFA
RFA produces frictional heating by alternating electromagnetic fields that agitate adjacent molecules around the probe
RFA requires no dispersive electrode because the current remains entirely within the probe
Grounding pads are used as a dispersive electrode
Soft-tissue charring and microbubble formation can increase impedance and reduce probe effectiveness
options_after: The ablation zone is well monitored in real time during RFA
RFA produces frictional heating by alternating electromagnetic fields that agitate adjacent molecules around the probe
RFA does not require dispersive electrode because the current remains predominantly within the probe
Grounding pads are used as a dispersive electrode
Soft-tissue charring and microbubble formation can increase impedance and reduce probe effectiveness
updates.explanation: RFA creates a simple electrical circuit through the body, generating frictional heating around the probe and coagulation necrosis. Grounding pads act as the dispersive electrode. Overly rapid heating can char tissue or form microbubbles, increasing impedance and limiting current flow. The source notes that the ablation zone is not well monitored in real time, which is one of RFA's limitations.

updates.question_text: Regarding situations where microwave ablation may be less precise or higher risk, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: MWA is safest for central tumours because the ablation zone can be precisely monitored in real time
MWA is preferred for very small tumours because it precisely controls the ablation shape
MWA carries higher risk near central tumours or critical structures because the ablation zone is not monitored in real time and its size and shape are relatively unpredictable
MWA is unsuitable for peripheral tumours because artificial ascites cannot protect adjacent structures
MWA probes are always smaller than cryoablation probes
options_after: MWA is safest for central tumours because the ablation zone can be precisely monitored in real time
MWA is preferred for very small tumours because it precisely controls the ablation shape
MWA carries higher risk near central tumours or critical structures because the ablation zone is not monitored in real time and its size and shape are relatively unpredictable
MWA is unsuitable for peripheral tumours because artificial ascites will not protect adjacent structures
MWA probes are characteristically smaller than cryoablation probes
updates.explanation: The source highlights that MWA uses larger probes and is higher risk near central tumours or critical structures because the ablation zone cannot be monitored in real time and the size and shape are relatively unpredictable. It is also less precise for smaller tumours. The illustrated case uses artificial ascites to protect adjacent diaphragm and body wall for a peripheral liver lesion.

updates.question_text: Regarding cryoablation technique and imaging features, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Rapid gas expansion within the probe cools the probe and creates an iceball in surrounding tissue
Only one rapid freezing cycle is performed, with no thawing phase
The iceball should extend at least 0.5 cm beyond the tumour to reduce recurrence risk
Cryoablation probes are ideally spaced at least 5 cm apart to avoid overlapping treatment zones
The iceball is well visualised in real time on CT, MRI, and ultrasound
options_after: Rapid gas expansion within the probe cools the probe and creates an iceball in surrounding tissue
A single freeze cycle followed by passive warming is sufficient for tumour ablation.
The iceball should extend at least 0.5 cm beyond the tumour to reduce recurrence risk
Cryoablation probes are ideally spaced at least 5 cm apart to avoid overlapping treatment zones
The iceball is well visualised in real time on CT, MRI, and ultrasound
updates.explanation: Cryoablation uses rapid gas expansion to cool the probe and form an iceball. At least two freeze-thaw cycles are performed, and probes are usually spaced 1-2 cm apart. The iceball should extend at least 0.5 cm beyond the tumour to reduce recurrence. A major advantage is real-time visualisation of the iceball on CT, MRI, and ultrasound.

updates.question_text: Regarding cryoablation advantages and disadvantages, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cryoablation has the lowest bleeding risk because it cauterises vessels during freezing
Cryoablation has comparatively less risk for central tumours and typically less post-procedure pain
Cryoablation is always faster than RFA because a single probe and short cycle are used
Cryoshock is a robust inflammatory response that may cause hypotension, multi-organ failure, and disseminated intravascular coagulation
Cryoablation cannot be performed with multiple probes simultaneously
options_after: Cryoablation has the lowest bleeding risk because it cauterises vessels during freezing
Cryoablation has comparatively less risk for central tumours and typically less post-procedure pain
Cryoablation is characteristically faster than RFA because a single probe and short cycle are used
Cryoshock is a robust inflammatory response that may cause hypotension, multi-organ failure, and disseminated intravascular coagulation
Cryoablation will not be performed with multiple probes simultaneously
updates.explanation: The source lists real-time visualisation, comparatively lower risk with central tumours, simultaneous multiple probes, lower complication rate, and less pain as cryoablation advantages. Its disadvantages include slightly increased bleeding risk due to lack of concurrent cautery, longer procedure time from multiple probes and freeze-thaw cycles, and higher cost. Cryoshock is a cytokine-mediated inflammatory response seen especially with large-volume liver cryoablation and can cause hypotension, multi-organ failure, and DIC.

updates.question_text: Regarding catheter-directed transarterial therapy for HCC and liver metastases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal liver parenchyma receives most of its blood supply from the portal vein
HCC is preferentially supplied by the hepatic artery
TACE and TARE exploit the difference between tumour and normal liver blood supply by delivering treatment into tumour-feeding arteries
TACE and TARE are used only for HCC and never as bridge therapy to liver transplant or for metastases
TACE and TARE can be used as bridging therapy to liver transplant in HCC and for locoregional treatment of other hepatic malignancies or metastases
options_after: Normal liver parenchyma receives most of its blood supply from the portal vein
HCC is preferentially supplied by the hepatic artery
TACE and TARE exploit the difference between tumour and normal liver blood supply by delivering treatment into tumour-feeding arteries
TACE and TARE are used primarily for HCC and not as bridge therapy to liver transplant or for metastases
TACE and TARE can be used as bridging therapy to liver transplant in HCC and for locoregional treatment of other hepatic malignancies or metastases
updates.explanation: The source explains the rationale for hepatic arterial therapies: normal liver is largely portal venous, whereas HCC is preferentially arterial. TACE and TARE use this mismatch to deliver treatment into feeding arteries while reducing injury to normal liver. They are used for palliative treatment of HCC, as bridge therapy to liver transplant, and for locoregional treatment of cholangiocarcinoma and hepatic metastases.

updates.question_text: Regarding conventional TACE and drug-eluting bead TACE, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conventional TACE consists only of bland embolization without chemotherapy
Conventional TACE consists of intra-arterial chemotherapy followed by embolization of tumour arterial supply
Drug-eluting bead TACE uses microspheres that both embolize and deliver chemotherapy
TACE promotes cell death by high-dose local chemotherapy and local hypoxia/ischaemia
DEB-TACE avoids arterial embolization and works entirely by external beam radiation
options_after: Conventional TACE consists primarily of bland embolization without chemotherapy
Conventional TACE consists of intra-arterial chemotherapy followed by embolization of tumour arterial supply
Drug-eluting bead TACE uses microspheres that both embolize and deliver chemotherapy
TACE promotes cell death by high-dose local chemotherapy and local hypoxia/ischaemia
DEB-TACE avoids arterial embolization and works predominantly by external beam radiation
updates.explanation: The source defines conventional TACE as intra-arterial chemotherapy followed by embolization using particles or gelfoam. DEB-TACE uses microspheres that both embolize and release chemotherapy. Both deliver a higher local cytotoxic dose than systemic therapy and create local hypoxia and ischaemia. Radiation-based intra-arterial treatment describes TARE rather than TACE.

updates.question_text: Regarding TACE contraindications and pre-procedure planning, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Portal vein thrombosis is a common contraindication because of post-treatment liver failure risk
High tumour burden and extrahepatic metastases are not considered contraindications
Decompensated cirrhosis and elevated bilirubin are preferred indications for TACE
Pre-procedure cross-sectional imaging is unnecessary because angiography alone evaluates all contraindications
Pre-procedure imaging assesses variant anatomy, extrahepatic collateral supply, and potential contraindications
options_after: Portal vein thrombosis is a common contraindication because of post-treatment liver failure risk
High tumour burden and extrahepatic metastases are not considered contraindications
Decompensated cirrhosis and elevated bilirubin are preferred indications for TACE
Pre-procedure cross-sectional imaging is unnecessary because angiography alone evaluates most contraindications
Pre-procedure imaging assesses variant anatomy, extrahepatic collateral supply, and potential contraindications
updates.explanation: The source lists portal vein thrombosis, high tumour burden greater than 50%, extrahepatic metastases, decompensated cirrhosis, and elevated bilirubin as common TACE contraindications. Cross-sectional imaging is used before treatment planning to evaluate variant anatomy, extrahepatic collateral supply such as the right phrenic artery, and contraindications.

updates.question_text: Regarding TACE procedural technique and post-procedure expectations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A celiac arteriogram is performed after arterial access to map anatomy
Embolic agents are always delivered from the aorta and never superselectively
Immediate post-procedural CT is usually recommended to exclude abscess because normal changes are not confusing
Materials are injected until stasis or low flow is seen, followed by arteriography to document persistent low flow or absence of flow
Post-embolization syndrome is common after TACE and may include right upper quadrant pain, fever, nausea, vomiting, and transaminitis
options_after: A celiac arteriogram is performed after arterial access to map anatomy
Embolic agents are delivered from a proximal aortic position rather than superselectively.
Immediate post-procedural CT is usually recommended to exclude abscess because normal changes are not confusing
Materials are injected until stasis or low flow is seen, followed by arteriography to document persistent low flow or absence of flow
Post-embolization syndrome is common after TACE and may include right upper quadrant pain, fever, nausea, vomiting, and transaminitis
updates.explanation: The TACE sequence begins with arterial access and celiac arteriography to map anatomy. Selective or superselective embolization can be performed for small tumours, while lobar embolization can be used for multiple lesions. Material is injected until low flow or stasis, then arteriography documents the endpoint. Immediate post-procedural CT is usually avoided because expected changes may mimic abscess, and post-embolization syndrome is very common.

updates.question_text: Regarding TARE compared with TACE, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: TARE has the same macro-embolic effect as TACE and therefore cannot be used with portal vein thrombosis
TARE consists of intra-arterial microspheres carrying radioactive isotope, with treatment effect dependent on emitted radiation rather than macroembolization
TARE routinely causes significant post-embolization syndrome and should be avoided for this reason
TARE is external beam radiation delivered after arterial coil embolization
TARE is contraindicated whenever HCC is supplied by the hepatic artery
options_after: TARE has the same macro-embolic effect as TACE and therefore will not be used with portal vein thrombosis
TARE consists of intra-arterial microspheres carrying radioactive isotope, with treatment effect dependent on emitted radiation rather than macroembolization
TARE routinely causes significant post-embolization syndrome and should be avoided for this reason
TARE is external beam radiation delivered after arterial coil embolization
TARE is contraindicated whenever HCC is supplied by the hepatic artery
updates.explanation: The source defines TARE, also called SIRT, as intra-arterial infusion of microspheres with radioactive isotopes such as Yttrium-90. It does not have the same macroembolic effect as TACE; tumour necrosis results from radiation emitted by the spheres. Because vessels are less disrupted, TARE can be performed in the setting of portal vein thrombosis. The source also states that TARE does not cause significant post-embolization syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding TARE mapping and contraindications, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Absolute contraindications include pregnancy and breastfeeding
Uncorrectable GI vascular reflux and uncorrectable hepatopulmonary shunting are absolute contraindications
Macroaggregated albumin mapping is performed after radioembolization and cannot assess non-target uptake risk
TARE should never be performed when there is a shunt to the GI tract because small amounts can cause enteritis or ulceration
Coil embolization of nearby arteries is forbidden because it increases non-target embolization
options_after: Absolute contraindications include pregnancy and breastfeeding
Uncorrectable GI vascular reflux and uncorrectable hepatopulmonary shunting are absolute contraindications
Macroaggregated albumin mapping is performed after radioembolization and will not assess non-target uptake risk
TARE should never be performed when there is a shunt to the GI tract because small amounts can cause enteritis or ulceration
Coil embolization of nearby arteries is forbidden because it increases non-target embolization
updates.explanation: The source lists pregnancy, breastfeeding, uncorrectable GI vascular reflux, and uncorrectable hepatopulmonary shunting as absolute contraindications. Mapping includes angiography followed by labelled macroaggregated albumin injection and nuclear medicine imaging before therapy; this approximates microsphere distribution and identifies lung, GI, skin, or other non-target uptake. GI shunting is a hard stop because even small amounts can cause enteritis or ulceration. Coil embolization of nearby arteries may be used to prevent non-target embolization.

updates.question_text: Regarding prostate artery embolization for benign prostatic hyperplasia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: PAE is recommended for all men regardless of urinary symptoms
PAE is a safe and effective treatment for BPH in patients with moderate to severe urinary obstruction symptoms
PAE causes ischaemic necrosis and subsequent reduction in prostate gland volume
The prostate artery has a fixed origin from the superior vesical artery in nearly all patients
Superselective catheterisation or coil embolization of anastomoses may be used to reduce non-target embolization risk
options_after: PAE is recommended for most men despite variation in urinary symptoms
PAE is a safe and effective treatment for BPH in patients with moderate to severe urinary obstruction symptoms
PAE causes ischaemic necrosis and subsequent reduction in prostate gland volume
The prostate artery has a fixed origin from the superior vesical artery in the large majority of patients
Superselective catheterisation or coil embolization of anastomoses may be used to reduce non-target embolization risk
updates.explanation: The source describes PAE as safe and effective for BPH and recommends it for moderate to severe obstructive urinary symptoms. It works by ischaemic necrosis of the prostate gland, reducing gland volume and improving symptoms. Pre-procedure cross-sectional imaging is used because internal iliac anatomy and prostate artery origin are highly variable. Superselective catheterisation or coil embolization of anastomoses can reduce non-target embolization.

updates.question_text: Regarding surgical arteriovenous fistulas for dialysis access, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A fistula can be used immediately after creation because it does not need to mature
A surgical fistula has good long-term patency, approximately 85% at two years
All fistulas mature reliably, with failure to mature described as exceptional
Maturation requires venous enlargement sufficient to allow high dialysis flow rates
Common fistula locations include radial artery to cephalic vein at the wrist and brachial artery to variable forearm veins
options_after: A fistula can be used immediately after creation because it does not need to mature
A surgical fistula has good long-term patency, approximately 85% at two years
Most fistulas mature reliably, with failure to mature described as exceptional
Maturation requires venous enlargement sufficient to allow high dialysis flow rates
Common fistula locations include radial artery to cephalic vein at the wrist and brachial artery to variable forearm veins
updates.explanation: The source states that surgical fistulas have good long-term patency, about 85% at two years, but need several months to mature. About 30% fail to mature. A fistula is mature when veins are enlarged enough to allow high dialysis flow rates. Common locations are radial artery to cephalic vein at the wrist and brachial artery to variable forearm veins.

updates.question_text: Regarding treatment goals for venous stenosis in surgical dialysis access, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Venous outflow stenoses are usually treated by prophylactic port placement
Cutting balloons are avoided because dialysis access stenoses are never fibrotic
The procedural goal is to restore a palpable thrill and pulse or reduce the venous-to-brachial artery pressure ratio below 0.4
Venous stenosis is not treated if thrombosis is present because thrombus alone explains access failure
High-pressure balloons are contraindicated in dialysis access stenosis
options_after: Venous outflow stenoses are usually treated by prophylactic port placement
Cutting balloons are avoided because dialysis access stenoses are not fibrotic
The procedural goal is to restore a palpable thrill and pulse or reduce the venous-to-brachial artery pressure ratio below 0.4
Venous stenosis is not treated if thrombosis is present because thrombus alone explains access failure
High-pressure balloons are contraindicated in dialysis access stenosis
updates.explanation: Venous outflow stenoses are typically treated with angioplasty and may require high-pressure or cutting balloons because lesions are often fibrotic. The stated aim is to restore a palpable thrill and pulse or restore the venous-to-brachial artery pressure ratio to below 0.4. When access thrombosis occurs, the underlying venous stenosis must also be treated.

updates.question_text: Regarding central venous access indications and general placement principles, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Common indications include inadequate peripheral venous access, frequent blood draws, chemotherapy, vasopressors, TPN, haemodialysis, and plasmapheresis
The preferred vein for centrally inserted catheters is the femoral vein in all patients
Access is obtained under ultrasound guidance
After placement, aspiration of blood should be avoided because it confirms malposition
Blood should be aspirated to confirm placement and the catheter should then be flushed with heparinised saline to prevent thrombosis
options_after: Common indications include inadequate peripheral venous access, frequent blood draws, chemotherapy, vasopressors, TPN, haemodialysis, and plasmapheresis
The preferred vein for centrally inserted catheters is the femoral vein in most patients
Access is obtained under ultrasound guidance
After placement, aspiration of blood should be avoided because it confirms malposition
Blood should be aspirated to confirm placement and the catheter should then be flushed with heparinised saline to prevent thrombosis
updates.explanation: The source lists common central venous access indications including poor peripheral access, frequent blood draws, irritant medications, haemodialysis, and plasmapheresis. The internal jugular vein is preferred for centrally inserted catheters, with other neck veins such as the external jugular used if necessary. Ultrasound guidance is used. After placement, blood aspiration confirms placement, then heparinised saline flush helps prevent thrombosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding nontunnelled and tunnelled central venous catheters, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Nontunnelled catheters require conscious sedation and are only placed in the IR suite
Nontunnelled catheters may be placed at bedside or in ICU when the patient is too unstable to travel
Prolonged weeks-to-months use of nontunnelled femoral, internal jugular, or subclavian catheters is preferred because infection risk is lower
Tunnelled catheters are placed in the interventional radiology suite and require conscious sedation
Ongoing infection or positive blood cultures are preferred indications for tunnelled catheter placement
options_after: Nontunnelled catheters require conscious sedation and are primarily placed in the IR suite
Nontunnelled catheters may be placed at bedside or in ICU when the patient is too unstable to travel
Prolonged weeks-to-months use of nontunnelled femoral, internal jugular, or subclavian catheters is preferred because infection risk is lower
Tunnelled catheters are placed in the interventional radiology suite and require conscious sedation
Ongoing infection or positive blood cultures are preferred indications for tunnelled catheter placement
updates.explanation: Nontunnelled catheters are typically bedside or ICU catheters for unstable patients and need only local anaesthesia. They are used for general central access indications, rapid resuscitation, and pressure monitoring, but prolonged use should be avoided because of infection risk. Tunnelled catheters are placed in the IR suite with conscious sedation and may last weeks to months or years. Ongoing infection or positive blood cultures are contraindications.

updates.question_text: Regarding drainage of body fluid collections, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Fluid collections include sterile serous collections and abscesses
Hematomas must never be aspirated because aspiration never improves symptoms
The direct trocar technique is safest for deep non-walled acute collections adjacent to bowel
Sterile technique is unnecessary if the collection is already infected
A fresh sterile preparation is needed for each separate fluid collection to avoid cross-contamination
options_after: Fluid collections include sterile serous collections and abscesses
Hematomas must will not be aspirated because aspiration will not improve symptoms
The direct trocar technique is safest for deep non-walled acute collections adjacent to bowel
Sterile technique is unnecessary if the collection is already infected
A fresh sterile preparation is needed for each separate fluid collection to avoid cross-contamination
updates.explanation: The source includes sterile serous collections and abscesses among body fluid collections. Although conventional wisdom discourages hematoma drainage, the text notes evidence that hematoma aspiration may provide faster symptom relief. Infection seeding can be minimised with sterile technique, and each separate collection needs a fresh sterile preparation to avoid cross-contamination.

updates.question_text: Regarding Seldinger and direct trocar drainage techniques, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The Seldinger technique places a catheter over a guidewire
The direct trocar technique requires wire access before the catheter can enter the collection
The direct trocar technique should never involve aspiration after stylet removal
The direct trocar technique can be safe for large superficial collections
In an acute non-walled collection, the guidewire or catheter may advance beyond the collection and perforate adjacent structures
options_after: The Seldinger technique places a catheter over a guidewire
The direct trocar technique requires wire access before the catheter can enter the collection
The direct trocar technique should not involve aspiration after stylet removal
The direct trocar technique can be safe for large superficial collections
In an acute non-walled collection, the guidewire or catheter may advance beyond the collection and perforate adjacent structures
updates.explanation: The Seldinger technique inserts a catheter over a guidewire. The direct trocar technique inserts the catheter directly into the collection with its inner stylet, then removes the stylet and aspirates to confirm position and obtain an initial sample. It can be used safely for large superficial collections. Acute collections without a mature inflammatory wall may not provide resistance, allowing guidewire or catheter passage beyond the collection and perforation of adjacent structures.

updates.question_text: Regarding post-procedure care for drainage catheters, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: Drainage catheters require no maintenance once they are locked
Catheter, connections, and fixation devices should be checked daily, and flushing with saline may be performed up to three times daily depending on the collection
The drain site should be kept wet to prevent skin crusting
Sepsis cannot occur after drainage because the collection has been decompressed
Persistent fistulous connection is not a recognised complication of indwelling catheters
options_after: Once secured, a drainage catheter needs dressing care but not daily connection checks or saline flushing.
Catheter, connections, and fixation devices should be checked daily, and flushing with saline may be performed up to three times daily depending on the collection
The drain site should be kept wet to prevent skin crusting
Sepsis will not occur after drainage because the collection has been decompressed
Persistent fistulous connection is not a recognised complication of indwelling catheters
updates.explanation: The source states that drainage catheters require daily maintenance. The catheter, connections, and fixation devices should be checked daily, and saline flushing may be needed up to three times daily depending on the collection. The drain site should be kept clean and dry. Sepsis should be anticipated around drainage procedures, and persistent fistulous connection can occur with indwelling catheters.

updates.question_text: Regarding the broad radiological approach to arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cartilage destruction is the hallmark of arthritis and may appear as joint-space narrowing on radiographs
All arthropathies can be confidently separated by the presence or absence of osteophytes alone
Rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthropathies, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis are included in the inflammatory category
Gout, calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate deposition, and hydroxyapatite deposition are included among crystal deposition arthropathies
Haemophilia is listed as a metabolic arthropathy rather than a haematologic arthropathy
options_after: Cartilage destruction is the hallmark of arthritis and may appear as joint-space narrowing on radiographs
Most arthropathies can be confidently separated by the presence or absence of osteophytes alone
Rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthropathies, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis are included in the inflammatory category
Gout, calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate deposition, and hydroxyapatite deposition are included among crystal deposition arthropathies
Haemophilia is listed as a metabolic arthropathy rather than a haematologic arthropathy
updates.explanation: The source frames cartilage destruction, visible as joint-space narrowing, as the hallmark of arthritis. It divides arthritis into degenerative, inflammatory, crystal deposition, haematologic, and metabolic categories. Rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthropathies, and JIA are inflammatory, while gout, CPPD, and hydroxyapatite are crystal arthropathies. Haemophilia is placed in the haematologic category.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteoarthritis in the knee, foot, and shoulder, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Knee osteoarthritis usually begins with symmetric narrowing of all three compartments without osteophytes
The great toe interphalangeal joint is the commonest foot joint affected by osteoarthritis
The degree of tibiofemoral cartilage-space narrowing is best assessed on standing weight-bearing views, often in slight flexion
The Grashey view best profiles the glenohumeral joint and demonstrates cartilage-space narrowing
Osteophytes determine the severity of knee osteoarthritis, while joint-space narrowing only determines whether osteoarthritis is present
options_after: Knee osteoarthritis usually begins with symmetric narrowing of most three compartments without osteophytes
The great toe interphalangeal joint is the commonest foot joint affected by osteoarthritis
The degree of tibiofemoral cartilage-space narrowing is best assessed on standing weight-bearing views, often in slight flexion
The Grashey view best profiles the glenohumeral joint and demonstrates cartilage-space narrowing
Osteophytes determine the severity of knee osteoarthritis, while joint-space narrowing primarily determines whether osteoarthritis is present
updates.explanation: The source states that knee OA typically has asymmetric medial tibiofemoral involvement, with severity assessed by the degree of joint-space narrowing on standing weight-bearing views. Osteophytes determine whether OA is present, while the narrowing determines severity. In the foot, OA most commonly affects the great toe MTP joint, not the interphalangeal joint. The Grashey view profiles the glenohumeral joint for shoulder OA assessment.

updates.question_text: Regarding rheumatoid hand deformities, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Boutonniere deformity consists of PIP hyperextension and DIP flexion
Boutonniere deformity consists of PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension
Swan-neck deformity consists of PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension
Swan-neck deformity consists of PIP hyperextension and DIP flexion
Rheumatoid deformities never arise from tendon or volar plate pathology
options_after: Boutonniere deformity consists of PIP hyperextension and DIP flexion
Boutonniere deformity consists of PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension
Swan-neck deformity consists of PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension
Swan-neck deformity consists of PIP hyperextension and DIP flexion
Rheumatoid deformities will not arise from tendon or volar plate pathology
updates.explanation: The source defines boutonniere deformity as PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension. Swan-neck deformity is the reverse pattern: PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion. The image captions note that these deformities can be caused by inflammation or trauma involving the extensor tendon, flexor tendon, or volar plate.

updates.question_text: Regarding sacroiliitis patterns in spondyloarthropathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Asymmetric sacroiliitis is typical of ankylosing spondylitis and inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthropathy
Symmetric sacroiliitis is caused by inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthropathy and ankylosing spondylitis
Asymmetric sacroiliitis is caused by psoriatic arthritis and reactive arthropathy
Unilateral sacroiliitis should raise concern for septic arthritis, especially in immunocompromised patients or intravenous drug use
Sacroiliitis never produces associated abscess
options_after: Asymmetric sacroiliitis is typical of ankylosing spondylitis and inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthropathy
Symmetric sacroiliitis is caused by inflammatory bowel disease-associated arthropathy and ankylosing spondylitis
Asymmetric sacroiliitis is caused by psoriatic arthritis and reactive arthropathy
Unilateral sacroiliitis should raise concern for septic arthritis, especially in immunocompromised patients or intravenous drug use
Sacroiliitis will not produce associated abscess
updates.explanation: The source uses a practical pattern rule: symmetric sacroiliitis is associated with IBD arthropathy and ankylosing spondylitis, whereas asymmetric sacroiliitis is associated with psoriatic arthritis and reactive arthropathy. Unilateral sacroiliitis is an important infection pattern, especially in immunocompromised patients or intravenous drug use. An associated abscess may be present, often anterior to the SI joint.

updates.question_text: Regarding psoriatic and reactive arthropathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Psoriatic arthritis commonly affects the hands and may produce oligoarthritis, polyarthritis, spondyloarthropathy, or arthritis mutilans patterns
Reactive arthropathy is thought to follow infectious diarrhoea, urethritis, or cervicitis
Reactive arthropathy predominantly affects the hands, whereas psoriatic arthritis predominantly affects the spine
Psoriatic arthritis and reactive arthropathy both produce fine marginal syndesmophytes identical to ankylosing spondylitis
In the spine, psoriatic and reactive arthropathy can produce coarse bony bridging that may be hard to distinguish between the two
options_after: Psoriatic arthritis commonly affects the hands and may produce oligoarthritis, polyarthritis, spondyloarthropathy, or arthritis mutilans patterns
Reactive arthropathy is thought to follow infectious diarrhoea, urethritis, or cervicitis
Reactive arthropathy predominantly affects the hands, whereas psoriatic arthritis predominantly affects the spine
Psoriatic arthritis and reactive arthropathy both produce fine marginal syndesmophytes closely comparable to ankylosing spondylitis
In the spine, psoriatic and reactive arthropathy can produce coarse bony bridging that may be hard to distinguish between the two
updates.explanation: The source lists multiple psoriatic arthritis patterns, including oligoarthritis, polyarthritis, spondyloarthropathy, and arthritis mutilans. Reactive arthropathy is described as a sequela of infectious diarrhoea, urethritis, or cervicitis and predominantly affects the feet. Both psoriatic and reactive arthropathy may produce coarse bony bridging in the spine, which can be difficult to distinguish between them. Delicate marginal syndesmophytes are the ankylosing spondylitis pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding the atlantoaxial joint in rheumatoid arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The transverse ligament extends across the dens from the lateral masses of C1 and maintains contact between the dens and the anterior arch of C1
Posterior atlantoaxial subluxation in rheumatoid arthritis is always due to ligament calcification
Vertical atlantoaxial subluxation is caused by osteophyte bridging across the disc spaces
Vertical atlantoaxial subluxation results from C1-C2 facet erosion and collapse with odontoid protrusion through the foramen magnum
Odontoid erosion may cause posterior atlantoaxial subluxation in rheumatoid arthritis
options_after: The transverse ligament extends across the dens from the lateral masses of C1 and maintains contact between the dens and the anterior arch of C1
Posterior atlantoaxial subluxation in rheumatoid arthritis is characteristically due to ligament calcification
Vertical atlantoaxial subluxation is caused by osteophyte bridging across the disc spaces
Vertical atlantoaxial subluxation results from C1-C2 facet erosion and collapse with odontoid protrusion through the foramen magnum
Odontoid erosion may cause posterior atlantoaxial subluxation in rheumatoid arthritis
updates.explanation: The source describes the transverse ligament as extending across the dens between the lateral masses of C1, maintaining the dens against the anterior arch. Vertical atlantoaxial subluxation, or impaction, results from C1-C2 facet erosion and collapse, allowing odontoid protrusion through the foramen magnum. Posterior atlantoaxial subluxation in RA is usually due to odontoid erosion, though fracture can also be responsible. Osteophyte bridging is not the mechanism described for RA impaction.

updates.question_text: Regarding foot findings in psoriatic and reactive arthropathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Psoriatic arthritis most commonly affects the subtalar joint and spares the toes
Reactive arthropathy produces late diffuse demineralisation as its defining feature
In psoriatic arthritis, the great toe interphalangeal and MTP joints are most commonly affected in the foot
Reactive arthropathy commonly involves the calcaneus with erosions, enthesophytes, and fluffy periosteal reaction
A degenerative calcaneal spur characteristically has reactive new bone identical to psoriatic arthritis
options_after: Psoriatic arthritis most commonly affects the subtalar joint and spares the toes
Reactive arthropathy produces late diffuse demineralisation as its defining feature
In psoriatic arthritis, the great toe interphalangeal and MTP joints are most commonly affected in the foot
Reactive arthropathy commonly involves the calcaneus with erosions, enthesophytes, and fluffy periosteal reaction
A degenerative calcaneal spur characteristically has reactive new bone closely comparable to psoriatic arthritis
updates.explanation: The source states that psoriatic arthritis in the foot most commonly affects the great toe interphalangeal and MTP joints. Reactive arthropathy predominantly affects the feet and commonly involves the calcaneus with erosions, enthesophytes, fluffy periosteal reaction, Achilles tendinitis, and soft-tissue thickening. Bony mineralisation is preserved in the later stage of reactive arthropathy. A degenerative calcaneal spur lacks the reactive new bone of psoriatic arthritis.

updates.question_text: Regarding dual-energy CT in gout and calcium pyrophosphate deposition, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Dual-energy CT cannot distinguish crystal composition and is limited to showing erosion morphology
Green post-processing always indicates calcium hydroxyapatite regardless of the selected algorithm
Dual-energy CT is an excellent modality to identify monosodium urate crystals
Dual-energy CT is only useful when radiographs are completely normal
Changing the post-processing parameters can also allow green colour coding of CPP crystals
options_after: Dual-energy CT will not distinguish crystal composition and is limited to showing erosion morphology
Green post-processing characteristically indicates calcium hydroxyapatite despite variation in the selected algorithm
Dual-energy CT is an excellent modality to identify monosodium urate crystals
Dual-energy CT is primarily useful when radiographs are completely normal
Changing the post-processing parameters can also allow green colour coding of CPP crystals
updates.explanation: The source states that dual-energy CT is excellent for identifying monosodium urate crystals, typically colour-coded green in post-processing. It also notes that by altering post-processing parameters, green coding can identify CPP crystals. The ankle example shows CT erosions and mineralisation with urate deposition highlighted on the gout algorithm. The colour coding is algorithm-dependent rather than automatically indicating hydroxyapatite.

updates.question_text: Regarding treatment of calcific tendinopathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ultrasound-guided barbotage can be an effective treatment
The condition is treated by aspirating intra-articular urate crystals from the joint space
The Achilles tendon is described as by far the commonest site in the body
The hip is by far the commonest site, with the rectus femoris tendon most commonly affected
Barbotage is performed with a fine 30-gauge needle and no lavage
