options_after: Ultrasound-guided barbotage can be an effective treatment
The condition is treated by aspirating intra-articular urate crystals from the joint space
The Achilles tendon is described as by far the commonest site in the body
The hip is by far the commonest site, with the rectus femoris tendon most commonly affected
Barbotage is performed with a fine 30-gauge needle without lavage
updates.explanation: The source states that ultrasound-guided barbotage is effective for calcific tendinopathy. It describes directing an 18–20 gauge needle into the calcific deposit and pulsing dilute anaesthetic/saline to break up the deposit, sometimes retrieving chalky material. The shoulder, not the hip, is by far the commonest site, with the supraspinatus tendon most commonly affected. This is not an intra-articular urate aspiration procedure.

updates.question_text: Regarding amyloid arthropathy, ochronosis, and sarcoidosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Amyloid arthropathy is a rare non-inflammatory arthropathy due to beta-pleated sheet deposition in bones, joints, and soft tissues
Bulky shoulder soft-tissue nodules with atrophic shoulder muscles can produce the shoulder-pad sign in amyloidosis
Ochronosis can produce intervertebral disc calcifications at every level with disc-space narrowing
Sarcoidosis characteristically causes punched-out skull lesions and no hand findings
Bilateral ankle involvement with erythema nodosum should raise suspicion for sarcoidosis and prompt a chest radiograph
options_after: Amyloid arthropathy is a rare non-inflammatory arthropathy due to beta-pleated sheet deposition in bones, joints, and soft tissues
Bulky shoulder soft-tissue nodules with atrophic shoulder muscles can produce the shoulder-pad sign in amyloidosis
Ochronosis can produce intervertebral disc calcifications at every level with disc-space narrowing
Sarcoidosis characteristically causes punched-out skull lesions without hand findings
Bilateral ankle involvement with erythema nodosum should raise suspicion for sarcoidosis and prompt a chest radiograph
updates.explanation: The source describes amyloid arthropathy as a rare non-inflammatory infiltrative arthropathy, with shoulder-pad sign from bulky soft-tissue nodules superimposed on atrophic shoulder muscles. Ochronosis from alkaptonuria specifically causes intervertebral disc calcifications at every level with disc-space narrowing. Sarcoidosis rarely has bony manifestations, but lace-like lytic lesions in the middle or distal phalanges are characteristic. Bilateral ankle involvement, especially with erythema nodosum, should prompt chest radiography.

updates.question_text: Regarding pseudotumour of haemophilia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a malignant vascular tumour arising from synovium
It is caused by recurrent intraosseous or subperiosteal bleeding
Radiographs are expected to show aggressive permeative destruction without a margin
It is defined by intervertebral disc calcification at every level
MRI may have a complex appearance because of different stages of blood products
options_after: It is a malignant vascular tumour arising from synovium
It is caused by recurrent intraosseous or subperiosteal bleeding
Radiographs are expected to show aggressive permeative destruction without a margin
It is defined by intervertebral disc calcification at routine level
MRI may have a complex appearance because of different stages of blood products
updates.explanation: The source defines pseudotumour of haemophilia as a benign lesion caused by recurrent intraosseous or subperiosteal bleeding. Chronic cyclical bleeding causes bony scalloping and pressure erosion, often with a soft-tissue mass. Radiographically it is benign appearing with well-circumscribed sclerotic margins. MRI can be complex because blood products are present at different stages.

updates.question_text: Regarding juvenile idiopathic arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a spectrum of chronic inflammatory arthropathies affecting children younger than 16 years
The most common form is polyarticular disease involving all joints from onset
Monoarticular or pauciarticular disease is most common and may affect knees, ankles, elbows, or wrists
Still disease is a systemic disorder in children younger than 5 with febrile illness, rash, adenopathy, pericarditis, and mild arthralgias
Growth disturbances are absent because affected physes fuse late
options_after: It is a spectrum of chronic inflammatory arthropathies affecting children younger than 16 years
The most common form is polyarticular disease involving most joints from onset
Monoarticular or pauciarticular disease is most common and may affect knees, ankles, elbows, or wrists
Still disease is a systemic disorder in children younger than 5 with febrile illness, rash, adenopathy, pericarditis, and mild arthralgias
Growth disturbances are absent because affected physes fuse late
updates.explanation: The source defines JIA as chronic inflammatory arthropathies in children under 16 years. Monoarticular or pauciarticular disease is the commonest pattern and may involve knees, ankles, elbows, or wrists. Polyarticular disease is systemic and involves multiple joints, including hands, feet, and cervical spine. Still disease affects children under 5 and has systemic febrile and inflammatory features. Growth disturbances are central radiographic hallmarks, especially in early-onset disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding overlap between juvenile idiopathic arthritis and haemophilic arthropathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Both can show a widened intercondylar notch in the knee
Only haemophilia can produce articular hyperaemia in children
JIA never affects the elbow
Haemophilia classically causes cervical facet ankylosis that mimics Klippel-Feil syndrome
Both can show radial head enlargement in the elbow
options_after: Both can show a widened intercondylar notch in the knee
Articular hyperaemia favours haemophilic arthropathy over juvenile idiopathic arthritis in children.
JIA will not affect the elbow
Haemophilia classically causes cervical facet ankylosis that mimics Klippel-Feil syndrome
Both can show radial head enlargement in the elbow
updates.explanation: The source explicitly notes that JIA and haemophilia may have similar radiographic findings, especially widened intercondylar notch in the knee and enlarged radial head in the elbow. JIA itself can involve the elbow and causes articular hyperaemia in the skeletally immature patient. Cervical facet ankylosis is a JIA feature, with Klippel-Feil syndrome listed as a differential diagnosis in a child with cervical spine ankylosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding atrophic neuropathic arthropathy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It most commonly occurs in the knee and causes hook-like MCP osteophytes
It is defined by periarticular calcification and distal phalangeal acro-osteolysis
It most commonly occurs in the shoulder with humeral head resorption and a sharp surgical-like margin
Syringomyelia should be suspected in upper-extremity neuropathic arthropathy and confirmed by cervical spine MRI
It is excluded if there is no history of trauma
options_after: It most commonly occurs in the knee and causes hook-like MCP osteophytes
It is defined by periarticular calcification and distal phalangeal acro-osteolysis
It most commonly occurs in the shoulder with humeral head resorption and a sharp surgical-like margin
Syringomyelia should be suspected in upper-extremity neuropathic arthropathy and confirmed by cervical spine MRI
It is excluded if there is an absence of history of trauma
updates.explanation: The source states that the atrophic variant occurs most commonly in the shoulder and has the classic radiographic appearance of humeral head resorption with a sharp, surgical-like margin. Upper-extremity neuropathic arthropathy should prompt suspicion for syringomyelia and cervical spine MRI confirmation. Trauma history is not required for neuropathic arthropathy, as lack of sensation is the key mechanism.

updates.question_text: Regarding pattern-based diagnosis across this batch, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acro-osteolysis with fingertip soft-tissue calcification supports scleroderma
Disc calcification at every spinal level with disc-space narrowing is the classic pattern of haemophilic arthropathy
Brachydactyly from premature physeal fusion supports juvenile idiopathic arthritis
An enlarged radial head and widened trochlear notch are specific for calcium hydroxyapatite deposition
A painless swollen foot with Lisfranc subluxation, debris, and disorganisation supports neuropathic arthropathy
options_after: Acro-osteolysis with fingertip soft-tissue calcification supports scleroderma
Disc calcification at a single spinal level with disc-space narrowing is the classic pattern of haemophilic arthropathy.
Brachydactyly from premature physeal fusion supports juvenile idiopathic arthritis
An enlarged radial head and widened trochlear notch are specific for calcium hydroxyapatite deposition
A painless swollen foot with Lisfranc subluxation, debris, and disorganisation supports neuropathic arthropathy
updates.explanation: This batch includes several high-yield pattern diagnoses. Scleroderma is supported by acro-osteolysis and soft-tissue calcification. JIA can cause brachydactyly from premature physeal fusion. Neuropathic arthropathy may present as a painless swollen foot with Lisfranc subluxation, debris, disorganisation, and no trauma history. Disc calcification at every level is ochronosis, while enlarged radial head and widened trochlear notch are seen in haemophilia and may overlap with JIA.

updates.question_text: Regarding the practical grouping of bone lesions in this source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In clinical practice, bone lesions more often have non-specific imaging features than a board-style pathognomonic appearance
Management of a non-specific lesion should be guided by aggressive versus non-aggressive appearance
Aggressive but non-specific lesions in adults most often have enchondroma and osteoid osteoma as the main differential
Non-aggressive but non-specific lesions should always be biopsied before considering follow-up
Characteristic lesions worth learning include both benign and malignant entities
options_after: In clinical practice, bone lesions more often have non-specific imaging features than a board-style pathognomonic appearance
Management of a non-specific lesion should be guided by aggressive versus non-aggressive appearance
Aggressive but non-specific lesions in adults most often have enchondroma and osteoid osteoma as the main differential
Non-aggressive but non-specific lesions should characteristically be biopsied before considering follow-up
Characteristic lesions worth learning include both benign and malignant entities
updates.explanation: The source explicitly warns that many bone lesions in clinical practice do not have specific imaging features. Management should therefore be determined by aggressive versus non-aggressive appearance. The characteristic lesions are still worth learning and include benign and malignant entities. Aggressive non-specific lesions in adults raise metastasis or myeloma rather than the common benign lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding permeative and pseudopermeative bone destruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Permeative destruction is seen in lymphoma, leukaemia, and Ewing sarcoma
Pseudopermeative change is distinguished from true aggressive permeation because it never extends to the cortex
True permeative destruction is very aggressive and consists of multiple tiny holes infiltrating bone
Moth-eaten destruction has a thin sclerotic rim and is almost always non-aggressive
Pseudopermeative appearance can be seen in osteoporosis and osseous haemangioma
options_after: Permeative destruction is seen in lymphoma, leukaemia, and Ewing sarcoma
Pseudopermeative change is distinguished from true aggressive permeation because it will not extend to the cortex
True permeative destruction is very aggressive and consists of multiple tiny holes infiltrating bone
Moth-eaten destruction has a thin sclerotic rim and is typically non-aggressive
Pseudopermeative appearance can be seen in osteoporosis and osseous haemangioma
updates.explanation: The source describes type 3 permeative destruction as multiple tiny holes infiltrating bone and calls it very aggressive, with lymphoma, leukaemia, and Ewing sarcoma as examples. Pseudopermeative appearance occurs in osteoporosis and osseous haemangioma, both benign conditions. Unlike true permeation, the pseudopermeative appearance extends to the cortex. Moth-eaten destruction is aggressive.

updates.question_text: Regarding age-based differential diagnosis of aggressive lytic bone lesions, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Age is irrelevant once a lesion has an aggressive lytic appearance
In adults over 40, non-ossifying fibroma is the leading diagnosis for aggressive lytic lesions
In teenagers, aggressive lytic lesions should always be presumed osteopoikilosis until proven otherwise
In a patient over age 40, metastasis and myeloma are the two most likely considerations
In a patient under age 20, eosinophilic granuloma, infection, and Ewing sarcoma are likely considerations
options_after: Age is irrelevant once a lesion has an aggressive lytic appearance
In adults over 40, non-ossifying fibroma is the leading diagnosis for aggressive lytic lesions
In teenagers, aggressive lytic lesions should characteristically be presumed osteopoikilosis until proven otherwise
In a patient over age 40, metastasis and myeloma are the two most likely considerations
In a patient under age 20, eosinophilic granuloma, infection, and Ewing sarcoma are likely considerations
updates.explanation: The source explicitly gives an age-based rule. In patients over 40, metastasis and myeloma are the two most likely diagnoses for an aggressive lytic bone lesion. In patients under 20, eosinophilic granuloma, infection, and Ewing sarcoma are likely considerations. Age is therefore a major first-pass discriminator, not an irrelevant detail.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteoid osteoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a benign chondroid lesion characterised by ring-and-arc matrix and no reactive sclerosis
The classic clinical presentation is night pain relieved by aspirin in a teenager or young adult
About 20% occur in the posterior elements of the spine and can cause painful scoliosis
It most commonly occurs in the epiphysis of the upper extremity
It is defined by a cartilage cap over 2 cm
options_after: It is a benign chondroid lesion characterised by ring-and-arc matrix without reactive sclerosis
The classic clinical presentation is night pain relieved by aspirin in a teenager or young adult
About 20% occur in the posterior elements of the spine and can cause painful scoliosis
It most commonly occurs in the epiphysis of the upper extremity
It is defined by a cartilage cap over 2 cm
updates.explanation: The source defines osteoid osteoma as a benign osteoblastic lesion with a nidus surrounded by reactive sclerosis, not a chondroid lesion. The classic presentation is night pain relieved by aspirin in a teenager or young adult. It most commonly occurs in the diaphyses of the femur and tibia. Around 20% occur in posterior spinal elements and may cause painful scoliosis.

updates.question_text: Which single treatment option is explicitly listed for osteoid osteoma in this source?
options_before: Long-term anticoagulation
Radiofrequency ablation by interventional radiology
Whole-limb external beam radiotherapy
Systemic chemotherapy
No treatment is ever appropriate because it is always asymptomatic
options_after: Long-term anticoagulation
Radiofrequency ablation by interventional radiology
Whole-limb external beam radiotherapy
Systemic chemotherapy
Observation is preferred because osteoid osteoma is typically asymptomatic.
updates.explanation: The source lists interventional radiology radiofrequency ablation as a treatment for osteoid osteoma, along with surgical curettage or resection. The condition is not framed as an asymptomatic incidental lesion; it classically causes night pain relieved by aspirin. Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and anticoagulation are not listed as osteoid osteoma treatments.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteoblastoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most common location is the posterior elements of the spine
Its pain is typically relieved by aspirin, making it clinically identical to osteoid osteoma
It is defined by diffuse pulmonary metastases at presentation
It is histologically the same as osteoid osteoma but is greater than 2 cm
It is approximately four times less common than osteoid osteoma
options_after: The most common location is the posterior elements of the spine
Its pain is typically relieved by aspirin, making it clinically closely comparable to osteoid osteoma
It is defined by diffuse pulmonary metastases at presentation
It is histologically the same as osteoid osteoma but is greater than 2 cm
It is approximately four times less common than osteoid osteoma
updates.explanation: Osteoblastoma is a benign osteoid-producing tumour histologically similar to osteoid osteoma but larger than 2 cm. It is about four times less common and also affects adolescents and young adults, but the pain is not typically relieved by aspirin. The posterior elements of the spine are the commonest location. It may rarely appear aggressive locally, but the source says it lacks metastatic potential.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteosarcoma in general, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Osteosarcoma is a benign group of cartilage-producing lesions derived from chondroid lineage
General imaging hallmarks include bony destruction, osteoid matrix, aggressive periosteal reaction, and a soft-tissue mass
All osteosarcoma subtypes produce abundant osteoid matrix
Secondary osteosarcoma may arise from Paget disease or after radiation
Secondary osteosarcoma arising in Paget disease is extremely indolent
options_after: Osteosarcoma is a benign group of cartilage-producing lesions derived from chondroid lineage
General imaging hallmarks include bony destruction, osteoid matrix, aggressive periosteal reaction, and a soft-tissue mass
Most osteosarcoma subtypes produce abundant osteoid matrix
Secondary osteosarcoma may arise from Paget disease or after radiation
Secondary osteosarcoma arising in Paget disease is extremely indolent
updates.explanation: The source defines osteosarcoma as a heterogeneous group of malignant tumours derived from osteoid lineage. Most, but not all, subtypes produce osteoid matrix; telangiectatic osteosarcoma is the key exception later in the section. Secondary osteosarcoma can arise from Paget disease or after radiation, and secondary osteosarcoma in Paget disease is described as extremely aggressive. Core imaging hallmarks are bony destruction, osteoid matrix, aggressive periosteal reaction, and soft-tissue mass, though early disease may be subtle sclerosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding subtle conventional osteosarcoma on radiography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Early osteosarcoma may be evident only as subtle sclerosis
Absence of visible periosteal reaction on radiography excludes osteosarcoma
MRI may show marrow replacement when the radiographic abnormality is subtle
The source example shows subtle sclerosis in the proximal tibial metaphysis
Subtle sclerosis in a metaphysis should always be dismissed as a bone island without further imaging
options_after: Early osteosarcoma may be evident only as subtle sclerosis
Absence of visible periosteal reaction on radiography excludes osteosarcoma
MRI may show marrow replacement when the radiographic abnormality is subtle
The source example shows subtle sclerosis in the proximal tibial metaphysis
Subtle sclerosis in a metaphysis should characteristically be dismissed as a bone island without further imaging
updates.explanation: The source specifically warns that early osteosarcoma may be subtle, sometimes evident only as sclerosis. The example shows subtle medial proximal tibial metaphyseal sclerosis without apparent periosteal reaction, which is unusual for osteosarcoma. MRI demonstrates marrow replacement and marrow oedema, showing why subtle sclerosis should not automatically be dismissed when the clinical or imaging context is concerning.

updates.question_text: Regarding when an osteoblastic focus becomes more diagnostically problematic, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Every bone island requires biopsy because bone scan is always intensely positive
Osteopoikilosis converts multiple bone islands into malignant lesions by definition
A giant bone island greater than 2 cm may be difficult to distinguish from low-grade osteosarcoma
A bone island is clinically important only because it may rarely mimic osteoblastic metastasis, osteoid osteoma, or low-grade osteosarcoma
Osteopathia striata is a benign asymptomatic dysplasia with typically normal bone scan
options_after: A bone island with intense uptake on bone scintigraphy requires biopsy.
Osteopoikilosis converts multiple bone islands into malignant lesions by definition
A giant bone island greater than 2 cm may be difficult to distinguish from low-grade osteosarcoma
A bone island is clinically important only because it may rarely mimic osteoblastic metastasis, osteoid osteoma, or low-grade osteosarcoma
Osteopathia striata is a benign asymptomatic dysplasia with typically normal bone scan
updates.explanation: The source frames bone islands as extremely common incidental findings, clinically relevant mainly because they can rarely mimic osteoblastic metastasis, osteoid osteoma, or low-grade osteosarcoma. A giant variant over 2 cm is especially difficult to separate from low-grade osteosarcoma. Bone scan is usually normal for bone island and typically normal in osteopathia striata. Osteopoikilosis is an autosomal dominant multiple bone island syndrome, not malignant transformation by definition.

updates.question_text: Regarding enchondroma in long bones and the hand, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: In the hand, enchondroma typically has no visible matrix and appears as a geographic lytic lesion
Enchondroma in the hand cannot be complicated by pathological fracture
Enchondroma is a malignant lesion of immature osteoid tissue
Long-bone enchondroma typically shows chondroid popcorn or ring-and-arc calcification
MRI usually helps differentiate medullary bone infarct from enchondroma
options_after: In the hand, enchondroma typically has no visible matrix and appears as a geographic lytic lesion
Enchondroma in the hand will not be complicated by pathological fracture
Enchondroma is a malignant lesion of immature osteoid tissue
Long-bone enchondroma typically shows chondroid popcorn or ring-and-arc calcification
MRI usually helps differentiate medullary bone infarct from enchondroma
updates.explanation: Enchondroma is a benign lesion of mature hyaline cartilage rests. In long bones it characteristically shows ring-and-arc or popcorn chondroid calcification, while in the hand it may appear as a geographic lytic lesion without visible matrix. MRI typically shows lobulated T2 hyperintensity and can help separate enchondroma from medullary bone infarct. Hand enchondromas can be complicated by pathological fracture.

updates.question_text: Regarding chondroblastoma and chondromyxoid fibroma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chondroblastoma is eccentric in the epiphysis of a long bone in a skeletally immature patient
Chondroblastoma usually shows low or intermediate T2 signal, unlike most chondroid lesions
Calcified chondroid matrix in chondroblastoma is present on almost all CT studies but only about half of radiographs
Chondromyxoid fibroma is typically eccentric in the tibial or femoral metaphysis about the knee
Chondromyxoid fibroma characteristically shows abundant ring-and-arc matrix in nearly all cases
options_after: Chondroblastoma is eccentric in the epiphysis of a long bone in a skeletally immature patient
Chondroblastoma usually shows low or intermediate T2 signal, unlike most chondroid lesions
Calcified chondroid matrix in chondroblastoma is present on almost all CT studies but only about half of radiographs
Chondromyxoid fibroma is typically eccentric in the tibial or femoral metaphysis about the knee
Chondromyxoid fibroma characteristically shows abundant ring-and-arc matrix in the large majority of cases
updates.explanation: Chondroblastoma is an eccentric epiphyseal lesion of skeletally immature patients, usually around the knee or proximal humerus. It is unusual among chondroid lesions because it typically has low or intermediate T2 signal. Calcified chondroid matrix is nearly always present on CT but only seen in about half of radiographs. Chondromyxoid fibroma is a rare benign cartilage tumour, eccentric in the tibial or femoral metaphysis near the knee, and rarely demonstrates chondroid matrix.

updates.question_text: Regarding chondrosarcoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Conventional intramedullary chondrosarcoma is the most common subtype
It is typically an expansile medullary lesion with ring-and-arc chondroid matrix
It may cause cortical thickening, endosteal scalloping, and an associated soft-tissue mass
Secondary chondrosarcoma may arise from enchondroma, Paget disease, or osteochondroma
Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is indolent and never contains non-chondroid sarcoma elements
options_after: Conventional intramedullary chondrosarcoma is the most common subtype
It is typically an expansile medullary lesion with ring-and-arc chondroid matrix
It may cause cortical thickening, endosteal scalloping, and an associated soft-tissue mass
Secondary chondrosarcoma may arise from enchondroma, Paget disease, or osteochondroma
Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is indolent and will not contain non-chondroid sarcoma elements
updates.explanation: The source describes conventional intramedullary chondrosarcoma as the commonest subtype. It is typically expansile in medullary bone with ring-and-arc matrix, endosteal scalloping or cortical thickening, and often a soft-tissue mass. Secondary forms arise from enchondroma, Paget disease, or osteochondroma. Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is aggressive and may contain fibrosarcoma or osteosarcoma elements.

updates.question_text: Regarding fibrous dysplasia in long bones and the pelvis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most frequent complication is pulmonary metastasis
It is a benign congenital non-neoplastic condition replacing cancellous bone with abnormal fibrous tissue
Polyostotic disease is typically bilateral and symmetric
Long-bone lesions tend to be central and metadiaphyseal with ground-glass matrix
Pelvic fibrous dysplasia is characteristically never cystic
options_after: The most frequent complication is pulmonary metastasis
It is a benign congenital non-neoplastic condition replacing cancellous bone with abnormal fibrous tissue
Polyostotic disease is typically bilateral and symmetric
Long-bone lesions tend to be central and metadiaphyseal with ground-glass matrix
Cystic change is incompatible with pelvic fibrous dysplasia.
updates.explanation: Fibrous dysplasia is a benign congenital non-neoplastic process replacing cancellous bone with abnormal fibrous tissue. In long bones it tends to be central and metadiaphyseal with ground-glass matrix and can cause bowing deformity. Polyostotic disease tends to be unilateral rather than symmetric. Pathological fracture, commonly at the femoral neck, is the frequent complication, and pelvic lesions may be cystic.

updates.question_text: Regarding skull-base fibrous dysplasia and its syndromic associations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Skull-base fibrous dysplasia is typically expansile and may look highly unusual on MRI
The primary differential of an expansile skull-base lesion is Paget disease, with age helping distinguish them
McCune-Albright syndrome comprises polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, precocious puberty, and café-au-lait spots
Mazabraud syndrome comprises fibrous dysplasia and intramuscular myxomas in the same region
Paget disease and fibrous dysplasia occur in identical age groups, so age is not useful
options_after: Skull-base fibrous dysplasia is typically expansile and may look highly unusual on MRI
The primary differential of an expansile skull-base lesion is Paget disease, with age helping distinguish them
McCune-Albright syndrome comprises polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, precocious puberty, and café-au-lait spots
Mazabraud syndrome comprises fibrous dysplasia and intramuscular myxomas in the same region
Paget disease and fibrous dysplasia occur in closely comparable age groups, so age is not useful
updates.explanation: The source states that skull-base fibrous dysplasia is expansile and can look unusual on MRI. Paget disease is the main differential for an expansile skull-base lesion, but fibrous dysplasia occurs in children and young adults, while Paget disease occurs in older adults. McCune-Albright syndrome combines polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, precocious puberty, and café-au-lait spots. Mazabraud syndrome combines fibrous dysplasia with intramuscular myxomas, often regionally related.

updates.question_text: Regarding giant cell tumour, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most lesions are malignant and behaviour is easily predicted from the primary imaging appearance
It is an epiphyseal lucent lesion at the articular end of long bones in skeletally mature patients aged 20?40
It is central in the diaphysis and usually avoids the articular surface
It remains confined to the metaphysis and cannot cross a closed physis
Multifocal giant cell tumours may be seen in Paget disease or hyperparathyroidism
options_after: Most lesions are malignant and behaviour is easily predicted from the primary imaging appearance
It is an epiphyseal lucent lesion at the articular end of long bones in skeletally mature patients aged 20?40
It is central in the diaphysis and usually avoids the articular surface
It remains confined to the metaphysis and will not cross a closed physis
Multifocal giant cell tumours may be seen in Paget disease or hyperparathyroidism
updates.explanation: Giant cell tumour is an eccentric epiphyseal lucent lesion at the articular end of long bones in skeletally mature patients aged 20?40. It arises from the metaphysis but crosses the closed physis to involve the epiphysis and articular end. Most are benign; about 5% are malignant, and behaviour cannot be predicted from primary imaging appearance. Multifocal lesions can occur in Paget disease or hyperparathyroidism.

updates.question_text: Regarding Langerhans cell histiocytosis/eosinophilic granuloma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mandibular or maxillary involvement produces dense alveolar sclerosis that fixes teeth in place
Long-bone lesions are always non-aggressive and never mimic Ewing sarcoma or lymphoma
It primarily affects adults over 40 and usually presents as an ivory vertebral body
Skull lesions classically have a lytic beveled-edge appearance
Spinal involvement may cause vertebra plana
options_after: Mandibular or maxillary involvement produces dense alveolar sclerosis that fixes teeth in place
Long-bone lesions are characteristically non-aggressive and will not mimic Ewing sarcoma or lymphoma
It primarily affects adults over 40 and usually presents as an ivory vertebral body
Skull lesions classically have a lytic beveled-edge appearance
Spinal involvement may cause vertebra plana
updates.explanation: The source frames LCH/eosinophilic granuloma as a disorder of histiocyte proliferation seen mainly in children aged 5?10 years. Classic imaging signs include bevelled-edge skull lytic lesions and vertebra plana. Mandibular or maxillary disease can cause floating teeth from alveolar bone resorption, not sclerosis. Long-bone lesions may look aggressive and mimic lymphoma or Ewing sarcoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding multiple myeloma and plasmacytoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It originates from yellow marrow and therefore preferentially involves low-red-marrow regions such as spinal pedicles
Multiple myeloma is always strongly positive on bone scan, unlike metastases
Most patients with solitary plasmacytoma develop full-blown myeloma within 5 years
Multiple myeloma is the most common primary malignant bone tumour in patients over 40
Its commonest presentation is diffuse blastic sclerosis without endosteal scalloping
options_after: It originates from yellow marrow and therefore preferentially involves low-red-marrow regions such as spinal pedicles
Multiple myeloma is characteristically strongly positive on bone scan, unlike metastases
Most patients with solitary plasmacytoma develop full-blown myeloma within 5 years
Multiple myeloma is the most common primary malignant bone tumour in patients over 40
Its commonest presentation is diffuse blastic sclerosis without endosteal scalloping
updates.explanation: Multiple myeloma is the most common primary malignant bone tumour in patients over 40. The commonest presentation is multiple lytic lesions; diffuse myelomatosis with endosteal scalloping is the severe form. Myeloma originates from red marrow and usually does not involve low-red-marrow regions such as spinal pedicles. It may be negative on bone scan, and most solitary plasmacytomas progress to full myeloma within 5 years.

updates.question_text: Regarding simple bone cyst, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is always located centrally within bone
It commonly has aggressive periosteal reaction even when there is no fracture
It is a benign local disturbance of bone growth in children and adolescents
It is typically found in the distal phalanges and skull base
The fallen fragment sign is pathognomonic when seen in a young patient in an appropriate location
options_after: It is always located centrally within bone
It commonly has aggressive periosteal reaction even when there is an absence of fracture
It is a benign local disturbance of bone growth in children and adolescents
It is typically found in the distal phalanges and skull base
The fallen fragment sign is pathognomonic when seen in a young patient in an appropriate location
updates.explanation: Simple bone cyst is a benign local disturbance of growth in children and adolescents, typically in the proximal diaphysis of the humerus or femur, and is always central in bone. It lacks periosteal reaction unless fractured. The fallen fragment sign is pathognomonic when seen in a young patient in an appropriate location. Fluid-fluid levels are non-specific.

updates.question_text: Regarding aneurysmal bone cyst, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is usually a solid lesion of older adults without cystic spaces
It cannot arise secondarily within another tumour
It is always central and never involves posterior spinal elements
It is histologically composed of blood-filled sinusoids and solid fibrous elements
It often features a smooth buttressing periosteal reaction at proximal and distal aspects
options_after: It is usually a solid lesion of older adults without cystic spaces
It will not arise secondarily within another tumour
It is characteristically central and will not involve posterior spinal elements
It is histologically composed of blood-filled sinusoids and solid fibrous elements
It often features a smooth buttressing periosteal reaction at proximal and distal aspects
updates.explanation: ABC is an expansile multicystic lesion of children and adolescents, made of blood-filled sinusoids and solid fibrous elements. It may arise secondarily within a pre-existing tumour, so ABC pathology from an aggressive lesion can mean the true lesion was missed. Unlike SBC, ABC may be central or eccentric and can occur in posterior spinal elements. Buttressing smooth periosteal reaction may be present.

updates.question_text: Regarding lytic and blastic metastasis patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lung is listed as the most common purely blastic osseous metastasis
Kidney and thyroid are listed under blastic rather than lytic osseous metastases
Transitional cell carcinoma is listed only as a purely lytic metastasis
Breast metastases may be lytic or blastic
Prostate and seminoma are listed among blastic metastases
options_after: Lung is listed as the most common purely blastic osseous metastasis
Kidney and thyroid are listed under blastic rather than lytic osseous metastases
Transitional cell carcinoma is listed primarily as a purely lytic metastasis
Breast metastases may be lytic or blastic
Prostate and seminoma are listed among blastic metastases
updates.explanation: The source lists lung as the most common purely lytic metastasis and includes thyroid and kidney among lytic patterns. Breast may be lytic or blastic. Blastic metastases include breast, prostate, seminoma, transitional cell carcinoma, mucinous tumours, and carcinoid. Transitional cell carcinoma is therefore a blastic category in this source.

updates.question_text: Regarding temporal evolution of myositis ossificans, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Weeks 1?2 usually show mature peripheral compact bone
After more than 6 months it typically continues enlarging indefinitely
Mature myositis ossificans always remains non-ossified indefinitely
Weeks 3?4 may show amorphous osteoid matrix and can be most suggestive of early osteosarcoma
Weeks 5?8 show maturation of the periphery into compact bone
options_after: Weeks 1?2 usually show mature peripheral compact bone
After more than 6 months it typically continues enlarging indefinitely
Mature myositis ossificans characteristically remains non-ossified indefinitely
Weeks 3?4 may show amorphous osteoid matrix and can be most suggestive of early osteosarcoma
Weeks 5?8 show maturation of the periphery into compact bone
updates.explanation: The source gives staged evolution of myositis ossificans. Weeks 1?2 may show only a soft-tissue mass, not mature bone. Weeks 3?4 show amorphous osteoid matrix and may resemble early osteosarcoma. Weeks 5?8 show peripheral maturation into compact bone; ossification continues up to 6 months, after which the lesion typically decreases in size.

updates.question_text: Regarding brown tumour, osteomyelitis, and cortical desmoid as tumour mimics, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Renal osteodystrophy may show rugger jersey spine in secondary hyperparathyroidism
Osteomyelitis never mimics aggressive malignancy
Brown tumour is a benign lytic lesion in hyperparathyroidism caused by increased osteoclast activation
Associated hyperparathyroid features are usually absent, so isolated imaging morphology is specific
Cortical desmoid is a classic do-not-touch lesion at the posteromedial distal femoral metaphysis
options_after: Renal osteodystrophy may show rugger jersey spine in secondary hyperparathyroidism
Osteomyelitis will not mimic aggressive malignancy
Brown tumour is a benign lytic lesion in hyperparathyroidism caused by increased osteoclast activation
Associated hyperparathyroid features are usually absent, so isolated imaging morphology is specific
Cortical desmoid is a classic do-not-touch lesion at the posteromedial distal femoral metaphysis
updates.explanation: Brown tumour is a benign lytic lesion in hyperparathyroidism due to osteoclast activation, but it has no specific imaging features and may mimic giant cell tumour. Associated hyperparathyroid features such as osteopenia, subperiosteal resorption, and soft-tissue calcifications are usually present; renal failure may add rugger jersey spine. Cortical desmoid is a do-not-touch traction lesion at the posteromedial distal femoral metaphysis. Osteomyelitis can mimic aggressive malignancy.

updates.question_text: Regarding high-grade liposarcoma on MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It usually shows a purely fatty mass with no enhancement
It may show a large heterogeneously enhancing mass with central necrosis
The appearance can overlap with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, or leiomyosarcoma
Pleomorphic and dedifferentiated liposarcoma cannot usually be differentiated by imaging
Fatty elements must always be present regardless of differentiation
options_after: It usually shows a purely fatty mass without enhancement
It may show a large heterogeneously enhancing mass with central necrosis
The appearance can overlap with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, or leiomyosarcoma
Pleomorphic and dedifferentiated liposarcoma cannot usually be differentiated by imaging
Fatty elements must characteristically be present despite variation in differentiation
updates.explanation: High-grade liposarcoma typically appears as a large mass with heterogeneous enhancement and often central necrosis. The source states that pleomorphic and dedifferentiated liposarcoma cannot usually be differentiated by imaging and can be considered together radiologically. Its appearance overlaps with other high-grade sarcomas, and fatty components may be absent depending on differentiation. A purely fatty non-enhancing mass would not fit the described high-grade pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding superficial fibromatosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Plantar fibromatosis is also called Ledderhose disease
Plantar fibromatosis is usually treated primarily with craniospinal radiotherapy
All fibromatosis lesions must be uniformly low signal on MRI because they are fibrous
Palmar fibromatosis is less common than plantar fibromatosis
Symptomatic palmar fibromatosis is typically treated surgically
options_after: Plantar fibromatosis is also called Ledderhose disease
Plantar fibromatosis is usually treated primarily with craniospinal radiotherapy
Most fibromatosis lesions must be uniformly low signal on MRI because they are fibrous
Palmar fibromatosis is less common than plantar fibromatosis
Symptomatic palmar fibromatosis is typically treated surgically
updates.explanation: Superficial fibromatosis includes palmar and plantar forms. Plantar fibromatosis is Ledderhose disease and is less common than palmar fibromatosis, usually managed conservatively with footwear modification or intralesional steroid injection. Palmar fibromatosis, also called Dupuytren disease or contracture, is more common and symptomatic disease is typically surgical. MRI signal can vary, and lesions with increased cellularity may enhance more prominently.

updates.question_text: Regarding lesions where biopsy or further tissue diagnosis is emphasised in this batch, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Atypical features in an otherwise lipomatous mass can justify biopsy
Nodular fasciitis is often biopsied because it appears as an enhancing mass despite being benign
PET-CT can help determine need for biopsy in suspected malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour
A simple imaging-confirmed lipoma must always be biopsied before conservative management
Morton neuroma usually needs biopsy in the proper clinical context
options_after: Atypical features in an otherwise lipomatous mass can justify biopsy
Nodular fasciitis is often biopsied because it appears as an enhancing mass despite being benign
PET-CT can help determine need for biopsy in suspected malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour
A simple imaging-confirmed lipoma must characteristically be biopsied before conservative management
Morton neuroma usually needs biopsy in the proper clinical context
updates.explanation: The source supports biopsy for complex lipomatous features suggesting atypical lipomatous tumour and notes that nodular fasciitis is usually biopsied because it presents as an enhancing mass that can mimic sarcoma. PET-CT is described as excellent for determining need for biopsy in suspected malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour. Imaging-confirmed simple lipoma is usually not resected or biopsied unless atypical or symptomatic, and Morton neuroma usually does not need biopsy in the correct clinical setting.

updates.question_text: Regarding T2-hyperintense enhancing masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Synovial sarcoma should be ignored if it appears near fluid signal intensity because contrast is unnecessary
Myxoma tends to be near fluid signal with only faint or minimal enhancement
Myxofibrosarcoma can be predominantly T2 hyperintense due to myxoid components
A T2-hyperintense enhancing mass is always a benign neurogenic tumour if circumscribed
Myxoid liposarcoma may be T2 hyperintense with whorl-like internal architecture
options_after: Synovial sarcoma should be ignored if it appears near fluid signal intensity because contrast is unnecessary
Myxoma tends to be near fluid signal with only faint or minimal enhancement
Myxofibrosarcoma can be predominantly T2 hyperintense due to myxoid components
A T2-hyperintense enhancing mass is characteristically a benign neurogenic tumour if circumscribed
Myxoid liposarcoma may be T2 hyperintense with whorl-like internal architecture
updates.explanation: The source repeatedly uses T2 hyperintensity across different lesions, so the finding is not specific. Myxoma has near-fluid signal with minimal enhancement, myxofibrosarcoma is T2 hyperintense because of myxoid elements, and myxoid liposarcoma can have T2 hyperintensity with whorl-like architecture. A near-fluid signal mass in a younger patient that does not communicate with a joint should raise consideration of synovial sarcoma and prompt contrast rather than be ignored.

updates.question_text: Which statements correctly describe how this section approaches soft tissue tumour differential diagnosis?
options_before: A large aggressive soft tissue mass can be reasonably approached with high-grade sarcoma differentials rather than one precise MRI diagnosis
A small circumscribed T2-hyperintense mass excludes synovial sarcoma from the differential
All T2-hyperintense soft tissue tumours should be diagnosed as myxoma if they are circumscribed
Specific helpful imaging features can sometimes point to entities such as lipoma, Morton neuroma, elastofibroma dorsi, or fibrolipomatous hamartoma
The presence of a target sign excludes malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour
options_after: A large aggressive soft tissue mass can be reasonably approached with high-grade sarcoma differentials rather than one precise MRI diagnosis
A small circumscribed T2-hyperintense mass excludes synovial sarcoma from the differential
Most T2-hyperintense soft tissue tumours should be diagnosed as myxoma if they are circumscribed
Specific helpful imaging features can sometimes point to entities such as lipoma, Morton neuroma, elastofibroma dorsi, or fibrolipomatous hamartoma
The presence of a target sign excludes malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour
updates.explanation: The source explicitly recognises that many large aggressive soft tissue tumours overlap on imaging and lists a high-grade sarcoma differential rather than a single reliable MRI diagnosis. It also provides a separate list of helpful imaging features for entities such as lipoma, atypical lipomatous tumour, Morton neuroma, elastofibroma dorsi, neurogenic tumour, and fibrolipomatous hamartoma. A circumscribed T2-hyperintense mass can include synovial sarcoma in the differential, and a target sign does not exclude malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour.

updates.question_text: Regarding synovial fluid analysis in suspected septic arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A synovial fluid WBC count greater than 50,000 is 92% specific for septic arthritis in the source table
A WBC count greater than 100,000 is the most sensitive threshold listed
A PMN percentage of at least 90% is 99% specific for septic arthritis
Empiric treatment is reasonable for a WBC count greater than 50,000
Crystal arthropathy cannot elevate synovial fluid WBC count
options_after: A synovial fluid WBC count greater than 50,000 is 92% specific for septic arthritis in the source table
A WBC count greater than 100,000 is the most sensitive threshold listed
A PMN percentage of at least 90% is 99% specific for septic arthritis
Empiric treatment is reasonable for a WBC count greater than 50,000
Crystal arthropathy will not elevate synovial fluid WBC count
updates.explanation: The source table states that synovial fluid WBC greater than 50,000 is 92% specific for septic arthritis and is seen in 62% of septic arthritis cases. Empiric treatment is reasonable above this threshold. WBC greater than 100,000 is highly specific but much less sensitive, while PMN at least 90% is listed as 73% sensitive and 79% specific. Crystal arthropathy is a common alternative cause of elevated WBC count.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteomyelitis classification and chronicity, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Osteomyelitis can only be classified by organism and not by route of spread
Osteomyelitis may be classified by route of spread as haematogenous, contiguous spread, or direct inoculation
Any route of spread can lead to either acute or chronic disease
Acute osteomyelitis is generally defined in this source as lasting more than three months
The pathologic hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis is bone necrosis
options_after: Osteomyelitis can primarily be classified by organism and not by route of spread
Osteomyelitis may be classified by route of spread as haematogenous, contiguous spread, or direct inoculation
Any route of spread can lead to either acute or chronic disease
Acute osteomyelitis is generally defined in this source as lasting more than three months
The pathologic hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis is bone necrosis
updates.explanation: The source classifies osteomyelitis both by route of spread and by chronicity. Routes include haematogenous spread, contiguous spread, and direct inoculation, and any route can result in acute or chronic disease. Acute osteomyelitis is generally less than two weeks in duration, while subacute disease lasts less than three months without acute symptoms. Chronic osteomyelitis is defined pathologically by bone necrosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding the radiographic evolution of haematogenous osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The first radiographic finding is always a sharply marginated cortical sequestrum
Radiographic lucency never crosses the epiphysis in young children
Early subtle radiographic changes include focal soft tissue swelling, regional osteopenia, and obliteration of soft tissue fat planes
A focal ill-defined lucent metaphyseal lesion is the radiographic appearance of medullary infection
Lamellated periosteal reaction excludes Ewing sarcoma from the differential
options_after: The first radiographic finding is characteristically a sharply marginated cortical sequestrum
Radiographic lucency will not cross the epiphysis in young children
Early subtle radiographic changes include focal soft tissue swelling, regional osteopenia, and obliteration of soft tissue fat planes
A focal ill-defined lucent metaphyseal lesion is the radiographic appearance of medullary infection
Lamellated periosteal reaction excludes Ewing sarcoma from the differential
updates.explanation: The source lists focal soft tissue swelling, regional osteopenia, and obliteration of soft tissue fat planes as subtle early radiographic changes. Medullary infection appears as a focal ill-defined lucent metaphyseal lesion. In young children, the lucency may cross the epiphysis when bridging vessels remain patent. Aggressive or lamellated periosteal reaction may mimic Ewing sarcoma rather than exclude it.

updates.question_text: Regarding organisms and biopsy strategy in haematogenous osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Haematogenous osteomyelitis is typically polymicrobial in children
Staphylococcus aureus is the usual organism in children
Positive blood cultures never remove the need for biopsy
If blood cultures are positive, biopsy is generally not needed because the organism can be targeted
In adults, haematogenous osteomyelitis most commonly affects the spine
options_after: Haematogenous osteomyelitis is typically polymicrobial in children
Staphylococcus aureus is the usual organism in children
Positive blood cultures will not remove the need for biopsy
If blood cultures are positive, biopsy is generally not needed because the organism can be targeted
In adults, haematogenous osteomyelitis most commonly affects the spine
updates.explanation: In children, haematogenous osteomyelitis is more common and usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Haematogenous infection is typically caused by a single organism. If blood cultures are positive, the organism can be targeted and biopsy is generally not needed. In adults, haematogenous osteomyelitis most commonly affects the spine.

updates.question_text: Regarding chronic and sclerosing osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Chronic osteomyelitis is an indolent infection lasting more than 6 weeks
Chronic osteomyelitis always appears purely lytic with a thinned cortex
A sequestrum is devascularised necrotic bone surrounded by granulation tissue and involucrum
Active chronic osteomyelitis may show interval development of periosteal reaction on serial radiographs
Sclerosing osteomyelitis of Garré can mimic lymphoma, sclerotic metastasis, or osteoid osteoma
options_after: Chronic osteomyelitis is an indolent infection lasting more than 6 weeks
Chronic osteomyelitis characteristically appears purely lytic with a thinned cortex
A sequestrum is devascularised necrotic bone surrounded by granulation tissue and involucrum
Active chronic osteomyelitis may show interval development of periosteal reaction on serial radiographs
Sclerosing osteomyelitis of Garré can mimic lymphoma, sclerotic metastasis, or osteoid osteoma
updates.explanation: Chronic osteomyelitis is described as an indolent infection lasting more than 6 weeks, in which devascularised necrotic bone forms a sequestrum surrounded by granulation tissue and involucrum. It may produce a mixed lytic and sclerotic appearance with cortical thickening, not a purely lytic thinned cortex pattern. Serial radiographs can show new periosteal reaction in active chronic disease. Sclerosing osteomyelitis of Garré is an uncommon chronic form with sclerosis and bone thickening, with lymphoma, sclerotic metastasis, and osteoid osteoma in the differential.

updates.question_text: Regarding three-phase Tc-99m MDP bone scan in suspected osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It becomes positive within 24–48 hours after onset of symptoms
Acute osteomyelitis is positive only on delayed images and negative on flow and blood pool
Acute osteomyelitis is positive on flow, blood pool, and delayed phases
Cellulitis is positive on flow and blood pool phases but negative on delayed images
A positive delayed phase alone is the specific definition of cellulitis in the source
options_after: It becomes positive within 24–48 hours after onset of symptoms
Acute osteomyelitis is positive primarily on delayed images and negative on flow and blood pool
Acute osteomyelitis is positive on flow, blood pool, and delayed phases
Cellulitis is positive on flow and blood pool phases but negative on delayed images
A positive delayed phase alone is the specific definition of cellulitis in the source
updates.explanation: The source states that three-phase Tc-99m MDP bone scan becomes positive within 24–48 hours after symptom onset. Acute osteomyelitis is positive on all three phases: flow, blood pool, and delayed. Cellulitis is positive on flow and blood pool phases but negative on delayed imaging. A delayed-only definition of cellulitis is therefore incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI diagnosis of osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The hallmark is replacement of normal fatty marrow signal with low T1 and high T2 signal from oedema and exudate
Abnormal fluid-sensitive signal alone is sufficient to confidently diagnose osteomyelitis
A negative MRI has low negative predictive value and cannot exclude osteomyelitis
Confluent intramedullary T1 signal change is strongly associated with osteomyelitis, especially with an adjacent ulcer
Hazy reticular and subcortical T1 patterns cannot reliably diagnose osteomyelitis
options_after: The hallmark is replacement of normal fatty marrow signal with low T1 and high T2 signal from oedema and exudate
Abnormal fluid-sensitive signal alone is sufficient to confidently diagnose osteomyelitis
A negative MRI has low negative predictive value and will not exclude osteomyelitis
Confluent intramedullary T1 signal change is strongly associated with osteomyelitis, especially with an adjacent ulcer
Hazy reticular and subcortical T1 patterns cannot reliably diagnose osteomyelitis
updates.explanation: MRI diagnosis depends on replacement of normal fatty marrow signal, with high T2 signal and low T1 signal from oedema and exudate. The source cautions that abnormal fluid-sensitive signal alone does not prove osteomyelitis, so T1-weighted images should be scrutinised. Confluent intramedullary T1 signal change is strongly associated with osteomyelitis, particularly next to an ulcer. Hazy reticular and subcortical T1 changes cannot reliably diagnose osteomyelitis, and a negative MRI essentially excludes it.

updates.question_text: Which statement about gadolinium in MRI evaluation of osteomyelitis is correct?
options_before: Gadolinium is mandatory to confidently diagnose osteomyelitis in all cases
Gadolinium replaces the need to inspect T1-weighted marrow signal
Gadolinium is helpful to delineate fluid collections and evaluate for nonenhancing necrotic bone
Gadolinium is primarily used to distinguish cellulitis from acute osteomyelitis on a three-phase bone scan
Gadolinium is contraindicated whenever sinus tracts are present
options_after: Gadolinium is mandatory to confidently diagnose osteomyelitis in more than 90% of cases
Gadolinium replaces the need to inspect T1-weighted marrow signal
Gadolinium is helpful to delineate fluid collections and evaluate for nonenhancing necrotic bone
Gadolinium is primarily used to distinguish cellulitis from acute osteomyelitis on a three-phase bone scan
Gadolinium is contraindicated whenever sinus tracts are present
updates.explanation: The source states that gadolinium is helpful to delineate fluid collections and to evaluate for nonenhancing necrotic bone, or sequestrum. It is not necessary to confidently diagnose osteomyelitis. T1-weighted marrow pattern remains important, and gadolinium is an MRI contrast agent rather than part of a three-phase bone scan interpretation.

updates.question_text: Regarding routes of spread in osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Haematogenous osteomyelitis begins in the medullary cavity and spreads outward through cortex and periosteum
Contiguous focus osteomyelitis begins in the medullary canal and always spreads to skin last
Contiguous focus osteomyelitis penetrates periosteum and cortex before subsequent medullary invasion
Direct inoculation cannot produce chronic osteomyelitis
Diabetic foot infection is a common adult example of contiguous spread
options_after: Haematogenous osteomyelitis begins in the medullary cavity and spreads outward through cortex and periosteum
Contiguous focus osteomyelitis begins in the medullary canal and characteristically spreads to skin last
Contiguous focus osteomyelitis penetrates periosteum and cortex before subsequent medullary invasion
Direct inoculation will not produce chronic osteomyelitis
Diabetic foot infection is a common adult example of contiguous spread
updates.explanation: The source contrasts inside-out haematogenous spread with outside-in contiguous focus infection. Haematogenous osteomyelitis begins in the medullary cavity and then spreads through cortex, periosteum, and soft tissues. Contiguous focus osteomyelitis begins from adjacent soft tissue infection and penetrates periosteum and cortex before medullary invasion. Diabetic foot infection is a common adult example, and any route of spread can lead to acute or chronic disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding complications and advanced features of chronic osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A sequestrum is expected to resolve without treatment because it is viable bone
A sequestrum can chronically harbour living organisms and act as a nidus for recurrent infection if not resected
Cloacae are abscesses confined entirely to articular cartilage
Chronic drainage of a sinus tract predisposes to squamous cell carcinoma
A sinus tract is only seen in cellulitis and is not related to osteomyelitis
options_after: A sequestrum is expected to resolve without treatment because it is viable bone
A sequestrum can chronically harbour living organisms and act as a nidus for recurrent infection if not resected
Cloacae are abscesses confined predominantly to articular cartilage
Chronic drainage of a sinus tract predisposes to squamous cell carcinoma
A sinus tract is primarily seen in cellulitis and is not related to osteomyelitis
updates.explanation: A sequestrum is devitalised necrotic bone separated from viable bone, and the source stresses that it is a surgical lesion because it can harbour organisms and act as a recurrent infection nidus if not resected. The involucrum may be perforated by cloacae, which can open to the skin as sinus tracts. Chronic sinus tract drainage predisposes to squamous cell carcinoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding juvenile Paget disease and osteopetrosis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hereditary hyperphosphatasia is an adult-only acquired disorder limited to the skull
Juvenile Paget disease affects infants and young children with diffuse bone involvement and severe deformity
Osteopetrosis is due to excess osteoclast resorption causing diffuse osteopenia
Osteopetrosis causes diffuse marked skeletal sclerosis but brittle bones with multiple fractures
Juvenile Paget disease is limited to the skull and never resembles adult Paget disease radiographically
options_after: Hereditary hyperphosphatasia is an adult-predominant acquired disorder limited to the skull
Juvenile Paget disease affects infants and young children with diffuse bone involvement and severe deformity
Osteopetrosis is due to excess osteoclast resorption causing diffuse osteopenia
Osteopetrosis causes diffuse marked skeletal sclerosis but brittle bones with multiple fractures
Juvenile Paget disease is limited to the skull and will not resemble adult Paget disease radiographically
updates.explanation: Hereditary hyperphosphatasia, or juvenile Paget disease, is autosomal recessive and affects infants/young children with diffuse cortical thickening, trabecular thickening, osteopenia, bowing, and severe deformity. It can appear radiographically similar to adult Paget disease apart from age and diffuse involvement, with possible epiphyseal sparing. Osteopetrosis is an extremely rare deficiency of osteoclastic carbonic anhydrase that prevents bone resorption, causing diffuse marked sclerosis and brittle bones with multiple fractures.

updates.question_text: Regarding myelofibrosis and mastocytosis on CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Myelofibrosis is progressive marrow fibrosis in older patients with anaemia and splenomegaly
Bone marrow fibrosis can lead to diffusely sclerotic bones
Mastocytosis may result in diffuse or patchy sclerosis from marrow reaction to infiltrating mast cells
Mastocytosis always produces purely lytic lesions without sclerosis
Myelofibrosis is defined by short fourth metacarpals and basal ganglia calcification
options_after: Myelofibrosis is progressive marrow fibrosis in older patients with anaemia and splenomegaly
Bone marrow fibrosis can lead to diffusely sclerotic bones
Mastocytosis may result in diffuse or patchy sclerosis from marrow reaction to infiltrating mast cells
Mastocytosis characteristically produces purely lytic lesions without sclerosis
Myelofibrosis is defined by short fourth metacarpals and basal ganglia calcification
updates.explanation: Myelofibrosis is progressive fibrosis of marrow in older patients, causing anaemia and splenomegaly, and the marrow fibrosis can make bones diffusely sclerotic. Mastocytosis is abnormal mast-cell proliferation and can produce either diffuse or patchy sclerosis from marrow reaction. Short fourth metacarpals and basal ganglia calcification belong to parathyroid disorders, not myelofibrosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding long-bone fracture description, which elements should be included according to the source?
options_before: Fracture location, such as proximal, mid-shaft, or distal
Direction of the fracture
Angulation of the distal segment
Position of the proximal segment only, while the distal segment is ignored
Whether the fracture extends to the articular surface
options_after: Fracture location, such as proximal, mid-shaft, or distal
Direction of the fracture
Angulation of the distal segment
Position of the proximal segment primarily, while the distal segment is ignored
Whether the fracture extends to the articular surface
updates.explanation: For long-bone fracture reporting, the source says to describe location, fracture direction, angulation, and position of the distal segment. It is also essential to mention articular surface extension. The reporting convention is based on the distal fragment, not ignoring it in favour of the proximal segment. A comminuted fracture is defined as more than two fragments.

updates.question_text: Regarding atraumatic fracture terminology, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A fatigue fracture is abnormal stress on normal bone
An insufficiency fracture is normal stress on abnormal bone
A pathologic fracture is a fracture through a focal lesion, most commonly a neoplasm
An atypical fracture only occurs in the medial cortex of the distal tibia
Fragility fractures are traumatic fractures in elderly osteoporotic patients caused by low-velocity mechanisms
options_after: A fatigue fracture is abnormal stress on normal bone
An insufficiency fracture is normal stress on abnormal bone
A pathologic fracture is a fracture through a focal lesion, most commonly a neoplasm
An atypical fracture primarily occurs in the medial cortex of the distal tibia
Fragility fractures are traumatic fractures in elderly osteoporotic patients caused by low-velocity mechanisms
updates.explanation: Fatigue fracture is repetitive submaximal force on normal bone, while insufficiency fracture is normal stress on abnormal bone, most commonly osteoporosis. Pathologic fracture occurs through a focal lesion, usually neoplasm and less commonly osteomyelitis. Fragility fractures are low-velocity traumatic fractures in elderly patients with osteoporosis and often sarcopenia. Atypical fracture is a special type of insufficiency fracture occurring in the lateral cortex of the proximal-to-mid femur, not the medial distal tibia.

updates.question_text: Regarding tendon degeneration and tearing on MRI, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Myxoid degeneration is an inflammatory tendon process, so tendinitis is the preferred term
The term tendinitis should be avoided because myxoid degeneration is not due to inflammation
MRI shows only low signal on both T1- and T2-weighted images when myxoid degeneration is present
MRI can always distinguish myxoid degeneration from partial tendon tear
A full-thickness, full-width tear appears as complete tendon discontinuity, often with retraction
options_after: Myxoid degeneration is an inflammatory tendon process, so tendinitis is the preferred term
The term tendinitis should be avoided because myxoid degeneration is not due to inflammation
MRI shows primarily low signal on both T1- and T2-weighted images when myxoid degeneration is present
MRI can characteristically distinguish myxoid degeneration from partial tendon tear
A full-thickness, full-width tear appears as complete tendon discontinuity, often with retraction
updates.explanation: The source states that ageing or overuse causes myxoid degeneration, clinically used interchangeably with tendinopathy and tendinosis, but the word tendinitis should not be used because the process is not inflammatory. MRI can show intermediate intratendinous signal on T1- and T2-weighted images and the tendon may be normal or enlarged. These features can be seen in both myxoid degeneration and partial tear, which often coexist and cannot be reliably distinguished by imaging. A full-thickness, full-width tear appears as complete discontinuity with frequent tendon retraction.

updates.question_text: Regarding Jones fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They occur at the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction of the fifth metatarsal
They have a better prognosis than avulsion fractures because the blood supply is increased at this location
They may require surgery
They are identical to zone 1 avulsion fractures at the most proximal metatarsal base
Their worse prognosis is related to reduced blood supply at the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction
options_after: They occur at the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction of the fifth metatarsal
They have a better prognosis than avulsion fractures because the blood supply is increased at this location
They may require surgery
They are closely comparable to zone 1 avulsion fractures at the most proximal metatarsal base
Their worse prognosis is related to reduced blood supply at the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction
updates.explanation: Jones fractures are zone 2 fractures at the fifth metatarsal metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction. They have a worse prognosis than avulsion fractures because of reduced blood supply at this junction, and treatment is variable with possible surgery. Zone 1 avulsion fractures occur at the most proximal base and are treated conservatively.

updates.question_text: Regarding metatarsal stress fracture imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The first radiographic sign is always a large displaced transverse fracture
Stress fractures are usually obvious on initial radiographs before any periostitis forms
The first radiographic sign may be a barely perceptible linear cortical lucency
Stress fractures may not become apparent radiographically until periostitis and callus form
MRI may show a fracture line with marrow oedema and periosteal oedema
options_after: The first radiographic sign is characteristically a large displaced transverse fracture
Stress fractures are usually obvious on initial radiographs before any periostitis forms
The first radiographic sign may be a barely perceptible linear cortical lucency
Stress fractures may not become apparent radiographically until periostitis and callus form
MRI may show a fracture line with marrow oedema and periosteal oedema
updates.explanation: The source emphasises that metatarsal stress fractures may be very subtle initially. The first radiographic sign may be a barely perceptible linear cortical lucency, and many stress fractures are not apparent until periostitis and callus form. MRI can show the fracture line, intramedullary oedema, periosteal oedema, and callus. A large displaced fracture is not the expected first sign.

updates.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes a bipartite hallux sesamoid from an acute sesamoid fracture?
options_before: A bipartite sesamoid has distracted fragments with non-corticated margins and surrounding oedema
A bipartite sesamoid is always smaller than the opposite sesamoid when the parts are summed
A sesamoid fracture has round fully corticated margins without oedema
A bipartite sesamoid is round, completely corticated, and the sum of the parts is larger than the other sesamoid
A bipartite sesamoid is diagnosed by fluid undercutting the talar dome
options_after: A bipartite sesamoid has distracted fragments with non-corticated margins and surrounding oedema
A bipartite sesamoid is characteristically smaller than the opposite sesamoid when the parts are summed
A sesamoid fracture has round fully corticated margins without oedema
A bipartite sesamoid is round, completely corticated, and the sum of the parts is larger than the other sesamoid
A bipartite sesamoid is diagnosed by fluid undercutting the talar dome
updates.explanation: The source states that a bipartite sesamoid is a normal variant that may mimic fracture. It is round, has completely corticated margins, and the summed parts are larger than the other sesamoid. In the illustrated acute sesamoid fracture, MRI shows absence of cortication at the fracture margins, distraction, capsular tear, and surrounding oedema.

updates.question_text: Regarding Lisfranc fracture-dislocation patterns and management, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lisfranc fracture-dislocation is a fracture-dislocation of the tarsometatarsal joint
Treatment is conservative because untreated Lisfranc injuries rarely cause long-term morbidity
Missed Lisfranc injury has no important long-term consequence because the longitudinal arch is preserved
In homolateral injury, all metatarsals dislocate medially
In divergent injury, the first metatarsal dislocates medially while the second through fifth metatarsals dislocate laterally
options_after: Lisfranc fracture-dislocation is a fracture-dislocation of the tarsometatarsal joint
Treatment is conservative because untreated Lisfranc injuries rarely cause long-term morbidity
Preservation of the longitudinal arch makes delayed treatment of a Lisfranc injury clinically acceptable.
In homolateral injury, most metatarsals dislocate medially
In divergent injury, the first metatarsal dislocates medially while the second through fifth metatarsals dislocate laterally
updates.explanation: Lisfranc fracture-dislocation involves the tarsometatarsal joint and is treated surgically. Missed or untreated injury can cause debilitating osteoarthritis and flattening of the longitudinal arch. The source classifies injuries by first metatarsal direction: divergent injury has medial first metatarsal dislocation with lateral dislocation of the second through fifth metatarsals, while homolateral injury has all metatarsals dislocating laterally.

updates.question_text: Regarding talar fractures and Hawkins sign, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Talar fractures are classified only as calcaneonavicular or talocalcaneal injuries
Talar neck fractures are classified by the Hawkins classification
Talar neck fracture may disrupt blood supply to the talus and predispose to osteonecrosis
Hawkins sign is a subchondral lucent band seen 6-8 weeks after ankle immobilisation and implies intact talar dome blood supply
The presence of Hawkins sign is a poor prognostic indicator
options_after: Talar fractures are classified primarily as calcaneonavicular or talocalcaneal injuries
Talar neck fractures are classified by the Hawkins classification
Talar neck fracture may disrupt blood supply to the talus and predispose to osteonecrosis
Hawkins sign is a subchondral lucent band seen 6-8 weeks after ankle immobilisation and implies intact talar dome blood supply
The presence of Hawkins sign is a poor prognostic indicator
updates.explanation: Talar fractures are divided anatomically into lateral process, posterior process, head, body, and neck fractures, and talar neck fractures are classified by Hawkins classification. Calcaneonavicular and talocalcaneal are hindfoot coalition types rather than talar fracture categories. A talar neck fracture may disrupt talar blood supply and predispose to osteonecrosis. Hawkins sign is a subchondral lucent band 6-8 weeks after immobilisation and is a good prognostic sign.

updates.question_text: Regarding osteochondral lesion of the talus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The term describes abnormalities of cartilage, subchondral bone plate, and subchondral bone
It represents only congenital coalition and not either chronic repetitive microtrauma or acute trauma
Radiographs usually show a normal talar dome without crescentic lucency
Fluid undercutting the lesion or cystic change deep to the lesion indicates stability
MRI assessment is similar to knee osteochondral lesion imaging
options_after: The term describes abnormalities of cartilage, subchondral bone plate, and subchondral bone
It represents primarily congenital coalition and not either chronic repetitive microtrauma or acute trauma
Radiographs usually show a normal talar dome without crescentic lucency
Fluid undercutting the lesion or cystic change deep to the lesion indicates stability
MRI assessment is similar to knee osteochondral lesion imaging
updates.explanation: Osteochondral lesion is a broad term covering cartilage, subchondral bone plate, and subchondral bone abnormalities. In the talus, it can describe chronic repetitive microtrauma/osteochondritis dissecans or an acute traumatic osteochondral defect, and radiographs may show a crescentic lucency. MRI is similar to knee osteochondral lesion imaging. Fluid undercutting or cystic change deep to the lesion indicates instability, not stability.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging triage after selected foot and hindfoot injuries, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Weight-bearing radiographs improve sensitivity for subtle Lisfranc malalignment
CT may show the true extent of Chopart fracture-dislocation
Traumatic calcaneal fracture should prompt consideration of further lumbar spine and/or abdominal imaging
MRI can clarify acute sesamoid fracture when radiographs cannot distinguish it from bipartite sesamoid
Initial radiographs always exclude metatarsal stress fracture when normal
options_after: Weight-bearing radiographs improve sensitivity for subtle Lisfranc malalignment
CT may show the true extent of Chopart fracture-dislocation
Traumatic calcaneal fracture should prompt consideration of further lumbar spine and/or abdominal imaging
MRI can clarify acute sesamoid fracture when radiographs cannot distinguish it from bipartite sesamoid
Initial radiographs characteristically exclude metatarsal stress fracture when normal
updates.explanation: The source repeatedly uses modality choice to avoid missing clinically important injuries.
