updates.question_text: Which statement about facet effusion and management implications is supported by the source?
options_before: Facet effusion proves that decompression alone is always optimal.
Facet effusion means facet arthropathy cannot be symptomatic.
Facet effusion excludes the need to assess flexion-extension motion.
Facet effusion is unrelated to surgical planning.
Facet effusion is associated with spinal instability, and fusion may be optimal if decompression is performed in the setting of instability.
options_after: Facet effusion proves that decompression alone is characteristically optimal.
Facet effusion means facet arthropathy will not be symptomatic.
Facet effusion excludes the need to assess flexion-extension motion.
Facet effusion is unrelated to surgical planning.
Facet effusion is associated with spinal instability, and fusion may be optimal if decompression is performed in the setting of instability.
updates.explanation: The source links facet effusion with spinal instability. If decompression is performed when instability is present, instrumented fusion is typically the optimal treatment. Active facet arthropathy may also be treated with pain interventions including intra-articular steroid injection, medial branch block and radiofrequency ablation.

updates.question_text: Regarding the conceptual approach to spine infection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diabetes, drug abuse and prior spinal surgery increase the risk of spine infection.
The source advises treating all spine infections as isolated disc disease only.
The adult intervertebral disc is directly vascularised and is usually the initial nidus of haematogenous infection.
Useful compartments include the retroperitoneum/psoas, disc-endplate complex, epidural space and facet joints.
Infection may originate in one compartment and spread to adjacent compartments.
options_after: Diabetes, drug abuse and prior spinal surgery increase the risk of spine infection.
The source advises treating most spine infections as isolated disc disease in typical cases.
The adult intervertebral disc is directly vascularised and is usually the initial nidus of haematogenous infection.
Useful compartments include the retroperitoneum/psoas, disc-endplate complex, epidural space and facet joints.
Infection may originate in one compartment and spread to adjacent compartments.
updates.explanation: The source frames spine infection by anatomical compartments, including psoas/retroperitoneum, disc-endplate complex, epidural space and facet joints. Infection may begin in any of these and spread contiguously. Diabetes, drug abuse and prior surgery are listed risk factors. In adults, haematogenous infection begins in the endplate rather than a directly vascularised disc.

updates.question_text: Regarding adult discitis/osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most common aetiology is direct traumatic inoculation into the disc.
Haematogenous spread is the most common aetiology.
The adult disc is directly vascularised and is usually infected before the endplate.
A single segmental artery can supply only one endplate, preventing spread across a disc space.
Infection starts in the endplate and can spread to the adjacent vertebral body through the disc.
options_after: The most common aetiology is direct traumatic inoculation into the disc.
Haematogenous spread is the most common aetiology.
The adult disc is directly vascularised and is usually infected before the endplate.
A single segmental artery can supply a single endplate, preventing spread across a disc space.
Infection starts in the endplate and can spread to the adjacent vertebral body through the disc.
updates.explanation: Haematogenous spread is the common pathway in adult discitis/osteomyelitis. The adult disc is not vascularised, but the endplates are supplied by end-capillary branches of segmental lumbar arteries. Infection begins in an endplate and may then spread to the adjacent vertebral body through the disc.

updates.question_text: Regarding facet septic arthritis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the commonest form of degenerative facet disease.
It should be considered when periarticular inflammatory change is out of proportion to relatively mild degeneration.
It is excluded if there is no visible facet joint effusion.
STIR can make posterior periarticular oedema more conspicuous than non-fat-suppressed T2-weighted imaging.
It is characterised by anterior vertebral body wedge collapse and disc sparing.
options_after: It is the commonest form of degenerative facet disease.
It should be considered when periarticular inflammatory change is out of proportion to relatively mild degeneration.
It is excluded if there is an absence of visible facet joint effusion.
STIR can make posterior periarticular oedema more conspicuous than non-fat-suppressed T2-weighted imaging.
It is characterised by anterior vertebral body wedge collapse and disc sparing.
updates.explanation: Facet septic arthritis is uncommon but should be suspected when inflammatory change is greater than expected for the degree of degenerative change. STIR improves conspicuity of oedema because fat and fluid can look similar on non-fat-suppressed T2-weighted images. The example shows capsular distension even without an obvious facet effusion.

updates.question_text: Regarding tuberculous vertebral osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is pyogenic infection in which the disc is usually the first structure destroyed.
It is also called Pott disease.
The discs are usually spared because Mycobacterium tuberculosis lacks proteolytic enzymes to break down disc substance.
It classically causes wedge-shaped anterior vertebral body compression with possible gibbus deformity.
Active pulmonary tuberculosis is present in nearly all patients with Pott disease.
options_after: It is pyogenic infection in which the disc is usually the first structure destroyed.
It is also called Pott disease.
The discs are usually spared because Mycobacterium tuberculosis lacks proteolytic enzymes to break down disc substance.
It classically causes wedge-shaped anterior vertebral body compression with possible gibbus deformity.
Active pulmonary tuberculosis is present in the large majority of patients with Pott disease.
updates.explanation: Tuberculous osteomyelitis is Pott disease. Unlike pyogenic discitis/osteomyelitis, the disc is usually spared because the organism lacks proteolytic enzymes to break down disc material. It classically produces wedge-shaped anterior compression and a gibbus deformity. The source states that approximately 10% have active pulmonary tuberculosis.

updates.question_text: Sagittal T1-weighted MR images show varying degrees of narrowing around the exiting nerve root. Which of the following statements are correct regarding neural foraminal stenosis?
options_before: Sagittal T1-weighted images are the best sequence for assessing the neural foramina.
Mild stenosis is complete effacement of epidural fat around the exiting root.
Moderate stenosis is defined only by anterior-posterior root contact without fat effacement.
A normal foramen contains no epidural fat.
Severe stenosis includes complete epidural fat effacement or nerve-root compression.
options_after: Sagittal T1-weighted images are the best sequence for assessing the neural foramina.
Mild stenosis is complete effacement of epidural fat around the exiting root.
Moderate stenosis is defined primarily by anterior-posterior root contact without fat effacement.
A normal foramen lacks epidural fat.
Severe stenosis includes complete epidural fat effacement or nerve-root compression.
updates.explanation: The foramina are best evaluated on sagittal T1-weighted images because epidural fat outlines the exiting root. Severe stenosis is complete loss of epidural fat or compression of the nerve root. Mild disease involves contact with preserved fat, while moderate disease includes contact on multiple sides with partial fat effacement.

updates.question_text: Axial T2-weighted MR images demonstrate examples of facet arthropathy. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Mild disease may show mild subchondral irregularity and tiny subchondral cysts.
Facet arthropathy cannot contribute to lateral recess stenosis.
Facet effusion proves that the facet joint is infected rather than degenerative.
Severe disease may show large osteophytes with mass effect on the spinal canal.
Secondary signs of active disease include effusion, reactive osseous oedema and reactive soft-tissue oedema.
options_after: Mild disease may show mild subchondral irregularity and tiny subchondral cysts.
Facet arthropathy will not contribute to lateral recess stenosis.
Facet effusion proves that the facet joint is infected rather than degenerative.
Severe disease may show large osteophytes with mass effect on the spinal canal.
Secondary signs of active disease include effusion, reactive osseous oedema and reactive soft-tissue oedema.
updates.explanation: Mild facet arthropathy may show small osteophytes, mild irregularity and tiny cysts. Severe disease can show bulky osteophytes and mass effect on the canal. Effusion and oedema are signs of active facet arthropathy, but the source does not treat effusion alone as proof of infection. Facet disease may contribute to spinal, foraminal or lateral recess stenosis.

updates.question_text: Axial T2 and sagittal STIR images show prominent posterior periarticular oedema around a facet joint. Which statement is supported by the source?
options_before: Facet septic arthritis is common and should be assumed in all facet arthropathy.
A visible intra-articular effusion is mandatory for facet septic arthritis.
T2-weighted imaging without fat suppression is more sensitive than STIR for oedema in this example.
Facet septic arthritis should be considered when periarticular inflammatory change is out of proportion to mild degeneration.
Facet septic arthritis is the same process as OPLL.
options_after: Facet septic arthritis is common and should be assumed in most facet arthropathy.
A visible intra-articular effusion is mandatory for facet septic arthritis.
T2-weighted imaging without fat suppression is more sensitive than STIR for oedema in this example.
Facet septic arthritis should be considered when periarticular inflammatory change is out of proportion to mild degeneration.
Facet septic arthritis is the same process as OPLL.
updates.explanation: The source states that facet septic arthritis is uncommon but should be considered when periarticular inflammation is disproportionate to only mild degeneration. The illustrated case has conspicuous STIR oedema and capsular distension even without an obvious facet joint effusion. Active degenerative facet arthropathy remains the more common mimic.

updates.question_text: Regarding the spread and compartmental anatomy of spine infection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The psoas/retroperitoneum, disc-endplate complex, epidural space and facet joints are useful compartments to consider.
In adults, haematogenous infection starts in the endplate because the disc is not vascularised.
In children, the disc is directly vascularised and can be the nidus for infection.
A single adult segmental endplate artery always infects both endplates simultaneously.
Infection may originate in one compartment and spread to adjacent compartments.
options_after: The psoas/retroperitoneum, disc-endplate complex, epidural space and facet joints are useful compartments to consider.
In adults, haematogenous infection starts in the endplate because the disc is not vascularised.
In children, the disc is directly vascularised and can be the nidus for infection.
A single adult segmental endplate artery characteristically infects both endplates simultaneously.
Infection may originate in one compartment and spread to adjacent compartments.
updates.explanation: The source recommends thinking anatomically in compartments: retroperitoneum/psoas, disc and vertebral bodies, epidural space and facet joints. Infection may begin in any of these and spread to adjacent compartments. In adults the disc is not vascularised, so haematogenous infection begins in the endplate; in children the disc is directly vascularised and can be the nidus.

updates.question_text: Regarding a unilateral lucent or absent-appearing pedicle, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A lytic lesion such as metastasis, osteoblastoma or aneurysmal bone cyst may be present.
The finding always represents congenital absence of the pedicle without need for cross-sectional imaging.
It is the expected radiographic appearance of a stable anterior compression fracture.
Cross-sectional imaging may show a pedicle-centred mass extending into the spinal canal.
It is a classic sign of epidural lipomatosis.
options_after: A lytic lesion such as metastasis, osteoblastoma or aneurysmal bone cyst may be present.
The finding characteristically represents congenital absence of the pedicle without need for cross-sectional imaging.
It is the expected radiographic appearance of a stable anterior compression fracture.
Cross-sectional imaging may show a pedicle-centred mass extending into the spinal canal.
It is a classic sign of epidural lipomatosis.
updates.explanation: A lucent pedicle with a normal contralateral pedicle should raise concern for a lytic lesion, including metastasis, osteoblastoma or aneurysmal bone cyst. The illustrated example shows a pedicle-centred lytic mass extending into the canal with near complete canal obliteration. Congenital absence is a rarer alternative pattern when one pedicle is lucent and the contralateral pedicle is sclerotic from stress-related change.

updates.question_text: Regarding the Denis three-column concept in spine trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It helps classify injury severity by assessing involvement of anterior, middle and posterior columns.
Injury limited to one column is generally unstable.
Involvement of two or more columns is generally unstable.
A burst fracture involves failure of the posterior column only.
The posterior vertebral cortex and posterior disc are part of the middle column.
options_after: It helps classify injury severity by assessing involvement of anterior, middle and posterior columns.
Injury limited to one column is generally unstable.
Involvement of two or more columns is generally unstable.
A burst fracture involves failure of the posterior column in typical cases.
The posterior vertebral cortex and posterior disc are part of the middle column.
updates.explanation: The Denis model remains useful for conceptualising stability. Single-column injuries are generally stable, while two-column or three-column injuries are unstable. A burst fracture fails the anterior and middle columns. The key point in the source is that the posterior vertebral cortex and posterior disc belong to the middle column.

updates.question_text: Regarding the subaxial injury classification and severity scale, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It scores only the osseous fracture morphology and excludes neurological status.
It includes injury morphology as one component.
It replaces the need to assess the discoligamentous complex.
It includes disruption of the discoligamentous complex.
Injuries with greater than 4 points are usually treated surgically.
options_after: It scores primarily the osseous fracture morphology and excludes neurological status.
It includes injury morphology as one component.
It replaces the need to assess the discoligamentous complex.
It includes disruption of the discoligamentous complex.
Injuries with greater than 4 points are usually treated surgically.
updates.explanation: SLICS gives points for injury morphology, disruption of the discoligamentous complex and neurological status. It is used to guide management, with injuries scoring greater than 4 points usually managed surgically. The source notes that detailed memorisation is not necessary, but the framework is well established.

updates.question_text: Regarding occipital condyle fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Type I is a stable nondisplaced comminuted impaction fracture from axial loading.
Type II is an avulsion fracture at the alar ligament attachment and is the most common unstable type.
Type III is an unstable distraction injury resulting in an avulsion fracture at the alar ligament attachment.
MRI is irrelevant because stability is based only on bone displacement.
Type III is the least common fracture type.
options_after: Type I is a stable nondisplaced comminuted impaction fracture from axial loading.
Type II is an avulsion fracture at the alar ligament attachment and is the most common unstable type.
Type III is an unstable distraction injury resulting in an avulsion fracture at the alar ligament attachment.
MRI is irrelevant because stability is based primarily on bone displacement.
Type III is the least common fracture type.
updates.explanation: Type I is a stable nondisplaced comminuted impaction fracture due to axial loading. Type II is a stable linear skull fracture extending into the condyle. Type III is an unstable distraction avulsion injury at the alar ligament attachment and is described as the most common type. MRI helps assess stability and ligament integrity.

updates.question_text: Regarding Jefferson fracture, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is caused by forced flexion producing a displaced spinous process avulsion.
It results from an acute axial blow to the vertex of the head.
It causes symmetrical fractures of the anterior and posterior arches of C1.
It is best assessed using only flexion-extension radiographs.
Open-mouth odontoid radiographs can show lateral displacement of the C1 lateral masses.
options_after: It is caused by forced flexion producing a displaced spinous process avulsion.
It results from an acute axial blow to the vertex of the head.
It causes symmetrical fractures of the anterior and posterior arches of C1.
It is best assessed using primarily flexion-extension radiographs.
Open-mouth odontoid radiographs can show lateral displacement of the C1 lateral masses.
updates.explanation: Jefferson fracture is an axial-loading injury of C1 that causes symmetrical fractures of the anterior and posterior arches. On an open-mouth odontoid radiograph, the C1 lateral masses are displaced laterally. The source states that the injury is best seen on axial CT.

updates.question_text: Regarding odontoid fractures, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Type I odontoid fracture involves the distal tip of the dens and is generally treated conservatively.
Type II fracture extends into the C2 vertebral body and is always stable.
Os odontoideum is a normal variant secondary ossification centre located at the base of the dens.
Type III fracture extends from the dens base into the C2 vertebral body.
Odontoid fractures are usually caused by flexion injuries.
options_after: Type I odontoid fracture involves the distal tip of the dens and is generally treated conservatively.
Type II fracture extends into the C2 vertebral body and is characteristically stable.
Os odontoideum is a normal variant secondary ossification centre located at the base of the dens.
Type III fracture extends from the dens base into the C2 vertebral body.
Odontoid fractures are usually caused by flexion injuries.
updates.explanation: Type I fracture affects the distal tip of the dens and is considered stable with conservative treatment. Type II is a base-of-dens fracture and is unstable, while type III extends into the C2 body and has variable stability in the literature. The differential for type I is os odontoideum, located at the tip of the dens, and odontoid fractures are usually due to flexion.

updates.question_text: Regarding thoracolumbar injury classification and posterior ligamentous complex injury, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: TLICS uses injury morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and neurological status.
The posterior ligamentous complex is a primary stabiliser of the posterior spinal column.
TLICS scores only osseous morphology and excludes neurological status.
Indirect imaging signs of posterior ligamentous complex injury include widening of the interspinous distance and widening of the facet joints.
Spinous process fracture and vertebral body subluxation or dislocation can be indirect signs of posterior ligamentous complex injury.
options_after: TLICS uses injury morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and neurological status.
The posterior ligamentous complex is a primary stabiliser of the posterior spinal column.
TLICS scores primarily osseous morphology and excludes neurological status.
Indirect imaging signs of posterior ligamentous complex injury include widening of the interspinous distance and widening of the facet joints.
Spinous process fracture and vertebral body subluxation or dislocation can be indirect signs of posterior ligamentous complex injury.
updates.explanation: TLICS parallels SLICS by scoring morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and neurological status. The posterior ligamentous complex is a major stabiliser of the posterior column. Indirect imaging signs of injury include widened interspinous distance, widened facet joints, spinous process fracture, and vertebral body subluxation or dislocation.

updates.question_text: Postoperative lumbar imaging shows instrumented fusion hardware and adjacent level degeneration. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lucency surrounding pedicle screws is expected normal healing and should never be reported.
Adjacent segment degeneration only occurs at remote non-adjacent levels.
Spinal hardware may fracture, loosen or be malpositioned.
The source estimates adjacent segment degeneration at approximately 30% per year.
Adjacent segment degeneration occurs when the level above or below a fusion undergoes degenerative change.
options_after: Lucency surrounding pedicle screws is expected normal healing and should not be reported.
Adjacent segment degeneration primarily occurs at remote non-adjacent levels.
Spinal hardware may fracture, loosen or be malpositioned.
The source estimates adjacent segment degeneration at approximately 30% per year.
Adjacent segment degeneration occurs when the level above or below a fusion undergoes degenerative change.
updates.explanation: Postoperative imaging should assess hardware fracture, screw position and lucency around screws, which may represent loosening. Adjacent segment degeneration is degeneration at the level above or below a fused segment. The source gives an approximate rate of 3% per year and notes increased risk with reduced paraspinal muscle quality.

updates.question_text: A patient has recurrent pain after decompressive lumbar surgery. MRI shows a recurrent L5-S1 protrusion with peripheral enhancement on post-contrast imaging. Which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Intravenous contrast-enhanced MRI can help distinguish recurrent disc herniation from scar or granulation tissue.
A recurrent disc herniation would not enhance or would enhance only peripherally.
Scar and granulation tissue usually enhance homogeneously.
Recurrent disc herniation and scar are indistinguishable on contrast-enhanced MRI according to the source.
Scar and granulation tissue usually enhance only peripherally like recurrent disc material.
options_after: Intravenous contrast-enhanced MRI can help distinguish recurrent disc herniation from scar or granulation tissue.
A recurrent disc herniation would not enhance or would enhance only peripherally.
Scar and granulation tissue usually enhance homogeneously.
Recurrent disc herniation and scar are indistinguishable on contrast-enhanced MRI according to the source.
Scar and granulation tissue usually enhance primarily peripherally like recurrent disc material.
updates.explanation: In the postoperative spine, contrast-enhanced MRI helps distinguish recurrent disc herniation from scar or granulation tissue. Recurrent disc does not enhance or enhances only peripherally, while scar and granulation tissue usually enhance homogeneously. This distinction matters because recurrent disc herniation may be treated surgically.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric upper airway obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Upper airway obstruction above the trachea is only infectious in childhood
Nasopharyngeal causes include choanal atresia, rhabdomyosarcoma and adenoidal hypertrophy
Peritonsillar abscess is listed as a nasopharyngeal cause
Oropharyngeal causes include peritonsillar abscess and thyroglossal duct cyst
Upper airway obstruction can be classified by anatomic level
options_after: Upper airway obstruction above the trachea is primarily infectious in childhood
Nasopharyngeal causes include choanal atresia, rhabdomyosarcoma and adenoidal hypertrophy
Peritonsillar abscess is listed as a nasopharyngeal cause
Oropharyngeal causes include peritonsillar abscess and thyroglossal duct cyst
Upper airway obstruction can be classified by anatomic level
updates.explanation: The source classifies upper airway obstruction above the trachea as congenital, neoplastic or infectious, and also by anatomic level. Nasopharyngeal examples include choanal atresia, rhabdomyosarcoma and adenoidal hypertrophy. Oropharyngeal examples include peritonsillar abscess and thyroglossal duct cyst. This framing is useful because the same symptom, stridor or obstruction, can arise from different anatomic compartments.

updates.question_text: Regarding subglottic haemangioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a malignant epithelial tumour that presents mainly in teenagers
It is a benign vascular neoplasm producing stridor in infancy
Its classic frontal radiographic appearance is symmetric subglottic narrowing identical to croup
It is associated with cutaneous haemangiomas and PHACES syndrome
PHACES includes posterior fossa malformation, haemangiomas, arterial anomalies, cardiac defects, eye abnormalities and subglottic haemangiomas
options_after: It is a malignant epithelial tumour that presents mainly in teenagers
It is a benign vascular neoplasm producing stridor in infancy
Its classic frontal radiographic appearance is symmetric subglottic narrowing closely comparable to croup
It is associated with cutaneous haemangiomas and PHACES syndrome
PHACES includes posterior fossa malformation, haemangiomas, arterial anomalies, cardiac defects, eye abnormalities and subglottic haemangiomas
updates.explanation: Subglottic haemangioma is the most common paediatric subglottic tracheal mass and is a benign vascular neoplasm causing stridor in infancy. It classically produces asymmetric subglottic narrowing on the frontal radiograph, distinguishing it from the symmetric narrowing of croup. The source links it with cutaneous haemangiomas and PHACES syndrome, including posterior fossa malformation, haemangiomas, arterial anomalies, coarctation/cardiac defects, eye abnormalities, subglottic haemangiomas, sternal clefts and supraumbilical raphes.

updates.question_text: Regarding tracheobronchomalacia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is fixed congenital narrowing of the pyriform aperture
It causes excessive expiratory airway collapse from weakness of tracheobronchial cartilage
A standard inspiratory CT may be normal
Dynamic four-dimensional CT or bronchoscopy is required for diagnosis
It has no association with oesophageal atresia or tracheo-oesophageal fistula
options_after: It is fixed congenital narrowing of the pyriform aperture
It causes excessive expiratory airway collapse from weakness of tracheobronchial cartilage
A standard inspiratory CT may be normal
Dynamic four-dimensional CT or bronchoscopy is required for diagnosis
It lacks association with oesophageal atresia or tracheo-oesophageal fistula
updates.explanation: Tracheobronchomalacia is excessive expiratory airway collapse due to weak tracheobronchial cartilage. It may be congenital or acquired after intubation, infection or chronic inflammation. Inspiratory CT can be normal, so dynamic four-dimensional CT or bronchoscopy is needed. A reduction of more than 50% in airway lumen area is suggestive, though forceful expiration can reach this threshold in normal patients; a common association is oesophageal atresia/tracheo-oesophageal fistula.

updates.question_text: Regarding right aortic arch with mirror-image branching, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is identical to pulmonary sling and always has a normal left arch
It is the typical form of right arch with aberrant left subclavian artery
It is usually isolated and never associated with intracardiac defects
More than 90% of cases are associated with intracardiac defects
Associated defects include tetralogy of Fallot, truncus arteriosus and double-outlet right ventricle
options_after: It is closely comparable to pulmonary sling and characteristically has a normal left arch
It is the typical form of right arch with aberrant left subclavian artery
An associated intracardiac defect argues against this diagnosis.
More than 90% of cases are associated with intracardiac defects
Associated defects include tetralogy of Fallot, truncus arteriosus and double-outlet right ventricle
updates.explanation: Right aortic arch with mirror-image branching is essentially the mirror image of a normal left arch. The source states that more than 90% of cases are associated with intracardiac defects, including tetralogy of Fallot, truncus arteriosus and double-outlet right ventricle. It is typically not a vascular ring, though a complete ring can occur with a circumflex aortic arch.

updates.question_text: Regarding left aortic arch with aberrant right subclavian artery, which of the following statements is correct?
options_before: It is a vascular ring because the ligamentum arteriosum impinges on the airway
It is the only congenital vascular cause of stridor with left arch
When symptomatic, it may cause dysphagia rather than stridor
It produces a large anterior oesophageal impression identical to pulmonary sling
It is routinely treated by ligating the non-dominant aortic arch
options_after: It is a vascular ring because the ligamentum arteriosum impinges on the airway
It is the principal congenital vascular cause of stridor with left arch
When symptomatic, it may cause dysphagia rather than stridor
It produces a large anterior oesophageal impression closely comparable to pulmonary sling
It is routinely treated by ligating the non-dominant aortic arch
updates.explanation: Left arch with aberrant right subclavian artery is not a ring or sling because the ligamentum arteriosum does not impinge on the trachea or oesophagus. It does not cause stridor; when symptomatic it may cause dysphagia lusoria. The source describes a smaller posterior oesophageal impression, unlike pulmonary artery sling, which produces an anterior oesophageal impression.

updates.question_text: Regarding innominate artery syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a complete vascular ring that always compresses both trachea and oesophagus
It may occur when a large infant thymus causes the normal innominate artery to press against the anterior trachea
It is the same lesion as pulmonary artery sling
It is the commonest vascular ring requiring ligation of the non-dominant arch
The source states that its clinical relevance as a cause of breathing difficulty is controversial
options_after: It is a complete vascular ring that characteristically compresses both trachea and oesophagus
It may occur when a large infant thymus causes the normal innominate artery to press against the anterior trachea
It is the same lesion as pulmonary artery sling
It is the commonest vascular ring requiring ligation of the non-dominant arch
The source states that its clinical relevance as a cause of breathing difficulty is controversial
updates.explanation: Innominate artery syndrome can occur in infants when the large thymus allows the normal innominate artery to press against the anterior trachea. It is not a vascular ring, and the source notes that whether it is clinically relevant as a breathing-difficulty entity is controversial. It should not be confused with pulmonary sling or double aortic arch.

updates.question_text: A lateral neck radiograph in a child shows marked prevertebral soft-tissue thickening. Which of the following is the most appropriate source-based interpretation?
options_before: This finding is diagnostic of exudative tracheitis without need for CT
Retropharyngeal abscess is possible, but CT is usually needed to determine the nature of swelling
The finding is specific for omega epiglottis
This excludes retropharyngeal cellulitis
The only complication to consider is pulmonary sling
options_after: This finding is diagnostic of exudative tracheitis without need for CT
Retropharyngeal abscess is possible, but CT is usually needed to determine the nature of swelling
The finding is specific for omega epiglottis
This excludes retropharyngeal cellulitis
The principal complication to consider is pulmonary sling
updates.explanation: The source example of retropharyngeal abscess shows marked prevertebral soft-tissue thickening on lateral neck radiograph, but this appearance is nonspecific. CT is usually required to determine whether swelling represents abscess, cellulitis, lymphoma or a foregut duplication cyst. Retropharyngeal abscess complications include Lemierre syndrome and mediastinitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding granular pulmonary opacities in a newborn, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Granular opacities in a newborn always indicate transient tachypnoea
Neonatal pneumonia is the differential diagnosis specifically highlighted by the source for granular opacities in a newborn
Group B streptococcal pneumonia is mentioned as an example in this differential
Pleural effusions favour surfactant deficiency disease over neonatal pneumonia
The source states that no newborn pneumonia pattern can resemble surfactant deficiency disease
options_after: Granular opacities in a newborn characteristically indicate transient tachypnoea
Neonatal pneumonia is the differential diagnosis specifically highlighted by the source for granular opacities in a newborn
Group B streptococcal pneumonia is mentioned as an example in this differential
Pleural effusions favour surfactant deficiency disease over neonatal pneumonia
A surfactant-deficiency-like radiographic pattern argues against neonatal pneumonia.
updates.explanation: The source specifically gives neonatal pneumonia, including group B streptococcal pneumonia, as the differential diagnosis for granular opacities in a newborn. Pleural effusions are described as a feature that typically accompanies neonatal pneumonia, not surfactant deficiency disease. This distinction matters because pneumonia and surfactant deficiency disease may otherwise overlap radiographically.

updates.question_text: Regarding the distinction between transient tachypnoea of the newborn and neonatal pneumonia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: TTN can always be confidently separated from neonatal pneumonia on the initial radiograph
Typical adult pneumonia signs such as fever and elevated white cell count are reliable discriminators in neonates
TTN and neonatal pneumonia can be clinically and radiographically difficult to distinguish
Antibiotics are often given initially even though TTN has no specific treatment
Known maternal infection or prolonged rupture of membranes suggests TTN rather than pneumonia
options_after: TTN can characteristically be confidently separated from neonatal pneumonia on the initial radiograph
Typical adult pneumonia signs such as fever and elevated white cell count are reliable discriminators in neonates
TTN and neonatal pneumonia can be clinically and radiographically difficult to distinguish
Antibiotics are often given initially even though TTN has no specific treatment
Known maternal infection or prolonged rupture of membranes suggests TTN rather than pneumonia
updates.explanation: The source states that TTN and neonatal pneumonia can be difficult to separate clinically and radiographically. Because of that overlap, antibiotics are often started initially even though TTN itself has no specific treatment. Prolonged rupture of membranes or known maternal infection points towards neonatal pneumonia, while adult signs such as fever and leucocytosis are unreliable in neonates.

updates.question_text: Regarding bronchopulmonary foregut malformations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are all purely vascular malformations without abnormal lung development
They form a spectrum combining normal or abnormal vasculature with normal or abnormal pulmonary parenchyma
Bronchopulmonary sequestration has anomalous systemic blood supply and no connection to the bronchial tree
Congenital lobar hyperinflation is defined by an anomalous connection between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary veins
Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation is a lesion of abnormal lung development without vascular abnormality
options_after: They are most purely vascular malformations without abnormal lung development
They form a spectrum combining normal or abnormal vasculature with normal or abnormal pulmonary parenchyma
Bronchopulmonary sequestration has anomalous systemic blood supply and no connection to the bronchial tree
Congenital lobar hyperinflation is defined by an anomalous connection between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary veins
Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation is a lesion of abnormal lung development without vascular abnormality
updates.explanation: The source frames bronchopulmonary foregut malformations as a spectrum of pulmonary parenchymal and vascular abnormality. Bronchopulmonary sequestration is aberrant lung tissue with anomalous systemic blood supply and no bronchial connection. Pulmonary AVM is the purely vascular lesion in the spectrum, while congenital lobar hyperinflation is abnormal lung development without a vascular anomaly.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital lobar hyperinflation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is lobar air trapping caused by intrinsic or extrinsic bronchial narrowing without destruction of lung parenchyma
It is most commonly caused by a systemic feeding artery from the thoracic aorta
Bronchomalacia is the most common cause, producing airway collapse on expiration
It usually affects the lower lobes only
Postnatally it appears as a hyperlucent and hyperexpanded lobe that may exert mass effect
options_after: It is lobar air trapping caused by intrinsic or extrinsic bronchial narrowing without destruction of lung parenchyma
It is most commonly caused by a systemic feeding artery from the thoracic aorta
Bronchomalacia is the most common cause, producing airway collapse on expiration
It usually affects the lower lobes in typical cases
Postnatally it appears as a hyperlucent and hyperexpanded lobe that may exert mass effect
updates.explanation: Congenital lobar hyperinflation is a syndrome of lobar air trapping from intrinsic or extrinsic bronchial narrowing, without parenchymal destruction. Bronchomalacia is the most common cause, causing expiratory airway collapse and hyperinflation. After birth, fluid clears and the affected lobe becomes hyperlucent and hyperexpanded, sometimes causing mediastinal shift. The source states that upper and middle lobes are usually involved.

updates.question_text: Regarding the imaging pitfall in congenital lobar hyperinflation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It should be treated as tension pneumothorax whenever the affected hemithorax is hyperlucent
Mistaking congenital lobar hyperinflation for tension pneumothorax is specifically warned against by the source
Chest tube placement in this setting may increase respiratory distress
The key imaging finding is bilateral small pleural effusions and fissural fluid
The source states that CT always identifies the obstructing cause
options_after: It should be treated as tension pneumothorax whenever the affected hemithorax is hyperlucent
Mistaking congenital lobar hyperinflation for tension pneumothorax is specifically warned against by the source
Chest tube placement in this setting may increase respiratory distress
The key imaging finding is bilateral small pleural effusions and fissural fluid
The source states that CT characteristically identifies the obstructing cause
updates.explanation: The source explicitly warns not to mistake congenital lobar hyperinflation for tension pneumothorax. Chest tube placement may worsen respiratory distress rather than help. CT can evaluate for bronchial obstruction, but a cause is found in only about half of cases. Fissural fluid and small pleural effusions are features of transient tachypnoea of the newborn, not the main pitfall in CLH.

updates.question_text: Regarding pulmonary arteriovenous malformations in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are hamartomatous proliferations of terminal bronchioles that communicate with the bronchial tree
They are caused by ipsilateral pulmonary hypoplasia from bowel herniation
They have anomalous systemic arterial supply and no bronchial connection
About 60% are associated with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia
They represent anomalous connections between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary veins
options_after: They are hamartomatous proliferations of terminal bronchioles that communicate with the bronchial tree
They are caused by ipsilateral pulmonary hypoplasia from bowel herniation
They have anomalous systemic arterial supply without bronchial connection
About 60% are associated with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia
They represent anomalous connections between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary veins
updates.explanation: Pulmonary AVM is described as a purely vascular malformation connecting pulmonary arteries and pulmonary veins. The source states that about 60% are associated with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia. A hamartomatous terminal bronchiole proliferation describes CPAM, while anomalous systemic supply without bronchial connection describes sequestration.

updates.question_text: Regarding CPAM and bronchopulmonary sequestration, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CPAM derives arterial supply from the pulmonary circulation
Sequestration usually appears cystic, whereas CPAM is usually solid
Both entities are defined by an anomalous pulmonary venous return into the inferior vena cava
CPAM has no communication with the bronchial tree
Sequestration derives its blood supply from the systemic circulation
options_after: CPAM derives arterial supply from the pulmonary circulation
Sequestration usually appears cystic, whereas CPAM is usually solid
Both entities are defined by an anomalous pulmonary venous return into the inferior vena cava
CPAM lacks communication with the bronchial tree
Sequestration derives its blood supply from the systemic circulation
updates.explanation: The source explicitly contrasts CPAM with sequestration by blood supply. CPAM is supplied by the pulmonary circulation, whereas sequestration derives supply from the systemic circulation. Sequestration is usually solid, while CPAM is cystic or multicystic. Scimitar syndrome, not either of these lesions, is partial anomalous pulmonary venous return.

updates.question_text: Regarding bronchopulmonary sequestration, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The key imaging finding is a systemic feeding artery
The most common location is the right upper lobe
The feeding artery usually arises from the thoracic aorta
It is usually solid, although hybrid lesions with CPAM components exist
It always communicates with the bronchial tree
options_after: The key imaging finding is a systemic feeding artery
The most common location is the right upper lobe
The feeding artery usually arises from the thoracic aorta
It is usually solid, although hybrid lesions with CPAM components exist
It characteristically communicates with the bronchial tree
updates.explanation: Bronchopulmonary sequestration is aberrant lung tissue with anomalous systemic blood supply and no bronchial-tree connection. The source identifies the systemic feeding artery as the key imaging finding, usually arising from the thoracic aorta. The usual location is the left lower lobe. Sequestration is usually solid, although hybrid lesions with CPAM components can occur.

updates.question_text: Regarding scimitar syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a form of partial anomalous pulmonary venous return
A curvilinear opacity extending from the right hilum towards the diaphragm may represent the scimitar sign
The anomalous scimitar vein may drain into the inferior vena cava
It is grouped within the bronchopulmonary foregut malformation spectrum in the source
It is defined by a systemic feeding artery supplying aberrant lung tissue with no bronchial connection
options_after: It is a form of partial anomalous pulmonary venous return
A curvilinear opacity extending from the right hilum towards the diaphragm may represent the scimitar sign
The anomalous scimitar vein may drain into the inferior vena cava
It is grouped within the bronchopulmonary foregut malformation spectrum in the source
It is defined by a systemic feeding artery supplying aberrant lung tissue without bronchial connection
updates.explanation: The source describes scimitar syndrome as a form of partial anomalous pulmonary venous return. The radiograph may show the scimitar sign, a curvilinear opacity extending from the right hilum toward the diaphragm. CT demonstrates the anomalous vein draining into the inferior vena cava. A systemic feeding artery with no bronchial connection is the defining feature of sequestration, not scimitar syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding scimitar syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It represents partial anomalous pulmonary venous return from right lower lobe pulmonary veins into the right atrium or IVC
It is equivalent to total anomalous pulmonary venous return, where all four pulmonary veins drain to the right atrium
The anomalous vein may appear like a Turkish sword on the frontal radiograph
A right-to-left shunt is unnecessary in total anomalous pulmonary venous return
It can be associated with hypoplasia and hyperlucency of the right lung
options_after: It represents partial anomalous pulmonary venous return from right lower lobe pulmonary veins into the right atrium or IVC
It is equivalent to total anomalous pulmonary venous return, where most four pulmonary veins drain to the right atrium
The anomalous vein may appear like a Turkish sword on the frontal radiograph
A right-to-left shunt is unnecessary in total anomalous pulmonary venous return
It can be associated with hypoplasia and hyperlucency of the right lung
updates.explanation: The source defines scimitar syndrome as partial anomalous pulmonary venous return from right lower lobe veins into the right atrium or inferior vena cava. The scimitar sign is produced by the anomalous vein on frontal radiography. Associated right lung hypoplasia and hyperlucency may occur. Total anomalous pulmonary venous return is contrasted separately, with all four pulmonary veins returning to the right atrium and an obligate right-to-left shunt for survival.

updates.question_text: Regarding chest radiography in bronchiolitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most reliable feature is lobar consolidation with pleural effusion
Hyperexpanded lungs may be seen, best appreciated by diaphragmatic flattening on the lateral view
The source states that experienced paediatric radiologists show no variability in interpreting these findings
Increased perihilar peribronchial markings and peribronchial cuffing are described findings
Radiographic findings always exclude bacterial pneumonia
options_after: The most reliable feature is lobar consolidation with pleural effusion
Hyperexpanded lungs may be seen, best appreciated by diaphragmatic flattening on the lateral view
The source states that experienced paediatric radiologists fail to show variability in interpreting these findings
Increased perihilar peribronchial markings and peribronchial cuffing are described findings
Radiographic findings characteristically exclude bacterial pneumonia
updates.explanation: The source lists hyperexpanded lungs, diaphragmatic flattening on lateral view, scattered atelectasis, increased perihilar peribronchial markings and peribronchial cuffing as radiographic features of bronchiolitis. It also warns that these findings are subjective, with high variability even among experienced paediatric radiologists. Focal air-space consolidation with air bronchograms and pleural effusions should prompt exclusion of bacterial pneumonia rather than support uncomplicated bronchiolitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding bronchiectasis in the paediatric population, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bronchiectasis is bronchial dilatation, most commonly due to inflammation
The signet ring sign describes a bronchus smaller than its adjacent pulmonary artery branch
The source limits paediatric bronchiectasis causes to cystic fibrosis only
Cystic fibrosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, post-infectious change and aspiration are listed causes
Intralobar sequestration is included as a possible cause, possibly due to recurrent infections
options_after: Bronchiectasis is bronchial dilatation, most commonly due to inflammation
The signet ring sign describes a bronchus smaller than its adjacent pulmonary artery branch
The source limits paediatric bronchiectasis causes to cystic fibrosis in typical cases
Cystic fibrosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, post-infectious change and aspiration are listed causes
Intralobar sequestration is included as a possible cause, possibly due to recurrent infections
updates.explanation: Bronchiectasis is defined as bronchial dilatation, most commonly inflammatory. The source lists multiple paediatric causes, including cystic fibrosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, post-infectious disease, tracheobronchomegaly, aspiration and intralobar sequestration. The signet ring sign is enlargement of the bronchiole so that it appears larger than the adjacent pulmonary arterial branch.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal thymus and thymic rebound in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal thymus can appear large in children up to 5 years of age
Normal thymus can show the thymic wave sign and thymic sail sign
Normal thymus causes tracheal mass effect
Thymic rebound after chemotherapy should always be treated as recurrent lymphoma
Thymic rebound can be FDG-avid on PET
options_after: Normal thymus can appear large in children up to 5 years of age
Normal thymus can show the thymic wave sign and thymic sail sign
Normal thymus causes tracheal mass effect
Thymic rebound after chemotherapy should characteristically be treated as recurrent lymphoma
Thymic rebound can be FDG-avid on PET
updates.explanation: The source warns that normal thymus can appear large in children up to 5 years and mimic an anterior mediastinal mass. Normal thymus may show undulating anterior rib margins, the thymic wave sign, and inferolateral extension into the minor fissure, the thymic sail sign. It allows overlapping pulmonary vascular markings and causes no tracheal mass effect. Thymic rebound after chemotherapy is physiologic regrowth and can be FDG-avid on PET.

updates.question_text: Regarding umbilical arterial catheters and PICCs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A UAC should ideally terminate in the right atrium
A UAC initially descends into the internal iliac artery before ascending the common iliac artery and abdominal aorta
The only acceptable UAC tip level is the portal vein
A PICC placed via an upper extremity approach should terminate in the distal SVC
A lower-extremity PICC should terminate in the left portal vein
options_after: A UAC should ideally terminate in the right atrium
A UAC initially descends into the internal iliac artery before ascending the common iliac artery and abdominal aorta
The principal acceptable UAC tip level is the portal vein
A PICC placed via an upper extremity approach should terminate in the distal SVC
A lower-extremity PICC should terminate in the left portal vein
updates.explanation: A UAC arises from the umbilical artery, descends into the internal iliac artery, then ascends through the common iliac artery and abdominal aorta. The ideal UAC tip is high at T6-T10 or low at L3-L5, avoiding aortic arch and abdominal branches. Upper-extremity PICCs should terminate in the distal SVC, whereas lower-extremity PICCs should terminate in the IVC just inferior to the right atrium.

updates.question_text: Regarding the plain film approach to suspected congenital heart disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Echocardiography is typically the imaging study of choice when a newborn has unexpected shortness of breath with concern for a cardiac cause
Plain radiography usually determines the exact congenital cardiac diagnosis without further imaging
Plain radiographs remain useful for describing features such as pulmonary vascularity and cardiomegaly
CTA or MRI is never useful once echocardiography is available
Most congenital heart disease is diagnosed in utero during routine fetal ultrasound
options_after: Echocardiography is typically the imaging study of choice when a newborn has unexpected shortness of breath with concern for a cardiac cause
Plain radiography usually determines the exact congenital cardiac diagnosis without further imaging
Plain radiographs remain useful for describing features such as pulmonary vascularity and cardiomegaly
CTA or MRI is not useful once echocardiography is available
Most congenital heart disease is diagnosed in utero during routine fetal ultrasound
updates.explanation: The source states that most congenital heart disease is diagnosed in utero and that echocardiography is typically the first imaging test when a newborn unexpectedly presents with shortness of breath and concern for a cardiac cause. Plain radiography may not provide the exact diagnosis, but it remains useful for describing pulmonary vascularity, cardiomegaly and related thoracic findings. Advanced imaging such as CTA or MRI can help in selected clinical situations.

updates.question_text: Regarding atrial septal defects, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: ASD is a common intracardiac left-to-right shunt but is rarely diagnosed in infants or young children
ASD usually presents in later childhood or early adulthood and is twice as common in females
Most ASDs are syndromic rather than isolated
Holt-Oram syndrome can include ASD and upper extremity bone deformities
ASD primarily causes left atrial enlargement because the left atrium cannot decompress
options_after: ASD is a common intracardiac left-to-right shunt but is rarely diagnosed in infants or young children
ASD usually presents in later childhood or early adulthood and is twice as common in females
Most ASDs are syndromic rather than isolated
Holt-Oram syndrome can include ASD and upper extremity bone deformities
ASD primarily causes left atrial enlargement because the left atrium will not decompress
updates.explanation: The source states that ASD is a common intracardiac left-to-right shunt but is rarely diagnosed in infants or young children. It usually presents in later childhood or early adulthood and is twice as common in females. Most are isolated, although Holt-Oram syndrome is an example of a rare syndromic association. ASD causes right heart volume overload while the left atrium is usually normal because blood decompresses into the right atrium.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiographic consequences of atrial septal defect, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Right atrial enlargement occurs initially, followed by right ventricular enlargement
The left atrium is always massively enlarged before the right heart enlarges
Right ventricular enlargement may appear as opacity in the retrosternal clear space on the lateral radiograph
Shunt vascularity is absent by the time an ASD becomes symptomatic
Treatment is pulmonary artery banding rather than closure
options_after: Right atrial enlargement occurs initially, followed by right ventricular enlargement
The left atrium is characteristically massively enlarged before the right heart enlarges
Right ventricular enlargement may appear as opacity in the retrosternal clear space on the lateral radiograph
Shunt vascularity is absent by the time an ASD becomes symptomatic
Treatment is pulmonary artery banding rather than closure
updates.explanation: The source states that ASD initially causes right atrial enlargement, followed by right ventricular enlargement. Right ventricular enlargement may be visible on the lateral view as opacity in the retrosternal clear space. Shunt vascularity is usually present by the time the lesion becomes symptomatic. Treatment is ASD closure, often using an Amplatzer or similar device.

updates.question_text: Regarding ventricular septal defect, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: VSD is typically diagnosed earlier than ASD, with many children presenting after the first month of life as pulmonary vascular resistance falls
VSD usually causes isolated right atrial dilatation without left heart involvement
VSD may occur in the membranous or muscular interventricular septum
Left-to-right shunting occurs in systole and causes left atrial and left ventricular dilatation
A VSD cannot lead to Eisenmenger syndrome
options_after: VSD is typically diagnosed earlier than ASD, with many children presenting after the first month of life as pulmonary vascular resistance falls
VSD usually causes isolated right atrial dilatation without left heart involvement
VSD may occur in the membranous or muscular interventricular septum
Left-to-right shunting occurs in systole and causes left atrial and left ventricular dilatation
A VSD will not lead to Eisenmenger syndrome
updates.explanation: VSD is usually diagnosed earlier than ASD, often after the first month of life as pulmonary vascular resistance falls. It may be membranous or muscular. Systolic left-to-right shunting causes volume overload of the left heart, with left atrial and ventricular dilatation. If unrepaired, Eisenmenger syndrome can develop, although it is rare because most patients undergo surgery before flow reversal.

updates.question_text: Regarding the classic radiographic evolution of ventricular septal defect, which statement is correct?
options_before: A VSD always produces a boot-shaped heart in the newborn period
Classic shunt vascularity and cardiomegaly typically take a few years to develop
The left atrium is never enlarged in VSD
Pulmonary vascular flow is decreased shortly after birth
VSD is primarily a pulmonary venous obstruction lesion
options_after: A VSD characteristically produces a boot-shaped heart in the newborn period
Classic shunt vascularity and cardiomegaly typically take a few years to develop
The left atrium is not enlarged in VSD
Pulmonary vascular flow is decreased shortly after birth
VSD is primarily a pulmonary venous obstruction lesion
updates.explanation: The source states that the classic imaging findings of VSD, namely shunt vascularity and cardiomegaly, usually take a few years to develop. Early after birth there may be mild cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular flow. The left atrium is often enlarged and may splay the mainstem bronchi at the carina. A boot-shaped heart belongs to tetralogy of Fallot.

updates.question_text: Regarding patent ductus arteriosus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The ductus arteriosus connects the proximal right pulmonary artery to the ascending aorta
A PDA creates a persistent left-to-right shunt
A small PDA usually causes severe neonatal congestive heart failure
The classic presentation is a premature infant developing radiographic congestive heart failure at 7-10 days as pulmonary vascular resistance falls
PDA is treated only with the arterial switch operation
options_after: The ductus arteriosus connects the proximal right pulmonary artery to the ascending aorta
A PDA creates a persistent left-to-right shunt
A small PDA usually causes severe neonatal congestive heart failure
The classic presentation is a premature infant developing radiographic congestive heart failure at 7-10 days as pulmonary vascular resistance falls
PDA is treated primarily with the arterial switch operation
updates.explanation: The ductus arteriosus normally connects the proximal left pulmonary artery to the descending aorta, and it usually functionally closes by 48 hours of life. A persistent PDA causes a left-to-right shunt. The classic presentation is a premature infant who develops radiographic evidence of congestive heart failure at 7-10 days as pulmonary vascular resistance falls. Treatment may be medical with indomethacin or surgical clip placement.

updates.question_text: Regarding pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It appears identical to tetralogy of Fallot on radiography with a normal-sized heart
It produces increased pulmonary arterial flow through a large VSD
It is in the same spectrum as pulmonary atresia with VSD
It appears identical to Ebstein anomaly on radiography, with massive right atrial enlargement and decreased pulmonary blood flow
Pulmonary blood flow depends on a left-to-right shunt such as a patent ductus
options_after: It appears closely comparable to tetralogy of Fallot on radiography with a normal-sized heart
It produces increased pulmonary arterial flow through a large VSD
It is in the same spectrum as pulmonary atresia with VSD
It appears identical to Ebstein anomaly on radiography, with massive right atrial enlargement and decreased pulmonary blood flow
Pulmonary blood flow depends on a left-to-right shunt such as a patent ductus
updates.explanation: Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum appears identical to Ebstein anomaly on radiography, with massive right atrial enlargement and decreased pulmonary blood flow. Because there is no VSD, pulmonary blood flow depends on a left-to-right shunt such as a PDA. The source distinguishes this from pulmonary atresia with VSD, which belongs to the tetralogy of Fallot spectrum and more often has a normal-sized heart.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiographic findings and associations of tetralogy of Fallot, which statement is correct?
options_before: Classic radiography shows cardiomegaly, narrow mediastinum and pulmonary oedema
The heart is usually massively enlarged and box-shaped
Pulmonary vascularity is increased because of admixture physiology
Classic radiography shows a normal-sized boot-shaped heart and decreased pulmonary vascularity
A right-sided aortic arch is never seen
options_after: Classic radiography shows cardiomegaly, narrow mediastinum and pulmonary oedema
The heart is usually massively enlarged and box-shaped
Pulmonary vascularity is increased because of admixture physiology
Classic radiography shows a normal-sized boot-shaped heart and decreased pulmonary vascularity
A right-sided aortic arch is not seen
updates.explanation: The classic tetralogy of Fallot radiograph shows a normal-sized boot-shaped heart, with the apex uplifted by right ventricular hypertrophy, and decreased pulmonary vascularity. The source states that 25% of cases have a right-sided aortic arch. Cardiomegaly with pulmonary oedema is the classic truncus arteriosus pattern, while a massive box-shaped heart is the pattern of Ebstein anomaly.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiography and surgery in D-TGA, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The egg-on-a-string appearance is actually uncommon
A right aortic arch is seen in most cases
The typical radiograph is always normal pulmonary vascularity and a broad superior mediastinum
Surgical treatment is the arterial switch procedure, which swaps the aorta and pulmonary artery and relocates the coronary arteries to the neo-aorta
The Norwood procedure is the source's named treatment for D-TGA
options_after: The egg-on-a-string appearance is actually uncommon
A right aortic arch is seen in most cases
The typical radiograph is characteristically normal pulmonary vascularity and a broad superior mediastinum
Surgical treatment is the arterial switch procedure, which swaps the aorta and pulmonary artery and relocates the coronary arteries to the neo-aorta
The Norwood procedure is the source's named treatment for D-TGA
updates.explanation: The classic egg-on-a-string appearance of D-TGA is described as uncommon. A more typical pattern is a slightly narrow superior mediastinum, absent main pulmonary artery bulge and increased pulmonary vasculature, although the radiographic appearance varies with the coexisting shunt. A right aortic arch is seen in 5%. The surgical treatment for D-TGA is the arterial switch or Jatene procedure, while the Norwood procedure belongs to hypoplastic left heart syndrome.

updates.question_text: Regarding tricuspid atresia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets with atrialisation of the right ventricle
It causes a fixed radiographic pattern regardless of VSD size
It is absence or dysplasia of the tricuspid valve resulting in no flow between the right atrium and right ventricle
A small associated VSD gives a normal-sized heart with decreased pulmonary vasculature
A large associated VSD gives an enlarged heart with increased pulmonary flow
options_after: It is apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets with atrialisation of the right ventricle
It causes a fixed radiographic pattern despite variation in VSD size
It is absence or dysplasia of the tricuspid valve resulting in no flow between the right atrium and right ventricle
A small associated VSD gives a normal-sized heart with decreased pulmonary vasculature
A large associated VSD gives an enlarged heart with increased pulmonary flow
updates.explanation: Tricuspid atresia is absence or dysplasia of the tricuspid valve, with no flow from the right atrium to the right ventricle. Its radiographic appearance varies with the size of the associated VSD. A small VSD gives a normal-sized heart and decreased pulmonary vasculature, while a large VSD gives an enlarged heart with increased pulmonary flow. Apical leaflet displacement and atrialisation of the right ventricle describe Ebstein anomaly.

updates.question_text: Regarding truncus arteriosus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A single great artery arises from the base of the heart to supply systemic, pulmonary and coronary circulations
The single great artery usually overrides an atrial septal defect only
The single great artery usually overrides a VSD
It is the most common congenital heart disease type to have a right aortic arch
The classic radiographic appearance is cardiomegaly, narrow mediastinum and pulmonary oedema
options_after: A single great artery arises from the base of the heart to supply systemic, pulmonary and coronary circulations
The single great artery usually overrides an atrial septal defect in typical cases
The single great artery usually overrides a VSD
It is the most common congenital heart disease type to have a right aortic arch
The classic radiographic appearance is cardiomegaly, narrow mediastinum and pulmonary oedema
updates.explanation: In truncus arteriosus, one great artery supplies systemic, pulmonary and coronary circulations and usually overrides a VSD. The source states that it is the most common congenital heart disease type to have a right aortic arch, occurring in 21-36% of cases. It is also associated with DiGeorge syndrome in 30-35% of cases. The classic radiograph shows cardiomegaly, narrow mediastinum and pulmonary oedema.

updates.question_text: Regarding total anomalous pulmonary venous return, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All pulmonary veins drain normally into the left atrium
All pulmonary veins connect anomalously to the systemic venous circulation instead of the left atrium
A right-to-left interatrial communication such as a large PFO or ASD is obligate for blood to reach the left heart
Classification is based on whether the aortic arch is right-sided or left-sided
Clinical and radiographic findings depend on the degree of pulmonary venous obstruction and admixture
options_after: Most pulmonary veins drain normally into the left atrium
All pulmonary veins connect anomalously to the systemic venous circulation instead of the left atrium
A right-to-left interatrial communication such as a large PFO or ASD is obligate for blood to reach the left heart
Classification is based on whether the aortic arch is right-sided or left-sided
Clinical and radiographic findings depend on the degree of pulmonary venous obstruction and admixture
updates.explanation: TAPVR means all pulmonary veins connect anomalously to systemic venous circulation rather than the left atrium. An interatrial right-to-left communication, such as a large PFO or ASD, is required for blood to reach the left heart. The source classifies TAPVR by the drainage position relative to the heart, not by aortic arch sidedness. Clinical and radiographic findings depend on obstruction and admixture.

updates.question_text: Regarding the radiographic pattern labels in the congenital heart disease summary, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Vein of Galen malformation and hepatic haemangioendothelioma are listed under extracardiac shunts causing CHF
Enlarged right atrium is highlighted for Ebstein anomaly in the summary
Enlarged left atrium is highlighted in the VSD pathway
Narrow mediastinum is highlighted in the TGA pathway
The summary states that TAPVR never causes increased pulmonary vascularity
options_after: Vein of Galen malformation and hepatic haemangioendothelioma are listed under extracardiac shunts causing CHF
Enlarged right atrium is highlighted for Ebstein anomaly in the summary
Enlarged left atrium is highlighted in the VSD pathway
Narrow mediastinum is highlighted in the TGA pathway
The summary states that TAPVR will not cause increased pulmonary vascularity
updates.explanation: The summary lists vein of Galen malformation and hepatic haemangioendothelioma under extracardiac shunt-related CHF. It flags enlarged right atrium for Ebstein anomaly and enlarged left atrium in the VSD pathway. Narrow mediastinum is shown in the TGA branch. TAPVR is included among increased-pulmonary-vascularity cyanotic lesions in the summary.

updates.question_text: Regarding pulmonary arteriovenous malformations after Glenn shunting, which statements are correct?
options_before: They are associated with the Glenn shunt
Their aetiology is thought to relate to lack of hepatic venous flow to the lungs
Regression has been shown after restoration of hepatic venous flow to the lungs, for example after Fontan revision
They are caused by the LeCompte manoeuvre moving the pulmonary artery anterior to the aorta
They are the reason the arterial switch operation is no longer preferred
options_after: They are associated with the Glenn shunt
Their aetiology is thought to relate to lack of hepatic venous flow to the lungs
Regression has been shown after restoration of hepatic venous flow to the lungs, for example after Fontan revision
They are caused by the LeCompte manoeuvre moving the pulmonary artery anterior to the aorta
They are the reason the arterial switch operation is not currently preferred
updates.explanation: The source links acquired pulmonary AVMs to the Glenn shunt. The proposed mechanism is absence of hepatic venous flow to the lungs after the procedure. Literature has shown regression after hepatic venous flow is restored, such as after Fontan revision. The LeCompte manoeuvre and arterial switch are D-TGA surgical concepts, not the cause of Glenn-associated AVMs.

updates.question_text: Regarding the Rastelli procedure, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It was initially designed for isolated D-TGA without VSD or LVOT obstruction
It is used only for isolated ASD and PDA closure
It creates an intraventricular baffle connecting the LV to the aorta and closes the VSD
It creates an extracardiac conduit from the RV to the pulmonary artery
It leaves the pulmonary valve open as the main systemic outlet
options_after: It was initially designed for isolated D-TGA without VSD or LVOT obstruction
It is used primarily for isolated ASD and PDA closure
It creates an intraventricular baffle connecting the LV to the aorta and closes the VSD
It creates an extracardiac conduit from the RV to the pulmonary artery
It leaves the pulmonary valve open as the main systemic outlet
updates.explanation: The source states that the Rastelli procedure was initially designed for D-TGA with VSD and LVOT obstruction, and can also repair pulmonary atresia with VSD or double-outlet RV with pulmonary stenosis or atresia. The operation creates an intraventricular baffle connecting the LV to the aorta and closes the VSD, plus an extracardiac conduit from the RV to the pulmonary artery. The pulmonary valve is surgically closed.

updates.question_text: Regarding visceroatrial situs, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It describes the relationship between thoracoabdominal viscera and atria
Attention to liver, spleen and stomach position is helpful in determining situs
It is determined only by the direction of the aortic arch
The right and left lung lobation pattern can contribute to situs assessment
It is unrelated to congenital heart disease assessment
options_after: It describes the relationship between thoracoabdominal viscera and atria
Attention to liver, spleen and stomach position is helpful in determining situs
It is determined primarily by the direction of the aortic arch
The right and left lung lobation pattern can contribute to situs assessment
It is unrelated to congenital heart disease assessment
updates.explanation: Visceroatrial situs describes the relationship of thoracoabdominal viscera to the atria. The source notes that liver, spleen and stomach position are useful clues, and it defines normal lung lobation as part of situs solitus. Situs assessment matters because ambiguous situs is strongly linked to congenital heart disease patterns.

updates.question_text: Regarding situs solitus and situs inversus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Situs solitus has right atrium and liver on the right, with left atrium, spleen and stomach on the left
Situs solitus has a bilobed right lung and trilobed left lung
Situs inversus is the opposite of situs solitus
Situs inversus is associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia
Situs inversus always means absent spleen
options_after: Situs solitus has right atrium and liver on the right, with left atrium, spleen and stomach on the left
Situs solitus has a bilobed right lung and trilobed left lung
Situs inversus is the opposite of situs solitus
Situs inversus is associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia
Situs inversus characteristically means absent spleen
updates.explanation: Situs solitus is normal arrangement, with right atrium and liver on the right, left atrium, spleen and stomach on the left, right lung trilobed and left lung bilobed. Situs inversus reverses this arrangement and is associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Absent spleen belongs to right-isomerism/asplenia, not situs inversus.

updates.question_text: Which cardiac mass distinction is supported by first-pass myocardial perfusion behaviour in the source?
options_before: Rhabdomyoma and fibroma both enhance avidly on first-pass perfusion
Haemangioma hypoenhances because it is non-vascular
Fibroma is identified by first-pass perfusion rather than delayed progressive enhancement
Teratoma and haemangioma cannot be distinguished by enhancement behaviour
Teratoma hypoenhances while haemangioma enhances avidly
options_after: Rhabdomyoma and fibroma both enhance avidly on first-pass perfusion
Haemangioma hypoenhances because it is non-vascular
Fibroma is identified by first-pass perfusion rather than delayed progressive enhancement
Teratoma and haemangioma will not be distinguished by enhancement behaviour
Teratoma hypoenhances while haemangioma enhances avidly
updates.explanation: The source states that teratomas are hypoenhancing on first-pass myocardial perfusion imaging, which differentiates them from haemangiomas. Haemangiomas are benign vascular tumours and enhance avidly on first-pass myocardial perfusion. Fibroma is characterised by progressive enhancement with a hypoenhancing core, while rhabdomyoma is hypoenhancing relative to myocardium.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiographic findings in necrotising enterocolitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The initial radiograph is always normal until perforation occurs
Early findings include bowel thickening and fixed distension of a bowel loop over serial examinations
Later findings may include pneumatosis, portal venous gas or pneumoperitoneum
Subserosal pneumatosis is a linear crescent of gas between smooth muscular and serosal layers and is more specific
Submucosal pneumatosis can be confused with intraluminal contents
options_after: The initial radiograph is characteristically normal until perforation occurs
Early findings include bowel thickening and fixed distension of a bowel loop over serial examinations
Later findings may include pneumatosis, portal venous gas or pneumoperitoneum
Subserosal pneumatosis is a linear crescent of gas between smooth muscular and serosal layers and is more specific
Submucosal pneumatosis can be confused with intraluminal contents
updates.explanation: Initial NEC radiographs may show bowel thickening and a fixed, distended loop on serial films. Later disease may show pneumatosis, portal venous gas or pneumoperitoneum related to perforation. The source distinguishes submucosal pneumatosis, which may mimic intraluminal contents, from the more specific subserosal crescent of gas.

updates.question_text: Regarding management and follow-up of NEC, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Early NEC always requires emergent surgery
Early NEC can be treated medically with antibiotics, TPN and cessation of oral feeds
Pneumoperitoneum can be ignored if pneumatosis is already present
