Pneumoperitoneum generally requires emergent surgery, although bowel-sparing percutaneous drainage is emerging in some cases
After recovery, contrast enema can evaluate for stricture, the most common delayed complication
options_after: Early NEC characteristically requires emergent surgery
Early NEC can be treated medically with antibiotics, TPN and cessation of oral feeds
Pneumoperitoneum can be ignored if pneumatosis is already present
Pneumoperitoneum generally requires emergent surgery, although bowel-sparing percutaneous drainage is emerging in some cases
After recovery, contrast enema can evaluate for stricture, the most common delayed complication
updates.explanation: The source separates early medical management from perforated disease. Early NEC may be treated with antibiotics, TPN and stopping oral feeds. Pneumoperitoneum usually requires emergent surgery, although bowel-sparing percutaneous drainage is an emerging option in selected cases. After recovery, contrast enema can assess for stricture, which is the most common delayed complication.

updates.question_text: Regarding malrotation with midgut volvulus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Malrotation predisposes to volvulus because of abnormal mesenteric fixation
Volvulus is a surgical emergency with high mortality due to bowel ischaemia
It typically presents with neonatal non-bilious emesis
Malrotation is associated with omphaloceles and heterotaxy syndromes
Bilious emesis never requires an upper GI study
options_after: Malrotation predisposes to volvulus because of abnormal mesenteric fixation
Volvulus is a surgical emergency with high mortality due to bowel ischaemia
It typically presents with neonatal non-bilious emesis
Malrotation is associated with omphaloceles and heterotaxy syndromes
Bilious emesis will not require an upper GI study
updates.explanation: Malrotation reflects failed embryologic rotation and abnormal mesenteric fixation, predisposing bowel to volvulus. Volvulus is a surgical emergency because bowel ischaemia can be fatal. It typically presents with neonatal bilious emesis and must be ruled out with upper GI when this symptom is present, after distal obstruction has been excluded. The source also links malrotation with omphaloceles and heterotaxy syndromes.

updates.question_text: Regarding the work-up of bilious emesis when malrotation is suspected, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Distal obstruction should be excluded on abdominal radiograph before upper GI
Upper GI in a neonate with distal obstruction has a high risk of false positives
The ligament of Treitz is fixed and cannot be distorted by distal bowel dilatation
Malrotation with volvulus must be ruled out with an upper GI when bilious emesis is present
Bilious emesis is always non-obstructive gastroenteritis
options_after: Distal obstruction should be excluded on abdominal radiograph before upper GI
Upper GI in a neonate with distal obstruction has a high risk of false positives
The ligament of Treitz is fixed and will not be distorted by distal bowel dilatation
Malrotation with volvulus must be ruled out with an upper GI when bilious emesis is present
Bilious emesis is characteristically non-obstructive gastroenteritis
updates.explanation: The source cautions that bilious emesis can come from distal neonatal obstruction as well as malrotation with volvulus. Therefore abdominal radiography should exclude distal obstruction before performing upper GI. Upper GI in distal obstruction risks false positives because the ligament of Treitz is lax and can be distorted by dilated distal loops. Malrotation with volvulus remains the key diagnosis to exclude when bilious emesis is present.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging signs of midgut volvulus and malrotation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The classic upper GI finding of midgut volvulus is a corkscrew appearance of twisted bowel
Plain radiographs are always diagnostic and never normal when malrotation is present
CT or ultrasound normally shows the SMA to the right of the SMV
Whirlpool sign on Doppler ultrasound or CT reflects twisted mesenteric vessels
The caecum in the right lower quadrant is listed as a clue to malrotation
options_after: The classic upper GI finding of midgut volvulus is a corkscrew appearance of twisted bowel
A normal abdominal radiograph excludes intestinal malrotation.
CT or ultrasound normally shows the SMA to the right of the SMV
Whirlpool sign on Doppler ultrasound or CT reflects twisted mesenteric vessels
The caecum in the right lower quadrant is listed as a clue to malrotation
updates.explanation: The classic upper GI sign of volvulus is the corkscrew appearance of twisted bowel. Plain films may show multiple dilated loops or a double bubble, but can also be normal in malrotation with vomiting. The source lists inversion of the normal SMA/SMV relationship, with the SMA to the right of the SMV, and the whirlpool sign from twisted mesenteric vessels. A caecum that is more midline than typical or frankly in the left lower quadrant can be a clue to malrotation.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound and radiography in intussusception, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Radiographs are nonspecific but may show paucity of gas or a soft tissue mass
CT is the primary diagnostic modality in the source
The target or pseudokidney sign consists of alternating bowel wall and mesenteric fat layers
Small bowel-to-small bowel intussusception is always symptomatic and always requires manual reduction
Ileocolic intussusception is suggested by diameter greater than 2.5 cm and internal mesenteric lymph nodes or fat
options_after: Radiographs are nonspecific but may show paucity of gas or a soft tissue mass
CT is the primary diagnostic modality in the source
The target or pseudokidney sign consists of alternating bowel wall and mesenteric fat layers
Small bowel-to-small bowel intussusception is characteristically symptomatic and characteristically requires manual reduction
Ileocolic intussusception is suggested by diameter greater than 2.5 cm and internal mesenteric lymph nodes or fat
updates.explanation: Radiographs are nonspecific in intussusception but may show paucity of gas or a soft-tissue mass. Ultrasound is the primary modality, demonstrating a target or pseudokidney sign from alternating bowel wall and mesenteric fat. Small bowel-to-small bowel intussusceptions are often incidental, transient and self-resolving. Ileocolic intussusception is distinguished by larger diameter and internal mesenteric lymph nodes or fat.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital proximal bowel obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All causes are medical and should be treated with water-soluble enema only
The main role of upper GI is to distinguish midgut volvulus from bowel atresia
Midgut volvulus requires emergent surgery
Bowel atresia requires emergent surgery before volvulus is excluded
Contrast enema is the first-line test for every proximal obstruction
options_after: Most causes are medical and should be treated with water-soluble enema in typical cases
The main role of upper GI is to distinguish midgut volvulus from bowel atresia
Midgut volvulus requires emergent surgery
Bowel atresia requires emergent surgery before volvulus is excluded
Contrast enema is the first-line test for routine proximal obstruction
updates.explanation: The source states that all causes of congenital proximal bowel obstruction are surgical. The primary purpose of upper GI is to distinguish volvulus, which requires emergent surgery, from bowel atresia, which requires non-emergent repair. Contrast enema is the imaging test of choice for distal obstruction, not the routine first-line test for proximal obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding associations and differential diagnosis of duodenal atresia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Associated abnormalities are absent in almost all cases
Down syndrome is the most common association, occurring in 30% of cases
Annular pancreas is not associated with duodenal atresia in the source
If distal bowel gas is present with a double bubble, the differential includes midgut volvulus, annular pancreas, duodenal stenosis and web
Duodenal anomalies are not associated with cardiac shunt vascularity
options_after: Duodenal atresia is usually isolated, with associated anomalies in fewer than 10% of cases.
Down syndrome is the most common association, occurring in 30% of cases
Annular pancreas is not associated with duodenal atresia in the source
If distal bowel gas is present with a double bubble, the differential includes midgut volvulus, annular pancreas, duodenal stenosis and web
Duodenal anomalies are not associated with cardiac shunt vascularity
updates.explanation: The source states that duodenal anomalies have associated abnormalities in 50% of cases, most commonly Down syndrome in 30%. Other associations include VACTERL, cardiac shunt vascularity, malrotation and annular pancreas, with annular pancreas seen in 20% of babies with duodenal atresia. If a double bubble has distal bowel gas, the differential includes volvulus, annular pancreas and less severe duodenal recanalisation variants.

updates.question_text: Regarding microcolon in neonatal distal obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Microcolon is abnormally small calibre colon, typically under 1 cm, secondary to disuse
The two most common causes are meconium ileus and ileal atresia
Jejunal atresia causes microcolon because there is no succus entericus to nourish the colon
Segmental Hirschsprung disease is the common Hirschsprung pattern and does not cause microcolon
Small left colon syndrome causes microcolon despite its name
options_after: Microcolon is abnormally small calibre colon, typically under 1 cm, secondary to disuse
The two most common causes are meconium ileus and ileal atresia
Jejunal atresia causes microcolon because there is an absence of succus entericus to nourish the colon
Segmental Hirschsprung disease is the common Hirschsprung pattern and does not cause microcolon
Small left colon syndrome causes microcolon despite its name
updates.explanation: Microcolon is a small-calibre colon due to disuse and requires relatively distal obstruction. The source states that meconium ileus and ileal atresia are the two commonest causes. Jejunal atresia does not cause microcolon because enough succus entericus is produced to nourish the colon. Segmental Hirschsprung disease is much more common than total colonic disease and does not cause microcolon; small left colon syndrome also does not cause microcolon.

updates.question_text: Regarding meconium ileus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It causes proximal obstruction from a duodenal web
It is the earliest manifestation of cystic fibrosis
Almost all babies with cystic fibrosis have meconium ileus, while about 10% of babies with meconium ileus have cystic fibrosis
The classic radiograph shows proximal obstruction with a double bubble and no distal gas
Contrast enema shows the smallest of all microcolons with rounded filling defects in a distended ileum
options_after: It causes proximal obstruction from a duodenal web
It is the earliest manifestation of cystic fibrosis
Almost most babies with cystic fibrosis have meconium ileus, while about 10% of babies with meconium ileus have cystic fibrosis
The classic radiograph shows proximal obstruction with a double bubble without distal gas
Contrast enema shows the smallest of all microcolons with rounded filling defects in a distended ileum
updates.explanation: Meconium ileus is obstruction from inspissated meconium in distal ileum and colon and is the earliest manifestation of cystic fibrosis. The source states that almost 100% of babies with meconium ileus have cystic fibrosis, while about 10% of babies with cystic fibrosis have meconium ileus. Radiographs show distal obstruction with possible right lower quadrant soap-bubble lucencies. Contrast enema shows a very small microcolon and rounded filling defects from inspissated meconium.

updates.question_text: Regarding meconium ileus complications and treatment, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Perforation can cause meconium peritonitis with abdominal or scrotal calcifications
Calcifications trapped between liver and diaphragm are seen in other common diffuse abdominal calcification causes
It is diagnosed and treated with therapeutic water-soluble gastrografin enema
Multiple attempts may be required to clear the inspissated meconium
Resistant cases never require surgery
options_after: Perforation can cause meconium peritonitis with abdominal or scrotal calcifications
Calcifications trapped between liver and diaphragm are seen in other common diffuse abdominal calcification causes
It is diagnosed and treated with therapeutic water-soluble gastrografin enema
Multiple attempts may be required to clear the inspissated meconium
Resistant cases will not require surgery
updates.explanation: Meconium ileus can perforate and produce meconium peritonitis with abdominal or scrotal calcifications. The source notes that calcifications trapped between the liver and diaphragm are not seen in other causes of diffuse abdominal calcification. Water-soluble gastrografin enema is both diagnostic and therapeutic, often requiring multiple attempts. Resistant cases may rarely need surgery.

updates.question_text: Regarding ileal or colonic atresia compared with meconium ileus, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Atresia of ileum or colon produces a normal-calibre colon distal to the atretic segment
Colonic atresia is the commonest neonatal obstruction cause in the source
Ileal and colonic atresia show rounded filling defects throughout bowel, identical to meconium ileus
Ileal and colonic atresia demonstrate an abrupt cutoff at the site of atresia
Ileal and colonic atresia always resolve with conservative enema therapy
options_after: Atresia of ileum or colon produces a normal-calibre colon distal to the atretic segment
Colonic atresia is the commonest neonatal obstruction cause in the source
Ileal and colonic atresia show rounded filling defects throughout bowel, closely comparable to meconium ileus
Ileal and colonic atresia demonstrate an abrupt cutoff at the site of atresia
Ileal and colonic atresia characteristically resolve with conservative enema therapy
updates.explanation: Ileal or colonic atresia creates a microcolon distal to the obstructed segment, and colonic atresia is rare. Unlike meconium ileus, ileal and colonic atresia demonstrate an abrupt cutoff at the site of atresia and do not show bowel filling defects. Rounded filling defects within distal ileum are the meconium ileus pattern, and atresia is a surgical obstruction rather than a conservative enema diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding small left colon syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a cause of true microcolon
It is strongly associated with cystic fibrosis and meconium ileus
It is caused by permanent aganglionosis of the anus and distal bowel
It is not associated with cystic fibrosis or meconium ileus despite the confusing name
It never resolves after enema treatment
options_after: It is a cause of true microcolon
It is strongly associated with cystic fibrosis and meconium ileus
It is caused by long-term aganglionosis of the anus and distal bowel
It is not associated with cystic fibrosis or meconium ileus despite the confusing name
It will not resolve after enema treatment
updates.explanation: Small left colon syndrome is also called functional immaturity of the colon or meconium plug syndrome and is the commonest diagnosis in neonates who fail to pass meconium. It reflects temporary functional immaturity of colonic ganglion cells, not permanent aganglionosis. It is not a cause of microcolon and is not associated with cystic fibrosis or meconium ileus. Contrast enema shows a small left colon with abrupt splenic-flexure transition and a normal-calibre distensible rectum, and the condition resolves with conservative therapy.

updates.question_text: Regarding Hirschsprung disease, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is caused by transient functional immaturity of colonic ganglion cells
The rectum is always spared and involved bowel is discontinuous
Contrast enema typically shows a gradual cone-shaped transition between narrowed distal colon and dilated proximal colon
A rectosigmoid index greater than 1 supports rectal involvement
Definitive diagnosis is made by therapeutic water-soluble enema
options_after: It is caused by transient functional immaturity of colonic ganglion cells
The rectum is characteristically spared and involved bowel is discontinuous
Contrast enema typically shows a gradual cone-shaped transition between narrowed distal colon and dilated proximal colon
A rectosigmoid index greater than 1 supports rectal involvement
Definitive diagnosis is made by therapeutic water-soluble enema
updates.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is distal bowel aganglionosis from arrested craniocaudal migration of vagal neural crest cells. Because the anus is always affected, involvement extends continuously proximally. Contrast enema usually shows a gradual cone-shaped transition from narrowed spastic distal colon to dilated proximal colon, and rectal involvement gives an abnormal rectosigmoid index less than 1. Definitive diagnosis is suction biopsy, and treatment is surgical.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric inguinal hernia causing bowel obstruction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Indirect inguinal hernias are more common and result from a patent processus vaginalis
Direct inguinal hernias are described as the usual mechanism in this paediatric section
Imaging can show bowel within the inguinal canal or scrotum
An irreducible hernia is described as having no risk of bowel incarceration
The section describes obstructing inguinal hernia as a primarily medical diagnosis without surgical relevance
options_after: Indirect inguinal hernias are more common and result from a patent processus vaginalis
Direct inguinal hernias are described as the usual mechanism in this paediatric section
Imaging can show bowel within the inguinal canal or scrotum
Irreducibility lowers the risk of bowel incarceration because the herniated bowel is fixed.
The section describes obstructing inguinal hernia as a primarily medical diagnosis without surgical relevance
updates.explanation: The section states that indirect inguinal hernias are more common and are caused by a patent processus vaginalis, maintaining peritoneal communication to the scrotum through the inguinal ring. Imaging of an obstructing hernia shows bowel in the inguinal canal or scrotum, as illustrated by the radiograph and ultrasound images. Irreducibility is specifically linked to risk of bowel incarceration.

updates.question_text: Regarding the clinical presentations and imaging of Meckel diverticulum, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Young children most commonly present with gastrointestinal bleeding if ectopic gastric mucosa is present
Pertechnetate scintigraphy is positive regardless of whether ectopic gastric mucosa is present
A Meckel diverticulum may act as a lead point for intussusception
Meckel diverticulitis reliably excludes appendicitis from the clinical differential
In adults, small bowel obstruction is described as the most common complication
options_after: Young children most commonly present with gastrointestinal bleeding if ectopic gastric mucosa is present
Pertechnetate scintigraphy is positive despite variation in whether ectopic gastric mucosa is present
A Meckel diverticulum may act as a lead point for intussusception
Meckel diverticulitis reliably excludes appendicitis from the clinical differential
In adults, small bowel obstruction is described as the most common complication
updates.explanation: The source states that young children most commonly present with bleeding when the diverticulum contains ectopic gastric mucosa. It can also cause intussusception by acting as a lead point, while adults most commonly present with small bowel obstruction. Pertechnetate scintigraphy is only positive when ectopic gastric mucosa is present, and Meckel diverticulitis can mimic rather than exclude appendicitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding Crohn disease in this paediatric bowel obstruction section, which statement is correct?
options_before: Crohn disease is excluded as a cause of childhood bowel obstruction
Newly diagnosed Crohn disease is described as almost exclusively an adult presentation
Crohn disease is listed only as a cause of neonatal bowel obstruction
Up to 30% of newly diagnosed Crohn disease presents in the paediatric population
Crohn disease is described as a cause of bowel obstruction only when Meckel diverticulum is also present
options_after: Crohn disease is excluded as a cause of childhood bowel obstruction
Newly diagnosed Crohn disease is described as predominantly an adult presentation
Crohn disease is listed primarily as a cause of neonatal bowel obstruction
Up to 30% of newly diagnosed Crohn disease presents in the paediatric population
Crohn disease is described as a cause of bowel obstruction primarily when Meckel diverticulum is also present
updates.explanation: The source explicitly notes that Crohn disease may be a cause of bowel obstruction and that up to 30% of newly diagnosed Crohn disease presents in the paediatric population. The other statements either remove Crohn disease from the obstruction differential or add restrictions not present in the source.

updates.question_text: Regarding neonatal hepatitis on hepatobiliary scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal hepatic uptake and clearance with no bowel excretion after 24 hours is the classic pattern
Delayed hepatic clearance beyond 12 hours may be seen
Any absence of bowel uptake at 60 minutes alone proves biliary atresia
The liver should show no uptake if neonatal hepatitis is present
Variable bowel excretion may occur
options_after: Normal hepatic uptake and clearance without bowel excretion after 24 hours is the classic pattern
Delayed hepatic clearance beyond 12 hours may be seen
Any absence of bowel uptake at 60 minutes alone proves biliary atresia
Absent hepatic uptake favours neonatal hepatitis over biliary atresia.
Variable bowel excretion may occur
updates.explanation: Neonatal hepatitis shows poor hepatic excretion, delayed hepatic clearance beyond 12 hours and variable bowel excretion. A single early image without bowel activity is insufficient by itself to diagnose biliary atresia. Normal hepatic uptake and clearance with persistent absence of bowel excretion at 24 hours is the pattern described for biliary atresia, not neonatal hepatitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding the differential approach to paediatric hepatobiliary masses in this section, which statement is correct?
options_before: The source states that imaging appearance alone always gives a single diagnosis
Differential diagnosis can usually be narrowed using cystic versus solid appearance, age and tumour markers
Tumour markers are not used in the source's approach to paediatric liver masses
Paediatric liver metastases are described as arising only from hepatoblastoma
Benign epithelial lesions such as focal nodular hyperplasia are discussed in detail in this paediatric subsection
options_after: The source states that imaging appearance alone characteristically gives a single diagnosis
Differential diagnosis can usually be narrowed using cystic versus solid appearance, age and tumour markers
Tumour markers are not used in the source's approach to paediatric liver masses
Paediatric liver metastases are described as arising primarily from hepatoblastoma
Benign epithelial lesions such as focal nodular hyperplasia are discussed in detail in this paediatric subsection
updates.explanation: The source states that the differential for paediatric liver tumours can usually be narrowed by imaging appearance, age and tumour markers such as AFP and endothelial growth factor. It also notes that liver metastases may be seen with neuroblastoma, Wilms tumour, sarcoma and Burkitt lymphoma. Benign epithelial lesions such as focal nodular hyperplasia and adenoma are deferred to the gastrointestinal imaging section.

updates.question_text: Regarding infantile hepatic haemangioma and haemangioendothelioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are the most common vascular hepatic tumours
They often occur in children under 1 year of age
AFP is elevated and endothelial growth factor is not elevated
They may cause congestive heart failure
Both entities are described as uniformly malignant with no tendency to involute
options_after: They are the most common vascular hepatic tumours
They often occur in children under 1 year of age
AFP is elevated and endothelial growth factor is not elevated
They may cause congestive heart failure
Both entities are described as uniformly malignant without tendency to involute
updates.explanation: Infantile haemangioma and haemangioendothelioma are described as related vascular neoplasms and the most common vascular hepatic tumours, often in children under 1 year. They can cause congestive heart failure in up to 25%. The source states that AFP is not elevated and endothelial growth factor is elevated. Infantile haemangioma is benign, while haemangioendothelioma is usually benign but has metastatic potential.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging features of hepatic infantile haemangioma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Lesions are typically hypovascular and T2 hypointense
They characteristically show no post-contrast enhancement
They are highly vascular and T2 hyperintense
Central necrosis, haemorrhage and calcification are excluded imaging features
They tend to show peripheral enhancement with delayed fill-in
options_after: Lesions are typically hypovascular and T2 hypointense
They characteristically fail to show post-contrast enhancement
They are highly vascular and T2 hyperintense
Central necrosis, haemorrhage and calcification are excluded imaging features
They tend to show peripheral enhancement with delayed fill-in
updates.explanation: The described hepatic infantile haemangiomas are highly vascular, T2 hyperintense lesions that tend to enhance peripherally with delayed fill-in. The source also allows calcification, central necrosis and haemorrhage, so excluding these features would be incorrect. The images demonstrate ultrasound vascularity, T2 hyperintensity and peripheral early enhancement with central non-opacification.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric hepatocellular carcinoma in this section, which statement is correct?
options_before: It typically occurs in children over 5 years of age and is often seen in the background of cirrhosis
It is the most common primary liver tumour of early childhood
AFP is never elevated in paediatric hepatocellular carcinoma
Fibrolamellar HCC is described as occurring only in cirrhotic toddlers
Venous invasion is described as a feature unique to hepatoblastoma and not seen in HCC
options_after: It typically occurs in children over 5 years of age and is often seen in the background of cirrhosis
It is the most common primary liver tumour of early childhood
AFP is not elevated in paediatric hepatocellular carcinoma
Fibrolamellar HCC is described as occurring primarily in cirrhotic toddlers
Venous invasion is described as a feature unique to hepatoblastoma and not seen in HCC
updates.explanation: The source states that paediatric HCC typically occurs in children older than 5 years and, similar to adults, is usually seen in the background of cirrhosis. AFP is elevated in conventional paediatric HCC, while the fibrolamellar variant is more common in patients aged 10-35 years without underlying liver disease or elevated AFP. HCC can show early arterial enhancement, rapid washout and venous invasion.

updates.question_text: Regarding distinguishing biliary atresia from neonatal hepatitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Ultrasound always excludes biliary atresia when a gallbladder is present
Any excretion into the gastrointestinal tract on hepatobiliary scintigraphy effectively rules out biliary atresia
Biliary atresia shows no small bowel excretion after 24 hours despite normal hepatic tracer uptake and clearance
Neonatal hepatitis is diagnosed by complete absence of hepatic tracer uptake
The HIDA agent is conjugated by the hepatocyte before biliary excretion
options_after: Ultrasound characteristically excludes biliary atresia when a gallbladder is present
Any excretion into the gastrointestinal tract on hepatobiliary scintigraphy effectively rules out biliary atresia
Biliary atresia shows no small bowel excretion after 24 hours despite normal hepatic tracer uptake and clearance
Neonatal hepatitis is diagnosed by complete absence of hepatic tracer uptake
The HIDA agent is conjugated by the hepatocyte before biliary excretion
updates.explanation: The key scintigraphic distinction is that biliary atresia shows normal hepatic uptake and clearance but no small bowel excretion after 24 hours. Conversely, any gastrointestinal excretion effectively rules out biliary atresia. A gallbladder can still be seen in a minority of biliary atresia cases, and the HIDA agent is transported into hepatocytes and excreted into bile rather than conjugated by the hepatocyte.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging evaluation of a child with febrile urinary tract infection and suspected reflux, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound is described as unsuitable for assessing VUR
A normal noncontrast ultrasound reliably excludes reflux
Urothelial thickening on ultrasound is suggestive of reflux
VCUG is avoided because it cannot evaluate the urethra
The work-up is controversial and may involve renal ultrasound and VCUG
options_after: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound is described as unsuitable for assessing VUR
A normal noncontrast ultrasound reliably excludes reflux
Urothelial thickening on ultrasound is suggestive of reflux
VCUG is avoided because it will not evaluate the urethra
The work-up is controversial and may involve renal ultrasound and VCUG
updates.explanation: The source states that the typical imaging evaluation of febrile UTI is controversial and may include renal ultrasound and VCUG. Noncontrast ultrasound is not sensitive for reflux, although urothelial thickening suggests reflux. Fluoroscopic VCUG is often preferred initially because it provides upper tract anatomy and urethral assessment, while contrast-enhanced ultrasound is increasingly used.

updates.question_text: Regarding treatment and nuclear medicine follow-up of VUR, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The goal of treatment is prevention of pyelonephritis and renal scarring
Grades I-III are initially treated surgically in all children
Radionuclide cystogram is the most sensitive test to evaluate reflux
DMSA scintigraphy is the gold standard for renal cortical scarring
High-grade reflux is initially managed medically in the same way as grade I disease in all children
options_after: The goal of treatment is prevention of pyelonephritis and renal scarring
Grades I-III are initially treated surgically in most children
Radionuclide cystogram is the most sensitive test to evaluate reflux
DMSA scintigraphy is the gold standard for renal cortical scarring
High-grade reflux is initially managed medically in the same way as grade I disease in most children
updates.explanation: The treatment goal is to prevent pyelonephritis and renal scarring, and grades I-III are initially treated medically with prophylactic antibiotics rather than automatic surgery. Radionuclide cystogram is described as the most sensitive test for reflux follow-up once anatomy is established, and DMSA scintigraphy is the gold standard for cortical scarring. Higher grade reflux is often treated surgically rather than managed identically to grade I disease.

updates.question_text: Regarding duplicated collecting systems and the Weigert-Meyer rule, which statement is correct?
options_before: The lower pole ureter inserts ectopically and is prone to obstruction
The upper pole ureter inserts orthotopically and is protected from obstruction
Both ureters must insert separately for the system to have no clinical significance
The upper pole ureter inserts ectopically, inferior and medial to the lower pole ureter
Reflux affects the obstructed upper pole moiety rather than the lower pole moiety
options_after: The lower pole ureter inserts ectopically and is prone to obstruction
The upper pole ureter inserts orthotopically and is protected from obstruction
Both ureters must insert separately for the system to lack clinical significance
The upper pole ureter inserts ectopically, inferior and medial to the lower pole ureter
Reflux affects the obstructed upper pole moiety rather than the lower pole moiety
updates.explanation: The Weigert-Meyer rule states that the upper pole ureter inserts ectopically, inferior and medial to the lower pole ureter, and is prone to obstruction, often from a ureterocele. The lower pole ureter inserts orthotopically but is prone to reflux. A duplicated system may be clinically insignificant if the ureters fuse before entering the bladder.

updates.question_text: Regarding ureteropelvic junction obstruction in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is the most common congenital anomaly of the genitourinary tract in neonates
It characteristically shows a dilated distal ureter with a normal renal pelvis
It is the most common cause of unilateral hydronephrosis in children
It is almost always caused by an ectopic ureterocele in a duplicated system
It is primarily a cause of bilateral bladder outlet obstruction in boys
options_after: It is the most common congenital anomaly of the genitourinary tract in neonates
It characteristically shows a dilated distal ureter with a normal renal pelvis
It is the most common cause of unilateral hydronephrosis in children
It is typically caused by an ectopic ureterocele in a duplicated system
It is primarily a cause of bilateral bladder outlet obstruction in boys
updates.explanation: UPJ obstruction is described as the most common congenital anomaly of the genitourinary tract in neonates and the most common cause of unilateral hydronephrosis in children. Imaging shows hydronephrosis with a dilated renal pelvis and normal calibre distal ureter. Ectopic ureterocele is a UVJ-level cause of obstruction, and posterior urethral valves cause bladder outlet obstruction rather than UPJ obstruction.

updates.question_text: Regarding posterior urethral valves and prune belly syndrome, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Posterior urethral valves are the most common cause of congenital bladder outlet obstruction
They occur exclusively in boys
Prune belly syndrome is the main differential and dilates only the prostatic urethra
Posterior urethral valves may produce a keyhole appearance on ultrasound
Prune belly syndrome is characterised by an isolated posterior urethral web at the verumontanum
options_after: Posterior urethral valves are the most common cause of congenital bladder outlet obstruction
They occur exclusively in boys
Prune belly syndrome is the main differential and dilates primarily the prostatic urethra
Posterior urethral valves may produce a keyhole appearance on ultrasound
Prune belly syndrome is characterised by an isolated posterior urethral web at the verumontanum
updates.explanation: Posterior urethral valves are the most common congenital bladder outlet obstruction and occur exclusively in boys. Ultrasound may show posterior urethral dilatation, trabeculated dilated bladder and bilateral hydronephrosis, producing a keyhole appearance. Prune belly syndrome is the main differential but causes dilatation of the entire collecting system and entire urethra rather than only the prostatic urethra; the obstructing posterior urethral web is the mechanism of posterior urethral valves.

updates.question_text: Regarding multilocular cystic nephroma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a malignant solid renal tumour arising from persistent metanephric blastema
It is a benign multiseptated cystic neoplasm
It has a bimodal distribution in young boys and middle-aged women
It has no association with DICER1 mutations or pleuropulmonary blastoma
It is reliably distinguished from cystic Wilms tumour by absence of any septal enhancement
options_after: It is a malignant solid renal tumour arising from persistent metanephric blastema
It is a benign multiseptated cystic neoplasm
It has a bimodal distribution in young boys and middle-aged women
It lacks association with DICER1 mutations or pleuropulmonary blastoma
It is reliably distinguished from cystic Wilms tumour by absence of any septal enhancement
updates.explanation: Multilocular cystic nephroma is a benign multiseptated cystic neoplasm with a bimodal age distribution in boys aged 3 months to 2 years and middle-aged women. It is associated with DICER1 mutations and pleuropulmonary blastoma. It can mimic cystic Wilms tumour and appears as a multiseptated cystic renal mass with enhancing septa, sometimes herniating into the renal pelvis.

updates.question_text: Regarding angiomyolipoma and the differential diagnosis of multiple solid renal masses, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Most angiomyolipomas contain macroscopic fat visible on CT or MRI
Angiomyolipoma larger than 4 cm has no haemorrhage risk in this source
Multiple angiomyolipomas are associated with tuberous sclerosis
The source's differential for multiple solid renal masses includes only lymphoma and excludes inflammatory disease
Multifocal pyelonephritis is excluded if the patient has fever
options_after: Most angiomyolipomas contain macroscopic fat visible on CT or MRI
Angiomyolipoma larger than 4 cm lacks haemorrhage risk in this source
Multiple angiomyolipomas are associated with tuberous sclerosis
The source's differential for multiple solid renal masses includes primarily lymphoma and excludes inflammatory disease
Multifocal pyelonephritis is excluded if the patient has fever
updates.explanation: Angiomyolipoma is a benign tumour made of blood vessels, muscle and fat, and most lesions contain macroscopic fat visible on CT or MRI. Multiple AMLs are associated with tuberous sclerosis, and lesions larger than 4 cm have haemorrhage risk. The differential diagram for multiple solid renal masses includes lymphoma, multifocal pyelonephritis, multiple infarcts and nephroblastomatosis, with fever supporting pyelonephritis rather than excluding it.

updates.question_text: Regarding neuroblastoma origin, presentation and associations, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Neuroblastoma is a primitive neural crest malignancy arising from the sympathetic chain
It most commonly arises in the anterior mediastinum
The adrenal gland is the most common site, followed by extra-adrenal retroperitoneum and posterior mediastinum
The source states that neuroblastoma has no syndromic associations
Opsoclonus-myoclonus may occur and is more frequently associated with thoracic primary lesions
options_after: Neuroblastoma is a primitive neural crest malignancy arising from the sympathetic chain
It most commonly arises in the anterior mediastinum
The adrenal gland is the most common site, followed by extra-adrenal retroperitoneum and posterior mediastinum
The source states that neuroblastoma lacks syndromic associations
Opsoclonus-myoclonus may occur and is more frequently associated with thoracic primary lesions
updates.explanation: Neuroblastoma is a primitive neural crest cell malignancy arising from the sympathetic chain, most often from the adrenal gland, then extra-adrenal retroperitoneum and posterior mediastinum. It is associated with NF1, Hirschsprung disease, DiGeorge syndrome and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Opsoclonus-myoclonus, with dancing eyes and dancing feet, may occur and is more frequent with thoracic primary lesions.

updates.question_text: Regarding ganglioneuroma and adrenal haemorrhage, which statement is correct?
options_before: Ganglioneuroma is more common in neonates than adrenal haemorrhage
Ganglioneuroma is always I-123 MIBG negative
Adrenal haemorrhage enlarges on follow-up and should not involute
Adrenal haemorrhage is typically a hypoechoic avascular suprarenal mass that involutes on follow-up
Neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma are distinguished because neuroblastoma never restricts diffusion
options_after: Ganglioneuroma is more common in neonates than adrenal haemorrhage
Ganglioneuroma is characteristically I-123 MIBG negative
Adrenal haemorrhage enlarges on follow-up and should not involute
Adrenal haemorrhage is typically a hypoechoic avascular suprarenal mass that involutes on follow-up
Neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma are distinguished because neuroblastoma will not restrict diffusion
updates.explanation: Adrenal haemorrhage is the most common adrenal mass-like lesion in neonates and is typically diagnosed on ultrasound as a hypoechoic avascular suprarenal mass. It may resemble neuroblastoma initially, but follow-up demonstrates involution; old haemorrhage may calcify. Ganglioneuroma affects slightly older children and only about half are MIBG-positive, while neuroblastoma classically restricts diffusion.

updates.question_text: Regarding congenital adrenal hyperplasia and adrenocortical carcinoma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CAH most commonly results from 21-hydroxylase deficiency
CAH imaging can suggest uniformly enlarged adrenals with a cerebriform appearance
Adrenocortical carcinoma in children may be associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann and Li-Fraumeni syndromes
Adrenocortical carcinoma is described as a common paediatric adrenal lesion with no adult peak
CAH usually presents only as a calcified unilateral adrenal mass
options_after: CAH most commonly results from 21-hydroxylase deficiency
CAH imaging can suggest uniformly enlarged adrenals with a cerebriform appearance
Adrenocortical carcinoma in children may be associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann and Li-Fraumeni syndromes
Adrenocortical carcinoma is described as a common paediatric adrenal lesion without adult peak
CAH usually presents primarily as a calcified unilateral adrenal mass
updates.explanation: CAH comprises enzymatic disorders in cortisol synthesis and most commonly reflects 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Imaging findings that suggest CAH include uniformly enlarged adrenals, with length greater than 20 mm or limb width greater than 4 mm, and a cerebriform appearance. Adrenocortical carcinoma is extremely rare, has a bimodal age distribution and may be associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann and Li-Fraumeni syndromes.

updates.question_text: Regarding cystic paediatric pelvic masses seen in either sex, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The most likely cause of a cystic paediatric pelvic mass is usually a solid neoplasm
A urachal anomaly results from incomplete obliteration of the embryologic allantois
A patent urachus is a non-communicating cyst between bladder and umbilicus
A rectal duplication cyst is normally left unresected because it has no malignant potential
Vesicourachal diverticulum is a blind-ending bladder diverticulum
options_after: The most likely cause of a cystic paediatric pelvic mass is usually a solid neoplasm
A urachal anomaly results from incomplete obliteration of the embryologic allantois
A patent urachus is a non-communicating cyst between bladder and umbilicus
A rectal duplication cyst is normally left unresected because it lacks malignant potential
Vesicourachal diverticulum is a blind-ending bladder diverticulum
updates.explanation: The source states that cystic paediatric pelvic masses are most likely congenital genitourinary anomalies. Urachal anomalies result from incomplete allantoic obliteration; patent urachus is a connection between bladder and umbilicus, while a urachal cyst is the non-communicating cyst between them. Rectal duplication cysts usually occur in the retrorectal space and are resected due to malignant potential. A vesicourachal diverticulum is a blind-ending bladder diverticulum.

updates.question_text: Regarding sex-specific cystic pelvic masses in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Hydrometrocolpos refers to dilatation of both vagina and uterus with fluid
Hematometrocolpos occurs at menarche with vaginal outflow tract obstruction
A Mullerian duct cyst in boys results from incomplete regression of Mullerian ducts
A prostatic utricle arises from the anterior urethra near the bladder dome
Ovarian dermoid cyst is listed under boys-only cystic pelvic masses
options_after: Hydrometrocolpos refers to dilatation of both vagina and uterus with fluid
Hematometrocolpos occurs at menarche with vaginal outflow tract obstruction
A Mullerian duct cyst in boys results from incomplete regression of Mullerian ducts
A prostatic utricle arises from the anterior urethra near the bladder dome
Ovarian dermoid cyst is listed under boys-predominant cystic pelvic masses
updates.explanation: Hydrometrocolpos is fluid distension of the vagina and uterus, while hematometrocolpos is blood distension at menarche due to vaginal outflow tract obstruction such as imperforate hymen. In boys, incomplete Mullerian duct regression can form a Mullerian duct cyst. The prostatic utricle is a midline terminal Mullerian remnant arising from the posterior urethra near the verumontanum, and ovarian dermoid cyst is listed for girls.

updates.question_text: Regarding solid paediatric pelvic masses in this section, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Solid pelvic masses are usually congenital genitourinary anomalies and are less concerning for neoplasm
Rhabdomyosarcoma is described as a rare adult sarcoma rather than a childhood sarcoma
Rhabdomyosarcoma occurs equally commonly in the pelvis and head and neck, together making up almost 80% of cases
Sacrococcygeal teratoma is always purely cystic without fat or solid components
The botryoid variant of rhabdomyosarcoma has a lobulated bunch-of-grapes appearance
options_after: Solid pelvic masses are usually congenital genitourinary anomalies and are less concerning for neoplasm
Rhabdomyosarcoma is described as a rare adult sarcoma rather than a childhood sarcoma
Rhabdomyosarcoma occurs equally commonly in the pelvis and head and neck, together making up almost 80% of cases
Sacrococcygeal teratoma is characteristically purely cystic without fat or solid components
The botryoid variant of rhabdomyosarcoma has a lobulated bunch-of-grapes appearance
updates.explanation: Solid pelvic masses are less likely to be congenital genitourinary anomalies and are more concerning for neoplasm. Rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common childhood sarcoma and occurs equally commonly in the pelvis and head and neck, with these sites together accounting for almost 80% of cases. The botryoid variant has a lobulated bunch-of-grapes appearance. Sacrococcygeal teratoma is heterogeneous with cystic, solid and fatty components.

updates.question_text: Regarding fractures in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Paediatric bones are more elastic than adult bones and may buckle, greenstick or plastically deform
Complete fracture healing is expected within 7-10 days in most children
Repeat radiographs in 7-10 days can help when the initial diagnosis is equivocal
Metaphyseal, skull and costochondral junction fractures always produce florid periosteal reaction
Periosteal reaction may be seen within the first week of fracture healing
options_after: Paediatric bones are more elastic than adult bones and may buckle, greenstick or plastically deform
Complete fracture healing is expected within 7-10 days in most children
Repeat radiographs in 7-10 days can help when the initial diagnosis is equivocal
Metaphyseal, skull and costochondral junction fractures characteristically produce florid periosteal reaction
Periosteal reaction may be seen within the first week of fracture healing
updates.explanation: The source emphasises that paediatric bones are more elastic and therefore often bend rather than break, producing buckle, greenstick and plastic fractures. A general dating timeline is periosteal reaction in less than a week and complete healing at around 12 weeks. Repeat radiographs after 7-10 days can reveal periosteal reaction when the original study is equivocal, although some fracture types may heal without periosteal reaction.

updates.question_text: Regarding specific Salter-Harris examples described in the source, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Toddler fracture is listed as the classic Salter-Harris V example
Gymnast's wrist can mimic rickets because of chronic physeal widening
Juvenile Tillaux fracture is a Salter-Harris III injury of the distal tibia
Triplane fracture is described as a simple metaphyseal fracture only
Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is listed as a Salter-Harris I example
options_after: Toddler fracture is listed as the classic Salter-Harris V example
Gymnast's wrist can mimic rickets because of chronic physeal widening
Juvenile Tillaux fracture is a Salter-Harris III injury of the distal tibia
Triplane fracture is described as a simple metaphyseal fracture in typical cases
Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is listed as a Salter-Harris I example
updates.explanation: The source lists SCFE and gymnast's wrist as Salter-Harris I examples, with gymnast's wrist potentially mimicking rickets through chronic physeal widening. Juvenile Tillaux fracture is a distal tibial epiphyseal and physeal Salter-Harris III injury. Triplane fracture is a complex distal tibial injury with metaphyseal, physeal and epiphyseal components, not a simple metaphyseal fracture.

updates.question_text: Regarding Salter-Harris V injury, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is usually obvious on initial radiographs because of marked displacement
It is caused by avulsion of a pelvic apophysis
It has the best prognosis of all Salter-Harris injuries
It is a crushed physis injury, often from axial loading
It is defined by a fracture through the epiphysis and metaphysis
options_after: It is usually obvious on initial radiographs because of marked displacement
It is caused by avulsion of a pelvic apophysis
It has the best prognosis of most Salter-Harris injuries
It is a crushed physis injury, often from axial loading
It is defined by a fracture through the epiphysis and metaphysis
updates.explanation: Salter-Harris V is a crush injury of the physis, often caused by axial loading. It can be easy to miss initially and is sometimes recognised retrospectively on comparison studies. The prognosis is very poor compared with lower-grade physeal injuries.

updates.question_text: Regarding elbow effusion and alignment lines in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A visible posterior fat pad indicates elbow joint effusion
A thin anterior fat pad is never normally seen
The anterior humeral line should miss the capitellum on a normal lateral view
The radiocapitellar line should pass through the capitellum on all views
An abnormal anterior humeral line suggests supracondylar fracture
options_after: A visible posterior fat pad indicates elbow joint effusion
A thin anterior fat pad is not normally seen
The anterior humeral line should miss the capitellum on a normal lateral view
The radiocapitellar line should pass through the capitellum on all views
An abnormal anterior humeral line suggests supracondylar fracture
updates.explanation: The posterior fat pad is not normally visible and indicates an effusion when present. The anterior fat pad may normally be seen as a thin linear lucency. The anterior humeral line should intersect the middle third of the capitellum on the lateral view, and abnormality suggests supracondylar fracture. The radiocapitellar line should pass through the capitellum on every view.

updates.question_text: Regarding pelvic apophyseal avulsion injuries, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An apophysis contributes primarily to longitudinal bone growth
Pelvic apophyses fuse during early infancy
The apophysis is the weakest link of the myotendinous unit in adolescents
Subacute apophyseal avulsions can appear aggressive because of mixed lytic and sclerotic donor-site change
These injuries occur almost exclusively in elderly adults
options_after: An apophysis contributes primarily to longitudinal bone growth
Pelvic apophyses fuse during early infancy
The apophysis is the weakest link of the myotendinous unit in adolescents
Subacute apophyseal avulsions can appear aggressive because of mixed lytic and sclerotic donor-site change
These injuries occur predominantly in elderly adults
updates.explanation: An apophysis is an ossification centre at a tendon attachment and is a growth plate that does not contribute to longitudinal growth. Pelvic apophyses close relatively late, making them vulnerable in athletic adolescents with strong muscles. Subacute injuries may look aggressive because the donor site develops mixed lytic and sclerotic change.

updates.question_text: Regarding a lesser trochanter avulsion fracture, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is always physiologic in older adults
It represents an adductor origin avulsion
It is caused by gluteus medius insertion in adolescents
It is specific for non-accidental trauma
In adults it is suspicious for a pathological fracture
options_after: It is characteristically physiologic in older adults
It represents an adductor origin avulsion
It is caused by gluteus medius insertion in adolescents
It is specific for non-accidental trauma
In adults it is suspicious for a pathological fracture
updates.explanation: The lesser trochanter is the iliopsoas insertion and may avulse in an athletic adolescent. The source specifically warns that a lesser trochanteric fracture in an adult is suspicious for a pathological fracture. This distinction prevents mislabelling an adult malignant avulsion-type presentation as a simple sports injury.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging for suspected child abuse, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A limited radiograph of only the symptomatic limb is the recommended complete assessment in children under two
A complete skeletal survey with high-resolution bone technique is recommended for children under two when abuse is suspected
Bone scintigraphy is more sensitive for skull fractures than radiography
Bone scintigraphy is more sensitive for posterior rib fractures
The radiologist should review the images while the child remains in the department
options_after: A limited radiograph of primarily the symptomatic limb is the recommended complete assessment in children under two
A complete skeletal survey with high-resolution bone technique is recommended for children under two when abuse is suspected
Bone scintigraphy is more sensitive for skull fractures than radiography
Bone scintigraphy is more sensitive for posterior rib fractures
The radiologist should review the images while the child remains in the department
updates.explanation: When there is concern for child abuse, the source recommends a complete skeletal survey using high-resolution bone technique in children under two, including long bones, oblique rib views, skull, pelvis, hands and feet, and spine. The radiologist reviews images while the child is still in the department. Bone scintigraphy is more sensitive for posterior rib fractures but has higher radiation dose, is insensitive for skull fractures and cannot assess fracture age morphology.

updates.question_text: Regarding fracture dating in suspected non-accidental trauma, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Callus formation suggests a fracture is at least about one week old
Absence of callus proves that a fracture occurred within the previous 24 hours
Absence of callus generally suggests a fracture is less than two weeks old
Healing speed is identical in all children regardless of age or nutrition
Malnourishment can alter fracture healing speed
options_after: Callus formation suggests a fracture is at least about one week old
Absence of callus proves that a fracture occurred within the previous 24 hours
Absence of callus generally suggests a fracture is less than two weeks old
Healing speed is closely comparable in most children despite variation in age or nutrition
Malnourishment can alter fracture healing speed
updates.explanation: The source uses rough guidelines: absence of callus suggests a fracture is less than two weeks old, while callus suggests at least one week. Younger children form callus and heal faster, and malnourishment can alter the speed of healing. These are approximate radiological estimates rather than precise dating tools.

updates.question_text: Regarding ultrasound criteria for DDH, which statement is correct?
options_before: The alpha angle is measured between the labrum and femoral shaft
More than 80% femoral head coverage is required for normality
An alpha angle below 60 degrees or femoral head coverage below 50% is abnormal
Radiographs are preferred before 6 weeks because ultrasound cannot show the cartilaginous head
The alpha angle should normally be below 30 degrees by age two
options_after: The alpha angle is measured between the labrum and femoral shaft
More than 80% femoral head coverage is required for normality
An alpha angle below 60 degrees or femoral head coverage below 50% is abnormal
Radiographs are preferred before 6 weeks because ultrasound will not show the cartilaginous head
The alpha angle should normally be below 30 degrees by age two
updates.explanation: The alpha angle is measured on coronal hip ultrasound between the bony ilium and acetabular roof. A normal alpha angle is greater than 60 degrees, and the bony acetabulum should cover at least half of the cartilaginous femoral head. An alpha angle below 60 degrees or coverage below 50% suggests DDH.

updates.question_text: Regarding important imaging goals and complications in SCFE, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The contralateral hip can be ignored because SCFE is never bilateral
The imaging goal includes identifying preslip SCFE before epiphysis and metaphysis become displaced
Preslip SCFE is better detected on radiography than MRI
Osteonecrosis of the femoral head is the major complication
Treatment is long-term antibiotics
options_after: The contralateral hip can be ignored because SCFE is not bilateral
The imaging goal includes identifying preslip SCFE before epiphysis and metaphysis become displaced
Preslip SCFE is better detected on radiography than MRI
Osteonecrosis of the femoral head is the major complication
Treatment is long-term antibiotics
updates.explanation: The source states that the contralateral hip should always be carefully evaluated because SCFE is frequently bilateral and asymmetric. A key imaging goal is to identify preslip SCFE, where the epiphysis and metaphysis remain aligned but physeal lucency suggests oedema; MRI is more sensitive for these findings. Osteonecrosis of the femoral head is the major complication, and treatment is screw fixation.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is most commonly haematogenous
The metaphyseal marrow is the common initial site of seeding
Salmonella is the common organism in all children without sickle cell disease
Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism in haematogenous osteomyelitis
Initial radiographic findings are usually obvious on the first day of symptoms
options_after: It is most commonly haematogenous
The metaphyseal marrow is the common initial site of seeding
Salmonella is the common organism in most children without sickle cell disease
Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism in haematogenous osteomyelitis
Initial radiographic findings are usually obvious on the first day of symptoms
updates.explanation: Paediatric osteomyelitis is usually haematogenous, initially seeding the well-vascularised metaphyseal marrow. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism, with Salmonella particularly noted in sickle cell patients. Radiographic findings are often subtle early and typically take 10-14 days to become evident.

updates.question_text: Regarding transphyseal spread of osteomyelitis, which statement is correct?
options_before: Infection crosses the physis most easily in older children because capillaries do not cross the physis
In infants, transphyseal vessels allow metaphyseal infection to cross into the epiphysis and joint
In adults, fused growth plates prevent epiphyseal spread
Epiphysitis and septic arthritis are impossible complications of infant osteomyelitis
Transphyseal spread is the same at all ages
options_after: Infection crosses the physis most easily in older children because capillaries do not cross the physis
In infants, transphyseal vessels allow metaphyseal infection to cross into the epiphysis and joint
In adults, fused growth plates prevent epiphyseal spread
Epiphysitis and septic arthritis are not considered a realistic possibility complications of infant osteomyelitis
Transphyseal spread is the same at most ages
updates.explanation: In infants, transphyseal vessels arise from the metaphysis and supply the epiphysis, allowing infection to cross the physis and produce epiphysitis or septic arthritis. In older children, capillaries do not cross the physis, so transphyseal extension is uncommon. When growth plates fuse in adults, infection can again extend into the epiphysis.

updates.question_text: Regarding imaging sensitivity and progression in osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI and scintigraphy are more sensitive than radiographs for early osteomyelitis
Bone scan findings cannot appear until at least 3 weeks after symptom onset
Initial radiographic focal osteopenia excludes hyperaemia as a mechanism
Periosteal reaction is absent in children because the periosteum is tightly adherent
The infection may spread through cortex and uplift the loosely adherent paediatric periosteum
options_after: MRI and scintigraphy are more sensitive than radiographs for early osteomyelitis
Bone scan findings will not appear until at least 3 weeks after symptom onset
Initial radiographic focal osteopenia excludes hyperaemia as a mechanism
Periosteal reaction is absent in children because the periosteum is tightly adherent
The infection may spread through cortex and uplift the loosely adherent paediatric periosteum
updates.explanation: MRI and scintigraphy are much more sensitive than radiography for early osteomyelitis. Bone scan abnormalities may be seen within 24-72 hours of symptom onset. Early radiographic focal osteopenia can reflect hyperaemia rather than excluding it. Infection may later erode through cortex and lift the loosely adherent paediatric periosteum, producing prominent periosteal reaction.

updates.question_text: Regarding paediatric discitis and spinal osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Isolated discitis is unique to adults because children lack direct disc blood supply
Isolated discitis is unique to children because vessels directly feed the intervertebral disc
Typical history is a young child with back pain or refusal to sit, often after upper respiratory tract infection
Plain radiographs are always abnormal at symptom onset
MRI may show disc space narrowing with marrow oedema in two adjacent vertebral bodies
options_after: Isolated discitis is unique to adults because children lack direct disc blood supply
Isolated discitis is unique to children because vessels directly feed the intervertebral disc
Typical history is a young child with back pain or refusal to sit, often after upper respiratory tract infection
Plain radiographs are characteristically abnormal at symptom onset
MRI may show disc space narrowing with marrow oedema in two adjacent vertebral bodies
updates.explanation: Isolated discitis is unique to children because blood vessels directly feed the intervertebral disc. The typical presentation is a young child up to 4 years old with preceding upper respiratory infection, back pain or refusal to sit, most often affecting the lumbar spine. Radiographs may be subtle or normal, so persistent back pain should prompt MRI when suspicion is high.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI features of paediatric discitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI may show narrowing of the disc space
Two adjacent vertebral bodies may show marrow oedema
Enhancement is limited to the disc and never involves vertebral bodies
Enhancement and oedema may extend into the soft tissues or epidural space
Persistent back pain in children is never normal and warrants further evaluation when suspicion is high
options_after: MRI may show narrowing of the disc space
Two adjacent vertebral bodies may show marrow oedema
Enhancement is limited to the disc and will not involve vertebral bodies
Enhancement and oedema may extend into the soft tissues or epidural space
Persistent back pain in children is never normal and warrants further evaluation when suspicion is high
updates.explanation: MRI in discitis may show disc space narrowing and marrow oedema of two adjacent vertebral bodies. The affected vertebral bodies may enhance, and oedema or enhancement can extend into soft tissues or epidural space. The source stresses that persistent back pain is never normal in children, so MRI is recommended when suspicion remains high.

updates.question_text: Regarding chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a pyogenic infection requiring positive blood culture for diagnosis
It cannot mimic infectious osteomyelitis on MRI
It is a nonpyogenic inflammatory disorder that tends to involve lower extremity long bones
It is typically diagnosed by demonstrating a soft tissue abscess, bony sequestrum or fistula
It is usually a diagnosis of exclusion and may require biopsy to exclude pyogenic infection
options_after: It is a pyogenic infection requiring positive blood culture for diagnosis
It will not mimic infectious osteomyelitis on MRI
It is a nonpyogenic inflammatory disorder that tends to involve lower extremity long bones
It is typically diagnosed by demonstrating a soft tissue abscess, bony sequestrum or fistula
It is usually a diagnosis of exclusion and may require biopsy to exclude pyogenic infection
updates.explanation: CRMO is a nonpyogenic inflammatory disorder that can mimic osteomyelitis and tends to affect lower extremity long bones. It is typically a diagnosis of exclusion and biopsy may be needed to exclude pyogenic infection. Unlike infectious osteomyelitis, CRMO does not feature soft tissue abscess, bony sequestra or fistula.

updates.question_text: Regarding cleidocranial dysostosis and wormian bones, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Delayed skull ossification and widened pubic symphysis are not described in cleidocranial dysostosis
Affected patients usually have severe cognitive impairment and normal height
Wormian bones are strongly associated with cleidocranial dysostosis but are nonspecific
Wormian bones are seen only in cleidocranial dysostosis
Complete or partial absence of the clavicles is the key radiographic finding
options_after: Delayed skull ossification and widened pubic symphysis are not described in cleidocranial dysostosis
Affected patients usually have severe cognitive impairment and normal height
Wormian bones are strongly associated with cleidocranial dysostosis but are nonspecific
Wormian bones are seen primarily in cleidocranial dysostosis
Complete or partial absence of the clavicles is the key radiographic finding
updates.explanation: The key cleidocranial dysostosis finding is complete or partial absence of the clavicles. Wormian bones are strongly associated but nonspecific, also appearing in hypothyroidism, osteogenesis imperfecta, healing rickets and Down syndrome. Additional findings do include neonatal delayed skull ossification and widened pubic symphysis later in life, so denying those findings is incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding rickets, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It results from inadequate vitamin D or abnormal vitamin D metabolism
It affects the zone of provisional calcification and growing bones
It is typically seen in newborns because maternal vitamin D is no longer functional
Radiographs may show metaphyseal expansion, irregularity, fraying and cupping
The rachitic rosary represents anterior rib cupping with widening of rib epiphyseal cartilage
options_after: It results from inadequate vitamin D or abnormal vitamin D metabolism
It affects the zone of provisional calcification and growing bones
It is typically seen in newborns because maternal vitamin D is not currently functional
Radiographs may show metaphyseal expansion, irregularity, fraying and cupping
The rachitic rosary represents anterior rib cupping with widening of rib epiphyseal cartilage
updates.explanation: Rickets is caused by inadequate vitamin D or abnormal vitamin D metabolism and affects calcification at the zone of provisional calcification. It mostly affects growing bones but is not seen in newborns because maternal vitamin D remains functional. Radiographs show metaphyseal expansion, irregularity, fraying and cupping, and the rachitic rosary reflects anterior rib cupping with widening of the rib epiphyseal cartilage.

updates.question_text: Regarding osseous LCH appearances by site, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Skull lesions may be bevelled edge or punched-out lytic lesions
Flat bones do not show a hole-within-a-hole lytic lesion
Spinal involvement may produce vertebra plana
Maxillary involvement does not produce floating teeth
Long-bone lesions are always sharply geographic with a narrow transition zone
options_after: Skull lesions may be bevelled edge or punched-out lytic lesions
Flat bones do not show a hole-within-a-hole lytic lesion
Spinal involvement may produce vertebra plana
Maxillary involvement does not produce floating teeth
Long-bone lesions are characteristically sharply geographic with a narrow transition zone
updates.explanation: The source describes site-dependent LCH appearances: skull lesions can be bevelled or punched out, flat bones can show a hole-within-a-hole appearance, spine can show vertebra plana and maxillary disease can produce floating teeth. Long-bone LCH may show permeative destruction with a wide transition zone before later lysis and faint sclerosis, not an always sharply geographic pattern.

updates.question_text: Regarding Sever disease, which statement is correct?
options_before: It is osteochondrosis of the medial epicondyle
It is calcaneal apophysitis and a cause of heel pain
Sclerosis of the calcaneal apophysis is always diagnostic of symptomatic disease
It is osteochondrosis of the second metatarsal head
It produces tibia vara and internal rotation
options_after: It is osteochondrosis of the medial epicondyle
It is calcaneal apophysitis and a cause of heel pain
Sclerosis of the calcaneal apophysis is characteristically diagnostic of symptomatic disease
It is osteochondrosis of the second metatarsal head
It produces tibia vara and internal rotation
updates.explanation: Sever disease is calcaneal apophysitis rather than an osteochondrosis and is a cause of heel pain. The source notes that sclerosis of the calcaneal apophysis is nonspecific and can be seen in asymptomatic children, although greater fragmentation may be associated with pain. Little league elbow affects the medial epicondyle and Freiberg infraction affects the second metatarsal head.

updates.question_text: Regarding periosteal reaction in infants and children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Periosteal reaction is a nonspecific response to injury or chronic stress with new bone production
Periostitis and periosteal new bone formation are commonly used as synonyms
It can be due to trauma, infection, inflammation, neoplasm or metabolic disturbance
Tumour- or infection-related periosteal reaction is never aggressive in appearance
The periosteum covers the entire bone surface including cartilage-covered regions
options_after: Periosteal reaction is a nonspecific response to injury or chronic stress with new bone production
Periostitis and periosteal new bone formation are commonly used as synonyms
It can be due to trauma, infection, inflammation, neoplasm or metabolic disturbance
Tumour- or infection-related periosteal reaction is not aggressive in appearance
The periosteum covers the entire bone surface including cartilage-covered regions
updates.explanation: Periosteal reaction is a nonspecific new-bone response to irritation or chronic stress, and terms such as periostitis and periosteal new bone formation are used similarly. Causes include trauma, infection, inflammation, neoplasm and metabolic disturbance. Tumours and infection can produce aggressive periosteal reaction. The periosteum covers bone except where cartilage covers the surface.

updates.question_text: Regarding causes and patterns of periosteal reaction in this section, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Physiologic periosteal reaction occurs in infants aged 1-4 months and is smooth, thin and symmetric
Neonates receiving prostaglandin therapy may develop periosteal reaction
Congenital syphilis is excluded from the causes of periosteal reaction
Rickets, scurvy and hypervitaminosis A can cause periosteal reaction
Caffey disease causes periostitis only in the distal tibia
options_after: Physiologic periosteal reaction occurs in infants aged 1-4 months and is smooth, thin and symmetric
Neonates receiving prostaglandin therapy may develop periosteal reaction
Congenital syphilis is excluded from the causes of periosteal reaction
Rickets, scurvy and hypervitaminosis A can cause periosteal reaction
Caffey disease causes periostitis primarily in the distal tibia
updates.explanation: Physiologic periosteal reaction occurs in infants aged 1-4 months, is smooth and thin and usually symmetrically involves the medial or lateral diaphyses of long bones. Prostaglandin therapy, congenital syphilis and metabolic disorders including rickets, scurvy and hypervitaminosis A can cause periosteal reaction. Caffey disease is infantile cortical hyperostosis affecting sites such as mandible, scapula and clavicle.

updates.question_text: Regarding torticollis and coalitions in children, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Torticollis is caused by fibromatosis coli with idiopathic sternocleidomastoid enlargement
It usually requires operative correction rather than physical therapy
Tarsal coalition is abnormal joining of two normally separate tarsal bones
Talocalcaneal and calcaneonavicular coalitions are rare and together account for less than 10% of tarsal coalitions
Tarsal coalition is always symptomatic at birth before ossification begins
options_after: Torticollis is caused by fibromatosis coli with idiopathic sternocleidomastoid enlargement
It usually requires operative correction rather than physical therapy
Tarsal coalition is abnormal joining of two normally separate tarsal bones
Talocalcaneal and calcaneonavicular coalitions are rare and together account for less than 10% of tarsal coalitions
Tarsal coalition is characteristically symptomatic at birth before ossification begins
updates.explanation: Torticollis is caused by fibromatosis coli, an idiopathic sternocleidomastoid enlargement, and usually resolves with physical therapy. Tarsal coalition is abnormal union of normally separate tarsal bones, and talocalcaneal plus calcaneonavicular coalitions make up about 90% of cases. It presents with foot pain as the coalition begins to ossify, not necessarily at birth.

updates.question_text: Regarding carpal coalition, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is abnormal joining of metacarpal bones rather than carpal bones
It is usually asymptomatic but may cause wrist pain
Like tarsal coalition, it is only osseous and not fibrous or cartilaginous
Lunotriquetral coalition is the most common carpal coalition
Capitohamate coalition is the least common carpal coalition
options_after: It is abnormal joining of metacarpal bones rather than carpal bones
It is usually asymptomatic but may cause wrist pain
Like tarsal coalition, it is primarily osseous and not fibrous or cartilaginous
Lunotriquetral coalition is the most common carpal coalition
Capitohamate coalition is the least common carpal coalition
updates.explanation: Carpal coalition is abnormal joining of carpal bones and is usually asymptomatic, though it can cause wrist pain. Like tarsal coalition, it may be fibrous, cartilaginous or osseous. Lunotriquetral coalition is the most common carpal coalition, and capitohamate is the second most common.

updates.question_text: Regarding the grading of germinal matrix-intraventricular haemorrhage, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Grade II haemorrhage requires ventriculomegaly
Grade II haemorrhage extends into the ventricles without ventriculomegaly
Grade III haemorrhage extends into the ventricles with ventriculomegaly
Parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction is identical to the old concept of direct extraventricular extension
Parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction can coexist with any grade
options_after: Grade II haemorrhage requires ventriculomegaly
Grade II haemorrhage extends into the ventricles without ventriculomegaly
Grade III haemorrhage extends into the ventricles with ventriculomegaly
Parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction is closely comparable to the old concept of direct extraventricular extension
Parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction can coexist with any grade
updates.explanation: Grade II haemorrhage extends into the ventricles without ventriculomegaly, whereas grade III haemorrhage includes ventriculomegaly. Parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction may coexist with any grade. The former grade IV category is now understood as periventricular haemorrhagic infarction from venous obstruction and congestion, not simple extension of ventricular haemorrhage into parenchyma.

updates.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the developmental basis of normal cortex in this source?
options_before: Normal cortex depends only on expansion of the dorsal brainstem
Normal cortex develops from pial overmigration through defects in the limiting membrane
Normal cortex depends on germinal matrix cell migration followed by organisation into the normal six-layered cortical lamination
