Normal cortex is organised into four primitive layers throughout life
Normal cortex develops independently of the primordial ventricular system
options_after: Normal cortex depends primarily on expansion of the dorsal brainstem
Normal cortex develops from pial overmigration through defects in the limiting membrane
Normal cortex depends on germinal matrix cell migration followed by organisation into the normal six-layered cortical lamination
Normal cortex is organised into four primitive layers throughout life
Normal cortex develops independently of the primordial ventricular system
updates.explanation: The primitive brain forms around the primordial ventricular system, which is lined by pluripotent germinal matrix cells. Normal cortical development depends on migration of these cells and subsequent organisation into the normal six-layered cortical lamination. Four primitive layers describe classic lissencephaly, not normal cortex.

updates.question_text: Regarding the MR appearance and clinical associations of polymicrogyria, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Affected cortex may appear thick with an irregular bumpy surface
Patients are expected to have normal development and no seizure tendency
High-resolution imaging may resolve multiple small individual gyri
The abnormal cortex is always smoothest in unmyelinated regions
The grey-white junction may have an irregular bumpy outline
options_after: Affected cortex may appear thick with an irregular bumpy surface
Patients are expected to have normal development without seizure tendency
High-resolution imaging may resolve multiple small individual gyri
The abnormal cortex is characteristically smoothest in unmyelinated regions
The grey-white junction may have an irregular bumpy outline
updates.explanation: The source describes polymicrogyric cortex as thick with an irregular bumpy surface, and high-resolution imaging can resolve multiple small gyri. The supplied T2 image shows an irregular bumpy grey-white interface. The cortex may look thin and bumpy in unmyelinated regions and thicker and smoother in myelinated regions, so the proposed absolute statement about unmyelinated regions is not supported.

updates.question_text: Regarding grey matter heterotopia, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It represents clusters of normal neurons in abnormal locations
It is caused by arrested radial migration of neurons
It is always isolated and has no association with other structural anomalies
It is the same process as parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction
Subtypes include periventricular nodular, focal subcortical, and leptomeningeal heterotopia
options_after: It represents clusters of normal neurons in abnormal locations
It is caused by arrested radial migration of neurons
It is characteristically isolated and lacks association with other structural anomalies
It is the same process as parenchymal haemorrhagic infarction
Subtypes include periventricular nodular, focal subcortical, and leptomeningeal heterotopia
updates.explanation: Grey matter heterotopia comprises normal neurons in abnormal locations due to arrested radial migration. It may be isolated or associated with other structural anomalies and can be a cause of seizures. The source lists periventricular nodular, focal subcortical, and leptomeningeal heterotopia as the three main subtypes.

updates.question_text: Regarding schizencephaly, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is a full-thickness cleft extending from the ventricle to the cortical surface
The cleft directly communicates with the subarachnoid space in all cases
The cleft is lined only by ependyma and contains no dysplastic grey matter
It is morphologically classified into open-lip and closed-lip forms
Only a schizencephalic cleft is lined by grey matter among the listed cortical clefts
options_after: It is a full-thickness cleft extending from the ventricle to the cortical surface
The cleft directly communicates with the subarachnoid space in more than 90% of cases
The cleft is lined primarily by ependyma and lacks dysplastic grey matter
It is morphologically classified into open-lip and closed-lip forms
Only a schizencephalic cleft is lined by grey matter among the listed cortical clefts
updates.explanation: Schizencephaly is a full-thickness cleft through the cerebral mantle, extending from the ependymal ventricular lining to the pial cortical surface, and lined by dysplastic grey matter. The source classifies it into open-lip and closed-lip forms. It does not directly communicate with the subarachnoid space because a roofing membrane covers the cleft.

updates.question_text: Regarding Joubert syndrome and related disorders, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: They are commonly associated with a large posterior fossa cyst and hydrocephalus identical to Dandy-Walker malformation
The primary abnormality is failure of regression of the primitive cephalic venous plexus
They typically present with bilateral vestibular schwannomas and hearing loss
They may show a molar tooth configuration of the midbrain
Hydrocephalus or a large posterior fossa cyst are uncommon compared with Dandy-Walker complex
options_after: They are commonly associated with a large posterior fossa cyst and hydrocephalus closely comparable to Dandy-Walker malformation
The primary abnormality is failure of regression of the primitive cephalic venous plexus
They typically present with bilateral vestibular schwannomas and hearing loss
They may show a molar tooth configuration of the midbrain
Hydrocephalus or a large posterior fossa cyst are uncommon compared with Dandy-Walker complex
updates.explanation: Joubert syndrome and related disorders may show a molar tooth configuration of the midbrain and typically present with hypotonia, developmental delay, and ataxia, often with ocular anomalies. The primary abnormality is thought to be aplasia or hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis, with dysplastic cerebellar tissue often present. Unlike the Dandy-Walker complex, hydrocephalus or a large posterior fossa cyst is uncommon.

updates.question_text: Regarding acute reactions to intravenous contrast media, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Reactions to iodinated and gadolinium-based contrast can be allergic-type or non allergic-type
All allergic-type reactions are severe and life-threatening
Many side effects of contrast agents are related to solution hyperosmolarity
Patients with asthma are at increased risk of an allergic-like contrast reaction
Seafood, shellfish, and povidone-iodine allergies do not increase the risk of allergic reaction to iodinated contrast more than other allergies
options_after: Reactions to iodinated and gadolinium-based contrast can be allergic-type or non allergic-type
Most allergic-type reactions are severe and life-threatening
Many side effects of contrast agents are related to solution hyperosmolarity
Patients with asthma are at increased risk of an allergic-like contrast reaction
Seafood, shellfish, and povidone-iodine allergies do not increase the risk of allergic reaction to iodinated contrast more than other allergies
updates.explanation: The source divides acute iodinated and gadolinium contrast reactions into allergic-type and non allergic-type mechanisms, both of which may range from mild to severe. Hyperosmolarity explains many contrast side effects, and asthma increases the risk of an allergic-like reaction. Seafood, shellfish, and povidone-iodine allergies do not confer special additional iodinated contrast risk beyond other allergies.

updates.question_text: Regarding premedication for patients with prior contrast reaction, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Premedication guarantees that no repeat reaction will occur
Elective premedication consists only of diphenhydramine immediately before contrast
Elective premedication includes prednisone at 13 hours, 7 hours, and 1 hour before the examination plus diphenhydramine 1 hour before
Emergent premedication is effective even if intravenous steroids are first given less than 4 hours before contrast
Emergent premedication includes hydrocortisone 200 mg IV at 5 hours and 1 hour before contrast administration plus diphenhydramine 1 hour before
options_after: Premedication prevents any repeat reaction will occur
Elective premedication consists primarily of diphenhydramine immediately before contrast
Elective premedication includes prednisone at 13 hours, 7 hours, and 1 hour before the examination plus diphenhydramine 1 hour before
Emergent premedication is effective even if intravenous steroids are first given less than 4 hours before contrast
Emergent premedication includes hydrocortisone 200 mg IV at 5 hours and 1 hour before contrast administration plus diphenhydramine 1 hour before
updates.explanation: For a patient with a known contrast allergy who still requires IV contrast, premedication is recommended, but reactions may still occur. The elective regimen in the source is prednisone 50 mg orally at 13, 7, and 1 hour, with diphenhydramine 50 mg 1 hour before. The emergent regimen uses hydrocortisone 200 mg IV at 5 hours and 1 hour, with diphenhydramine 1 hour before; IV steroids have not been shown effective if given sooner than 4 hours before contrast.

updates.question_text: Which statement best reflects the source guidance for a patient with a prior severe allergic-type reaction to intravenous contrast?
options_before: Repeat IV contrast is routine if shellfish allergy is absent
Only oral hydration is required before repeat IV contrast
A repeat reaction is always less severe than the prior reaction
Intravenous contrast is generally contraindicated
Metformin should be stopped but no other precautions are needed
options_after: Repeat IV contrast is routine if shellfish allergy is absent
Oral hydration without premedication is sufficient before repeat IV contrast after a prior severe reaction.
A repeat reaction is characteristically less severe than the prior reaction
Intravenous contrast is generally contraindicated
Metformin should be stopped but other precautions are unnecessary
updates.explanation: The source states that a repeat reaction is most likely to be similar to the prior reaction but may be more or less severe. If IV contrast is necessary after a previous reaction, premedication is recommended, but reactions may occur despite it. Intravenous contrast is generally contraindicated after a prior severe allergic-type reaction.

updates.question_text: Which statement best reflects the source guidance on nonionic iodinated contrast in patients with pheochromocytoma?
options_before: Nonionic contrast is absolutely contraindicated because all agents raise catecholamines
Only gadolinium can be used because iodinated agents are never safe
It is safe to administer nonionic contrast media
Oral contrast is safe but intravascular nonionic contrast is not discussed
Nonionic contrast must always be preceded by dialysis
options_after: Nonionic contrast is absolutely contraindicated because most agents raise catecholamines
Gadolinium is preferred because nonionic iodinated contrast still provokes catecholamine release.
It is safe to administer nonionic contrast media
Oral contrast is safe but intravascular nonionic contrast is not discussed
Nonionic contrast must characteristically be preceded by dialysis
updates.explanation: The source states that it is safe to administer nonionic contrast media to patients with pheochromocytoma. Older studies showed increased serum catecholamines after high-osmolality contrast agents, but those agents are no longer in current use. The section does not require dialysis or substitution with gadolinium for pheochromocytoma.

updates.question_text: Regarding iodinated contrast, thyroid uptake, and metformin, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Iodinated contrast increases thyroid I-131 uptake to approximately 150% at one week
If radioactive I-131 therapy is planned, iodinated contrast should be avoided for one month beforehand
Metformin must be stopped before gadolinium-based contrast in all patients
Metformin does not need to be discontinued in patients with normal renal function receiving iodinated contrast
In patients with multiple comorbidities, metformin should be stopped at contrast administration and withheld for 48 hours
options_after: Iodinated contrast increases thyroid I-131 uptake to approximately 150% at one week
If radioactive I-131 therapy is planned, iodinated contrast should be avoided for one month beforehand
Metformin must be stopped before gadolinium-based contrast in most patients
Metformin does not need to be discontinued in patients with normal renal function receiving iodinated contrast
In patients with multiple comorbidities, metformin should be stopped at contrast administration and withheld for 48 hours
updates.explanation: Iodinated contrast reduces thyroid I-131 uptake to about 50% one week after injection, so it should be avoided for one month before planned I-131 therapy. Metformin does not need to be stopped in patients with normal renal function. In patients with multiple comorbidities it should be discontinued at the time of contrast administration and withheld for 48 hours. The source states that metformin does not need to be stopped before gadolinium-based contrast.

updates.question_text: Regarding iodinated contrast in pregnancy and breast feeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Iodinated contrast crosses the placenta and enters the fetal circulation
Iodinated contrast has proven mutagenic effects in vivo
Iodinated contrast is never acceptable in pregnancy, even if medically necessary
Breast feeding mothers do not need to halt breast feeding after iodinated contrast
The total infant absorbed dose from breast milk is approximately 10% of the maternal dose
options_after: Iodinated contrast crosses the placenta and enters the fetal circulation
Iodinated contrast has proven mutagenic effects in vivo
Iodinated contrast is not acceptable in pregnancy, even if medically necessary
Breast feeding mothers do not need to halt breast feeding after iodinated contrast
The total infant absorbed dose from breast milk is approximately 10% of the maternal dose
updates.explanation: Iodinated contrast crosses the placenta and enters the fetal circulation, but no mutagenic or teratogenic effects have been observed in vivo. It may be administered in pregnancy if medically necessary, with informed consent recommended for examinations involving ionising radiation and iodinated contrast. Breast feeding does not need to stop; the source estimates total infant absorbed dose at about 0.01% of the maternal dose.

updates.question_text: Regarding NSF risk and gadolinium use in reduced renal function, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Patients with eGFR <30 have no reported NSF risk after gadolinium exposure
Gadolinium-based contrast is preferred in patients on dialysis because it prevents CIN
Patients with end-stage renal disease may have a 1% to 7% chance of NSF even after a single gadolinium exposure
NSF is common in patients with eGFR >30
In general, gadolinium-based contrast should not be given to patients on dialysis, with eGFR <30, or with AKI
options_after: Patients with eGFR <30 lack reported NSF risk after gadolinium exposure
Gadolinium-based contrast is preferred in patients on dialysis because it prevents CIN
Patients with end-stage renal disease may have a 1% to 7% chance of NSF even after a single gadolinium exposure
NSF is common in patients with eGFR >30
In general, gadolinium-based contrast should not be given to patients on dialysis, with eGFR <30, or with AKI
updates.explanation: The source gives a 1% to 7% NSF risk after even a single gadolinium exposure in end-stage renal disease. In general, gadolinium-based contrast should not be administered to patients on dialysis, with eGFR <30, or with AKI. NSF is exceedingly rare between eGFR 30 and 59, and only one established case is noted with eGFR >30.

updates.question_text: Regarding practical consequences of X-ray interactions with matter, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Compton scattered photons travel only in the forward direction
Compton scatter dominates above 25 keV in soft tissue
Photoelectric effect dominates below 40 keV in bone
A 30 keV electron cannot produce meaningful ionisation damage
Photoelectric inner-shell electron energy is deposited locally
options_after: Compton scattered photons travel primarily in the forward direction
Compton scatter dominates above 25 keV in soft tissue
Photoelectric effect dominates below 40 keV in bone
A 30 keV electron will not produce meaningful ionisation damage
Photoelectric inner-shell electron energy is deposited locally
updates.explanation: The source states that Compton scatter dominates above 25 keV in soft tissue and above 40 keV in bone, while photoelectric effect dominates below those energies. Scattered photons from Compton interactions go in all directions, not only forwards. The ejected inner-shell electron energy from photoelectric absorption is deposited locally; the source notes that a 30 keV electron can cause significant damage via approximately 1,000 ionisations.

updates.question_text: Regarding linear and mass attenuation coefficients, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The transmitted fraction through thickness is described by e to the power of negative mu times thickness
For weakly attenuating material with small mu, mu cannot approximate the proportion of photons interacting with matter
For large mu, attenuation is linear and the exponential formula should be avoided
Mass attenuation coefficient equals mu divided by density
Mass attenuation coefficient increases directly with density because density is not accounted for
options_after: The transmitted fraction through thickness is described by e to the power of negative mu times thickness
For weakly attenuating material with small mu, mu will not approximate the proportion of photons interacting with matter
For large mu, attenuation is linear and the exponential formula should be avoided
Mass attenuation coefficient equals mu divided by density
Mass attenuation coefficient increases directly with density because density is not accounted for
updates.explanation: The source gives the transmitted fraction as e to the power of negative mu times thickness. If mu is small, below 0.1/cm, it approximates the proportion of photons interacting with matter; if larger, the full exponential formula is used. Mass attenuation coefficient is mu divided by density, and because density is accounted for, it is independent of density.

updates.question_text: Regarding scatter and grids in radiography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The typical scatter-to-primary ratio in radiography is 1:5 to 1:10
Scatter increases image contrast
Grid ratio is grid height divided by width
Only about 7% of primary radiation passes through the grid
Typical radiographic grid ratios are between 2 and 4
options_after: The typical scatter-to-primary ratio in radiography is 1:5 to 1:10
Scatter increases image contrast
Grid ratio is grid height divided by width
Approximately 7% of primary radiation passes through a radiographic grid.
Typical radiographic grid ratios are between 2 and 4
updates.explanation: The source gives a typical radiographic scatter-to-primary ratio of 5-10:1, not 1:5 to 1:10, with scatter reducing contrast. Grid ratio is height divided by width. Typical radiographic grid ratios are 8-12, and approximately 70% of primary radiation passes through the grid.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT attenuation and Hounsfield units, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CT reconstructs only tissue weighting factors rather than attenuation coefficients
A Hounsfield unit measures relative CT attenuation
A material with twice the attenuation of water measures 100 HU
Ten HU corresponds to a 1% contrast difference
Gray matter and white matter differ by approximately 5% contrast
options_after: CT reconstructs primarily tissue weighting factors rather than attenuation coefficients
A Hounsfield unit measures relative CT attenuation
A material with twice the attenuation of water measures 100 HU
Ten HU corresponds to a 1% contrast difference
Gray matter and white matter differ by approximately 5% contrast
updates.explanation: CT images are produced by rotating a fan beam and reconstructing linear attenuation coefficients, not tissue weighting factors. Hounsfield units describe relative CT attenuation using water as the reference. The source states that 10 HU corresponds to a 1% contrast difference, and material with twice the attenuation of water is 1000 HU, not 100 HU. Gray and white matter differ by only 0.5% contrast.

updates.question_text: Regarding CTDI and CTDIvol, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: CTDI is the average phantom dose for a single axial slice including scatter
CTDI is measured only with a 32 cm phantom, regardless of head or body protocol
CTDI is measured in Gy
CTDIvol equals CTDIw divided by pitch
CTDIvol increases with scan length
options_after: CTDI is the average phantom dose for a single axial slice including scatter
CTDI is measured primarily with a 32 cm phantom, despite variation in head or body protocol
CTDI is measured in Gy
CTDIvol equals CTDIw divided by pitch
CTDIvol increases with scan length
updates.explanation: CTDI is the average phantom dose for a single axial slice, including scatter, and is measured in Gy. The source describes both 16 cm and 32 cm phantoms, with the 16 cm phantom always giving a higher dose. CTDIvol equals CTDIw divided by pitch and is independent of scan length.

updates.question_text: Regarding pitch, DLP, and estimating CT radiation risk, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: DLP is independent of scan length
DLP is expressed in mSv without a conversion factor
Effective dose from DLP uses one universal conversion factor for all body parts
Pitch less than 1 overscans and increases radiation exposure
Pitch greater than 1 skips areas and decreases exposure
options_after: DLP is independent of scan length
DLP is expressed in mSv without a conversion factor
Effective dose from DLP uses one universal conversion factor for most body parts
Pitch less than 1 overscans and increases radiation exposure
Pitch greater than 1 skips areas and decreases exposure
updates.explanation: Pitch relates to table speed: pitch less than 1 overscans and increases exposure, while pitch greater than 1 skips areas and decreases exposure. DLP is CTDIvol multiplied by scan length and is expressed in mGy*cm. Effective dose is estimated from DLP using body-part-specific conversion factors, not a universal factor.

updates.question_text: Regarding radiographic image quality, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Increasing scatter increases contrast
Collimation decreases scatter and dose
Collimation is described as improving image quality only by increasing dose
Increasing kV increases contrast when automatic exposure control is used
Screen-film contrast is related to screen latitude or gradient
options_after: Increasing scatter increases contrast
Collimation decreases scatter and dose
Collimation is described as improving image quality primarily by increasing dose
Increasing kV increases contrast when automatic exposure control is used
Screen-film contrast is related to screen latitude or gradient
updates.explanation: Scatter decreases contrast. Collimation reduces scatter and dose, so it is highlighted as a rare technique that both improves image quality and decreases dose. With automatic exposure control, increasing kV decreases contrast. In screen-film imaging, contrast relates to screen latitude or gradient.

updates.question_text: Regarding fetal radiation effects and dose limits for pregnant radiation workers, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Weeks 15-25 have no listed mental retardation risk after significant exposure
Weeks 0-2 are described as an all-or-nothing period
Lead apron attenuation increases externally measured dose by a factor of 20
Weeks 8-15 carry a mental retardation risk of 40% per Sv after significant exposure
The fetal dose limit for a pregnant radiation worker is 0.5 mSv/month, approximately 5 mSv per pregnancy
options_after: Weeks 15-25 lack listed mental retardation risk after significant exposure
Weeks 0-2 are described as an all-or-nothing period
Lead apron attenuation increases externally measured dose by a factor of 20
Weeks 8-15 carry a mental retardation risk of 40% per Sv after significant exposure
The fetal dose limit for a pregnant radiation worker is 0.5 mSv/month, approximately 5 mSv per pregnancy
updates.explanation: The source describes weeks 0-2 as an all-or-nothing period and gives weeks 8-15 as a sensitive period for mental retardation risk at 40% per Sv. Weeks 15-25 have a lower listed mental retardation risk of 10% per Sv. The fetal dose limit is 0.5 mSv/month, approximately 5 mSv per pregnancy. A lead apron attenuates, not increases, externally measured dose by a factor of 20.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI safety and regulation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: MRI can be performed at any stage of pregnancy, although gadolinium is contraindicated throughout pregnancy
Quenching releases oxygen, which removes the need for evacuation
The fringe field surrounding the controlled access area can exceed 50 Gauss
The FDA regulates only acoustic noise and does not regulate static magnetic field strength
Specific absorption ratio describes ionising radiation absorbed per unit mass
options_after: MRI can be performed at any stage of pregnancy, although gadolinium is contraindicated throughout pregnancy
Quenching releases oxygen, which removes the need for evacuation
The fringe field surrounding the controlled access area can exceed 50 Gauss
The FDA regulates primarily acoustic noise and does not regulate static magnetic field strength
Specific absorption ratio describes ionising radiation absorbed per unit mass
updates.explanation: The source states that MRI can be performed at any stage of pregnancy but gadolinium is contraindicated throughout pregnancy. Quenching releases helium that displaces oxygen, requiring emergency evacuation. The fringe field cannot exceed 5 Gauss around the controlled access area. FDA-regulated MRI parameters include static field strength above 4T and acoustic noise above 140 dB; SAR is RF power absorbed per unit mass, not ionising radiation.

updates.question_text: Regarding MRI heating, peripheral nerve stimulation, and SNR, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Time-varying magnetic fields cannot cause peripheral nerve stimulation or discomfort
Smaller voxel volume proportionally increases SNR
Conductive loops such as crossed arms or ECG leads can cause local heating
Metallic objects can absorb radiofrequency energy and become hot
Wide receiver bandwidth reduces chemical shift artefact but adds noise and reduces SNR
options_after: Time-varying magnetic fields will not cause peripheral nerve stimulation or discomfort
Smaller voxel volume proportionally increases SNR
Conductive loops such as crossed arms or ECG leads can cause local heating
Metallic objects can absorb radiofrequency energy and become hot
Wide receiver bandwidth reduces chemical shift artefact but adds noise and reduces SNR
updates.explanation: Conductive loops and metallic objects can cause local heating, while time-varying magnetic fields can produce peripheral nerve stimulation, muscle movement, and discomfort. Wide receiver bandwidth enables faster acquisition and reduces chemical shift artefact but adds noise and reduces SNR. A smaller voxel volume proportionally decreases, not increases, SNR.

updates.question_text: Regarding activity, cumulative activity, and effective half-life, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Activity is independent of decay rate
Cumulative activity is the total number of nuclear decays over time
Cumulative activity represents the area under the decay curve over time
Effective half-life accounts only for physical half-life and ignores biological clearance within an organ
Effective half-life ignores biological clearance
options_after: Activity is independent of decay rate
Cumulative activity is the total number of nuclear decays over time
Cumulative activity represents the area under the decay curve over time
Effective half-life accounts primarily for physical half-life and ignores biological clearance within an organ
Effective half-life ignores biological clearance
updates.explanation: Activity is the number of decays per unit time. Cumulative activity is the total number of nuclear decays over time and corresponds to the area under the decay curve. Effective half-life accounts for both intrinsic physical half-life and biological clearance within an organ, rather than ignoring biological clearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding nuclear medicine system resolution, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: System resolution accounts for the intrinsic resolution of the scintillation camera and the resolution of the collimator
Intrinsic resolution is camera resolution without a collimator
System resolution is determined only by the dose calibrator
Collimator resolution is unrelated to system resolution
System resolution is unrelated to the imaging system
options_after: System resolution accounts for the intrinsic resolution of the scintillation camera and the resolution of the collimator
Intrinsic resolution is camera resolution without a collimator
System resolution is determined primarily by the dose calibrator
Collimator resolution is unrelated to system resolution
System resolution is unrelated to the imaging system
updates.explanation: System resolution accounts for both the intrinsic resolution of the scintillation camera and the resolution of the collimator. Intrinsic resolution refers to the camera without a collimator, while collimator resolution is the other component. Dose calibrator tests assess the dose calibrator rather than the imaging system.

updates.question_text: Regarding CT correlation in PET/CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The CT portion is always a full diagnostic-quality contrast-enhanced CT.
Most modern PET studies are performed without CT because CT cannot contribute to localisation.
Paediatric PET may be performed without CT to reduce radiation exposure.
Dense retained oral contrast and metallic prostheses cannot affect attenuation correction.
The CT component is used for anatomic localisation and attenuation correction.
options_after: The CT portion is characteristically a full diagnostic-quality contrast-enhanced CT.
Most modern PET studies are performed without CT because CT will not contribute to localisation.
Paediatric PET may be performed without CT to reduce radiation exposure.
Dense retained oral contrast and metallic prostheses will not affect attenuation correction.
The CT component is used for anatomic localisation and attenuation correction.
updates.explanation: The source describes PET/CT as the usual modern approach, with CT used for anatomic localisation and attenuation correction. In paediatric imaging, PET may be performed alone to reduce radiation exposure from CT. Dense oral contrast or metal can create artefactual uptake through attenuation-correction error. The CT is often lower dose than diagnostic-quality CT and protocol details vary by institution.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal physiologic FDG uptake outside the brain and urinary tract, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Salivary glands, tonsils and thyroid should show no physiologic FDG uptake.
Cardiac uptake is fixed and unrelated to insulin, glucose levels or fasting state.
Muscle uptake is normally high in a fasting resting patient.
Brown fat can be mildly to moderately FDG avid, especially if the patient is cold or after food intake.
Liver uptake is usually moderate and largely homogeneous.
options_after: Salivary glands, tonsils and thyroid should fail to show physiologic FDG uptake.
Cardiac uptake is fixed and unrelated to insulin, glucose levels or fasting state.
Muscle uptake is normally high in a fasting resting patient.
Brown fat can be mildly to moderately FDG avid, especially if the patient is cold or after food intake.
Liver uptake is usually moderate and largely homogeneous.
updates.explanation: The source describes moderate homogeneous liver uptake, variable cardiac uptake, and mild to moderate symmetric activity in salivary glands, tonsils and thyroid. Brown fat may be FDG avid in characteristic adult distributions, especially when cold or after food intake. Muscle uptake is normally low, but may rise with insulin or recent exercise.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET/CT in lymphoma and breast cancer, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: PET/CT has a key role in staging and restaging lymphoma.
Most Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas are FDG avid.
Focal increased marrow uptake is more likely to represent lymphoma than diffuse marrow uptake.
Standard PET/CT is routinely used for all stage I-III breast cancers.
Standard PET/CT is not used to evaluate small nodal metastases in breast cancer.
options_after: PET/CT has a key role in staging and restaging lymphoma.
Most Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas are FDG avid.
Focal increased marrow uptake is more likely to represent lymphoma than diffuse marrow uptake.
Standard PET/CT is routinely used for most stage I-III breast cancers.
Standard PET/CT is not used to evaluate small nodal metastases in breast cancer.
updates.explanation: PET/CT is central to lymphoma staging/restaging and most lymphoma types are FDG avid, although some low-grade lymphomas are less avid. Diffuse marrow uptake can reflect G-CSF, rebound chemotherapy effect or malignant infiltration, while focal uptake is more suggestive of lymphoma. In breast cancer, standard PET/CT can be used for recurrent or stage IV disease but is not routinely used for stage I-III disease or small nodal metastases.

updates.question_text: Regarding FDG PET/CT in oesophageal cancer and tumours with limited FDG avidity, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: FDG PET/CT is highly sensitive for all hepatocellular carcinomas.
Primary tumour staging of oesophageal cancer is better assessed with endoscopic ultrasound than PET/CT.
Persistent FDG uptake after neoadjuvant therapy proves that chemotherapy is effective.
Most prostate cancers have intense FDG uptake and are routinely staged with FDG PET/CT.
In oesophageal cancer, PET/CT is mainly used to identify stage IV disease that would preclude surgery.
options_after: FDG PET/CT is highly sensitive for most hepatocellular carcinomas.
Primary tumour staging of oesophageal cancer is better assessed with endoscopic ultrasound than PET/CT.
Persistent FDG uptake after neoadjuvant therapy proves that chemotherapy is effective.
Most prostate cancers have intense FDG uptake and are routinely staged with FDG PET/CT.
In oesophageal cancer, PET/CT is mainly used to identify stage IV disease that would preclude surgery.
updates.explanation: The primary PET/CT role in oesophageal cancer is identifying stage IV disease in non-surgical candidates, while endoscopic ultrasound is better for primary tumour staging. Reduced FDG avidity after neoadjuvant treatment suggests a more favourable prognosis and can identify ineffective chemotherapy. FDG has limited utility in some tumour types: only about half of HCCs and RCCs are FDG avid, and most prostate cancers have low uptake.

updates.question_text: Regarding Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is primarily used for routine FDG staging of early breast cancer.
It is a new first-line diagnostic imaging modality for neuroendocrine tumours.
It is most useful for poorly differentiated tumours with high FDG uptake and absent somatostatin receptor expression.
It cannot be complementary to FDG PET/CT because both studies identify exactly the same tumour phenotype.
It is primarily an FDG substitute for routine staging of stage I-III breast cancer.
options_after: It is primarily used for routine FDG staging of early breast cancer.
It is a new first-line diagnostic imaging modality for neuroendocrine tumours.
It is most useful for poorly differentiated tumours with high FDG uptake and absent somatostatin receptor expression.
It will not be complementary to FDG PET/CT because both studies identify exactly the same tumour phenotype.
It is primarily an FDG substitute for routine staging of stage I-III breast cancer.
updates.explanation: Ga-68 DOTATATE targets somatostatin receptor expression and is used for neuroendocrine tumours and related SSTR-expressing tumours including pheochromocytoma, paraganglioma, neuroblastoma and meningioma. The source describes DOTATATE PET/CT as the new first-line diagnostic study for neuroendocrine tumours, replacing older Octreoscan and MIBG scintigraphy. DOTATATE and FDG are complementary because well-differentiated tumours tend to show DOTATATE uptake whereas poorly differentiated tumours may show high FDG uptake. It is not presented as a routine breast cancer staging agent.

updates.question_text: Regarding cerebral perfusion tracers, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Tc-99m DTPA and pertechnetate do not cross an intact blood-brain barrier.
Tc-99m DTPA and pertechnetate are now mainly used for SPECT brain parenchymal imaging.
HMPAO and ECD do not cross the blood-brain barrier and therefore show no grey matter activity.
ECD is generally preferred for brain imaging because it better characterises perfusion and is taken up only by living cells.
HMPAO and ECD are both used for SPECT imaging.
options_after: Tc-99m DTPA and pertechnetate do not cross an intact blood-brain barrier.
Tc-99m DTPA and pertechnetate are now mainly used for SPECT brain parenchymal imaging.
HMPAO and ECD do not cross the blood-brain barrier and therefore fail to show grey matter activity.
ECD is generally preferred for brain imaging because it better characterises perfusion and is taken up only by living cells.
HMPAO and ECD are both used for SPECT imaging.
updates.explanation: DTPA and pertechnetate are transient perfusion agents that do not cross an intact blood-brain barrier and are reserved for planar imaging, now uncommonly used. HMPAO and ECD are lipophilic perfusion agents that cross the blood-brain barrier and show grey matter activity. ECD is generally preferred because of rapid blood pool clearance, better shelf life, more accurate perfusion characterisation and uptake only by living cells. Both HMPAO and ECD are SPECT tracers.

updates.question_text: Regarding luxury perfusion in subacute infarct imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Luxury perfusion can increase HMPAO uptake despite infarcted tissue.
ECD shows the true defect representing infarct core because it is taken up only by living cells.
HMPAO uptake is purely a marker of living cell viability rather than perfusion.
ECD and HMPAO never differ in subacute infarction.
Luxury perfusion is the reason DTPA is preferred for SPECT dementia imaging.
options_after: Luxury perfusion can increase HMPAO uptake despite infarcted tissue.
ECD shows the true defect representing infarct core because it is taken up only by living cells.
HMPAO uptake is purely a marker of living cell viability rather than perfusion.
ECD and HMPAO will not differ in subacute infarction.
Luxury perfusion is the reason DTPA is preferred for SPECT dementia imaging.
updates.explanation: The source contrasts HMPAO and ECD in subacute infarction. Luxury perfusion may increase HMPAO uptake because HMPAO reflects perfusion, whereas ECD is taken up only by living cells and therefore shows the true infarct core defect. This distinction is separate from dementia imaging and does not make DTPA a preferred SPECT parenchymal tracer.

updates.question_text: Regarding thyroid nuclear medicine in pregnancy and breastfeeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: I-131 is contraindicated in pregnancy because thyrotropic agents cross the placenta
Fetal iodine uptake begins only after birth, so pregnancy does not alter the use of radioiodine
A mother receiving an ablative I-131 dose must permanently stop breastfeeding for the current child
I-123 requires permanent cessation of breastfeeding for the current child
Tc-99m thyroid imaging allows immediate breastfeeding with no interruption
options_after: I-131 is contraindicated in pregnancy because thyrotropic agents cross the placenta
Fetal iodine uptake begins primarily after birth, so pregnancy does not alter the use of radioiodine
A mother receiving an ablative I-131 dose must permanently stop breastfeeding for the current child
I-123 requires long-term cessation of breastfeeding for the current child
Tc-99m thyroid imaging allows immediate breastfeeding without interruption
updates.explanation: The source states that all thyrotropic agents cross the placenta and that I-131 is contraindicated in pregnancy. Fetal iodine uptake begins at about 12 weeks of gestation, so pregnancy is directly relevant to radioiodine decisions. After an I-131 ablative dose, breastfeeding must stop permanently for the current child. The text gives shorter interruption periods for I-123 and Tc-99m rather than permanent cessation or no interruption.

updates.question_text: Regarding scintigraphic assessment of thyroid nodules, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: All thyroid nodules should undergo radionuclide imaging before cytology
A cold thyroid nodule is almost always a benign adenoma
Hyperfunctioning thyroid nodules are almost always benign adenomas
A warm nodule requires no further assessment even if oblique views remain indeterminate
A discordant nodule may be malignant and biopsy is usually recommended
options_after: Most thyroid nodules should undergo radionuclide imaging before cytology
A cold thyroid nodule is typically a benign adenoma
Hyperfunctioning thyroid nodules are almost always benign adenomas
A warm nodule does not require further assessment even if oblique views remain indeterminate
A discordant nodule may be malignant and biopsy is usually recommended
updates.explanation: The source states that thyroid nodules are typically imaged only when cytology is indeterminate. Hyperfunctioning nodules are almost always benign adenomas. Cold nodules have a malignancy risk, although the commonest cold nodule is a benign colloid cyst. Warm nodules may still need biopsy if oblique views are indeterminate. A nodule that is hot on pertechnetate but cold on I-123 has maintained trapping but not organification, and biopsy is usually recommended because malignancy is possible.

updates.question_text: Regarding toxic multinodular goitre and Hashimoto thyroiditis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Toxic multinodular goitre usually presents in children with hypothyroidism
Toxic multinodular goitre can show one or more hot nodules with suppression of remaining thyroid tissue
Hashimoto thyroiditis may have scan appearances ranging from Graves-like increased uptake to patchy multinodular uptake
Most patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis are hypothyroid
A dominant cold nodule within a multinodular goitre should always be ignored because malignancy is impossible
options_after: Toxic multinodular goitre usually presents in children with hypothyroidism
Toxic multinodular goitre can show one or more hot nodules with suppression of remaining thyroid tissue
Hashimoto thyroiditis may have scan appearances ranging from Graves-like increased uptake to patchy multinodular uptake
Most patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis are hypothyroid
A dominant cold nodule within a multinodular goitre should characteristically be ignored because malignancy is not considered a realistic possibility
updates.explanation: Toxic multinodular goitre is described in middle-aged to elderly women with hyperthyroidism and a heterogeneous nodular scan pattern. Hashimoto thyroiditis has variable hormone status by stage, but most patients are hypothyroid, and its scan can resemble either Graves disease or multinodular goitre. A dominant cold nodule in a multinodular goitre should undergo further investigation, even though malignancy is relatively uncommon overall.

updates.question_text: Regarding sulfur colloid imaging for ectopic or redistributed reticuloendothelial tissue, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An intrapancreatic splenule can be confirmed when the suspected tissue shows sulfur colloid uptake
Splenosis appears as photopenic abdominal masses because splenic tissue does not take up sulfur colloid
Tc-99m damaged red cell imaging can also be used for suspected intrapancreatic splenic tissue
FNH should never show uptake on sulfur colloid or HIDA imaging
Splenosis can show scattered focal abdominal uptake after splenectomy and trauma
options_after: An intrapancreatic splenule can be confirmed when the suspected tissue shows sulfur colloid uptake
Splenosis appears as photopenic abdominal masses because splenic tissue does not take up sulfur colloid
Tc-99m damaged red cell imaging can also be used for suspected intrapancreatic splenic tissue
FNH should not show uptake on sulfur colloid or HIDA imaging
Splenosis can show scattered focal abdominal uptake after splenectomy and trauma
updates.explanation: Sulfur colloid uptake confirms functioning splenic tissue, including an intrapancreatic splenule or splenosis after trauma and splenectomy. Tc-99m damaged red cell imaging is an alternative splenic tissue study. FNH may show sulfur colloid uptake because it contains Kupffer cells and can also take up HIDA because it contains biliary ductules. Splenosis is therefore an uptake diagnosis, not a photopenic defect diagnosis.

updates.question_text: Regarding scintigraphic assessment of oesophageal reflux, transit and aspiration, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Reflux scintigraphy is performed only in adults because radiolabelled milk is contraindicated in neonates
Delayed lung images can be obtained after reflux scintigraphy to assess aspiration
Salivagram is less sensitive than reflux scintigraphy for aspiration in paediatric patients
A salivagram places sulfur colloid at the tongue base or sublingual region and looks for activity in the bronchi or lungs
Esophageal transit scintigraphy requires intravenous tracer injection during swallowing
options_after: Reflux scintigraphy is performed primarily in adults because radiolabelled milk is contraindicated in neonates
Delayed lung images can be obtained after reflux scintigraphy to assess aspiration
Salivagram is less sensitive than reflux scintigraphy for aspiration in paediatric patients
A salivagram places sulfur colloid at the tongue base or sublingual region and looks for activity in the bronchi or lungs
Esophageal transit scintigraphy requires intravenous tracer injection during swallowing
updates.explanation: Reflux scintigraphy is most commonly performed in neonates using formula or milk mixed with tracer, and delayed lung images can assess aspiration. Salivagram is described as more sensitive for detecting aspiration in paediatric patients. It involves placing a drop of tracer at the tongue base or sublingual region and imaging for bronchial or pulmonary activity. Esophageal transit uses swallowed tracer in water, not an intravenous injection.

updates.question_text: Regarding tagged red blood cell scintigraphy for acute gastrointestinal bleeding, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A positive study shows activity that changes shape or position over time due to intraluminal blood movement
Tagged red blood cell scintigraphy is used only after angiography has already localised the bleed
Sulfur colloid is preferred when prolonged imaging is required because it remains intravascular for many hours
Tagged red blood cell scintigraphy can help identify patients who may be suitable for angiography
Free pertechnetate uptake in the thyroid confirms active gastrointestinal bleeding
options_after: A positive study shows activity that changes shape or position over time due to intraluminal blood movement
Tagged red blood cell scintigraphy is used primarily after angiography has already localised the bleed
Sulfur colloid is preferred when prolonged imaging is required because it remains intravascular for many hours
Tagged red blood cell scintigraphy can help identify patients who may be suitable for angiography
Free pertechnetate uptake in the thyroid confirms active gastrointestinal bleeding
updates.explanation: A positive tagged red blood cell study shows an initial focus that changes shape or position over time as intraluminal blood moves antegrade or retrograde. It can detect low-rate bleeding and help select patients for angiography. Sulfur colloid clears rapidly from the blood, so it is not the better choice for prolonged imaging. Thyroid uptake from free pertechnetate is a labelling or biodistribution issue, not a marker of active GI bleeding.

updates.question_text: Regarding HIDA protocol logic, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Gallbladder nonvisualisation at one hour always proves acute cholecystitis without any need for augmentation or delay
Morphine redirects bile into the cystic duct by contracting the sphincter of Oddi
Morphine should be given before confirming any tracer excretion into bowel
If the gallbladder is visualised, acute cholecystitis is ruled out
Four-hour delayed imaging is an alternative when morphine cannot be given
options_after: Gallbladder nonvisualisation at one hour characteristically proves acute cholecystitis without any need for augmentation or delay
Morphine redirects bile into the cystic duct by contracting the sphincter of Oddi
Morphine should be given before confirming any tracer excretion into bowel
If the gallbladder is visualised, acute cholecystitis is ruled out
Four-hour delayed imaging is an alternative when morphine cannot be given
updates.explanation: HIDA interpretation uses gallbladder visualisation as a key decision point: once the gallbladder is seen, acute cholecystitis is ruled out. If the gallbladder is not seen by one hour, morphine can redirect bile into the cystic duct by contracting the sphincter of Oddi, but the source cautions that morphine should only be given if tracer is already in the small bowel. If morphine cannot be used, delayed imaging up to four hours is an alternative. Nonvisualisation at one hour alone is not the complete diagnostic endpoint.

updates.question_text: Regarding false-positive and false-negative HIDA interpretation for acute cholecystitis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Recent meal or prolonged fasting can cause gallbladder nonvisualisation without acute cholecystitis
Gallbladder visualisation always excludes acalculous cholecystitis in every clinical setting
Pancreatitis and severe illness are listed causes of false-positive gallbladder nonvisualisation
Duodenal diverticulum simulating the gallbladder is a false-positive mechanism that cannot be clarified by lateral imaging
A right extrarenal pelvis in a jaundiced patient may simulate gallbladder activity
options_after: Recent meal or prolonged fasting can cause gallbladder nonvisualisation without acute cholecystitis
Gallbladder visualisation characteristically excludes acalculous cholecystitis in most clinical settings
Pancreatitis and severe illness are listed causes of false-positive gallbladder nonvisualisation
Duodenal diverticulum simulating the gallbladder is a false-positive mechanism that will not be clarified by lateral imaging
A right extrarenal pelvis in a jaundiced patient may simulate gallbladder activity
updates.explanation: False-positive HIDA nonvisualisation can result from preparation or clinical factors such as a recent meal, prolonged fasting, pancreatitis, severe illness, parenteral nutrition, chronic cholecystitis or recent CCK. False-negative visualisation is rare but can occur with acalculous cholecystitis and a patent cystic duct, so gallbladder visualisation is not an absolute exclusion in every clinical setting. Duodenal diverticulum or choledochal cyst can simulate gallbladder activity, and a lateral view can help differentiate duodenal diverticulum. A right extrarenal pelvis in jaundiced patients with increased renal excretion may also simulate gallbladder activity.

updates.question_text: Regarding high-probability metastatic patterns and treatment response on bone scan, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A single sternal lesion in a patient with breast cancer is due to metastasis about 80% of the time
Multifocal increased activity in nonadjacent ribs is suspicious for metastases
Increased uptake within three months of chemotherapy always proves disease progression
A single photopenic lesion in neuroblastoma, renal cell carcinoma, or thyroid cancer is often metastatic
Treated metastases should keep increasing in uptake indefinitely after chemotherapy
options_after: A single sternal lesion in a patient with breast cancer is due to metastasis about 80% of the time
Multifocal increased activity in nonadjacent ribs is suspicious for metastases
Increased uptake within three months of chemotherapy characteristically proves disease progression
A single photopenic lesion in neuroblastoma, renal cell carcinoma, or thyroid cancer is often metastatic
Treated metastases should keep increasing in uptake indefinitely after chemotherapy
updates.explanation: The source gives several high-risk patterns: a single sternal lesion in breast cancer, multifocal nonadjacent rib uptake, and a single photopenic lesion in malignancies such as neuroblastoma, renal cell carcinoma and thyroid cancer. The flare phenomenon can cause treated metastases to show increased uptake within the first three months after chemotherapy due to healing. Uptake should regress by six months after treatment, so indefinite progression is not expected.

updates.question_text: Regarding false-negative bone scans in malignancy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Bone scan is most sensitive for purely marrow-replacing lesions without bone turnover
Predominantly osteoclastic or lytic metastases can have low sensitivity on bone scan
Multiple myeloma, renal cell carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, aggressive anaplastic tumours and neuroblastoma are examples of tumours that may produce false-negative bone scans
Lymphoma always produces intensely positive delayed skeletal uptake
Aggressive lytic or marrow-confined lesions may be better seen with FDG PET/CT
options_after: Bone scan is most sensitive for purely marrow-replacing lesions without bone turnover
Predominantly osteoclastic or lytic metastases can have low sensitivity on bone scan
Multiple myeloma, renal cell carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, aggressive anaplastic tumours and neuroblastoma are examples of tumours that may produce false-negative bone scans
Lymphoma characteristically produces intensely positive delayed skeletal uptake
Aggressive lytic or marrow-confined lesions may be better seen with FDG PET/CT
updates.explanation: Bone scan performs best when metastases induce bone turnover or are osteoblastic. Predominantly osteoclastic, lytic or marrow-confined disease can be falsely negative, with examples including multiple myeloma, renal cell carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, aggressive anaplastic tumours, neuroblastoma and marrow-replacing lymphoma. The source specifically notes that aggressive lytic or marrow-confined lesions are better seen on FDG PET/CT. This is a modality-selection point, not a request to memorise tracer chemistry.

updates.question_text: Regarding extraosseous uptake on bone scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Diffuse soft-tissue uptake can be seen in renal failure
Focal intense breast uptake is usually a normal physiologic variant
Recent breast biopsy cannot cause tracer uptake
Recent infarction may cause uptake in the brain, heart or spleen
Renal parenchymal uptake excludes urinary obstruction
options_after: Diffuse soft-tissue uptake can be seen in renal failure
Focal intense breast uptake is usually a normal physiologic variant
Recent breast biopsy will not cause tracer uptake
Recent infarction may cause uptake in the brain, heart or spleen
Renal parenchymal uptake excludes urinary obstruction
updates.explanation: Diffuse soft-tissue uptake can be seen in renal failure, and recent infarction can produce uptake in organs such as the brain, heart or spleen. Faint breast uptake may be normal, but focal intense breast uptake suggests breast carcinoma, while recent breast procedures can also produce uptake. Diffuse parenchymal renal uptake can be seen with urinary obstruction, hyperparathyroidism, chemotherapy or thalassaemia. These patterns are interpretive pitfalls on bone scan.

updates.question_text: Regarding primary bone tumours on bone scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Osteosarcoma typically causes markedly increased uptake and may involve the entire affected limb
Ewing sarcoma is usually photopenic on all phases
Benign tumours never show intense uptake
Ewing sarcoma may be positive on all three phases and mimic osteomyelitis
Osteoid osteoma has a vascular central nidus that can demonstrate intense activity
options_after: Osteosarcoma typically causes markedly increased uptake and may involve the entire affected limb
Ewing sarcoma is usually photopenic on most phases
Benign tumours will not show intense uptake
Ewing sarcoma may be positive on all three phases and mimic osteomyelitis
Osteoid osteoma has a vascular central nidus that can demonstrate intense activity
updates.explanation: Osteosarcoma typically produces markedly increased uptake, sometimes in the whole affected limb. Ewing sarcoma shows intense homogeneous activity and can be positive on all three phases, mimicking osteomyelitis. Osteoid osteoma has a vascular nidus with intense activity, forming the basis of the double density sign. Several benign bone tumours, including osteoid osteoma and osteoblastoma, can also show intense uptake.

updates.question_text: Regarding fracture patterns on bone scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: An acute fracture shows increased uptake surrounding the fracture site
Skull fractures routinely show intense radiotracer activity
In the subacute phase, radiotracer activity becomes more focal at the fracture
All healing fractures fully normalise within one month
Toddler's fracture is a spiral tibial fracture in a recently ambulatory child and scintigraphy is useful when radiographs are negative
options_after: An acute fracture shows increased uptake surrounding the fracture site
Skull fractures routinely show intense radiotracer activity
In the subacute phase, radiotracer activity becomes more focal at the fracture
Most healing fractures fully normalise within one month
Toddler's fracture is a spiral tibial fracture in a recently ambulatory child and scintigraphy is useful when radiographs are negative
updates.explanation: Acute fractures show increased uptake around the fracture site, with activity becoming more focal during the subacute phase. Healing activity gradually decreases, but a substantial minority can remain abnormal after one year. Skull fractures rarely show activity. Toddler's fracture is a spiral tibial fracture in a recently ambulatory child, and skeletal scintigraphy is sensitive when radiographs are negative.

updates.question_text: Regarding painful hip or knee prosthesis evaluation with bone scintigraphy, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Any uptake around a cemented prosthesis within the first month is diagnostic of infection
Activity around a non-cemented prosthesis must disappear by three months
Focal activity at the lesser trochanter and distal femoral prosthetic tip beyond the expected postoperative period suggests loosening
Generalised increased radiotracer activity surrounding the prosthesis may suggest osteomyelitis
Mild to moderate activity limited to the greater trochanter always proves loosening
options_after: Any uptake around a cemented prosthesis within the first month is diagnostic of infection
Activity around a non-cemented prosthesis must disappear by three months
Focal activity at the lesser trochanter and distal femoral prosthetic tip beyond the expected postoperative period suggests loosening
Generalised increased radiotracer activity surrounding the prosthesis may suggest osteomyelitis
Mild to moderate activity limited to the greater trochanter characteristically proves loosening
updates.explanation: Activity around a cemented prosthesis can be normal for up to 12 months, and activity around a non-cemented prosthesis can persist up to two years as bony ingrowth continues. Beyond these windows, focal activity at the lesser trochanter and distal femoral prosthetic tip suggests loosening. Generalised increased uptake around the prosthesis may suggest osteomyelitis. Uptake limited to the greater trochanter/intertrochanteric region is often heterotopic ossification rather than loosening.

updates.question_text: Regarding three-phase bone scan patterns in musculoskeletal infection, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Cellulitis is positive on all three phases including delayed skeletal images
Osteomyelitis is positive on all three phases of a bone scan
Cellulitis shows increased flow and soft-tissue phase activity but a negative skeletal phase
Discitis appears as isolated uptake in only one vertebral body
Septic arthritis is positive on all three phases on both sides of the joint
options_after: Cellulitis is positive on most three phases including delayed skeletal images
Osteomyelitis is positive on all three phases of a bone scan
Cellulitis shows increased flow and soft-tissue phase activity but a negative skeletal phase
Discitis appears as isolated uptake in a single vertebral body
Septic arthritis is positive on all three phases on both sides of the joint
updates.explanation: Osteomyelitis is positive on all three phases, and this is very specific when the radiograph is normal and fracture has been excluded. Cellulitis increases the blood flow and soft-tissue phases but has a negative delayed skeletal phase. Septic arthritis is positive on all three phases on both sides of the joint. Discitis shows increased skeletal activity in two adjacent vertebral bodies, not only one.

updates.question_text: Regarding improving specificity for osteomyelitis when the skeleton is already abnormal, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Indium-111 or Tc-99m labelled WBC imaging combined with sulfur colloid marrow imaging can increase specificity
Sulfur colloid marrow imaging is used because infected bone always has increased colloid uptake
Gallium is diagnostic only when its uptake is lower than the bone scan uptake
Focal WBC activity in a region devoid of colloid marrow activity suggests osteomyelitis
A positive three-phase bone scan is most specific for osteomyelitis when there is a fracture at the same site
options_after: Indium-111 or Tc-99m labelled WBC imaging combined with sulfur colloid marrow imaging can increase specificity
Sulfur colloid marrow imaging is used because infected bone characteristically has increased colloid uptake
Gallium is diagnostic primarily when its uptake is lower than the bone scan uptake
Focal WBC activity in a region devoid of colloid marrow activity suggests osteomyelitis
A positive three-phase bone scan is most specific for osteomyelitis when there is a fracture at the same site
updates.explanation: When fracture, prosthesis or other structural abnormality reduces the specificity of bone scan, labelled WBC imaging combined with sulfur colloid marrow imaging can help. Focal WBC uptake in a region devoid of colloid marrow activity suggests osteomyelitis. Gallium can also increase specificity if gallium uptake exceeds bone scan uptake at the area of concern. The three-phase pattern is most specific when the radiograph is normal, confirming no fracture.

updates.question_text: Regarding practical modality and pattern matching across this batch, which of the following pairings are correct?
options_before: Normal perfusion scan in suspected PE: ventilation imaging is not required
Bone scan superscan: look for diffuse skeletal uptake with faint or absent renal visualisation
Suspected osteomyelitis with an abnormal underlying skeleton: combine labelled WBC imaging with sulfur colloid marrow imaging to improve specificity
Pregnant patient with suspected PE, normal chest radiograph, no asthma/COPD and negative leg duplex: low-dose perfusion scan can be appropriate
Stress fracture: typically negative on all three phases when symptomatic
options_after: Normal perfusion scan in suspected PE: ventilation imaging is not required
Bone scan superscan: look for diffuse skeletal uptake with faint or absent renal visualisation
Suspected osteomyelitis with an abnormal underlying skeleton: combine labelled WBC imaging with sulfur colloid marrow imaging to improve specificity
Pregnant patient with suspected PE, normal chest radiograph, no asthma/COPD and negative leg duplex: low-dose perfusion scan can be appropriate
Stress fracture: typically negative on most three phases when symptomatic
updates.explanation: These pairings summarise clinically useful decisions from the source. A normal perfusion scan ends the V/Q examination without ventilation imaging. Superscan is recognised by diffuse skeletal uptake and absent or faint kidneys. In an abnormal skeleton, labelled WBC plus sulfur colloid marrow imaging improves osteomyelitis specificity. A low-dose perfusion study can be appropriate in the carefully selected pregnant patient described by the source. Symptomatic stress fracture is typically positive on all three phases rather than negative.

updates.question_text: Regarding normal renogram phases, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The flow phase assesses perfusion, and a slow upslope suggests decreased perfusion
The clearance phase normally begins before the kidney is visible after aortic visualisation
Lack of pelvicalyceal clearance excludes obstruction
A normal kidney should retain essentially all cortical activity at 20 minutes
Delayed cortical uptake suggests decreased renal function
options_after: The flow phase assesses perfusion, and a slow upslope suggests decreased perfusion
The clearance phase normally begins before the kidney is visible after aortic visualisation
Lack of pelvicalyceal clearance excludes obstruction
A normal kidney should retain more than 90% of cortical activity at 20 minutes
Delayed cortical uptake suggests decreased renal function
updates.explanation: A normal renogram has flow, cortical function and clearance phases. The flow phase has a sharp upslope, and a slow upslope suggests decreased perfusion. The cortical phase peaks shortly afterwards, and delayed cortical uptake reflects reduced function. The clearance phase represents urinary excretion into the collecting system; lack of pelvicalyceal clearance suggests obstruction rather than excluding it.

updates.question_text: Regarding Lasix renography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: It is used when hydronephrosis is present to distinguish obstruction from non-obstructive collecting-system dilatation
Tc-99m MAG3 is the usual radiotracer
A distended bladder can never cause a false-positive obstructed pattern
A clearance half-time greater than 20 minutes suggests obstruction
Renal failure and dehydration can contribute to false-positive interpretation
options_after: It is used when hydronephrosis is present to distinguish obstruction from non-obstructive collecting-system dilatation
Tc-99m MAG3 is the usual radiotracer
A distended bladder will not cause a false-positive obstructed pattern
A clearance half-time greater than 20 minutes suggests obstruction
Renal failure and dehydration can contribute to false-positive interpretation
updates.explanation: Diuretic renography is used to distinguish fixed obstruction from non-obstructive hydronephrosis, and MAG3 is the usual tracer. After Lasix, rapid clearance is normal, while a clearance half-time greater than 20 minutes suggests obstruction. Dehydration, a distended bladder and renal failure can produce false-positive obstructed patterns. These factors matter clinically because they can mimic obstruction without a fixed mechanical blockage.

updates.question_text: Regarding ACE inhibitor renography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The examination is performed to confirm vesicoureteric reflux in children
ACE inhibitor administration improves GFR by constricting efferent arterioles
A positive study is relatively specific for renal artery stenosis as a cause of hypertension
The hallmark is a post-ACE inhibitor renogram that becomes abnormal or more abnormal, usually unilaterally
A normal captopril study in a two-day protocol always requires a baseline study the following day
options_after: The examination is performed to confirm vesicoureteric reflux in children
ACE inhibitor administration improves GFR by constricting efferent arterioles
A positive study is relatively specific for renal artery stenosis as a cause of hypertension
The hallmark is a post-ACE inhibitor renogram that becomes abnormal or more abnormal, usually unilaterally
A normal captopril study in a two-day protocol characteristically requires a baseline study the following day
updates.explanation: ACE inhibitor renography evaluates renovascular hypertension from renal artery stenosis. In compensated stenosis, angiotensin II maintains GFR by constricting the efferent arteriole; ACE inhibition relaxes the efferent arteriole, so GFR can fall. The hallmark is a renogram that becomes abnormal or more abnormal after ACE inhibition, usually unilaterally. In the two-day protocol, a normal captopril study excludes renovascular hypertension and removes the need for a baseline study.

updates.question_text: Regarding radionuclide cystography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: The radiotracer is administered intravenously and filtered into the bladder
It is the most sensitive test for reflux in the paediatric population and has less radiation exposure than VCUG
Grade III reflux is confined to the ureter only
The selected tracer is injected retrograde into the catheterised bladder
Grade I reflux extends into the pelvicalyceal system
options_after: The radiotracer is administered intravenously and filtered into the bladder
It is the most sensitive test for reflux in the paediatric population and has less radiation exposure than VCUG
Grade III reflux is confined to the ureter in typical cases
The selected tracer is injected retrograde into the catheterised bladder
Grade I reflux extends into the pelvicalyceal system
updates.explanation: Radionuclide cystography evaluates vesicoureteric reflux in children with high sensitivity and less radiation exposure than VCUG. The tracer is injected retrograde into the catheterised bladder rather than given intravenously. Minimal grade I reflux is confined to the ureter, grade II reaches the pelvicalyceal system, and grade III causes severe reflux with a tortuous ureter and/or dilated intrarenal system.

updates.question_text: Regarding renal transplant evaluation with radionuclide renography, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A normal transplant is visualised on the flow phase within seconds after the iliac vessels
Acute tubular necrosis shows absent perfusion with no renal function immediately after surgery
Hyperacute rejection causes immediate vascular thrombosis with absent perfusion and markedly reduced or absent function
Urine leak presents as progressive accumulation of activity outside the urinary tract
Fixed perirenal photopenic areas may represent urinoma, haematoma or lymphocele
options_after: A normal transplant is visualised on the flow phase within seconds after the iliac vessels
Acute tubular necrosis shows absent perfusion without renal function immediately after surgery
Hyperacute rejection causes immediate vascular thrombosis with absent perfusion and markedly reduced or absent function
Urine leak presents as progressive accumulation of activity outside the urinary tract
Fixed perirenal photopenic areas may represent urinoma, haematoma or lymphocele
updates.explanation: A normal transplant should appear on the flow phase within seconds of the iliac vessels and then show cortical and clearance phases similar to a native kidney. Hyperacute rejection produces immediate vascular thrombosis with absent perfusion and markedly reduced or absent function. Urine leak appears as progressive extra-urinary-tract activity, while urinoma, haematoma and lymphocele may be fixed perirenal photopenic areas. Acute tubular necrosis instead has normal perfusion but poor function with cortical retention and delayed clearance.

updates.question_text: Regarding transplant rejection and nephrotoxicity patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Acute rejection occurs within weeks to three months and presents with decreased perfusion and marked cortical retention
Chronic rejection occurs months to years after surgery with progressive worsening perfusion and function
Cyclosporin nephrotoxicity appears similar to hyperacute rejection and must occur immediately after surgery
Hyperacute rejection has normal perfusion with delayed clearance only
Cyclosporin nephrotoxicity appears similar to ATN but occurs later, after ATN should have resolved
options_after: Acute rejection occurs within weeks to three months and presents with decreased perfusion and marked cortical retention
Chronic rejection occurs months to years after surgery with progressive worsening perfusion and function
Cyclosporin nephrotoxicity appears similar to hyperacute rejection and must occur immediately after surgery
Hyperacute rejection has normal perfusion with delayed clearance in typical cases
Cyclosporin nephrotoxicity appears similar to ATN but occurs later, after ATN should have resolved
updates.explanation: Acute rejection occurs within weeks to three months and shows decreased perfusion with marked cortical retention. Chronic rejection is later, months to years after surgery, with progressive deterioration of perfusion and function, cortical thinning and pelvicalyceal dilatation. Cyclosporin nephrotoxicity resembles ATN but occurs later, after ATN should have resolved. Hyperacute rejection is the immediate vascular thrombosis pattern with absent perfusion.

updates.question_text: Regarding MIBG imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Normal MIBG distribution excludes salivary glands, liver, kidneys and bladder
Normal distribution includes sites of sympathetic innervation such as salivary glands, heart, liver, kidneys and bladder
I-131 MIBG can be used to treat neuroblastoma in children
MIBG is never taken up by paraganglioma, carcinoid or medullary thyroid carcinoma
Thyroid uptake may be intentionally blocked with Lugol's solution
options_after: Normal MIBG distribution excludes salivary glands, liver, kidneys and bladder
Normal distribution includes sites of sympathetic innervation such as salivary glands, heart, liver, kidneys and bladder
I-131 MIBG can be used to treat neuroblastoma in children
MIBG is not taken up by paraganglioma, carcinoid or medullary thyroid carcinoma
Thyroid uptake may be intentionally blocked with Lugol's solution
updates.explanation: Normal MIBG distribution includes areas of sympathetic innervation such as salivary glands, heart, liver, kidneys and bladder. Thyroid uptake is typically intentionally blocked with Lugol's solution to reduce thyroid dose. I-131 MIBG can be used therapeutically for neuroblastoma in children. MIBG can also be taken up, to a lesser extent, by other neuroendocrine tumours including carcinoid, medullary thyroid carcinoma and paraganglioma.

updates.question_text: Regarding labelled white cell imaging and gallium for infection or inflammation, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Indium-111 WBC imaging lacks physiologic bowel accumulation, which helps evaluate abdominal or bowel infection
Tc-99m HMPAO WBC imaging has earlier imaging and better counts than Indium-111 WBC imaging
Tc-99m HMPAO WBC imaging can be limited by physiologic gastrointestinal and genitourinary activity
Gallium imaging is preferred over WBC imaging for abdominal infection because it has no bowel uptake
Indium-111 WBC imaging can be combined with sulfur colloid or MDP bone scans for suspected osteomyelitis in abnormal bone
options_after: Indium-111 WBC imaging lacks physiologic bowel accumulation, which helps evaluate abdominal or bowel infection
Tc-99m HMPAO WBC imaging has earlier imaging and better counts than Indium-111 WBC imaging
Tc-99m HMPAO WBC imaging can be limited by physiologic gastrointestinal and genitourinary activity
Gallium imaging is preferred over WBC imaging for abdominal infection because it lacks bowel uptake
Indium-111 WBC imaging can be combined with sulfur colloid or MDP bone scans for suspected osteomyelitis in abnormal bone
updates.explanation: Indium-111 WBC imaging has the practical advantage of lacking physiologic bowel accumulation, which helps in abdominal and bowel infection or inflammation. Tc-99m HMPAO WBC imaging can be performed earlier and has better counts, but unbound tracer produces gastrointestinal and genitourinary activity that limits bowel evaluation. Indium-111 WBC imaging can also be combined with sulfur colloid or MDP bone imaging to improve specificity in abnormal bone. Gallium is limited in the abdomen by high bowel and liver uptake.

updates.question_text: Regarding gallium imaging patterns, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: Persistent gallium uptake in the kidneys after 24 hours is abnormal and suggests renal disease or obstruction
Diffuse pulmonary gallium uptake is normal physiological biodistribution
The panda sign is specific for sarcoidosis and has no other differential diagnosis
Gallium scans remain first-line for most oncologic staging instead of FDG PET/CT
The panda sign plus the lambda sign strongly suggests sarcoidosis
options_after: Persistent gallium uptake in the kidneys after 24 hours is abnormal and suggests renal disease or obstruction
Diffuse pulmonary gallium uptake is normal physiological biodistribution
The panda sign is specific for sarcoidosis and lacks other differential diagnosis
Gallium scans remain first-line for most oncologic staging instead of FDG PET/CT
The panda sign plus the lambda sign strongly suggests sarcoidosis
