updates.explanation: Persistent renal gallium uptake after 24 hours is never normal and suggests renal disease or obstruction. Diffuse pulmonary uptake is also abnormal and has a broad infectious and inflammatory differential. The panda sign reflects uptake in the nasopharynx, parotid and lacrimal glands; it is not specific for sarcoidosis, but when combined with the lambda sign it strongly suggests sarcoid. Gallium scans have largely been replaced by FDG PET/CT, with residual first-line use for spinal discovertebral osteomyelitis.

updates.question_text: Regarding nuclear medicine evaluation of osteomyelitis in abnormal bone or prosthesis, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: A positive triple-phase MDP bone scan is only specific for osteomyelitis if the radiograph is abnormal
SPECT/CT, gallium or WBC imaging can increase specificity when there is an underlying abnormality
In prosthesis evaluation, increased WBC uptake with decreased sulfur colloid uptake suggests marrow replacement by WBCs consistent with osteomyelitis
Normal marrow should show WBC uptake but no sulfur colloid uptake
Gallium has no residual first-line role in spinal discovertebral osteomyelitis
options_after: A positive triple-phase MDP bone scan is primarily specific for osteomyelitis if the radiograph is abnormal
SPECT/CT, gallium or WBC imaging can increase specificity when there is an underlying abnormality
In prosthesis evaluation, increased WBC uptake with decreased sulfur colloid uptake suggests marrow replacement by WBCs consistent with osteomyelitis
Normal marrow should show WBC uptake but absent sulfur colloid uptake
Gallium lacks residual first-line role in spinal discovertebral osteomyelitis
updates.explanation: The source states that a positive triple-phase bone scan is specific only when the radiograph is normal. If there is an underlying abnormality, SPECT/CT, gallium or WBC imaging can increase specificity. In infected prosthesis evaluation, a discordant region with increased WBC uptake and decreased sulfur colloid uptake suggests osteomyelitis, while normal marrow is expected to show uptake on both studies. Gallium has a residual first-line application for spinal discovertebral osteomyelitis, so saying it has no role there is incorrect.

updates.question_text: Regarding pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma imaging, which of the following statements are correct?
options_before: I-123 MIBG is generally considered first-line for adrenal pheochromocytoma
Indium-111 pentetreotide may obscure an adrenal lesion because of normal renal uptake
Extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma may lose MIBG uptake due to dedifferentiation, altered membrane transport proteins or medication interference
Indium-111 pentetreotide has no role in extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma
Most metastatic extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas are not FDG avid according to the source
options_after: I-123 MIBG is generally considered first-line for adrenal pheochromocytoma
Indium-111 pentetreotide may obscure an adrenal lesion because of normal renal uptake
Extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma may lose MIBG uptake due to dedifferentiation, altered membrane transport proteins or medication interference
Indium-111 pentetreotide has negligible role in extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma
Most metastatic extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas are not FDG avid according to the source
updates.explanation: I-123 MIBG is first-line for adrenal pheochromocytoma. Pentetreotide can be considered second-line if MIBG is negative, but normal renal uptake may obscure an adrenal lesion. For extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma, MIBG sensitivity is variable, and loss of uptake may be caused by dedifferentiation, altered membrane transport proteins or medication interference. Pentetreotide is also an option, and the source says most metastatic extra-adrenal pheochromocytomas are FDG avid.

updates.question_text: Which statement best describes the sentinel node concept in lymphoscintigraphy?
options_before: The sentinel node is the last node visualised after tracer has equilibrated throughout all nodal basins
The sentinel node is the first node visualised after peritumoral tracer injection and is used for tumour staging
The sentinel node is defined by focal breast uptake on molecular breast imaging
The sentinel node is diagnosed by renal excretion after MAG3 injection
The sentinel node is a false-positive bowel focus on Octreoscan
options_after: The sentinel node is the last node visualised after tracer has equilibrated throughout most nodal basins
The sentinel node is the first node visualised after peritumoral tracer injection and is used for tumour staging
The sentinel node is defined by focal breast uptake on molecular breast imaging
The sentinel node is diagnosed by renal excretion after MAG3 injection
The sentinel node is a false-positive bowel focus on Octreoscan
updates.explanation: For cancers that metastasise first to regional lymph nodes, such as melanoma and breast carcinoma, lymphoscintigraphy maps drainage from the tumour after peritumoral injection. The first node visualised is the sentinel node and can be localised intraoperatively with a gamma probe for excision. The other choices describe unrelated nuclear medicine applications from the same chapter.
